articles.title: Cisco and OpenAI launch Shirudo open-source infrastructure shield to prevent AI-driven cyberattacks
articles.text:
Cisco and OpenAI launch Shirudo open-source infrastructure shield to prevent AI-driven cyberattacks
Cybercriminals have gained the ability to discover vulnerabilities in software and take advantage of them in seconds, and it’s all thanks to artificial intelligence. Enterprises need a better way to defend themselves, so it’s fitting that one of the world’s top AI companies, OpenAI Group PBC, together with Cisco Systems Inc., is stepping up with a solution.
They’ve just announced a new, open-source and extremely ambitious initiative called the Secure Infrastructure Project, which aims to ensure that all AI computing infrastructure is secure by design and capable of defending against lightning-fast AI-driven attacks. The first project within that initiative is Shirudo, which is designed to protect infrastructure systems automatically from critical exploits before they can be patched.
In a blog post, Cisco Security Chief Technology Officer and Vice President of Engineering Thomas Graf explained that the industry has always treated security as an afterthought, essentially something that’s bolted onto systems after the fact. It has gotten away with this because much of the world’s computing infrastructure was built for workflows that proceed at human speeds. But with the emergence of AI models that can discover and work out how to exploit vulnerabilities in a matter of seconds, this kind of reactive security is no longer enough.
According to Graf, even now, when a major vulnerability is discovered in widely used software, it can take weeks or even months to come up with a fix and ensure that every major system is patched against it. “That timeframe is no longer acceptable given that the mean time to exploitation has become negative, meaning that a growing number of vulnerabilities are now being exploited before they are publicly disclosed,” he said. “This will only accelerate with the further evolution of AI models and cybersecurity capabilities, becoming the norm in open-weight models.”
To counter these kinds of automated attacks, Cisco and OpenAI believe that infrastructure has to be rebuilt from scratch with security in mind. They argue that it’s time to abandon static defenses and embrace systems that are hardened by default, immutable and rebuildable from a previous “good” state, so users can quickly revert back in the event of an attack. To do this, infrastructure systems must be based on Trusted Platform Modules and utilize reinforcement learning techniques to safely test their own defenses so they can adapt when faced with novel cyberattacks from previously unknown vectors.
Graf said the key to doing this is to secure workloads at runtime, which is why the initial focus of Cisco’s and OpenAI’s initiative is Shirudo, an evolution of the open-source Tetragon runtime security project that aims to provide autonomous defense for AI agents.
Shirudo, named after the Japanese word for “shield,” is based on extended Berkeley Packet Filter or eBPF, which is a Linux kernel technology that acts like a kind of sandbox within the operating system. Similar to how JavaScript makes web browsers programmable without a restart, eBPF enables small, verified programs to run inside the Linux kernel to observe an application’s activity and modify its behavior without altering its source code or rebooting it.
Graf explained that Cisco and OpenAI chose to use eBPF because there are no other real alternatives. Human-focused security consoles and policy languages are simply too slow for AI agents, and will limit their productivity.
By exposing programmable kernel interfaces, eBPF enables AI agents to capture granular telemetry, evaluate mitigations in monitoring mode and deploy cryptographically-signed shields in milliseconds. So cyberattacks that exploit unknown vulnerabilities can be blocked in real time without causing disruption to their live workloads.
“There is nothing more important than giving security teams the tools they need to match the speed of the AI-driven threats they are facing,” said Cisco President and Chief Product Officer Jeetu Patel. “We need self-defending infrastructure that acts at the speed of code, learns in real time and shields itself until patches are safely rolled out.”
OpenAI’s role in this is to prove that eBPF is up to the job, and it has already deployed Shirudo as part of an agentic control plane that’s powered by its Codex coding agent. When given details of a new vulnerability, Codex can use Shirudo to autonomously build an exploit reproducer and then design a mitigation strategy. It then validates the mitigation code and deploys the cryptographically-signed shields across all affected nodes.
The two partners recently tested Shirudo against a critical new vulnerability in OpenJDK called Java4Shell, and it was able to rapidly generate Java bytecode that it injected directly into a running Elasticsearch agent to block malicious Base64 overwrites that would have compromised the system.
OpenAI co-founder and President Greg Brockman said the goal of Shirudo is to help companies protect their systems from new threats until they can build and deploy a more durable patch. “When one team finds a better way to protect a system, others shouldn’t have to start from scratch,” he explained.
To that end, Cisco and OpenAI say they’re welcoming developers, kernel engineers, platform builders and security experts to collaborate on Shirudo and other initiatives within their broader Secure Infrastructure Project.

articles.title: Penguin shows off photonic memory box at SC26 that can expand AI accelerator capacity over optical links — device sports up to 576GB of HBM3E, customer samples expected in 2027
articles.text:
Penguin shows off photonic memory box at SC26 that can expand AI accelerator capacity over optical links — device sports up to 576GB of HBM3E, customer samples expected in 2027
Additional support is required for existing accelerators
Penguin Solutions showed off its MemoryAI Photonic Appliance remote memory system at Supercomputer 2026 (SC26), with customer samples scheduled for the second half of 2027. The device supports up to 576 GB of HBM3E with an aggregate bandwidth of up to 7.2 TB/s, and connects to systems using optical interconnects via the CXL.mem 3.1 protocol. HBM memory capacity is usually one of the major bottlenecks of contemporary AI accelerators, which is why, when developers face it, they tend to add or upgrade their accelerators. Penguin Solutions' new device aims to solve that, but there are drawbacks.
The MemoryAI Photonic Appliance is designed to accommodate up to 576 GB of HBM3E and 16 TB of DDR5 memory, with overall bandwidth targeting 7.2 TB/s. The external memory box supports three memory access configurations: HBM Direct Mode, HBM-DDR5 Cached Mode, and DDR5 Direct Mode. The first provides access to external HBM3E, the second combines HBM3E and DDR5 in a tiered memory sub-system with HBM3E acting like a write-through cache for DDR5, while the third provides access to DDR5 without an intermediate HBM cache. Meanwhile, hardware semaphores (HSEMs) enable software-managed memory consistency across multiple host processors (i.e., if more than one host processor accesses the same memory location, software can use semaphores to ensure that only one host processor can modify data).
The Penguin appliance relies on Marvell's architecture that consists of Photonic Fabric Memory Modules (PFMMs) and Photonic Fabric network interface cards (PF-NICs). The device uses eight PFMM modules; each integrates a memory controller, eight DDR5 DIMM interfaces, 72 GB of HBM3E cache, and a photonic interposer with 16 transmit and 16 receive channels operating at 224 Gbps. This provides approximately 7.2 Tbps of aggregate bidirectional optical bandwidth per module, or 57.6 Tbps (7.2 TB/s) for the entire appliance, equivalent to approximately 3.6 TB/s in each direction.
Marvell offers two ways to connect processors to the external memory pool. The first uses a Photonic Fabric network interface card (PF-NIC) with PCIe 6.0 and CXL 3.1 connectivity, which provides up to 2 Tbps of bandwidth and memory access latency below 350ns, excluding PCIe/CXL overhead. The second relies on a Photonic Fabric chiplet integrated into an XPU, which offers up to 14.4 Tbps of bandwidth and latency below 200ns. Both approaches enable processors to access shared memory over optical links across distances of up to 30 meters. Meanwhile, the chiplet approach requires accelerator designers to install the chiplet, while transparent memory expansion using the PF-NIC requires the host to support its memory mapping at both the hardware and software levels.
Marvell's architecture is designed to enable compatible host systems to access external memory through ordinary load/store memory operations rather than RDMA data transfers, but this requires specific hardware capabilities on the host side. Most modern CPUs support PCIe as well as the CXL.mem protocol for memory expansion. However, the situation is different for AI GPUs.
Nvidia's data center GPUs support PCIe, NVLink, and various memory management mechanisms, but they do not support a general-purpose CXL.mem host interface for memory expansion. Similarly, AMD's Instinct accelerators use PCIe and Infinity Fabric for connectivity, but they do not generally support CXL.mem. In theory, accelerators without native CXL.mem support could theoretically access the appliance through a CXL-capable CPU, provided their coherent interconnect supports access to CXL-attached memory. However, this would introduce additional latency, which will extend well beyond the advertised sub-350ns figure (which already excludes PCIe/CXL overhead), which could greatly reduce the actual performance benefits provided by extra capacity.
As a result, PFMMs and Penguin's MemoryAI Photonic Appliance can extend usable memory capacity only for select host systems without major performance penalties. These could include custom XPUs equipped with Marvell's Photonic Fabric chiplets, CPUs or other PUs that support CXL.mem and PF-NIC with memory mapping mechanism, and potentially future AI accelerators that support CXL.mem or integrate Marvell's Photonic Fabric. Obviously, this means that such systems will get an indisputable advantage over machines based on conventional accelerators from AMD and Nvidia in the form of memory upgrades.
Speaking of advantages, we must note that while an aggregate bi-directional bandwidth target of 7.2 TB/s (3.6 TB/s in both directions) seems formidable (it is only a bit lower than memory bandwidth of B300 SXM that comes at 7.7 TB/s), it is set to be shared between multiple accelerators (eight accelerators in a hypothetical scenario), which will provide limited bandwidth to each one. Although Penguin promises transparent access to external memory without modifications to applications, the appliance will require compatible memory management software (in addition to host hardware), which will treat external memory as another memory tier. While extra memory is always welcome, performance benefits of complex multi-tier memory subsystems depend heavily on workloads and efficient data placement. Consequently, the appliance's practical advantages remain to be demonstrated.
Penguin showcased the appliance this week; however, customer samples are scheduled for the second half of 2027, which likely means that the device and/or underlying hardware, firmware, and software need polishing. That said, practical performance and economic advantages of Penguin's MemoryAI Photonic Appliance remain to be seen when everything works as intended. In any case, do not expect deployments of such systems before 2028. This begs the question of where Penguin Solutions plans to source HBM3E in volume in 2028, when the industry will have transitioned to HBM4 and will be in the midst of transition to HBM4E.
Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: Investigadores espiaron conversaciones y siguieron por GPS a un Volkswagen ID.4 mediante Bluetooth
articles.text:
Investigadores de la empresa húngara de ciberseguridad PCA Cyber Security demostraron que un Volkswagen ID.4 puede ser intervenido por Bluetooth para escuchar a sus ocupantes y seguir su ubicación por GPS. Ante esta situación, Volkswagen afirmó que ya distribuye una actualización y que no habrá retiro de vehículos.
La demostración se realizó en Budapest, capital de Hungría, ante periodistas del diario británico The Times. Desde una computadora fuera del auto, los expertos activaron el micrófono del sistema de manos libres, rastrearon el auto y accionaron la calefacción, los limpiaparabrisas y el techo corredizo.
Los investigadores leyeron mensajes de texto y contactos del celular conectado, grabaron una charla entre conductor y acompañante con el micrófono pensado para llamadas a emergencias, y mostraron en la pantalla un mensaje que decía “hackeado por PCA”.
Una cadena de cuatro fallas conocida desde 2025
El ataque usado durante la investigación usa cuatro vulnerabilidades, bautizadas PerfektBlue, en BlueSDK, un programa de Bluetooth de la empresa OpenSynergy que varios fabricantes integran en el sistema de información y entretenimiento de sus autos. PCA publicó el aviso técnico el 7 de julio de 2025. Según ese documento, encadenadas permiten ejecutar código ajeno con un solo clic del usuario.
El aviso detalla que PCA comprobó el ataque en el sistema de un ID.4 y en el de un Skoda Superb, sumado a un banco de pruebas de Mercedes-Benz. También detectó parte de las fallas en varios BMW, aunque no completó un ataque en esos autos.
PCA afirma que OpenSynergy confirmó los errores y distribuyó parches en septiembre de 2024, pero que no todos los fabricantes los recibieron hasta junio de 2025.
Según el mismo documento, PCA comunicó al grupo de respuesta a incidentes de Volkswagen el 19 de junio de 2024, el día en que confirmó las fallas en el ID.4.
Qué dice Volkswagen y qué debe hacer el dueño de cada vehículo
Un vocero de Volkswagen dijo a heise online que la empresa investigó las vulnerabilidades y que el problema afecta a una generación anterior del sistema, que aparentemente ya no se instala en modelos eléctricos actuales como el ID. Polo. Aseguró que los atacantes no pueden acceder dirección, frenos ni acelerador: “En ningún momento hubo ni hay peligro” para clientes o vehículos.
La empresa explicó que corrigió la falla rápido en los modelos ID. con software posterior a la versión 5.0. En las versiones anteriores tardó más porque debió modificar un sistema de gestión ya planificado y completar nuevos procesos de seguridad.
La actualización 3.9.1 llega desde hace unas tres semanas a autos con software anterior a la versión 4.0 y se instala de forma inalámbrica, por red de datos o WiFi, con el auto estacionado. Los autos con versiones posteriores a la 4.0 deben pasar por un taller. Según Volkswagen, los que tienen la versión 5.6 o una más reciente no están afectados.
El ataque exige condiciones concretas: el conductor debe aceptar una solicitud de emparejamiento Bluetooth. Volkswagen aconseja no aceptar nunca solicitudes desconocidas ni conectar dispositivos USB ajenos. PCA advierte que, según cómo cada fabricante configure el sistema, en algunos dispositivos las fallas podrían alcanzarse antes del emparejamiento.
Cuál información queda expuesta cuando falla el sistema Bluetooth
El riesgo principal de una intrusión en el sistema de información y entretenimiento no se limita a funciones del vehículo. Estos sistemas suelen concentrar la libreta de contactos, registros de llamadas, mensajes, ubicaciones recientes y datos de los teléfonos que se conectaron al auto. Esa información puede revelar rutinas, vínculos personales y trayectos frecuentes de los ocupantes.
Asimismo, la separación entre los sistemas de confort y conectividad, por un lado, y los controles de conducción, por otro, reduce la posibilidad de que una falla afecte el manejo del vehículo. Sin embargo, no elimina el impacto sobre la privacidad. Por eso, las actualizaciones de software y una gestión cuidadosa de los dispositivos vinculados son parte de la seguridad cotidiana de un auto conectado.

articles.title: CrowdStrike's Zscaler deal is a $44B vote for platformization and a long-term threat to Palo Alto Networks
articles.text:
CrowdStrike’s Zscaler deal is a $44B vote for platformization and a long-term threat to Palo Alto Networks
For decades, the security industry has told buyers to choose best-of-breed security products, leaving practitioners to stitch them together.
This has been perpetuated by the major analyst firms, which have a Wave for this product and a Magic Quadrant for that product. The reality is that choosing best-of-breed everywhere has never led to best-in-class threat protection.
Palo Alto Networks Inc. has long articulated the value of security platformization. To be precise, Fortinet Inc. was the first vendor to advance the concept of a security platform, but no security provider has pushed the industry as hard as Palo Alto. Chief Executice Nikesh Arora has been vocal about platforms as the only way to truly protect the entire attack surface.
CrowdStrike Holdings Inc.’s agreement to acquire Zscaler Inc. for $43.9 billion strongly supports the thesis. SiliconANGLE has been covering the deal, so I won’t rehash the details. In short, the leader in endpoint security is buying the leader in cloud-delivered zero-trust access. The combined company is expected to start with more than $10 billion in annual recurring revenue, and the deal is expected to close between August 2027 and January 2028.
Over the long term, the combination poses a real threat to Palo Alto. In the short term, it is a strong co-sell opportunity for CrowdStrike and Zscaler, with significant integration work between the two.
A $44B vote for platformization
Arora has long argued that customers want fewer vendors and integrated platforms. Getting there can be challenging, as security teams often operate with an “if it ain’t broke, don’t fix it” mentality. The mere thought of replacing a working product is enough to keep even the most seasoned security pros up at night. In February 2024, when he cut guidance to fund the platform push, Palo Alto’s stock fell 28% in a day. Since then, the stock has recovered nicely, validating his strategy, and its rival has now raised $44 billion to head down its own platform journey.
In some ways, CrowdStrike and Zscaler were the strongest argument against platformization, though one could argue that each was its own smaller “platform,” depending on how you define it. Each led its category, and the two were close partners, with more than 2,000 shared customers and 16 product integrations. If best-of-breed products, tied together by integrations, could work anywhere, it was here. The two companies are now taking it a step further. “When you integrate as partners, there’s only so much you can do,” Zscaler founder and CEO Jay Chaudhry said on the analyst call.
The “why now?” question is worth asking, as the coming together of these two companies has been rumored for some time. The answer is that agentic AI creates new challenges and risks that are difficult to address through a partnership. An AI agent runs on a device and then crosses the network to access models, tools, and data, operating at machine speed around the clock. A vendor that sees only the device or only the network sees only half of what the agent does. CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz said adversaries are “exploiting the seams and the gaps between companies’ integrations.”
I agree. Every seam between products is a place for an attacker to hide, and AI-driven attacks exploit those seams faster than security teams can close them. But a platform is more than one vendor and one contract. It means one dataset, one agent, and one policy engine, so a detection on a laptop triggers enforcement across the network without a person in the middle. If that’s the standard, CrowdStrike, while it currently describes itself as a platform, is not today.
A best-in-class SASE stack built for resilience
With Zscaler, CrowdStrike is more than just a product to fill a gap. Zscaler is a best-in-class Secure Access Service Edge stack that protects half of the Fortune 500 and runs what it calls the world’s largest inline security cloud.
It is also built for resilience, which matters more than ever. Last week, I wrote about six major outages over six days at organizations ranging from Microsoft to the Federal Aviation Administration. Zscaler sits between every user and every application, so if it fails, the business stops. That has forced the company to engineer for failure.
Its Business Continuity Cloud provides each customer with a dedicated backup environment in third-party data centers, on separate networks and DNS, with software updates deliberately staggered so a bad release can’t affect both simultaneously. “No linkage — no network, no shared routers, no switches, no shared network operations,” Chaudhry told me in a previous conversation.
Of all companies, CrowdStrike should value that. In July 2024, a faulty Falcon update affected an estimated 8.5 million Windows devices. The standard objection to platformization is concentration risk, and it intensifies when a single vendor controls both the endpoint agent and the path to every application. Zscaler’s continuity design is the best answer to that objection I’ve seen, and CrowdStrike should extend it across Falcon.
Short-term, a great co-sell opportunity
The near-term value is commercial. CrowdStrike says about 8,000 Zscaler customers don’t yet buy from it. Channel partners already sell both companies, and the two sales teams already work deals together.
After the close, Zscaler will transition to Falcon Flex, CrowdStrike’s licensing model. “A Zscaler customer can add Falcon. A Falcon customer can add Zscaler. One contract, one platform,” Kurtz said. CrowdStrike expects about $1 billion in annualized revenue synergies within 30 months of closing.
This target seems bullish but achievable, as it requires no code integration — only sales execution, which both companies are good at.
The integration work is still ahead
Today, the Falcon sensor and Zscaler’s client run as separate agents on separate clouds with different release schedules. Kurtz promised that it will collapse into one. “The brand promise, single agent, that’s not going to change,” he said. CrowdStrike’s next-generation sensor can already inspect and proxy network traffic, he added, which should make the job easier.
Kurtz was also candid about the effort: “Yes, there’s hard work to be done. There always is in an acquisition.” CrowdStrike gave no timeline. The engineering teams can’t combine until the deal closes, which is at least eight months away. CrowdStrike’s largest prior acquisition cost less than $1 billion. Folding Zscaler’s global security cloud into Falcon is far harder than anything it has attempted. Until that work is done, the platform exists on slides.
A long-term threat to Palo Alto Networks
That gap gives Palo Alto time to further its own platform. It closed its CyberArk acquisition in February, renamed the business Idira, and is already cross-selling it to its existing customers.
The long term looks different. If CrowdStrike delivers a single agent and a single dataset, Palo Alto will face something it hasn’t had: a rival of similar scale with the leading endpoint product and the leading zero-trust cloud on one platform. Palo Alto is most exposed in SASE, where its Prisma SASE business has been chasing Zscaler.
The missing piece is a firewall
CrowdStrike plus Zscaler make a formidable platform, but it still lacks a firewall. Zscaler is a cloud proxy, and many enterprises that use it still run firewalls in their data centers, campuses, and clouds. That is Palo Alto’s core area of strength.
Looking ahead, that should open the door to another acquisition. Check Point is the obvious choice, as it will struggle over the long term as a firewall pure-play in a market shifting to platforms, and it would give CrowdStrike a large installed base. If CrowdStrike wants a broader networking portfolio, Fortinet is the bigger swing, with switching, wireless and software-defined wide-area network alongside its firewalls. The two already partner on endpoint and firewall protection.
Either deal would add more integration work to Zscaler, so I wouldn’t expect either to happen soon. But a company that wants to displace Palo Alto can’t leave the firewall to someone else forever. I understand zero trust can replace a number of firewalls, particularly in branch offices, but firewalls are here to stay for the foreseeable future.
Smaller vendors are now in play
The deal also puts smaller security vendors in play. Netskope and Cato Networks are both independent SASE vendors competing against a bundle, and Oppenheimer has already named Netskope an attractive target.
Fortinet is an obvious acquirer, but the buyer pool extends beyond security companies. Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co., following its acquisition of Juniper Networks Inc., is embedding security across its network and may seek to bolster that portfolio. Dell Technologies Inc. lags in security, with a portfolio centered on data protection and resilience, and could benefit from an acquisition to close the gap.
What this means for buyers
Nothing changes today, and customers shouldn’t pause their projects. I’d use the waiting period to prepare in advance.
Buy what is integrated. Ask for the integration roadmap with dates for the single agent, the shared data set and unified policy. Until those ship, evaluate CrowdStrike and Zscaler as two products.
Use leverage. Palo Alto is trying to pry Zscaler accounts loose, and CrowdStrike and Zscaler want commitments before the close. As Sanchit Vir Gogia of Greyhound Research told CSO, “Consolidation is sold at the first signature and priced at the second.” Negotiate price caps for renewals now.
Get interoperability in writing. When asked about lock-in, Kurtz said, “We have and will continue to work well with all of the other technologies and ecosystem.” If you run Zscaler with another endpoint product or Falcon with another access provider, include that promise in your contract.
Make resilience a requirement. Ask CrowdStrike to commit to maintaining Zscaler’s Business Continuity Cloud and its staggered updates, and to apply the same discipline to a combined agent.
Final thoughts
This deal settles the argument over platformization. Who wins is still unclear. CrowdStrike has to do the integration work, and Palo Alto has the better part of a year to persuade customers not to wait. The great news for customers is that big moves like this create a wave of innovation. AI is changing security faster than ever before, and a CrowdStrike-vs.-Palo Alto battle is good for everyone.
Zeus Kerravala is a principal analyst at ZK Research, a division of Kerravala Consulting. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE.

articles.title: Forget Sonos, this stunning Dolby Atmos soundbar from a home theater newcomer is easily my favorite model I’ve tested — I'd even chose it over Bose, JBL, Sony, and more
articles.text:
Marshall’s awesome Dolby Atmos soundbar is the stunning centerpiece of my living room, and easily my favorite Sonos Arc Ultra alternative — here's why I prefer it over options from Bose, JBL and Sony
The most beautiful soundbar ever made, now at a record-low price
A Dolby Atmos soundbar can take movie nights to a whole new level — expansive, multi-dimensional audio, crystal-clear dialogue, and powerful bass can make it feel as if you’re down at the local multiplex, rather than sitting in the comfort of your own home. And right now, you can get my favorite Dolby Atmos soundbar around for less, because the Marshall Heston 120 is $999 (was $1,299) at Amazon.
In the UK? I've got you. The Marshall Heston 120 is £599 (was £899) at John Lewis, taking it to a record-low price. With a $300 / £300 saving, there's truly no better time to get your hands on the Heston 120, which offers immersive — no, hypnotic sound, exceptional features, and a jaw-droppingly gorgeous design.
• Browse the full Amazon Black Friday sale
I've been using the Marshall Heston 120 as my main soundbar at home for more than a year now, and I absolutely love it. Today's best Marshall Heston 60 deals

Right now, you can save 40% on one of the best compact soundbars on the market. The Marshall Heston 60 carries the same visual allure as its big sibling, with ultra-clear dialogue, impressive bass, and excellent Atmos effects to match. And you'll struggle to find any other soundbar this good for less than £300.
In my Marshall Heston 120 review, I awarded the audio specialist's first-ever soundbar five stars, describing it as "an unforgettable debut in the home theater world". It's great for movies, with regimented, driven bass that can make action-packed sequences and dark movie scores feel so impactful, dialogue is always exceptionally clear, and the 11 active drivers conjure up an almost tangible sense of space.
But there are so many other things that make the Heston 120 ideal for everyday life. For instance, there are so many connectivity options, including HDMI eARC, Wi-Fi (for higher-res music streaming on the fly), Bluetooth, and RCA. I'm also a big fan of the 4K 120Hz HDMI passthrough port, which I use for my Nintendo Switch 2.
And I love the Marshall Heston 60 too — I also reviewed this one and gave it a very high 4.5-star rating. The thing that stands out about the Heston 60 for me is the sheer scale of its Atmos effects. With 4K Blu-rays, I found that the Heston 60 created an incredible sense of depth to its sound, and it often truly felt as if sounds were coming from above me, or even the corners of our testing room.
If you want a great soundbar deal during Black Friday, look no further — these Marshall models are top-tier, and with discounts like this, I couldn't recommend them enough.

articles.title: CyberPowerPC Expands AI Workstation Line with Compact AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 Powered Desktop
articles.text:
Monday, November 23rd 2026
CyberPowerPC Expands AI Workstation Line with Compact AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 Powered Desktop
CyberPowerPC, a leading manufacturer of high-performance custom PCs, gaming rigs, and workstations, today announced its compact AI Workstation ASRock AI BOX-A395, powered by the AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 processor. The company also previewed its upcoming enterprise-grade AMD Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 AI Workstation Series, planned for release in Q4 2026.
Designed to bring powerful computing capabilities to a compact desktop footprint, the AI BOX-A395 combines a 16-core AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 processor, 128 GB of LPDDR5X memory and integrated AMD Radeon 8060S graphics. The system lets developers, engineers, AI practitioners and creative professionals run AI models locally, develop applications and run productivity and creative software.AI development is moving from the cloud to local setups. Compact workstations such as CyberPowerPC's AI workstation let users build, test, and run AI applications on their own hardware. It includes substantial memory, integrated graphics acceleration, and high-speed connectivity to handle compatible local AI models and other compute-heavy tasks.
Eric Cheung, CyberPowerPC CEO"AI is creating new demands for desktop computing, and professionals need systems that can handle AI workloads alongside their everyday applications. Our AI BOX-A395 brings substantial processing power and 128 GB of memory into a compact system that gives developers and creators a practical platform for local AI experimentation and demanding workloads. With our upcoming AMD Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 workstation series, we're also preparing to address the needs of enterprise customers looking for powerful, compact AI computing solutions."
Compact Design, Serious AI Computing Capabilities
The CyberPowerPC AI Workstation ASRock AI BOX-A395 is designed to deliver robust computing capabilities without the footprint of a traditional tower workstation.
Key features include:
- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 processor: A 16-core processor with boost speeds up to 5.1 GHz, designed to support demanding multitasking, development and compute-intensive workloads.
- 128 GB LPDDR5X memory: High-capacity onboard memory operating at up to 8,000 MT/s, providing room for compatible AI models, development environments and memory-intensive applications.
- Integrated AMD Radeon 8060S graphics: Integrated graphics acceleration for supported AI, visualization and creative workloads.
- Configurable PCIe NVMe storage: Two M.2 PCIe Gen 4 x4 SSD slots provide storage expansion options for applications, datasets, project files and local AI model libraries.
- High-speed connectivity: USB4, Wi-Fi 7, 10 Gb Ethernet and 2.5 Gb Ethernet support connectivity to compatible peripherals, storage and networks.
- Space-saving enclosure: The compact aluminium chassis measures approximately 200 × 100 × 232 mm (7.87" x 3.94" x 9.13"), making it suitable for professional desks, development spaces and other environments where space is at a premium.
This workstation is well suited for AI development and experimentation, local model inference, software development, engineering projects, digital content creation, and demanding multitasking workloads.
Coming in Q4: AMD Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 AI Workstation Series
Building on its current AI workstation offering, CyberPowerPC is preparing an enterprise-oriented workstation series powered by AMD Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 processors, with a planned Q4 2026 release.
The forthcoming series is intended to extend compact AI computing into professional and enterprise environments, combining high-performance processing, substantial unified memory and integrated graphics and AI acceleration in a small-form-factor desktop platform.
The AMD Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 processor platform features 16 Zen 5 CPU cores, integrated AMD Radeon 8065S graphics with 40 compute units, and a dedicated neural processing unit (NPU) rated at up to 55 TOPS. The platform also supports enterprise-focused security capabilities and professional deployment considerations.
CyberPowerPC plans to offer a configuration featuring 128 GB of LPDDR5X memory and configurable PCIe NVMe SSD storage, targeting developers, engineering teams, data scientists and organizations looking to run supported AI workloads locally.
By bringing enterprise-oriented processing and AI acceleration into a compact desktop design, the planned PRO series is intended to complement existing workstation environments and provide another option for organizations evaluating local AI infrastructure.
Additional details, including final system configurations, pricing and availability, will be announced closer to launch.
Availability
The CyberPowerPC AI Workstation ASRock AI BOX-A395 is available now with a starting price of $4,579, including 128 GB of LPDDR5X memory and a 1 TB PCIe NVMe SSD. Additional storage and configuration options are available.
Source:
				CyberPowerPC

articles.title: JBL Live 770NC : ce casque Bluetooth avec 65 heures d'autonomie perd plus de 100 €
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 - Le casque à réduction de bruit JBL Live 770NC est à 76,99 € (-57 %)
Réduction de bruit adaptative, multipoint et jusqu'à 65 heures d'autonomie : le casque JBL Live 770NC passe à 76,99 € chez Amazon.
Vendu et expédié par Amazon, le casque sans fil JBL Live 770NC en noir affiche 76,99 € contre 179,99 € pour le prix conseillé, soit une remise de 57 %. Il est noté 4,6/5 sur près de 3 600 avis, et plus de 500 exemplaires ont été achetés le mois dernier. Nous lui avons attribué 3 étoiles sur 5 lors de notre test.
Un son puissant et une réduction de bruit adaptative
Ce casque circum-auriculaire est équipé de haut-parleurs de 40 mm et prend en charge le JBL Spatial Sound. Sa réduction de bruit adaptative s'ajuste à l'environnement, tandis que le mode Smart Ambient laisse entendre ce qui se passe autour de soi.
Lors de notre test, nous avons apprécié son son très puissant, sa bonne isolation et son ergonomie.
Une autonomie de 65 heures
Le point fort de ce casque reste son autonomie, annoncée jusqu'à 65 heures. Une recharge rapide de 5 minutes offre 4 heures d'écoute supplémentaires. Il gère la connexion multipoint et peut aussi s'utiliser en filaire grâce au câble audio fourni. La musique se met en pause quand on retire le casque et reprend quand on le remet.
Notre test relève toutefois une scène sonore étroite, des basses trop en avant et un micro inutilisable dans un environnement bruyant.

articles.text:

Cette sélection s’ouvre sur les neuf produits que nous avons testés, de l’iPhone Air à la Kindle Colorsoft, avant de passer à ceux que nous n’avons pas eus entre les mains. Elle couvre les smartphones, l’audio, le Mac, les TV et écrans de jeu, la maison connectée et l’électroménager, avec des remises de 9 % à 67 % sur le prix barré. La plus forte économie en euros concerne l’écran LG UltraGear de 45 pouces (800 € de moins), la plus forte en pourcentage la caméra Blink Outdoor 4 (-67 %).

Maison et beauté 🏠

iPhone Air : 350 € de moins sur l’iPhone le plus fin, noté 8/10, à 979 €
Notre test de l’iPhone Air lui a attribué 8/10. Il ne mesure que 5,6 mm d’épaisseur pour 165 g, moins que l’iPhone 16e, et reprend la puce A19 Pro avec un cœur graphique en moins. Cette version 256 Go Noir sidéral est vendue et expédiée par Amazon.
✅ Points forts
- Un format plume : 5,6 mm d’épaisseur et 165 g, plus léger que l’iPhone 16e.
- La puce des iPhone Pro : l’A19 Pro, avec un cœur graphique en moins que sur l’iPhone 17 Pro Max.
- À savoir : l’autonomie tient une journée, sans plus, et il n’a qu’un capteur photo et un haut-parleur.
AirPods Pro 3 : nos écouteurs notés 9/10 sous les 190 €, à 188 €
Notre test des AirPods Pro 3 leur a attribué 9/10, avec la note maximale pour l’isolation et le micro. Nous avons mesuré un peu plus de 8 h 20 d’autonomie avec la réduction de bruit, et la certification passe à IP57, boîtier compris.
✅ Points forts
- Une isolation au sommet : 10/10 en isolation et en microphone dans notre test.
- Plus robustes : la certification IP57 les protège de la poussière et des immersions.
- À savoir : le boîtier n’assure plus que deux recharges complètes.
MacBook Air M5 : 200 € de remise sur le portable noté 8/10, à 1 199 €
Notre test du MacBook Air M5 lui a attribué 8/10, en saluant une puce M5 qui se passe de ventilateur, plus de stockage pour le même prix et un excellent combo clavier/trackpad. Cette offre porte sur le modèle de 13 pouces avec 16 Go de mémoire et 512 Go de SSD.
✅ Points forts
- Un silence absolu : la puce M5 se passe de ventilateur.
- 512 Go dès l’entrée de gamme : un SSD que notre test juge enfin rapide.
- À savoir : nous avons mesuré 10 à 12 heures d’autonomie, contre 18 heures annoncées par Apple, et le modèle 13 pouces est livré sans adaptateur secteur.
Mac mini M6 : 160 € de remise sur le mini PC d’Apple noté 8/10, à 889 €
Notre test du Mac mini M6 lui a attribué 8/10, en saluant la puissance de la puce M6 et un boîtier de 12,7 cm de côté qui ne chauffe pas et ne fait pas de bruit. L’offre porte sur l’entrée de gamme, avec 16 Go de mémoire et 256 Go de SSD.
✅ Points forts
- Une puissance qui fascine : environ 15 % plus rapide en monocœur et près de 56 % en multicœur que le Mac mini M4 sous Cinebench R24, selon notre test.
- Un format minuscule : 12,7 cm de côté pour 670 g, avec trois ports Thunderbolt 4, une sortie HDMI et de l’Ethernet 2,5 Gigabit.
- À savoir : seulement 256 Go de stockage dans cette configuration, et le SSD est soudé.
Galaxy S26 Ultra : 470 € de remise sur le smartphone noté 9/10, à 1 099 €
Notre test du Galaxy S26 Ultra lui a attribué 9/10, en saluant la qualité de son écran, le filtre de confidentialité intégré à la dalle, ses performances et sa charge enfin rapide. Cette version 256 Go Noir est vendue et expédiée par Amazon, avec un chargeur secteur 25 W dans la boîte.
✅ Points forts
- Un écran anti-espion : le filtre de confidentialité est intégré directement à la dalle.
- Une charge enfin rapide : jusqu’à 60 W, l’un des points forts relevés dans notre test.
- À savoir : notre test lui reproche un design qui évolue peu et un prix de lancement très élevé.
Sony WH-1000XM5 : le casque noté 9/10 sous son plus bas des 30 derniers jours, à 217,99 €
Notre test du Sony WH-1000XM5 lui a attribué 9/10. Nous avons mesuré environ 30 heures d’autonomie avec la réduction de bruit en AAC, et 3 minutes de charge rendent environ 3 heures d’écoute. Amazon le vend 217,99 €, sous les 245 € de son prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours.
✅ Points forts
- Une autonomie confirmée : environ 30 h avec réduction de bruit lors de notre test.
- Une recharge express : 3 minutes de charge pour environ 3 heures d’écoute.
- À savoir : il ne se plie plus, et son successeur, le WH-1000XM6, est désormais en vente.
Switch 2 + Zelda: Ocarina of Time : la console notée 8/10 avec le remake en code, à 509,98 €
Notre test de la Nintendo Switch 2 lui a attribué 8/10. Son écran LCD de 7,9 pouces passe en 1080p à 120 Hz avec HDR, et elle embarque 12 Go de mémoire. Amazon la vend avec le code de téléchargement de Zelda: Ocarina of Time, dans sa version à batterie remplaçable par l’utilisateur.
✅ Points forts
- Un écran plus grand et plus fluide : 7,9 pouces en 1080p à 120 Hz avec HDR.
- Un jeu inclus : le remake de Zelda: Ocarina of Time, exclusif à la Switch 2, en code de téléchargement.
- À savoir : Amazon ne vend plus la console seule en promotion : la remise passe par ce pack.
JBL Xtreme 4 : l’enceinte notée 8/10 à moitié prix, à 169,99 €
Notre test de la JBL Xtreme 4 lui a attribué 8/10, en saluant un rendu de qualité, une autonomie gargantuesque et une batterie remplaçable. Certifiée IP67, elle annonce jusqu’à 24 heures d’autonomie, selon la fiche Amazon.
✅ Points forts
- Costaude : certification IP67 contre l’eau et la poussière.
- Une batterie remplaçable : un atout rare relevé dans notre test.
- À savoir : elle pèse 2,1 kg et a perdu son entrée ligne.
Kindle Colorsoft : la liseuse couleur d’Amazon à 45 % de remise, à 164,99 €
Cette Kindle Colorsoft de 16 Go, modèle 2024, est la liseuse à écran couleur d’Amazon. Notre test de la Kindle Colorsoft, mené sur la version Signature Edition, lui a attribué 6/10 : nous y avons trouvé une liseuse très réactive, avec très peu de rémanence.
✅ Points forts
- Très réactive : même lors des zooms, selon notre test.
- Très peu de rémanence : les pages se tournent sans traces visibles.
- À savoir : notre test a relevé les défauts habituels des dalles Kaleido 3 et l’enfermement dans les services Amazon.
Galaxy Buds3 Pro : les écouteurs haut de gamme de Samsung à moitié prix, à 119,99 €
Selon la fiche Amazon, ces écouteurs combinent réduction active de bruit, audio 360 et fonctions Galaxy AI. Le prix barré de 249,95 € est un ancien prix pratiqué par Amazon. Nous ne les avons pas testés : leur successeur a obtenu 8/10 dans notre test des Galaxy Buds 4 Pro.
✅ Points forts
- Plus de la moitié de remise : 52 % sous l’ancien prix pratiqué par Amazon.
- Réduction de bruit et audio 360 : les deux fonctions phares annoncées par Samsung.
- À savoir : les fonctions avancées sont pensées pour les smartphones Galaxy.
Galaxy Watch8 : 110 € de moins sur la montre connectée de Samsung, à 219,99 €
Samsung présente la Galaxy Watch8 comme sa Galaxy Watch la plus fine et la plus confortable à ce jour, avec un coach running et un coach sommeil qui conseille l’heure du coucher après trois nuits, selon la fiche Amazon. Cette version 40 mm Argent est livrée avec un chargeur rapide 25 W. Nous ne l’avons pas testée.
✅ Points forts
- Un coach sommeil : des conseils sur l’heure idéale du coucher après seulement trois nuits, selon Samsung.
- Un suivi sportif complet : programmes personnalisés et coach running, d’après la fiche.
- À savoir : le coach sommeil demande trois nuits de port avant ses premiers conseils.
AirPods 4 : la réduction de bruit sur des écouteurs ouverts, à 129 €
Cette version des AirPods 4 ajoute la réduction active du bruit et l’Audio adaptatif au format ouvert, sans embouts, des AirPods classiques, avec la puce H2 et un boîtier USB-C compatible avec la recharge sans fil, selon la fiche Amazon. Nous ne les avons pas testés.
✅ Points forts
- Un format ouvert : un contour affiné et une tige plus courte, sans embouts en silicone.
- La puce H2 : pour l’Audio adaptatif, le mode Transparence et l’isolement de la voix en appel.
- À savoir : un design ouvert isole forcément moins que des AirPods Pro.
Magic Keyboard Touch ID : le clavier complet d’Apple à -31 %, à 137,65 €
Cette version du Magic Keyboard ajoute au modèle de base le capteur Touch ID, pour déverrouiller le Mac d’une pression du doigt, et un pavé numérique. Elle est réservée aux Mac équipés d’une puce Apple, en disposition française et touches blanches. Nous ne l’avons pas testée.
✅ Points forts
- Touch ID intégré : le déverrouillage du Mac d’une pression du doigt.
- Un pavé numérique : utile pour saisir des chiffres dans un tableur.
- À savoir : il est conçu pour les Mac équipés d’une puce Apple : vérifiez votre modèle avant de commander.
Samsung 65QN70H : le Mini LED 65 pouces sous les 650 €, à 649 €
Ce téléviseur 2026 de 65 pouces associe un rétroéclairage Mini LED à des Quantum Dots, avec le processeur NQ4 AI et l’assistant Vision AI Companion, selon la fiche Amazon. Nous ne l’avons pas testé. Le QN90F, un Mini LED plus haut de gamme sorti en 2025, avait obtenu 8/10 dans notre test du Samsung QN90F.
✅ Points forts
- Le Mini LED en 65 pouces : associé à des Quantum Dots, selon Samsung.
- 341 € de remise : sur le prix conseillé de 990 €.
- À savoir : il se place sous la gamme QN90 que nous avons testée.
Samsung 65M70H : un Mini LED 65 pouces 144 Hz sous les 500 €, à 499,98 €
Ce téléviseur 2026 de 65 pouces passe au rétroéclairage Mini LED et monte à 144 Hz, avec VRR et Auto Game Mode pour les consoles, selon la fiche Amazon. Son design métal sans bordure sur trois côtés intègre l’assistant Vision AI Companion. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts

- À savoir : ses 144 Hz ne servent qu’avec une console ou un PC compatibles.

✅ Points forts

- Un format polyvalent : 48 pouces, assez compact pour un bureau ou une petite pièce.

✅ Points forts
- Un zoom optique : de 0,98 à 1,3:1, sans perte de qualité, selon XGIMI.
- Google TV intégré : et le son Harman Kardon, sans barre de son externe.
- À savoir : 1 600 lumens ISO demandent une pièce sombre pour profiter de la 4K.
Blink Outdoor 4 : la caméra extérieure sans fil à moins de 25 €, à 24,99 €
Cette caméra sans fil filme en 1080p, voit la nuit en infrarouge et permet de parler aux visiteurs grâce à l’audio bidirectionnel, selon la fiche Amazon. Les deux piles AA au lithium fournies lui donnent jusqu’à deux ans d’autonomie. Nous ne l’avons pas testée.
✅ Points forts
- Deux ans d’autonomie : annoncés avec les piles fournies.
- La plus forte remise de la sélection : 67 % sous le prix conseillé.
- À savoir : Amazon la vend comme caméra supplémentaire, et l’enregistrement des clips dans le cloud demande un abonnement Blink.
Fire TV Stick HD : la clé de streaming d’Amazon à moins de 24 €, à 23,99 €
Amazon présente ce Fire TV Stick HD comme son lecteur HD en streaming le plus rapide, avec la nouvelle interface Fire TV, une télécommande vocale Alexa et une alimentation directe par le téléviseur. Il donne accès à Prime Video, Netflix, YouTube, Disney+, Canal+ ou TF1+. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Toutes les applications : Prime Video, Netflix, Disney+, Canal+, TF1+, M6+ et les autres.
- Facile à installer : alimenté directement par le téléviseur, selon Amazon.
- À savoir : il se limite à la HD : pour une TV 4K, mieux vaut le Fire TV Stick 4K Max.
Fire TV Stick 4K Max : la clé 4K Wi-Fi 6E à moins de 53 €, à 52,99 €
Le stick de streaming le plus puissant d’Amazon prend en charge le Wi-Fi 6E, la 4K Ultra HD avec Dolby Vision, HDR10+ et le son Dolby Atmos, selon la fiche Amazon. Il reçoit la nouvelle interface Fire TV de 2026 et la fonction Écran dynamique. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- 4K, Dolby Vision et Dolby Atmos : l’image et le son les plus complets de la gamme Fire TV.
- Wi-Fi 6E : pour un flux plus stable sur une box récente.
- À savoir : le Wi-Fi 6E ne sert qu’avec une box ou un routeur compatible.
Ring sonnette vidéo 2K : la sonnette 2K sans fil à moitié prix, à 49,99 €
Cette sonnette vidéo sans fil filme en 2K, zoome jusqu’à 6x et permet de voir, entendre et parler aux visiteurs en temps réel, selon la fiche Amazon. Elle fonctionne sur batterie intégrée et s’installe soi-même. Nous ne l’avons pas testée.
✅ Points forts
- Une vidéo 2K : avec un zoom jusqu’à 6x pour inspecter les détails.
- Sans fil : batterie intégrée, installation sans électricien.
- À savoir : l’abonnement Ring, nécessaire pour retrouver les vidéos enregistrées, n’est offert que 30 jours.
Kindle Paperwhite : 70 € de remise sur une des meilleures ventes d’Amazon, à 154,99 €
Cette Paperwhite de 2024 passe à un écran antireflet de 7 pouces, résiste à l’eau et tient jusqu’à 12 semaines sur une charge, selon Amazon. Nous ne l’avons pas testée : la génération précédente avait obtenu 7/10 dans notre test de la Kindle Paperwhite 2021.
✅ Points forts
- Un écran de 7 pouces : antireflet, réglable du blanc à l’ambre.
- Jusqu’à 12 semaines d’autonomie : annoncées par Amazon.
- À savoir : elle reste liée à la boutique Kindle.
Bose SoundLink Flex : la petite enceinte baroudeuse à moitié prix, à 89,99 €
Cette enceinte ultra-portable annonce 12 heures d’autonomie, une résistance à l’eau et à la poussière et une lanière pour l’accrocher à un sac, selon la fiche Amazon. Nous n’avons pas testé cette deuxième génération : la première avait fait l’objet de notre test de la Bose SoundLink Flex.
✅ Points forts
- Ultra-portable : elle tient dans la main ou s’accroche à un sac.
- 12 heures d’autonomie : annoncées par Bose.
- À savoir : son format compact limite la puissance face à une JBL Xtreme 4.
Black Friday 2026 : jusqu’à quand durent les offres d’Amazon ?
Le Black Friday tombe le vendredi 27 novembre, et le Cyber Monday le lundi 30 novembre. Amazon a ouvert sa Black Friday Week bien avant : les prix de cette sélection ont été relevés le lundi 23 novembre et peuvent changer d’une heure à l’autre, au gré des stocks. Toutes nos sélections du moment sont réunies sur notre page Black Friday.
Comment savoir si une promo high-tech est vraiment intéressante ?
Regardez d’abord ce que désigne le prix barré : Amazon affiche tantôt le prix conseillé par la marque, tantôt son prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours, ce qui est plus exigeant. Vérifiez ensuite que le produit est vendu et expédié par Amazon et non par un vendeur tiers, souvent plus cher sur les consoles et les smartphones très demandés. Enfin, comparez la configuration exacte, stockage, mémoire ou accessoires fournis, avant de comparer les prix d’une offre à l’autre.

articles.title: GTA 6 curiosidades: Arthur Morgan de RDR2 hace una aparición especial con su icónico vestuario
articles.text:
Arthur Morgan no es un personaje dentro de GTA 6, pero Rockstar Games incluyó referencias directas al protagonista de Red Dead Redemption 2 en el mundo abierto de Leonida. La más visible permite conseguir su sombrero de vaquero, una prenda reconocible para los jugadores que siguieron la historia del integrante de la banda de Van der Linde.
El guiño importa porque GTA 6 ocurre en una época contemporánea, más de un siglo después de los sucesos de Red Dead Redemption 2, ambientados en 1899. Por eso, la presencia de Arthur no puede formar parte de la trama principal, aunque sus objetos y referencias permiten conectar ambas franquicias mediante detalles repartidos por el mapa.
El sombrero de Arthur Morgan puede comprarse en Port Gellhorn
El homenaje más directo está en una venta de garaje ubicada al sur de Port Gellhorn. Allí, Jason y Lucía pueden adquirir por 35 dólares un sombrero de cuero desgastado idéntico al que utiliza Arthur Morgan durante buena parte de Red Dead Redemption 2.
La prenda puede equiparse en ambos protagonistas. No cambia las habilidades, los atributos ni el desarrollo de la historia, pero añade una opción estética para quienes quieren recorrer Vice City, los cayos o los pantanos con un elemento procedente del western de Rockstar.
El detalle adquiere sentido por el valor simbólico del sombrero. En Red Dead Redemption 2, Arthur lo lleva durante momentos centrales de su recorrido como forajido y se convirtió en uno de los objetos más asociados con su imagen dentro de la comunidad.
Un chihuahua lleva un muñeco de Arthur en un campo de minigolf
La segunda referencia aparece en Frontier Adventure Golf, un parque temático de estética del Oeste situado en el condado de Leonard. En una de sus zonas, los jugadores pueden encontrar un perro chihuahua con un muñeco de vaquero sobre el lomo.
El diseño del muñeco reproduce el aspecto de Arthur Morgan. Es una referencia menor, pero confirma que Rockstar distribuyó homenajes en lugares alejados de las misiones principales. El parque mezcla decorados de frontera, actividades recreativas y elementos humorísticos, un contexto habitual para los secretos de la saga.
Este tipo de hallazgos invita a recorrer el mapa sin seguir únicamente los objetivos de la campaña. GTA 6 incluye ciudades, carreteras, marinas, zonas industriales, pantanos y espacios turísticos donde pueden aparecer objetos, personajes o referencias ocultas.
Leonida también incluye pistas sobre el universo Red Dead
Los guiños no terminan con el sombrero y el muñeco. En Leonida se encontraron matrículas de vehículos vinculadas con New Austin, uno de los territorios reconocibles de Red Dead Redemption 2.
También hay un libro en Brian’s Marina que relata sucesos y menciona a personajes del juego anterior, entre ellos el pistolero Flaco Hernández. Estos elementos no confirman que ambos mundos compartan una continuidad directa, pero funcionan como homenajes reconocibles para quienes conocen la franquicia western.
Rockstar suele incluir referencias cruzadas entre sus producciones. Los carteles, objetos, programas de radio y nombres de negocios permiten que los jugadores encuentren conexiones sin alterar el argumento central de cada entrega.
En este caso, las alusiones a Red Dead Redemption 2 refuerzan la sensación de que Leonida está construida para ser examinada con atención. El sombrero de Arthur se convierte así en una recompensa para quienes exploran áreas secundarias y revisan los objetos disponibles.
Arthur Morgan sigue siendo uno de los personajes más recordados de Rockstar
Arthur Morgan se ganó un lugar entre los protagonistas más valorados de los videojuegos por su arco de redención. Al inicio de Red Dead Redemption 2, aparece como un ejecutor duro, leal a Dutch van der Linde y acostumbrado a resolver conflictos mediante la violencia.
Su diagnóstico de tuberculosis modifica esa perspectiva. Arthur no elimina su pasado ni se convierte en un personaje sin contradicciones, pero utiliza el tiempo que le queda para proteger a John Marston, Abigail y Jack, además de ayudar a otras personas durante actividades secundarias.
El contraste entre su apariencia de forajido y su mundo interior también explica parte de su impacto. Su diario incluye escritos y dibujos de animales y paisajes, mientras sus interacciones revelan inseguridad, arrepentimiento y humor seco.
La interpretación de Roger Clark, reconocida en The Game Awards 2018, dio peso a esos rasgos mediante voz, captura de movimiento, silencios y cambios de tono. El sistema de Honor permitió además que cada jugador definiera cómo afrontaba la etapa final del personaje.
Aun así, el sombrero, el muñeco y las referencias a New Austin permiten que Arthur Morgan siga presente. Los guiños no cambian la historia de GTA 6, pero reconocen a un personaje que marcó una etapa narrativa para Rockstar Games.

articles.title: AMD's top-performing Ryzen 9800X3D is down to its lowest price ever at $399 — get the fastest gaming CPU and save $80 off list price
articles.text:
AMD's top-performing Ryzen 9850X3D is now the same price as the 9800X3D, an all-time low — get the fastest gaming CPU and save $100 off list price
The fastest gaming CPU at the lowest price.
The Ryzen 7 9850X3D needs no introduction. It's the best CPU for gaming, without question, leveraging AMD's latest Zen 5 architecture alongside its 3D V-Cache to accelerate frame rates as much as 30% above the competition. It's down to its lowest price ever in the run-up to Black Friday, dropping to $399 after an instant coupon on Amazon.
Although we see frequent discounts on the Ryzen 7 9800X3D, the newer Ryzen 7 9850X3D has rarely gone on sale. At $399, this is one of the best CPU deals we've seen this Black Friday. In fact, the Ryzen 7 9850X3D and Ryzen 7 9800X3D are the same price right now.
If you're after the ultimate in gaming performance, there's no better option than the Ryzen 7 9850X3D. Thanks to its 93MB of L3 cache, this 8-core/16-thread processor can push out class-leading frame rates in every game out there. With only a 120W TDP, it even stays cooler than the competition, saving you a few extra bucks on that expensive AIO purchase.
As you can see from our CPU benchmark hierarchy, the Ryzen 7 9850X3D is the fastest gaming processor money can buy. The Ryzen 7 9850X3D is identical to the Ryzen 7 9800X3D outside of a slight boost in clock speed. We found that the base Ryzen 7 9800X3D can reach the same performance level with AMD's Precision Boost Overdrive (PBO), and it usually remains the cheaper of the two CPUs. Right now, however, the two chips are the same price.
The Ryzen 7 9850X3D remains the gold standard for gaming performance. The closest chip without 3D V-Cache is Intel's Core i9-14900K, which itself only provided 78.2% of the 1080p gaming performance of the 9800X3D. That's despite the fact that the chip often runs below 100W in games, and it has access to only eight cores and 16 threads.
Those eight cores can pose some limitations in heavily threaded apps, particularly compared to the Intel competition. If you're less focused on gaming, a CPU like the Core Ultra 7 270K Plus remains our recommendation. If you just dabble in non-gaming applications, however, the Ryzen 7 9850X3D is a great option.
Intel may have superior core counts, but the Ryzen 7 9850X3D comes with eight full, fat Zen 5 cores, and it can clock up to 5.6 GHz, giving you plenty of grunt for content creation applications alongside games. It slots into existing AM5 motherboards with a 600- or 800-series chipset, though you may need a BIOS update.
This chip comes with AMD's second-gen 3D V-Cache, which places the extra SRAM under the compute die. This gives the cores direct access to the Integrated Heat Spreader (IHS), meaning the chip can boost as well as its non-X3D counterpart without the SRAM acting as an insulating layer.

articles.title: "Nunca voté, pero veo que es necesario": las colas en los consulados españoles dejan el primer termómetro del 29N
articles.text:
Queda aún la recta final, pero el 29N puede presumir ya de ser una campaña excepcional. Y por varias razones. No todas las elecciones se convocan arrastradas por una crisis social, lidian con una huelga general y la dimisión de un ministro y permiten ver a tres de los principales candidatos a la Moncloa sentados en el estudio de un youtuber. Más allá de esas peculiaridades, el 29N es especial por otro motivo: la relevancia de los electores residentes en el extranjero, marcados por las disputas en torno a la 'ley de nietos' y los bulos que cuestionan la fiabilidad del voto por correo.
Con ese telón de fondo, este fin de semana los consulados de España en el extranjero se han encontrado con una ‘fotografía’ poco habitual: largas colas de cientos de españoles que aguardaban horas para emitir sus votos.
Y llegó el 21N. Aunque parece que la maquinaria del 29N lleva semanas a pleno rendimiento, la realidad es que su calendario avanza poco a poco y aún no ha alcanzado todos sus hitos.
Por ejemplo, los españoles que viven en el extranjero no han podido depositar su voto de forma presencial en las embajadas hasta hace un par de días. Desde el 3 de noviembre tenían la opción de hacerlo por correo, pero quienes querían entregar su papeleta en mano han tenido que esperar algo más: al período comprendido entre el sábado 21 y el jueves 26.
¿Por qué es noticia? Porque el mismo sábado algunos consulados españoles en el extranjero se encontraron con colas formadas por decenas (en algunos casos cientos) de votantes deseosos de emitir su papeleta para el 29N.
Lo contaba este fin de semana Edgar Sapiña en EFE: frente a las oficinas consulares de París se formaron largas colas con centenares de españoles residentes en Francia. Y no es un caso único. Llega con echar un vistazo a Google o X para comprobar que se han vivido escenas similares en otras sedes diplomáticas de España, como las situadas en Londres o Washington. En Panamá fue la propia embajada la que compartía en X una foto en la que mostraba cómo “numerosos ciudadanos” habían acudido a su oficina para entregar su papeleta.
La cifra: 2,7 millones. Esas imágenes se entienden mejor al conocer un dato. El registro CERA (Censo Electoral de Residentes Ausentes) para el 29N asciende a 2,78 millones de personas, si bien EFE precisa que esa cifra incluye todos los nacionalizados al amparo de la 'ley de nietos'. Por países, la mayor parte del censo exterior se concentra en Argentina (524.000), Francia (268.000), EEUU (213.700), México (192.300), Reino Unido (156.000) y Venezuela (131.000).
Fuerte: Más de 100 personas en la cola para votar en la Embajada de España en Washington. https://t.co/oPzewv0aP9
— Rafael Yuste Muñoz (@rayusmu) November 21, 2026
Cua impressionant x votar al consolat espanyol a Londres. Més de 6oo metres, i la gent segueix arribant. @diariARA @socialistes_cat @Esquerra_ERC @AdaColau https://t.co/uCv5XpmL41
— Quim Aranda (@ArandaQuim) November 21, 2026
“Es necesario”. El sábado algunos de esos votantes llegaron a esperar hasta tres horas para ejercer su derecho en el consulado de París. Juan Allende, un jubilado asturiano que emigró a Francia en 1966, reconocía que este año ha hecho una excepción: “Nunca voté, no me gusta la política, pero veo que es necesario”. Él insiste en que España ahora “está muy arriba” y quiere contribuir para que se mantenga ahí.
Otros inscritos en el CERA, como Arancha, vallisoletana residente en Reino Unido, reconocía el sábado que quería votar en persona porque no se “fía” del Gobierno y tampoco ve descabellado que pueda “manipularse” el voto por correo.
La otra cifra: 9%. En un interesante análisis sobre la evolución del voto CERA, José Á. Carpio, de DatosRTVE, recordaba hace unos días dos datos relevantes del electorado residente en el extranjero. El primero tiene que ver con su número. Los 2,8 millones registrados por el INE representan el 7,2% del censo total de electores, un peso considerable que ha ido subiendo de forma sostenida a lo largo de las últimas décadas. En 1996 el censo CERA suponía apenas el 1,6% del registro total y en 2016 representaba el 5,3%.
Que ese porcentaje crezca no implica necesariamente que el voto CERA sea cada vez más relevante. Para que sea así debe cumplirse otro requisito: una subida en los niveles de participación (una cosa es tener un derecho, otra ejercerlo). Y la realidad es que los porcentajes de 2023 muestran que su capacidad para influir en el Congreso es muy limitada.
Hasta 2008 los niveles de participación del censo CERA se movieron entre el 20 y 36%, pero cayeron a partir de 2011, cuando se aplicó el sistema de voto rogado. En poco tiempo esa horquilla se redujo hasta quedarse en un 5-7%. En 2022 la supresión del requisito hizo que la participación volviese a subir, pero aun así durante los comicios de 2023 se mantuvo un parco 9%. ¿Cuál ha sido el resultado? Que en la práctica el voto CERA solo ha alterado tres escaños desde 1986.
Consulado de España en París 🤯 https://t.co/rgVW6Ig5Qw
— Daniel P (@danpast_) November 21, 2026
Hoy, la cola para votar en el Consulado Español en Zurich. 2 horas de espera en el frio de noviembre suizo. Esperemos que haya servido la pena! #EleccionesGenerales29N https://t.co/8WoOQ5mvmt
— Mercedes 🇪🇦🇨🇭 (@spaniard_071) November 21, 2026
La lupa del 29N. Tal vez el impacto cuantitativo del voto CERA sea cuestionable, pero desde luego estas elecciones han tenido una repercusión importante a nivel cualitativo.
¿La razón? En septiembre el Tribunal Supremo suspendió los efectos electorales de la ‘ley de nietos’, lo que afectó directamente a miles de altas en el CERA. De aquello hace ya bastante, pero el alcance de esa decisión cautelar ha seguido desde entonces en el foco del debate público. De hecho el viernes, apenas nueve días antes del 29N, el Supremo exigió a la Junta Electoral que garantice que más de 160.000 españoles que han obtenido la nacionalidad a través de la Ley de Memoria Democrática se mantengan fuera del censo electoral.
El fantasma del pucherazo. Quizás parezca una cuestión técnica, pero el debate legal ha estado bien salpimentado de política desde antes incluso de la convocatoria del 29N. En junio el líder del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, incluso llegó a calificar la 'ley de nietos' de “ingeniería electoral”. Santiago Abascal fue más allá y durante un mitin acusó a Sánchez de querer “secuestrar las elecciones generales”.
No es el único debate que probablemente ha movilizado a los votantes CERA. Desde hace semanas parte de la oposición ha agitado las dudas en torno a la fiabilidad del voto por correo y el fantasma de un pucherazo. De hecho hace poco se podían leer publicaciones que aseguraban que 16 embajadas han reducido los controles para el voto exterior, una afirmación falsa según TVE, que recuerda que la Ley Electoral exige remitir los votos por valija diplomática y el correo postal solo se usa en el envío de papeletas al consulado.

The best wireless speakers, all tested by our experts — from JBL, Sonos, Bose, and more
The best wireless speakers you can buy for your home
Drawing on decades of combined audio expertise and hands-on testing across countless models, our team has tracked down the very best wireless speakers you can buy today. Whether you’re after a compact Bluetooth-and-Wi-Fi speaker for a single room or a flagship multi-room powerhouse, you’ll find the right fit in this guide.
Every model on our list pairs rich, room-filling sound with the freedom of a clutter-free setup. By connecting over your home Wi-Fi network, these speakers deliver high-quality streaming without messy cables. And most also include Bluetooth for effortless playback on the go. Many top picks even double as smart speakers, offering built-in voice control (Alexa, Google Assistant, or Siri), support for the best music streaming services, and companion apps for fine-tuning your EQ settings.
Before making the cut, every speaker is rigorously tested by our reviewers in real-world home environments. We judge each model on what matters most, such as audio fidelity, smart features, day-to-day ease of use, and overall value, before debating and agreeing on the final lineup as a team.
I've reviewed over 150 audio products since becoming a tech journalist, ranging from super-budget earbuds to high-end Hi-Res Audio music players. The JBL Authentics 200 is one incredibly impressive speaker. For starters, it looks gorgeous. It could have topped multiple categories in this guide, but for now, we’re naming it our best overall wireless speaker – the top choice for most people.
Expect excellent audio across the range, with full bass, rich mids and plenty of detailed treble. In our review we also commented: “Separation is impressive, and there’s a depth to its soundstage that delivers remarkable immersion for a single speaker.” The result is a lot of depth and a listening experience we described as “sublime”
All of the top features are here, including multi-room audio and connectivity to the intuitive JBL One app. There’s also Wi-Fi streaming from several services. You can integrate the app with a range of streaming platforms, as well as customize the EQ settings – but we found it most enjoyable to do that manually by turning the treble and bass knobs on the speaker itself. If you like using voice commands, there’s support for Google Assistant and Amazon Alexa to choose from.
The JBL Authentics 200 has a refreshingly different aesthetic. In our review we wrote that it delivers “a dose of vintage style in a market crowded by neutral designs”. This is down to the curved foam grille and the aluminium frame – a nod to the look of older amps. Then again, it’s not overtly retro. It doesn’t look like a regular speaker cosplaying as a cool one, is what we’re saying. All of the design choices here look subtle and the result is a stunning build and finish that also feels premium, too.
It’s not the cheapest speaker in this guide. It’s also lacking Atmos compatibility, which you can find for less. But it’s one of the most appealing right now for its combination of superb sound, a refreshing, retro look and excellent feature set. As we pointed out in our review, “there’s really nothing else like the Authentics 200.”

If your goal is to get the most sound for your money, the Sonos Era 100 SL is the budget wireless speaker we recommend. At $189 / £169 / AU$289, it brings detailed, room-filling audio to the table with fewer compromises than you might expect at this price.
