articles.title: NVIDIA reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.text:
NVIDIA reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
Just 11 days after his resignation from the company, Jensen Huang is back at Nvidia as president, CEO, and board director.
Nvidia has reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as its president, chief executive officer, and board director, with immediate effect, less than two weeks after his resignation from the company.
The unanimous decision follows discussions between Huang and the board, alongside inputs from senior US government officials, the company said.
“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution. I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment… I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work,” Huang said.
This marks a swift reversal of decisions at Nvidia, the world’s leading AI chipmaker. However, questions surrounding the circumstances of Huang's departure remain unresolved.
Huang’s resignation was announced on November 12. The board had subsequently cited "personal behaviour inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct and standards". The development came amid reports that Huang had been targeted in a foreign intelligence effort, following media coverage of his relationship with Alice Huang.
Nvidia had said it had no reason to believe that national security or company secrets had been compromised. However, it established an independent investigation into the matter.
Nvidia is also establishing a national security and export control oversight committee and recruiting a chief compliance officer, signalling that governance and regulatory scrutiny will remain its priorities.
Explaining the decision to reinstate Jensen Huang, board chair Harvey C. Jones said, “The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers.”
Jones will remain as board chair.
The board also thanked CFO Colette Kress, who served as the interim chief executive, for her service.
Founded in 1993, Nvidia initially built its business around graphics processing units (GPUs), chips designed to handle many calculations simultaneously. Their parallel-processing capabilities have made them particularly valuable in the AI race, both for training models and running them in response to user requests. The company has consequently become a central player in the expansion of AI data centres.
Nvidia's financial performance underscores the stakes involves. The company reported a revenue of $115.8 billion for the third quarter of fiscal 2027, up 103% year on year, with data-centre revenue reaching $107.6 billion.

articles.title: Cómo instalar XUPER TV en Android o Smart TV: la búsqueda que expone contraseñas y daña dispositivos
articles.text:
Buscar cómo instalar XUPER TV, antes conocida como Magis TV, en un celular Android o un Smart TV puede parecer un atajo para acceder gratis a series, películas y transmisiones deportivas.
El problema aparece cuando la instalación exige descargar archivos desde páginas ajenas a las tiendas oficiales, una práctica que puede exponer datos personales, contraseñas y archivos almacenados en el dispositivo.
ESET analizó el archivo de instalación de Magis TV como ejemplo de los riesgos asociados a este tipo de servicios. La aplicación solicita accesos que exceden las necesidades de una plataforma convencional de streaming y que, en manos maliciosas, pueden afectar al teléfono, al televisor conectado e incluso a la red doméstica.
Por qué es peligroso instalar XUPER TV
Muchas aplicaciones de este tipo no están disponibles en Google Play Store o App Store. Por eso, quienes intentan instalarlas deben buscar archivos de instalación en sitios alternativos, enlaces compartidos en redes sociales, grupos de mensajería o páginas que prometen versiones actualizadas del servicio.
Ese recorrido elimina una de las barreras de seguridad habituales. Las tiendas oficiales aplican controles sobre las aplicaciones que publican, aunque no son infalibles. Fuera de esos entornos, es más difícil conocer quién desarrolló el archivo, si fue modificado o si contiene componentes añadidos para recopilar información.
Qué pasa al descargar una APK desde una página desconocida
El principal riesgo es instalar una APK distinta de la que el usuario cree haber descargado. Un archivo puede incluir programas espía, troyanos u otras herramientas capaces de observar la actividad del dispositivo, obtener datos privados o incorporar publicidad fraudulenta.
Los expertos advierten que estas apps pueden convertirse en una puerta de entrada para malware. En un celular, puede alcanzar fotos, documentos, grabaciones y cuentas vinculadas. En un Smart TV, el impacto puede extenderse a otros aparatos conectados al mismo router, como computadoras, consolas, cámaras o teléfonos.
Por qué los permisos solicitados por una aplicación deben generar alerta
El análisis de Magis TV identificó solicitudes de acceso que no parecen necesarias para reproducir contenidos audiovisuales. Entre ellas, hay funciones que permiten conocer qué otras aplicaciones están activas, revisar archivos guardados, modificar contenidos del almacenamiento y mostrar avisos en pantalla.
Además, puede pedir capacidad para instalar otros paquetes en el dispositivo. Esa autorización abre la posibilidad de que aparezcan supuestas actualizaciones o complementos que, en realidad, instalen software adicional sin que el usuario comprenda su origen.
Cómo puede una app maliciosa comprometer contraseñas y archivos personales
El acceso a documentos, imágenes, videos y audios puede facilitar la extracción de información sensible. Entre esos archivos pueden figurar copias de documentos, conversaciones exportadas, comprobantes bancarios, notas de voz o fotos con datos que permitan suplantar la identidad de una persona.
Asimismo, la información recolectada puede utilizarse para crear campañas de engaño más creíbles. Por ejemplo, una notificación enviada desde la propia aplicación podría imitar un aviso del banco, del servicio de correo o de una plataforma de pagos. El objetivo es inducir al usuario a entregar credenciales, códigos de verificación o datos de tarjetas.
Qué riesgos hay para el Smart TV y la red WiFi de la casa
Un televisor inteligente no es un dispositivo aislado. Comparte conexión con el resto de los aparatos del hogar y, según su configuración, puede tener acceso a cuentas de streaming, perfiles de compra, asistentes de voz o servicios de almacenamiento en la nube.
Si una aplicación maliciosa logra alterar el funcionamiento del dispositivo puede afectar la privacidad de la red. Puede consumir recursos, desplegar anuncios, modificar configuraciones o intentar comunicarse con otros dispositivos conectados.
Para evitar riesgos hay que mantener actualizado el sistema operativo del televisor y evitar archivos de páginas desconocidas.

articles.title: Cronología del lío de Nvidia: las fechas clave desde el contrato con Megaspeed hasta la vuelta de Jensen Huang como CEO
articles.text:
Jensen Huang vuelve para liderar Nvidia. La junta ha votado por unanimidad este lunes para reincorporarlo como presidente, director ejecutivo y consejero, con efecto inmediato. En el comunicado, la compañía aclaraba que había recibido información de “altos cargos del gobierno de Estados Unidos” y que confían en que su regreso no supone ningún riesgo para la seguridad nacional.
Como estas últimas semanas han estado muy agitadas en las oficinas de Nvidia, hemos pensado que igual tener una cronología de toda esta montaña rusa de sucesos nos puede ayudar a comprender un poco el panorama. El tema viene de bastante antes, así que bajo estas líneas te lo resumimos.
La cronología
Octubre-Diciembre 2023: Nuevo cliente
- Cuatro días después de un cambio de titularidad, la empresa de centros de datos de Singapur Megaspeed se convertía en socio de Nvidia Cloud. Alice Huang (que por si acaso quedaba alguna duda, no tiene relación ni parentesco con Jensen Huang) la había dirigido durante ocho meses antes de esa venta.
- The Straits Times informaba de que ambos fueron vistos en un restaurante de Singapur ya en diciembre de 2023. The Wall Street Journal contaba que Kang Wei, un empresario al que Jensen conocía desde hacía años, los presentó. Y precisamente el medio también señalaba que Kang era el marido de Alice Huang.
- Precio de las acciones de Nvidia en ese momento: aproximadamente 41-49 dólares (ajustadas por división de acciones, aproximado).
2024-mediados de 2025: Washington empieza a hacer preguntas
- Funcionarios del Departamento de Comercio abrieron una investigación sobre Megaspeed en 2024. En septiembre de 2024, un oficial del departamento encontró supuestamente equipos de Nvidia aún en sus cajas en su centro de datos de Malasia, según comparte el NYT.
- Una declaración conjunta de Comercio y Justicia indica que Nvidia incluyó a Megaspeed en su lista de “no vender” en junio de 2025. Singapur había abierto su propia investigación en febrero de 2025.
9 de octubre de 2025: suenan las alarmas contra Megaspeed
- El NYT informó de que Comercio estaba examinando si Megaspeed estaba ayudando a empresas chinas a eludir las normas de exportación. Añadía que Megaspeed estaba a punto de comprar alrededor de 2.000 millones de dólares en tecnología de Nvidia y que uno de sus ejecutivos había socializado con Huang.
- Acciones: alrededor de 192 dólares, un máximo histórico en aquel momento.
Primavera de 2026: advertencias dentro del Gobierno
- Desde el Times señalaban que el secretario de Estado Marco Rubio escribió comunicado interno clasificado sobre la relación de Huang, con fecha del 30 de marzo. CNN informa que Trump recibió una sesión informativa en mayo, antes de un viaje a China al que se sumó Huang.
- Según explican los medios, a Huang no se le dio una sesión informativa defensiva.
6 de octubre de 2026: Nvidia toca techo
29 de octubre de 2026: la exclusiva del NYT
- El medio alega en un artículo que funcionarios estadounidenses veían a Huang como el objetivo de una operación de inteligencia china. Sospechaban que Alice Huang era un activo de inteligencia, y ella había estado bajo vigilancia.
- Huang dijo a Bloomberg que los tratos con Megaspeed eran “completamente normales y nada inusuales”. China calificaba el informe de infundado.
- Acciones: 213,66 dólares, luego 204,64 dólares al día siguiente.
6-7 de noviembre: más malas noticias
- El mismo NYT compartía un comunicado interno donde se explicaba que el Ministerio de Seguridad del Estado de China había reclutado a Alice Huang. El Financial Times añadía que Washington creía que la relación era romántica.
- Acciones: 186,64 dólares (cierre del 6 de noviembre).
8 de noviembre: la confesión
- Huang lanzó un comunicado disculpándose ante el personal de Nvidia y su familia por infidelidad, tal y como contaban desde el WSJ. No mencionó el nombre de la otra persona. La junta anunció una investigación, pero dijo que no tenía motivos para creer que la seguridad nacional o los secretos de la empresa se hubieran visto comprometidos.
- Acciones: 178,67 dólares (cierre del 9 de noviembre).
11-12 de noviembre: una segunda relación y la dimisión
- El mismo NYT señalaba, citando a empleados de Nvidia, otra relación de Jensen Huang con Kimberly Powell, vicepresidenta del departamento de Salud en Nvidia. En ese momento el WSJ dijo que la junta se estaba preparando para destituirlo.
- La junta aceptó su dimisión el 11 de noviembre y la anunció el 12, al día siguiente. La directora financiera Colette Kress se convirtió en directora ejecutiva interina y Harvey Jones fue nombrado presidente.
- Acciones: 173,73 dólares (11 de noviembre), 166,19 dólares (12 de noviembre).
13-16 de noviembre: repercusiones y rumores de un regreso
- Reuters compartía en otro artículo una relación de Huang con una segunda empleada. Por otro lado, el Financial Times informaba de que Huang estaba sopesando regresar, pero varios medios señalaban que la junta no lo estaba considerando.
- Acciones: 162,85 dólares (13 de nov), 156,14 dólares (16 de nov).
17 de noviembre: “Honrado”, pero la junta dice que no
- Huang dijo en X que había cometido “graves errores” y que se sentiría honrado de regresar si la junta lo consideraba oportuno. Ese día, Jones dijo en la conferencia sobre resultados que la junta no tenía intención de reincorporarlo.
- Acciones: 155,46 dólares.
19-20 de noviembre: la peor semana
- Reuters y el NYT informaron de una investigación de la SEC sobre la contabilidad de Nvidia. Las acciones cayeron casi un 14 % el 20 de noviembre, y alrededor de 2,7 billones de dólares en valor de mercado se habían esfumado desde el máximo de octubre. Trump dijo que quería que Huang tuviera una segunda oportunidad.
- Acciones: 145,98 dólares (19 de noviembre), 125,53 dólares (20 de noviembre).
23 de noviembre: Huang está de vuelta
- La junta votó por unanimidad reincorporarlo tras reuniones que la dejaron satisfecha con su “franqueza y capacidad de liderazgo”. Kress vuelve a dedicación plena a su puesto de directora financiera. Las acciones subieron más de un 30 % antes de la apertura, borrando las pérdidas de sus 11 días de ausencia.
- Acciones: alrededor de 166 dólares en las primeras operaciones (cierre del viernes: 125,53 dólares).
Lo que aún está sin resolver
- La cuestión del espía. El fiscal general de Estados Unidos, Todd Blanche, dijo que el Departamento de Justicia no había llegado a ninguna conclusión sobre si Alice Huang era una espía. El NYT informaba de que funcionarios estadounidenses confiaban en sus contactos con la inteligencia china, y el país niega cualquier implicación. Singapur dijo que no la investigó por espionaje.
- Las investigaciones. La investigación independiente de la junta “continuará hasta su conclusión”, según la publicación de la SEC. Este organismo, junto al Departamento de Justicia y el fiscal general de California también están investigando a Nvidia y a Megaspeed.
- El Congreso. Huang ha aceptado acudir a una entrevista en la Cámara de Representantes el 1 de dic. El Comité Bancario del Senado también le ha pedido que comparezca.

Un affichage soigné et la puissance de la puce M6

articles.title: Miren launches flexible application deployment platform built for the agentic era
articles.text:
Miren launches flexible application deployment platform built for the agentic era
Miren Inc., an agentic infrastructure company, launched its platform today to make it easier for developers to deploy applications anywhere they need, without requiring them to become a solutions expert or set up and configure the application.
Artificial intelligence coding agents have changed the playing field for developers by making it easier than ever to build applications, but getting that software into deployment has remained a challenge. Configuration of resources, storage and the actual end maintenance of infrastructure that keeps everything running can be a burden that requires constant attention.
“[Our platform] transforms a computer anywhere you want into a place for your application to live,” Chief Executive Evan Phoenix told SiliconANGLE in an interview.
Miren gives developers a way to turn virtually any computer, from a virtual machine or bare-metal server to a local system, into a platform for running applications. Developers write their code locally, or have an AI coding agent generate it, and then hand it over to Miren, which handles building, running and much of the configuration necessary to deploy it. Once deployed, the application is accessible through a URL, without the developer having to set up and manage the underlying infrastructure individually.
The idea is to take much of the heavy lifting off the developer so they can do what they do best: designing, coding and strategizing.
“I was always interested in this, like the application development is sort of like the final boss of someone’s great idea, right? They’re working on this great idea, and they’re like, ‘Oh, now I need to share it with somebody,'” Phoenix explained.
The deployment is easy. A developer logs into their virtual machine or bare-metal server and installs Miren server, which then acts like a technician on the other end, watching over maintenance and deployment. The developer can then code locally, sandbox and do all of their work on a laptop or local machine, and when they’re ready, deploy to production with a command.
Critically, all of a developer’s data and application resources exist and run on their chosen infrastructure, virtual machines and servers. Phoenix stressed that this provides customers the flexibility to run wherever they choose and however they like. One customer in particular wanted to run software inside a German sovereign cloud environment, something that could be difficult with traditional platform-as-a-service providers that restrict users to their infrastructure. Miren lets the customer choose an appropriate environment while keeping the same development and deployment workflow.
“We’ve really attempted to have people be able to control where it runs, but still have the ease and the flexibility of it just running on the internet at the same time,” Phoenix said.
Miren Cloud for coordination and discovery
Miren also provides a third service that complements the developer client and the server: Miren Cloud, which is optional for a standalone deployment. However, it becomes particularly useful when multiple developers need to work with the same infrastructure.
Miren Cloud provides the organizational layer, coordinating cluster discovery and authentication. A developer can log in, discover available clusters and present signed credentials to access them without manually managing addresses and certificates. It acts as a coordination layer for infrastructure, pointing to where applications are hosted and helping with domain name registration, credentials and other authentication and attestation needs.
“Miren is addressing one of the biggest challenges in modern application development: giving developers the flexibility to run applications anywhere without adding another layer of operational complexity,” said Paul Nashawaty, practice lead and principal analyst, application development at ECI Research. “As enterprises expand across hyperscalers, sovereign clouds and private infrastructure, managing distributed clusters becomes increasingly difficult.”
Nashawaty cited ECI internal research, noting that 61% of developers cite tool fragmentation as the biggest barrier, making more unified approaches to application delivery and operations a top need.
Bridging the gap between code and infrastructure
Alongside the platform, Miren is also introducing Workbench, an AI-powered infrastructure operator built into Miren Cloud that can help developers manage and troubleshoot their applications. Unlike coding agents that primarily work with application code, Workbench has access to deployed clusters and specialized knowledge of Miren’s infrastructure. Developers can ask it to investigate performance problems, examine logs and analyze traffic without having to manually navigate the underlying systems.
“Think of it as a teammate, a sysadmin teammate,” Phoenix said.
Phoenix added that many customers were already bridging the gap between development and deployment using their own AI coding agents, allowing agents to generate application code, deploy it and then check results. With Workbench, they can extend this into the operational environment where the application runs in production, where the agentic operator can investigate problems and help navigate issues specific to the end infrastructure and relate them back to the coding agent.
Miren is also introducing paid support packages, giving customers a direct line to the company’s team, which has primarily provided community support until now. Phoenix said the company is expanding Miren Cloud with services that improve the reliability of customer-operated infrastructure, including automatic database backups.
Phoenix also sees an opportunity to turn customer support into a continuously improving layer of automation. Rather than having engineers repeatedly diagnose the same problems for different customers, Miren wants to feed the knowledge gained from individual support interactions back into its AI operators.
In theory, that would allow the platform to recognize and resolve familiar problems before other customers encounter them, shortening the cycle between discovering an issue and making its solution available across the platform. This follows a broader industry trend in which companies have begun building self-diagnosing, learning AI agents that improve themselves.

Milk preparation is superb as well. You can prepare any kind of milk with a manual steam wand, but automatic steaming systems on coffee machines are usually optimized for full-fat dairy. That's not the case with the Sage Barista Touch Impress with Cold Extraction, which turns any kind of milk into silky foam.
It's a superb package for any coffee-lover, regardless of your level of experience, and is the machine I'd recommend to anyone.

The Philips Baristina is an excellent little coffee maker, particularly if you're making the switch from capsules to whole beans, and want to keep things as simple as possible. It's compact, smart-looking, and remarkably affordable at $449.99 / £299.99 / AU$599. In fact it's the cheapest bean-to-cup machine I've tested, and Philips hasn't skimped on quality to his that bargain price point.
The Baristina uses what Philips calls a "one-swipe" system. Push the portafilter handle into place, pick your drink (espresso or lungo, with the option to increase the dosage for a stronger brew) and the Baristina will do the rest. Just step back and watch while it measures and grinds a dose of coffee into the filter basket, tamps it down, then propels it over to the brew group and pulls your shot.
At the end, pull out the handle, clean out the basket, rinse the brew group by holding a button for a few seconds, and empty the drip tray. It's a million times easier than cleaning an automatic coffee maker where all the messy parts of coffee-making happen inside the case.
For me, the biggest downside of the Philips Baristina is the inability to adjust the grind size. On one hand, this is one less thing for new users to worry about, but on the other it means that there's nothing you can do to change the extraction rate. If it's too fast or slow, you'll need to try a different coffee until you find something that works with the Baristina as-is. There's no steam wand for preparing milk either, though you can buy the Baristina bundled with a separate Philips milk frother if you're into your lattes.
All in all though, this is a superb little entry-level coffee maker at a bargain price, and one that's easy to recommend.

What makes the Aromis so practical is its approach to milk drinks and cleaning. You get two separate milk carafes — one for hot foam, one for cold — and both disassemble into three pieces, making them far easier to clean than any system with fiddly tubes or hidden chambers. The maintenance hatch is also thoughtfully designed: it’s hinged, so you won’t misplace it, and the brew unit lifts out in one go for a proper rinse. There’s one quirk to be aware of: if you rush from a hot espresso straight to an iced milk drink, the brew group needs to cool down first, or you’ll end up with a warm ‘iced’ latte. But for most users, the Aromis’ premium build, straightforward maintenance, and sheer breadth of drinks genuinely justify its price. 9. De'Longhi Dedica Duo
Our expert review:
Specifications
Reasons to buy
Reasons to avoid
✅ You have a small kitchen: The Dedica Duo is one of the most compact espresso machines we've ever tested at TechRadar.
✅ You enjoy cappuccinos and lattes: Unusually for a machine this size, the Dedica Style has a manual steam wand.
❌ You want to use single-walled baskets: Swapping the pressurized baskets that come with the Dedica Duo is quite simple, but the machine doesn't come with single-walled baskets.
❌ You want an integrated grinder: You'll need to buy one separately, or settle for using pre-ground coffee.
The De'Longhi Dedica Duo is my pick for the best small coffee machine around right now, and it's one of the most affordable too, with a list price of just $299.95 / £279.99 (details for Australia are yet to be announced).
It's a successor to the excellent De'Longhi Dedica Style, and retains all the features that made that machine so successful, including a fast-heating boiler, consistent boiler pressure, and a solid build that you might not expect from a coffee machines at such an affordable price.
It measures a mere 12 x 5.9 x 13 inches / 30.4 x 14.9 x 33cm, meaning you can tuck it into even a tiny kitchen (I currently have it between my toaster and the wall), and the Duo has a more modern-looking design with cleaner lines and a wider drip tray to more easily accommodate two espresso cups at once. It also comes in a more contemporary range of colors, including pistachio, rose, and vanilla shades inspired by gelato (according to De'Longhi).
It performed consistently well during my tests, proving much more reliable than similarly-priced coffee makers from the likes of Casabrews. My only criticism is that it has a tendency to drip a little after the pump has stopped, but I certainly don't think that should be a deal-breaker.
Read our De'Longhi Dedica Duo review
We also tested
We test new coffee machines every month here at TechRadar. Here are some we've reviewed recently that didn't quite make our shortlist.
Ninja Luxe Café Mini
A clever all-in-one machine with a grinder, espresso maker, filter brewer, scale and milk frother in one relatively compact package. It produces tasty coffee, but the learning curve and inconsistent results mean the full-size Luxe Café remains the better choice in our books.
Read our full Ninja Luxe Café Mini review
KitchenAid KF3 Espresso Machine
A smart, compact espresso machine that delivers excellent coffee and good milk foam for the money, but doesn't offer a distinct enough advantage over our main picks.
Read our full KitchenAid KF3 Espresso Machine review
KitchenAid KF4 Automatic Coffee Maker
A compact automatic coffee maker that produces great espresso and milk drinks, but its limited customisation means it didn't quite make the cut as our fully automatic pick.
Read our full KitchenAid KF4 Automatic Coffee Maker review
De'Longhi Eletta Ultra
An extremely versatile bean-to-cup machine with a huge range of hot and cold drinks, but the coffee and milk foam aren't quite as impressive as you'd expect at this price.
Read our full De'Longhi Eletta Ultra review
Melitta AromaFresh Therm Pro
The Melitta AromaFresh Therm Pro brings a built-in grinder into the equation, making it a neat alternative to the Sage Luxe Brewer Thermal for anyone wanting an all-in-one filter setup. During testing, however, the grinder’s inconsistency was noticeable and ultimately limited the quality of the brew.
Read our full Melitta AromaFresh Therm Pro review
How to choose the best coffee maker for you
There are so many different options on the market that it can be hard to know which is the best coffee maker for you.
If you enjoy a simple americano and don’t like milk-based drinks, then a drip filter coffee maker will be a great option. Plus, these machines can make as many as 12 cups of coffee in one go.
If you just want small quantities of coffee, though, we’d recommend a single-serve coffee maker from Keurig or Nespresso.
If you like milk-based coffee, then there are quite a few options available. Some models are fully automated and have a built-in frother that will be able to create a variety of milk textures, while others have steam arms which you place into a jug of milk and froth the milk yourself. There’s a third option too - and this includes buying a separate milk frother which is a stand-alone machine. You’ll be able to use these to make everything from lattes to hot chocolates, and they make a great accompaniment to a pod coffee maker.
Coffee drinkers that like plenty of customization options will be best suited to a coffee maker that lets you adjust the strength of your brew and create different sizes of hot drinks. Many premium coffee makers will let you do both of these things, but you can also adjust the strength and the aroma of your coffee with a good drip filter model.
The final thing to consider is how involved you’d like to be in the coffee-making process – and the clean-up afterwards. Some designs are smart-enabled so you can simply switch them on from your phone, however, others will require you to pack down ground coffee and pull your own shot of espresso before frothing the milk yourself. Some of the best coffee machines have self-cleaning systems which purge the steam wand to prevent milk residue drying in the pipes, while others have systems to flush out any build-up in the machine.
If you’re still not sure, you can find a more detailed breakdown in our article covering which type of coffee maker to buy.
Frequently asked coffee maker questions
Can espresso machines make regular coffee?
Yes, technically speaking, as espresso forms the foundation of nearly every café drink, an espresso machine can easily double as a versatile all-rounder. If your machine has a dedicated hot water dispenser (a common feature on many top models), you can top up a shot to make an Americano. For milk-based favorites like lattes, cappuccinos, and flat whites, you’ll just need a model with a built-in steam wand—or you can pair a basic espresso maker with a standalone milk frother.
How do coffee makers work?
With so many different types of coffee makers on offer, it’s no surprise that each type of machine works slightly differently. Here we focus on espresso machines and pod coffee makers but for a more detailed explanation, head to our feature on how coffee makers work.
Espresso machines work by using a pump to push pressurized water through coffee grounds so that it infuses with the water to make a smooth shot of espresso. If an espresso machine has a milk frother, it will use a boiler to push steam out of the machine which is then used to give the milk a velvety texture. Pod coffee makers work by using a compacted capsule of coffee and piercing a hole in the capsule. Hot water is then powered up through the machine and pushed through the capsule to create a coffee. Some more advanced pod machines, such as the Nespresso Vertuo Next, spin the coffee pod around at high speeds so that the contents evenly infuse with water for an even smoother cup of coffee.
How to clean a coffee maker
Keeping your coffee maker clean will not only ensure it looks great, but it’s crucial for maintaining working order and keeping it hygienic. We’ve written a full feature on how to clean a coffee maker and all its parts but the good news is that you’ll be able to clean thoroughly using products you’ve most likely got at home already. To clean your machine’s water tank, you can make a solution with one part water and one part white vinegar and simply leave it to soak inside your water reservoir for a couple of hours. To give the pipes a good flush through, let the vinegar solution run through the machine by switching it on as you would do normally for water.
We're also got a dedicated article on how to clean a Nespresso machine and how to clean a Keurig, for those that have single-serve coffee makers at home.
What is the best coffee maker for home use?
Whether you’re working remotely or cutting back on daily coffee shop visits, the right home coffee maker delivers café-quality drinks for a fraction of the price.
For authentic espresso, a dedicated espresso machine lets you fine-tune flavor and strength by adjusting water volume, brew time, and puck tamping pressure. They take some practice and cleanup, but the results are worth it. Short on space? Try the Breville Bambino or Bambino Plus (branded as Sage in the UK). Have more room and budget? Consider the De’Longhi La Specialista Arte EC9155MB or the Breville/Sage Oracle Touch.
If you prefer convenience over tinkering, a single-serve pod machine offers great espresso with minimal mess. We like the Nespresso Vertuo Next; check out which Nespresso machine is best for more models, or read Nespresso vs Keurig if you're in the US and weighing both brands.
Which type of coffee maker should I choose?
For those that want to perfect their coffee-making skills, consider an espresso machine. This is the best coffee maker for people who prefer to handle every part of the brewing process, from compacting the coffee grounds into a puck or small disc (a process known as tamping) to the brew volume and duration to create the perfect cup of coffee to suit you. If you’re new to this type of coffee maker, discover how to use an espresso machine in-depth in our article.
Alternatively, for the same coffee-shop standard hot drinks but with a hands-off approach, opt for a bean-to-cup coffee machines, which automate the processes described above to rustle up a cup of joe at the touch of a button.
If you’re looking to make a cup of coffee with as minimal amount of fuss as possible, a single-serve coffee maker is the best fit. Also known as pod coffee machines, they use capsules filled with ground coffee to create a hot drink with far less mess than espresso machines.
Nespresso and Keurig are the biggest brands when it comes to single-serve coffee machines and offer a range of machines each. However, pod coffee machines have a poor reputation when it comes to sustainability as many of the capsules end up in landfill. Follow our guide on how to recycle Nespresso pods to help ensure this doesn’t happen.
Finally, the drip coffee maker is a familiar style to most of us and it's the best coffee machine for those that want to brew large quantities of Java at any one time. Discover in-depth how coffee makers work in our article then, find out how to make your favorite coffee at home
How we test the best coffee makers
We take testing the best coffee makers seriously and put all the machines through their paces to see if they really can do everything they promise to. We test each coffee maker for the crema it produces on an espresso, how easy it is to use and set up, and also for consistency from one cup to another.
When we’re testing, we take into account the overall design of each coffee maker - how it looks, how much space it’ll take up on your kitchen counter, whether the water tank is removable for easy refills, and how the machine looks as a whole.
For coffee makers with milk frothers, we test the milk texture to see if it’s silky and smooth and of course, we wouldn’t be doing our jobs if we didn’t drink plenty of coffee along the way to see how each cup measures up for the overall taste.
We test models to see how much control you have over each cup of coffee, and whether it’s a case of simply pressing a button or whether more of a hands-on approach is needed. All the best coffee machines will require regular cleaning so we’re always sure to note what maintenance is involved and how easy these machines are to keep in top condition.

articles.title: Après Android, les messages WhatsApp à lecture unique arrivent aussi sur iPhone
articles.text:
Déjà testée en version Android, la lecture unique des messages fait aussi son apparition sur iPhone.
WhatsApp a travaillé sur de nombreuses évolutions ces dernières semaines. La messagerie de Meta vous permettra bientôt de sauvegarder vos discussions directement sur ses serveurs. Une nouvelle protection pour les numéros de téléphone est également en préparation. Mais ce n’est pas tout : la lecture unique, déjà en test sur Android, devrait bientôt arriver sur iPhone.
La lecture unique est en cours de test sur iOS
L’équipe de WABetaInfo a découvert une nouveauté intéressante dans la version bêta 26.45.10.73 de WhatsApp : la lecture unique, déjà disponible pour les bêta-testeurs Android dans la version 2.26.45.6, a été développée pour le système iOS.
Pour l’activer, c’est tout simple : il suffit de rédiger son message comme d’habitude, puis de garder le doigt appuyé sur le bouton d’envoi. Un menu apparaît et propose la programmation de l’envoi mais aussi la lecture unique. Cette dernière envoie immédiatement le contenu au destinataire.
Une fois le message reçu, votre contact n’a qu’à toucher la bulle pour l’ouvrir. Le texte s’affiche alors dans une fenêtre dédiée qui rappelle les protections appliquées. Une fois refermé, le message disparaît à tout jamais. Le texte ne peut pas être relu, ni par l’expéditeur ni par le destinataire.
Une fonction bien pensée, mais pas infaillible
Les messages à lecture unique sont destinés, avant tout, aux contenus qui sont confidentiels. Pour plus de sécurité, l'équipe en charge du développement de WhatsApp a également prévu quelques garde-fous supplémentaires : pendant la lecture du texte, les contacts ne peuvent pas faire de captures ou d’enregistrements d’écran. Il est également impossible de copier, transférer ou d’enregistrer le contenu du message.
- Chiffrement de bout en bout.
- Appels audio et vidéo gratuits.
- Compatibilité multiplateforme.
Les petits malins l’auront compris : rien n’empêche votre interlocuteur de photographier l'écran avec un autre appareil. L’option est donc loin d’être totalement infaillible. Malgré tout, elle sera bien utile pour tous ceux qui souhaitent partager des codes d’accès, des adresses ou toute autre information sensible.
Pour le moment, seuls quelques testeurs iOS peuvent accéder à cette nouvelle fonctionnalité. Meta devrait toutefois ouvrir le test à d’autres comptes dans les prochaines semaines. Pour l’instant, la firme n’a partagé aucune date de déploiement global. Il faudra donc patienter un peu pour accéder à une version publique.

articles.title: Independent Web Browser/Engine "Ladybird" Goes Into Alpha Release
articles.text:
Monday, November 23rd 2026
Independent Web Browser/Engine "Ladybird" Goes Into Alpha Release
One of the few independent web browser/engine projects, called Ladybird, has entered its alpha release, moving towards the final release. After four years of independent development, Ladybird is finally in alpha, allowing users and testers to try it out and provide feedback before the final version arrives. Originally, Ladybird was spun out of SerenityOS development with its browser engine and HTML viewer, later becoming one of the rare independent projects. As most modern browsers focus on monetizing their user base by collecting data or offering cryptocurrency tokens, Ladybird aims to challenge that and stand out as one of the few designs not based on Chromium, Gecko, or WebKit.
Modern browsers like Chrome run on Chromium, Firefox uses Gecko, and other alternatives like Brave and Edge also use Chromium, leaving little room for independence. Monopolies are inherently problematic, and Ladybird seeks to offer users a choice with a lightweight, modern browser focused solely on browsing the web. Furthermore, one of the most important aspects of human-machine interactions is the web browser, which should remain under user control and not become a tool for data collection. Supporting open alternatives is always a good idea, ensuring your freedom to browse without becoming a product or a target for ads is more important now than ever. Currently, Ladybird builds only for macOS and Linux, but we can expect future Windows builds to be available natively, although WSL is supported.
This is an alpha, so some websites won't work, and it will crash sometimes. When that happens, tell us! You can report a broken site from inside the browser. After a crash, you can read the crash report and decide whether to send it.

articles.title: Códigos de Free Fire para reclamar diamantes y skins gratis este 23 de noviembre de 2026
articles.text:
Garena habilitó una nueva serie de códigos de Free Fire para reclamar recompensas sin costo este lunes 23 de noviembre de 2026. Las combinaciones permiten intentar obtener diamantes, skins, atuendos, accesorios y cajas con contenido para usar dentro del videojuego.
Cada clave tiene condiciones propias de disponibilidad. El sistema puede limitar su uso por región, cantidad de canjes o plazo de activación. Por ese motivo, los jugadores deben ingresarlas cuanto antes y comprobar que su perfil esté vinculado con uno de los métodos de acceso aceptados por la plataforma.
Cuáles son los códigos de Free Fire disponibles para canjear hoy
La siguiente lista reúne las combinaciones para intentar canjear recompensas en Free Fire. Deben copiarse sin modificar mayúsculas, números ni orden de los caracteres. Tampoco deben incluir espacios antes o después del código:
- H8YCAJDUDKQ9.
- JDI3SX5NMJ64V.
- FFSGT7KSBHD82.
- B1FCCUIDN68YT.
- BR43FMAPYEZZ.
- FFSGT7KNFQ2X.
- 4ST1ZTBZBRP9.
- UPQ7X5NMJ64V.
- H8YC4TN6VKQ9.
- S9QK2L6VP3MR.
- FPSTQ7MXNPY5.
- B1RK7C5ZL8YT.
- 4N8M2XL9R1G3.
- FF6YH3BFD7VT.
Los premios pueden variar según cada clave y la disponibilidad que figure. Algunas combinaciones entregan artículos coleccionables o accesorios, mientras que otras pueden habilitar diamantes, trajes o skins de armas. La confirmación definitiva aparece una vez que el portal procesa la solicitud.
Cómo redimir los códigos en el portal oficial de Garena
El canje se realiza desde el portal oficial de recompensas de Garena. Allí, el usuario debe iniciar sesión con la misma cuenta que utiliza en el juego y luego buscar el campo destinado a introducir el código promocional.
La plataforma admite perfiles asociados con Google, Facebook, Apple o VK. Después de seleccionar el acceso correcto, corresponde pegar la clave y revisar cada carácter antes de confirmar. Una letra equivocada, un número omitido o un espacio adicional pueden hacer que el portal rechace el pedido.
Por qué sale el mensaje de código inválido o expirado?¿
El aviso de código inválido o expirado suele indicar que la combinación alcanzó el máximo de usos establecido, que su plazo de vigencia terminó o que no está disponible para el servidor desde el cual se intenta reclamar el premio. Las restricciones pueden cambiar según la región de la cuenta.
Asimismo, es posible que el problema responda a un error al copiar la secuencia. Los códigos combinan letras y números, así que resulta preferible pegarlos directamente en lugar de escribirlos de forma manual. Conviene verificar que no haya espacios al principio o al final y que se mantengan las mayúsculas originales.
Quiénes no pueden reclamar premios en Free Fire a través de códigos
Las cuentas de invitado no pueden utilizar el sistema de recompensas, incluso cuando el código aún aparece como activo. El portal necesita una cuenta registrada para identificar el perfil que recibirá los objetos y enviar el contenido correspondiente al buzón del juego.
Quienes juegan con un perfil de invitado deben vincularlo antes con alguno de los proveedores habilitados. Google, Facebook, Apple y VK figuran entre las alternativas disponibles. La vinculación de la cuenta permite que los premios queden asignados al usuario correcto y evita inconvenientes durante el proceso.
Cuánto demoran en llegar los diamantes al inventario
Los artículos obtenidos mediante los códigos suelen enviarse al correo interno de Free Fire. El plazo habitual de entrega es inferior a 24 horas, aunque algunos premios pueden tardar en reflejarse en el inventario principal del usuario.
Después de completar el canje, es clave revisar la sección de correo del juego. Los diamantes se encuentran entre las recompensas más buscadas, porque permiten acceder a contenido de pago, pero su entrega depende de la clave validada y de las condiciones que mantenga activas el sistema.
La pauta principal es utilizar únicamente el portal oficial de recompensas de Garena y descargar el juego desde tiendas verificadas. En los teléfonos con Android, la vía indicada es Google Play Store; en los dispositivos de Apple, corresponde usar App Store.

articles.title: Samsung Odyssey G8 G80SH 32-inch 4K OLED gaming monitor review: Color, performance and style
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The Samsung Odyssey G8 G80SH is one of the best HDR OLEDs I’ve reviewed. It delivers a stunning image with no need for calibration and addictive gaming that will keep you playing for hours.
Reasons to buy
- + Bright and colorful image
- + Exceptional HDR quality
- + Dynamic tone mapping for HDR10 content
- + Matte anti-glare screen is very effective
- + Accurate out of the box
- + Excellent game performance
- + Plenty of inputs and USB ports
- + Unique yet understated styling
- + Solid build quality
- + Good value
Reasons to avoid
- - No internal speakers
- - No variable brightness for SDR
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
If you’re shopping for one of the best OLED gaming monitors, the 240 Hz QHD category offers the most choices and the best bang for the buck. But 4K at 240 Hz is creeping downward in price and only represents a small upcharge. It also means that you can go to 32 inches and maintain good pixel density. If you have enough video card horsepower to push frame rates over 180fps, the quality is unmatched.
Samsung slides into the neither-expensive-nor-inexpensive position with its Odyssey G8 G80SH. This 32-inch Quantum Dot OLED runs 240 Hz at 4K resolution with Adaptive-Sync, HDR10, HDR10+, wide gamut color, factory calibration, and high brightness for HDR content. Let’s take a look.
Samsung Odyssey G8 G80SH Specs
| Panel Type / Backlight | Quantum Dot Organic Light Emitting Diode | 
| Screen Size / Aspect Ratio | 32 inches / 16:9 | 
| Max Resolution and Refresh Rate | 3840x2160 @ 240 Hz | 
| Row 3 - Cell 0 | FreeSync and G-Sync Compatible | 
| Native Color Depth and Gamut | 10-bit / DCI-P3+ | 
| Row 5 - Cell 0 | HDR10, HDR10+ | 
| Row 6 - Cell 0 | VESA DisplayHDR True Black 500 | 
| Response Time (GTG) | 0.03ms | 
| Brightness (mfr) | 300 nits full field | 
| Row 9 - Cell 0 | 1,000 nits 3% window | 
| Contrast | Unmeasurable | 
| Speakers | None | 
| Video Inputs | 1x DisplayPort 2.1 | 
| Row 13 - Cell 0 | 2x HDMI 2.1, 1x USB-C | 
| Audio | 3.5mm headphone output | 
| USB 3.2 | 2x down | 
| Power Consumption | 48.8w, brightness @ 200 nits | 
| Panel Dimensions WxHxD w/base | 28.3 x 18.5-23.2 x 10.4 inches (719 x 470-589 x 264mm) | 
| Panel Thickness | 1.9 inches (48mm) | 
| Bezel Width | Top/sides: 0.3 inch (7mm) | 
| Row 20 - Cell 0 | Sides: 0.4 inch (11mm) | 
| Row 21 - Cell 0 | Bottom: 0.6 inch (15mm) | 
| Weight | 17.2 pounds (7.8kg) | 
| Warranty | 3 years | 
First, I want to clear up any potential confusion with another recently reviewed Samsung display, the G80HS. That is a 6K resolution dual-refresh mode model that currently costs around $1,600. The G80SH I’m covering here is a 4K screen with a single 240 Hz mode, and it’s currently selling for $900.
The G80SH delivers the best of everything in the premium OLED category. It’s 4K with a Quantum Dot layer that delivers a measured 106% coverage of DCI-P3. That’s about average among the QD-OLEDs I’ve tested, which range from 104 to 108%. The visual difference there is extremely small, not enough to affect a purchase decision. The G80SH also offers excellent out-of-the-box accuracy courtesy of a factory calibration. Though my sample didn’t need any tweaking, it benefited from a few adjustments. And that capability extends to HDR content, where you have full control of color temp, brightness, and luminance tracking.
Speaking of HDR, you get the requisite HDR10 support that all monitors have, plus Samsung’s answer to Dolby Vision, HDR10+. This extension of HDR10 includes dynamic tone mapping where the content matches its luminance curve to whatever display it’s shown on. Since HDR is mastered to a specific peak luminance, usually 1,000 nits but sometimes as high as 10,000, it’s beneficial when the screen can adapt to the incoming metadata to accommodate a lower or higher limit. You’ll see the same fine detail and nuance that the content creator did.
Gaming benefits from the aforementioned 240 Hz refresh rate plus a flawless implementation of Adaptive-Sync. The G80SH works with equal precision on G-Sync and FreeSync platforms, as well as the VRR output from gaming consoles. To help with your aim, there are reticles available in different colors and shapes, with a dynamic mode that keeps them in contrast with the background.
Like every Samsung monitor I’ve experienced, the G80SH delivers high style and solid build quality. The main color is silver, which you can see everywhere except the front, keeping the screen and surrounding bezel all black. There’s a matte anti-glare coating too, effectively eliminating all ambient light reflections. If you have a sunny room, this monitor can handle it without a degradation in image quality. You also get the latest video interfaces, four in total, plus USB and a headphone jack. LED lighting is featured on the back and can be controlled from the OSD.

So, just to recap before we jump into the tests, this is the Odyssey G8 G80SH, a 4K 240 Hz OLED that sells for $900. If you’re interested in learning more about the 6K model, my review from a few months ago is here.
Assembly and Accessories
Samsung still uses crumbly foam to ship its monitors, and my G80SH sample arrived safe and sound. The base, upright, and stand assemble with a captive bolt and a snap-on to create a solid package. To keep the panel thin, the power supply is external. It’s quite large, so consider that when fitting it into your space. The accessory bundle includes right-angle power cables plus one each of DisplayPort, HDMI, and USB-C.
Product 360
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
The G80SH’s silver trim is visible from the front in the base and a thin border around the screen that wraps around from the back. The actual bezel is very narrow and flush, so you can’t see it when the power’s off. A small protrusion in the bottom center says Samsung in tiny letters and houses an equally tiny power LED that can’t be seen from the front. Samsung is one of the few manufacturers to offer matte-screened OLEDs, and this implementation is excellent. Even a bright flashlight can’t throw a reflection onto the screen. Sunny office dwellers, this is your monitor.
In the back, it’s all silver all the time with a smooth finish and minimalist styling. There’s a thin ventilation grill on top, a small logo on one side, and hooray, inputs that face backward. You get two HDMI 2.1, a DisplayPort 2.1, USB-C with 98 watts, and two USB-A downstream ports. There are no internal speakers, but there is a 3.5mm headphone jack. On one side of the I/O panel is a joystick, the G80SH’s sole control key. Around the stand’s attachment point is an LED ring with colors and effects available in the OSD. If you remove the stand, a 100mm VESA mount is revealed should you prefer an aftermarket solution. Fasteners are not included.
That large external power supply keeps the panel thin at just under two inches. The stand is solid and wobble-free and offers 2/25 degrees tilt, 30 degrees swivel, a 90-degree portrait mode and a 4.7-inch height range. Movements are firm and smooth, in keeping with the G80SH’s premium status.
OSD Features
The G80SH’s OSD keeps Samsung’s traditional gaming monitor styling with its control panel appearance. Up top are portholes that deliver information about game-related settings. No refresh rate info, though. It would be nice to have that.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
In the Game menu, you get an Adaptive-Sync toggle, aiming points, a black equalizer to enhance shadow detail, and the LED lighting control. The reticles come in two shapes and three colors. Or you can use AI Mode, which changes the color to maintain contrast with the background. You can also position the aiming point somewhere other than the center of the screen. The lighting has multiple effects or can remain a single static color. One miss here is a frame counter. There’s no way to monitor the refresh rate.
In the Picture menu are all the G80SH’s calibration controls. You get five color temps, all adjustable, and seven gamma presets. The Contrast Enhancer is a field dimming control. True variable brightness is only active in HDR mode. You can choose between static and active tone mapping for HDR, which is handy for HDR10 content because it helps bring out highlights without clipping fine shadow detail.
You won’t find an sRGB mode among the color space choices, but if you pick Auto, the G80SH will render sRGB for SDR content. This is an approach that I like, and almost no other manufacturers do it that way. If you’d rather see the full gamut for all content, just leave it on Native. Peak Brightness does just what it says for HDR content; it raises the peak output. In my HDR tests, I saw 530 nits from a 25% window pattern.
Remaining menu items include port version control, an off timer, DSC toggle, and USB-C control. You also get two panel care options: logo brightness (dimming, actually) and pixel refresh. You can pause the incoming video signal while this is running if you wish.
Samsung Odyssey G8 G80SH Calibration Settings
The G80SH includes a factory calibration with a report saved in the monitor’s firmware. I found visually perfect color and grayscale tracking, but gamma was a little light. Two clicks of the gamma slider made that much better. I noted that though the default picture mode is called Eco, it is just as bright as the other presets, so that you can use it for all content. In HDR mode, you get Display HDR, which has excellent tone mapping and color accuracy. Suppose you want sRGB; just set Color Space to Auto. Then the G80SH will automatically render sRGB for SDR and the full gamut for HDR, which covers 106% of DCI-P3. If you want full color for SDR, set it to Native. My recommended settings are below.
| Picture Mode | Eco | 
| Brightness 200 nits | 27 | 
| Brightness 120 nits | 9 | 
| Brightness 100 nits | 5 | 
| Brightness 80 nits | 1 (min. 78 nits) | 
| Contrast | 50 | 
| Color Space | Auto | 
| Gamma | -2 | 
| Color Temp Warm 1 | Red -4, Green -3, Blue 2 | 
Gaming and Hands-on
The G80SH’s color quality and accuracy make it well suited for duty as a post-production monitor or perhaps an on-site display for location shoots. Only a slight gamma anomaly separates it from perfection. It nails grayscale and gamut tracking, which you can read about on pages four and five. And it’s bright enough for any indoor space. I noted that there was no variable brightness option for SDR, but you can turn on a dynamic contrast option, which equates to field dimming. In HDR mode, dimming occurs at the pixel level, and you can choose between Active and Static tone mapping. The former delivers more punch to HDR10 content.
I also noted the G80SH’s excellent color balance. SDR lets you choose between Native and Auto. Native shows the full gamut, which covers 106% of DCI-P3 and is very colorful. It will be the likely choice for most users. If you prefer sRGB for SDR, set the color space to Auto. Then, it will switch automatically. This is something very few monitors offer. I also noted that the HDR mode allows calibration of grayscale and gamma, another thing I rarely see.
With the image dialed in, I turned to a few afternoons of gaming where the G80SH provided the addictive quality that all premium OLEDs have. It doesn’t have a frame counter, so I had to use FRAPS to monitor the refresh rate, which stayed around 200fps at the max detail settings in Doom Eternal. This was fast enough to provide blur-free motion and input lag low enough to keep up with my most frenetic movements. You’ll see on the next page that it offers response typical of other 4K 240 Hz OLEDs. That means you’ll be able to aim and shoot with speed and precision. I got extra credit in hoard mode for jump shots where I was able to land grenades on target while flying through the air. Turn and shoot became second nature as I mowed through my opponents.
Detail in close encounters made me stop and admire the picture more than a few times. Tiny highlights like sweat and other bodily fluids popped right out, making the characters look three-dimensional. Other textures like stone and metal looked better thanks to strong reflections. These highlights moved smoothly over objects like the player’s weapon, which further enhanced realism. The G80SH has some of the best-looking HDR I’ve seen of late.
It makes a great workday monitor too, with understated styling that stands out but doesn’t scream for attention. The LED lighting is just a ring in the back with smoothly playing effects or static colors available, or you can shut it off. The stand is rock solid with comfortable and usable ergonomics. The joystick navigates the OSD intuitively and efficiently. I really appreciated the rear-facing ports, which were easy to see and access. You get two USB-A downstream ports, which can accommodate peripherals once you make a connection to the USB-C input, which doubles as a charger with 98 watts of power. There are no internal speakers, but headphones plug into the 3.5mm jack.
Takeaway: If Samsung keeps the G80SH’s price below $1,000, it will sell a lot of them. It’s a super versatile display for any form of productivity or entertainment. It’s addictive for gaming, with smooth operation and quick response. The image looks stunning in every respect, whether moving or static. Color accuracy is good enough that calibration isn’t required. It has unique but understated styling and excellent ergonomics with a solid stand and rear-facing ports. Aside from a lack of internal speakers, there is nothing missing here.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia's OORI partners with Oumla to digitise private market investments
articles.text:
Saudi Arabia's OORI partners with Oumla to digitise private market investments
- Saudi-based private markets investment platform OORI has announced a strategic partnership with Oumla, a Saudi digital asset infrastructure provider, to develop digital investment infrastructure for banks and financial institutions.
- The partnership will integrate Oumla's asset digitisation and blockchain-based recordkeeping infrastructure with OORI OS, OORI's B2B platform that manages investment discovery, due diligence, Shariah screening, investor onboarding, portfolio management and reporting.
- OORI, which is licensed by Saudi Arabia's Capital Market Authority (CMA), uses AI agents and analytics to automate private market investment workflows. Oumla, founded in 2022, provides tokenisation, digital asset custody and blockchain connectivity services for financial institutions.
- Both companies receive technical and infrastructure support from the Avalanche ecosystem. The partnership aims to reduce administrative costs, improve transaction traceability and help financial institutions digitise private market investment operations.
Press release:
OORI, the Saudi-based investment platform focused on private markets, announced today a strategic partnership with Oumla, a Saudi-based digital assets infrastructure provider, to advance the digital investment capabilities available to banks and financial institutions.
The partnership combines OORI’s private markets expertise and its B2B technology platform, OORI OS, with Oumla’s innovative technology solutions. OORI OS streamlines and digitises the entire private-market investment lifecycle, bringing together opportunity discovery, due diligence, Shariah screening, investment structuring, investor onboarding, portfolio management, and reporting in one platform. Powered by AI agents and advanced analytics, it simplifies operations and supports better investment decisions.
Oumla’s infrastructure layer will enable financial institutions to fully digitise their operations, automate complex workflows, and reduce administrative overhead, which will strengthen the core infrastructure of private market investing. Enhanced ownership recordkeeping and transaction traceability deliver complete visibility, while accelerated processing ensures a seamless experience across every stage of the investment lifecycle.
OORI and Oumla are both backed by Avalanche, an ADGM-regulated digital assets foundation which provides technical and infrastructure support. This shared infrastructure will support closer collaboration as the partnership develops and help both companies reach institutions across a wider ecosystem.
Naif Alajmi, Co-Founder, Board Member and Head of Arranging at OORI, said, "With Saudi private investment fund assets reaching SAR 700 billion in Q1 2026, up 26.1% year on year, the demand is clear. What has been missing is infrastructure that makes serving it cost-effective. Oumla’s technology and OORI’s OORI OS platform allows us to bring private market opportunities to eligible investors at a fraction of the traditional cost, through a modern and scalable solution for modern investors.
Mohammed Aljasser, Chief Executive Officer of Oumla, said, "Digital assets only matter if they change who can access an investment and what it costs to get there. OORI is proving that in Saudi private markets. Our infrastructure handles the asset digitisation and on-chain record keeping behind it, built to the security standards institutions expect, so OORI can focus on its investors.”
The partnership reflects a growing priority among financial institutions to modernise how investment products are distributed, administered, and monitored in a manner that is secure, transparent, and aligned with regulatory expectations. By embedding advanced technology within a platform institutions already rely on, OORI and Oumla aim to make that modernisation practical and scalable.

articles.title: Jensen Huang tenía un as escondido en la Casa Blanca: su apoyo ha sido clave para su vuelta al frente de Nvidia
articles.text:
El pasado 12 de noviembre, Jensen Huang dimitía como CEO de Nvidia, hundido por un truculento escándalo en el que se mezclaban infidelidades, geopolítica y sospechas de espionaje para China. Once días después, el mismo consejo que aceptó su salida lo ha vuelto a readmitir como CEO por unanimidad.
Entre una fecha y otra, hubo una mano que no dejó de presionar a Nvidia para que Huang "volviera al trabajo": Donald Trump. La readmisión de Huang resuelve un gigantesco problema sucesorio para Nvidia, pero arroja una duda sobre la compañía: ¿hasta qué punto es independiente Nvidia de las decisiones que se toman en el despacho oval?
Una amistad con contraprestaciones. Según contaba NBC, el vínculo entre Huang y Donald Trump nació en una cena en Mar-a-Lago. Esa confianza fue creciendo hasta el punto de que, tal y como Huang reconoció en una entrevista con AP, el presidente "me llama en mitad de la noche y quiere hablar de alguno de estos temas". Huang ha pisado la Casa Blanca nueve veces y en septiembre se sentó en la mesa principal de una cena de Estado, junto a Trump y Xi Jinping.
También acompañó al presidente en su viaje oficial a China en mayo, donde incluso se desvió el plan de vuelo del Air Force One para recoger a Huang en Alaska. La Administración le devolvió el favor al suavizar restricciones de Biden, lo que permitió vender sus chips de la generación anterior a China. Huang defendía que era más seguro enganchar a las empresas chinas a la tecnología de EEUU que empujarlas a buscar otra.
Dinero y altavoz para la IA. Por su parte, Nvidia ha financiado con mucho dinero las iniciativas de Trump. La tecnológica aportó 25 millones de dólares al salón de baile de la Casa Blanca situándose como una de las principales donantes, solo empatada con Apple y la familia Adelson. Su gasto en lobby se ha multiplicado por ocho en este mandato y superó los 2,5 millones en el tercer trimestre, según los registros públicos que cita NBC.
En pleno evento All-In, Trump le llamó mientras todavía estaba en el escenario y Huang pidió un micro para que todos oyeran al presidente tachar de "engaño" la petición de frenar la IA. Su respuesta: "Tiene usted razón. No vamos a permitir que eso suceda, señor". Lo que calló es que si la IA se ralentiza, caen los pedidos de chips, y esos chips los fabrica Nvidia. Una mano frota a la otra.
Esa espía de la que usted me habla. Alice Huang, exdirectiva de Megaspeed, estaba siendo investigada por desviar chips a China algunos meses antes de que se hiciera público su affair con Huang. Según el NYT, Washington la vigilaba desde hacía un año. Pekín niega su implicación en el caso de espionaje.
Trump, sin embargo, restó peso al asunto. Dijo que no sabía si era espía, a pesar de los avisos de sus propios servicios, y afirmó: "Si la mujer era una espía, sí. Si no lo era, quizás sería diferente". Ante los periodistas añadió que a cualquier mujer hermosa que llega de China "dicen que es una espía". El Gobierno que la vigilaba tan de cerca como para conocer qué relación mantenía con Huang es el que ahora da por buena la vuelta de Huang.
Un consejo que da marcha atrás. El lunes 16 Trump dijo que "no le importaría" ver de vuelta a Huang al frente de Nvidia. El domingo escribió en su red social Truth que readmitirlo "sería lo mejor para la empresa y también para Estados Unidos". Una recogida de firmas con más de 206.000 participantes, entre ellos figuras como Elon Musk, también presionaba para que el consejo oyera las peticiones de readmisión de Huang.
Harvey Jones, presidente del consejo, había dicho apenas seis días antes que no había intención de restituirlo. Ya se advertía de que hacerlo parecería obedecer a la Casa Blanca. Pero ha pasado.
La llamada del presidente. En su comunicado, el consejo de administración de Nvidia asegura que recibió información de altos cargos del Gobierno de EEUU y que, con ella, la vuelta de Huang no es un riesgo para la seguridad nacional. Lo que Nvidia no cuenta en su comunicado es que también recibió la llamada de Trump presionando a su junta directiva para que Huang recuperara su puesto, tal y como desvela Semafor.
Trump celebró que la junta "ha tomado la decisión correcta y adecuada", y las acciones de la compañía se dispararon hasta subir más del 31% antes de la apertura. Nvidia no es una empresa estatal, pero el calendario sugiere quién marcó el ritmo para que Huang volviera a ser su CEO.

articles.title: How flexibility, services, and employee experience are driving IndiQube’s growth
articles.text:
How flexibility, services, and employee experience are driving IndiQube’s growth
IndiQube, which manages close to 11 million square feet of office space, is broadening its offerings through integrated services, design solutions, and sustainability offerings to drive growth and enhance employee experience.
Managed office space provider IndiQube continues to see strong demand as it expands its offering to cater to the growing requirements of the market.
Founded in 2015, IndiQube entered the market at a time when India's startup ecosystem was witnessing rapid growth, driven by sectors such as ecommerce, mobility, and food delivery. The founders realised that similar disruption would also come into the real estate sector, which offered limited flexibility and standardised services.
The company identified three key requirements for businesses: flexibility, services, and a superior employee experience. It has since evolved into an integrated managed workspace provider, serving 884 clients.
IndiQube reported a 34% year-on-year rise in revenue to Rs 492 crore in the second quarter of FY27, while narrowing its losses by 80% to Rs 6 crore.
At the end of the quarter, the company was present in 17 cities with 138 centres and managing 10.86 million square feet of space.
In an interview with YourStory, Meghna Agarwal, Co-founder of IndiQube, highlighted the company’s growth drivers and what are they doing to remain ahead of the game.
Edited excerpts.
YourStory (YS): How do you see IndiQube’s performance in the second quarter of FY27?
Meghna Agarwal (MA): Our profitability has improved due to our steady state of occupancy, which has increased from 89% to 91%, which has boosted our growth. Given our economies of scale, we expect our top line revenue growth to be in the range of about 30% and EBITDA to be in the range of 19-21%, and our PAT would be in the range of about 8-10%.
YS: What are the factors that are driving demand for IndiQube?
MA: Earlier, it was startups. But now we have expanded into Indian enterprises, multi-national corporations, and global capability centres (GCCs), which is a balanced mix.
In terms of the cities, it is very important to have a presence in Tier I locations because of the presence of a large number of companies. Among the top 10 cities, Bengaluru is the largest in terms of area. It is not that we just focus on top tier cities as we are also present in places such as Coimbatore and Madurai.
Our strategy is to have a wider presence as well as go deeper in the existing cities. For example, a client will be keen to have multiple locations within the city of Bengaluru or Mumbai. A deeper penetration gives us economies of scale and we keep testing the water with a wider presence. It has to be a balance between both.
YS: How is IndiQube expanding its offerings for customers?
MA: We call ourselves a managed integrated platform. I have four models. One is the growth, which is plug and play services. Second is DesignQube, which provides interior services where we do it not only for IndiQube clients but also for non-IndiQube customers. Third is IndiQare where we provide services like food, transport, etc., and there is consistency of experience regardless of their location. Lastly, it is the eco-sustainability solutions, which looks into energy and water management, green buildings, etc.
YS: What do you think are the USPs of IndiQube?
MA: Our biggest asset is the manner in which we lease properties. We are not tied to a building or asset, but to talent. Wherever the talent is going, we will go there. For example, we have renovated one-third of the properties in our portfolio. Second is the flexibility in our offerings where it can range from Rs 8,000 per seat going all the way up to Rs 20,000. Third is the wide array of services that we provide where we ensure that the quality and experience remains the same across all our properties. The fourth part, which is very underrated, is corporate governance. The intent of the founders has always been to create value for everyone—clients, shareholders, and the team. Lastly, it is our focus on sustainability and we have been doing this since early 2000. Today, around 85% of our properties are green certified buildings. IndiQube places emphasis on building long-term relationships with our clients.

articles.title: HWiNFO Can Now Serve Sensor Readings to Phones and Tablets Over Your Network
articles.text:
Monday, November 23rd 2026
HWiNFO Can Now Serve Sensor Readings to Phones and Tablets Over Your Network
HWiNFO has released version 8.61 Beta (build 6125), which adds a built-in REST API server. That addition now allows HWiNFO to serve every tracked sensor as JSON over HTTP or HTTPS, along with details such as units, descriptions, and sensor groupings. This basically means that HWiNFO's sensor readings can now be viewed in a web browser on any device connected to your home network, including phones and tablets. This definitely increases the convenience factor for users who want to stay on top of their hardware monitoring stats at all times.
HWiNFO has also put up a GitHub package with an API guide, along with sample dashboards and material for building dashboards with AI agents. To set it up, users have to navigate to the Sensors window, where a new Remote Center button opens an API panel. Then, users pick an IP address and port, choose whether to use HTTPS, and hit Start. HWiNFO has included a ready-made dashboard modeled on the Sensors window, but you can also add custom pages. Without a license, the REST API server is limited to 12 hours of operation. This is the same cap the free version already puts on Shared Memory support as well as remote sensor monitoring. Power users can extend that time by picking up HWiNFO Pro. As far as security goes, HWiNFO recommends keeping the server on trusted networks only.

articles.title: Nvidia reverses course, reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.text:
Nvidia reverses course, reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO
Artificial intelligence chip giant Nvidia Corp. today announced that Jensen Huang has been reinstated as chief executive, president and board director effective immediately after resigning almost two weeks ago.
The company’s rockstar leather-jacket-wearing CEO faced turmoil earlier this month after it was revealed that he had been embroiled in a scandal involving multiple extramarital affairs, including with an Nvidia executive and a suspected Chinese spy. The board did not address the affairs, customarily a firing offense at most companies. in its statement.
News of his affair with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, an executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed International Pte. Ltd., broke on Nov. 10, reported by The Information. She was reportedly instrumental in helping China earn over $7.5 billion in chip sales through Nvidia, which is currently sanctioned by the United States from shipping to the country under trade restrictions.
Huang resigned amid reports that Nvidia’s board was in talks with plans to replace him. Today’s announcement marks a major about-face by the company.
In today’s announcement, the board said it voted unanimously to reinstate him to his vacated roles after a series of discussions and that it was “satisfied with his candor and ability to lead.” The board added that it received input from “senior levels of United States government” on its decision, and is “confident” that Huang poses no national security risk.
Huang thanked Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, who stood in as interim CEO, for taking up the helm in his absence before taking back control of the company.
“I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.”
Nvidia shares surged around 29% following Huang’s reinstatement. The stock had fallen almost 33% after Huang admitted to the affair with Alice Huang earlier in November.
“Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia CEO is a stunning new development, but not an altogether surprising one,” eMarketer Inc. analyst Jacob Bourne told SiliconANGLE. “After more than three decades at the helm, Huang has become so central to Nvidia’s identity and the broader AI trade that his departure fueled uncertainty during an already volatile period for the industry.”
Bourne added that Huang’s return may assuage investor upset and restore confidence in the company, reflected in the current stock upsurge, but the upheaval echoes the brief ouster of OpenAI Group PBC CEO Sam Altman in 2023. Between Nvidia and OpenAI, removing and then welcoming back CEOs amid disagreement and now scandal raises pertinent questions about corporate governance and how the outsized influence of individual leaders in the AI industry will affect the future.
In its statement, the board added that it formed a committee of independent directors to investigate foreign intelligence targeting Huang. The same committee has retained independent counsel to assist it and intends to reach a conclusion despite his reinstatement.
Huang announced his full support for the investigation and said he would cooperate fully.
The board also announced the formation of a National Security and Export Control Committee, composed of independent directors, to oversee trade compliance and national security risks. The company added that it will make certain the committee oversees national security matters and trade controls and is currently searching to fill a new chief compliance officer role.

articles.title: Trump halts Iowa detonation, says new governor to blame if it blows accidentally
articles.text:
President Trump took to social media Monday afternoon to announce that he has ordered the US military to halt plans to detonate 68 deteriorating barrels of lead azide at an Army ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa. Trump claimed that the fate of the unstable, highly explosive material is now in the hands of a federal court and Rob Sand, Iowa’s governor-elect, who won’t be sworn into office until January.
The Army had planned to detonate the barrels on November 20, but delayed the blast on Thursday amid public outcry and a legal challenge from environmental groups. The explosion will launch a plume of toxic gases and neurotoxic lead that could reach up to 100 miles away from the Iowa facility, the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP).
Iowa residents and officials said they learned of the detonation only days beforehand. The environmental groups, led by Earthjustice, claimed in an emergency court filing that the Army had not fully considered safer options for disposing of the lead azide before planning the detonation.
Late Thursday, a federal appeals court granted Earthjustice’s request to put a hold on the Army’s permit from the Environmental Protection Agency, which allowed for the controlled detonation to be carried out. Around the same time, Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle said the detonation would be postponed until Monday so the military could communicate with Iowans about the situation and plans.
Lead azide risk
Documents released by the Army last week said that the military first learned in March that the lead azide had started to degrade and crystallize. Lead azide is used in detonators for munitions, but in crystallized form it becomes highly unstable and sensitive to physical movement or friction. The IAAAP is said to contain around 9,700 pounds (4.4 tons) of lead azide in barrels held in earth-covered containers.

The best espresso machines 2026: our expert-led guide to better coffee at home
Get a morning jump-start with perfectly brewed espresso
The best espresso machine can kickstart your day with a rich, velvety hit of caffeine without you ever having to leave the house. To help you find the right machine for you, we’ve tested the latest models from major brands like Breville, Gaggia, and De'Longhi.
While there is no shortage of coffee makers on the market, as you'll see in our selection of the best coffee machines, nothing quite matches the versatility of a dedicated espresso machine. Whether you want a hands-on manual setup that lets you hone your barista skills, or a beginner-friendly bean-to-cup machine that grinds, brews, and steams at the touch of a button, we’ve got you covered.
During testing, we evaluate everything from heat-up times and decibel levels to portafilter (or brew group) build quality, grinder settings, steam wand performance, and drink customization. Above all, we test for cup-to-cup consistency—so you can count on café-quality coffee every single morning.
