How to choose an espresso machine
Espresso machines are some of the best coffee makers. They come in all shapes and sizes, including some of the best bean-to-cup coffee machines, and the best espresso makers help you achieve barista-quality results. They often include their own integrated bean grinder for your convenience but do bear in mind that extra equipment adds bulk and often increases the price as well. If you're looking for something fast, cheap and that doesn't need a lot of counter space you might prefer a single-serve or pod coffee machine.
If espresso is definitely for you, the first decision is to choose whether you want an espresso machine that offers manual control over dispensing water or a device that takes on that work for you; the latter is probably better for those new to playing barista.
Next, consider if you want a machine that you can use with ground coffee, single-serve pods, or a mixture of the two. Coffee pods are less messy than using ground coffee. They can be handy if you occasionally want to make decaf coffee using the machine – but they don’t produce the thick, rich crema you get with freshly ground coffee.
If you regularly make espresso for two or more people, look for a coffee machine with a double spot on the tray that can fill two separate cups simultaneously. And if you like longer coffee drinks with milk, such as cappuccinos and lattes, choose an espresso machine with a built-in steam wand or factor in the cost of a standalone milk frother.
Finally, take note of the size of the espresso maker to see if you have sufficient room for it on your kitchen countertop – or, if you plan to store it away in a cupboard, consider its weight to see that you’ll be able to lift it easily.
If you're on a budget, take a look at our guide to the best cheap coffee maker deals, too.
How we tested these espresso machines
We put every espresso machine through rigorous testing to see if it truly lives up to its promises. First and foremost, we judge the coffee itself; we look for a rich, intense shot free of bitter or burnt notes, topped with a thick, stable crema that holds its own even after sugar is sprinkled on top. We also measure extraction temperatures to ensure cup-to-cup consistency and monitor how loud the machine gets during brewing.
If a machine includes a built-in steam wand, we test its ability to microfoam both dairy and plant-based milks, checking for tiny bubbles that create a velvety, smooth texture; again keeping an ear out for excessive noise.
Finally, we evaluate the day-to-day user experience: how intuitive it is to set up and operate, whether it offers enough manual control for aspiring home baristas, and how easily the water tank removes for refills. We also factor in overall aesthetics and how much counter space it will claim in your kitchen.
Espresso machine FAQs
How do I make an espresso?
Espresso is made by passing water at high pressure through compacted ground coffee.
However, a set ‘recipe’, which usually refers to a ratio and brewing duration, is generally given by the roaster (the brands that roast and blend coffee beans). The most common recipe is 1:2 in 25 to 35 seconds, effectively turning each gram of ground coffee into 2g of liquid espresso in that period.
How compacted the ground coffee is will affect how quickly or slowly the espresso brews. If the coffee is too tightly packed, it will take longer to brew and be too strong; loosely compacted coffee means it will be dispensed too quickly and subsequently weak. Prefer a cappuccino, latte, or a flat white? Find out how to make your favorite coffee in our article.
If you'd like expert advice on making coffee-shop-worthy drinks at home, we have some great tips and tricks for you – and while you're at it, check out our guide to the game-changing coffee maker trick that will ensure you never drink bitter espresso again.
How is an espresso machine different from a coffee machine?
An espresso machine differs from other coffee machines because it uses pressurized hot water passed through a disc of compacted coffee grounds called a puck. It's possible to adjust the volume of water passed through the grounds and how tightly packed the coffee is to change the strength of the hot drink brewed.
Single-serve coffee machines, or pod coffee machines as they're sometimes known, still use pressurized hot water, but the coffee is contained in a capsule or pod. The coffee machine punctures the capsule several times to allow the water to flow through the coffee ground to brew the drink. However, while some single-serve coffee machines let you adjust how much water is used to create different volumes of coffee, it's impossible to tweak how compacted the grounds are.
Finally, drip coffee makers pass hot water through compacted coffee grounds. As a result, it's not at the same pressure as when using an espresso machine, and there's no set volume of water used. Instead, the brewing takes place until the water tank runs dry or the coffee maker is switched off. This creates a more traditional filter coffee rather than espresso.

O Galaxy AI integrado, por sua vez, otimiza a análise desses dados oferecendo uma leitura mais completa da qualidade do sono e dos níveis de energia corporal. Essas características justificam a presença do Galaxy Watch 8 entre no ranking de melhores smartwatches para treinos segundo o Tecnoblog.
Vale pontuar que a queda de preços recente se dá pelo lançamento do Galaxy Watch 9 no mercado, que pode ser encontrado em promoção por cerca de R$ 1,5 mil (50% acima do antecessor). articles.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO following unanimous vote by company board — 11-day exit from company saw stock prices fall by 24% after affair scandal
articles.text:
Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO following unanimous vote by company board — 11-day exit from company saw stock prices fall by 24% after affair scandal
He's back.
Nvidia has reinstated CEO Jensen Huang by a unanimous vote from its board of directors, the company announced Monday.
"Nvidia today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board," a statement reads. "The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk."
Shares of the company surged more than 30% ahead of the Nasdaq's open, erasing all of the losses incurred during Huang's leave of absence. In a Truth Social post, President Donald Trump said Nvidia "has made the correct and proper decision" in reinstating Huang, stating the USA needs his leadership and Nvidia to ensure "the success and prosperity of not only the company, but the American economy." He further stated that the U.S. Attorney General has no evidence Huang engaged "in any unlawful conduct."
The board said that it is confident that Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk, and part of this reassurance seems to have come from a senior level of the United States government.
“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board, stated. "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer."
Huang said he was "honored" to return to Nvidia, but took the responsibility "with the greatest humility and renewed commitment."
Huang remains under investigation following reports he was entangled in an extramarital affair with a Chinese intelligence asset, with the board stating the investigation will proceed to conclusion. Reports emerged some weeks ago that Jensen Huang was having an affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, a company under criminal investigation for the export of illicit AI GPUs into China. Meanwhile, a second affair with VP of health care Kimberly Powell was brought to light, prompting Huang's resignation.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Nvidia has also formed a National Security and Export Control Committee of independent directors "to oversee trade compliance and national security risks." The committee will continue its work, and the company is also hiring a Chief Compliance Officer "to oversee compliance across Nvidia and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee."

He has covered the world of consumer tech from nearly every angle, including supply chain rumors, patents, and litigation, and more. When he's not at work, he loves reading about history and playing video games.

articles.title: Figma employee sues, alleging company forced her to confront harassers
articles.text:
A Figma engineer is suing the design software company and its co-founder and CEO, Dylan Field, over allegations that she faced sexual harassment and retaliation while managers and HR repeatedly told her to confront the very people she accused of misconduct.
The lawsuit, filed Monday in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, alleges that Figma’s culture of “direct feedback” led managers and HR to make engineer Serry Park address harassment herself rather than investigate her complaints. Park, who joined Figma in 2022, alleges the company’s response damaged her career, compensation, and mental health. The lawsuit also alleges that Park, who is Asian, faced racial and gender discrimination, including performance criticism based on stereotypes that Asian women are meek, timid, and conflict-averse.
“Figma was my dream company for a long time,” Park told TechCrunch in an interview before the lawsuit was filed. “It was a place where I felt that I could level up in my career, working on a lot of really cool, interesting things at scale.”
Park is seeking damages, a jury trial, and a court order prohibiting Figma from requiring employees who report harassment to confront their alleged harassers. She also wants the company to adopt and enforce a process for investigating harassment complaints promptly and confidentially.
When reached for comment, a spokesperson for Figma said, “Figma does not tolerate discrimination or harassment. Figma also does not tolerate extortion. These claims have no merit, and we will present the facts in court.”
Faith in the Process
Park told TechCrunch she initially had faith in Figma’s complaint process, expecting that if she documented the alleged harassment and reported it to the right people, the company would act. But as an engineer in a male-dominated field, Park told TechCrunch, “I don’t feel that they took me seriously throughout this process.”
Park, who is still employed at Figma, joined its San Francisco office in October 2022. Within weeks, her onboarding mentor — a fellow engineer — asked her on a date and continued pursuing her after she declined, Park alleges. She initially feared reporting him, worrying that her manager would “dismiss her reports or view her as the problem,” according to the lawsuit.
Park says she tried to avoid her onboarding mentor. In early 2023, for example, she delayed choosing a work project until he had picked one. When her manager criticized her for not being a “team player,” Park explained that she was trying to avoid the colleague she accused of harassment, according to the suit.
Her manager allegedly dismissed her concerns, saying he had “met his wife at work too” and treating the behavior as “harmless flirtation.” When Park asked to be kept off projects with the onboarding mentor, HR allegedly instructed her to confront him directly about his behavior.
The lawsuit ties that response to Figma’s culture of direct feedback, which Park alleges Field established and enforced. It says the company’s People organization trains managers to direct employees, including those reporting harassment, to give feedback directly to the person involved.
In March 2023, her manager assigned him to a major project she was leading, despite her request to be separated from him. Park told her manager that she would “figure it out,” but alleges that having to work with him affected her performance. Her manager gave her a 2 out of 5 on her performance review, criticizing her for not speaking up enough or engaging with others and for lacking presence. Park was put on a coaching plan, which she completed in late 2023.
Changing managers didn’t help, according to the lawsuit. Her second manager also refused to separate them, allegedly telling Park that someone at her level should be able to resolve conflicts with teammates and that separating them would be “avoiding the problem.” Like her previous manager, he allegedly pointed out that he had met his partner at work.
Park alleges the harassment continued throughout 2023.
In April 2024, she transferred to another team, a move she claims set back her career by resetting her performance and promotion timeline.
On her new team, which had more women, Park said she felt better and no longer had to work with her alleged harasser. Her performance reviews improved, but in late 2025, she alleges another incident of sexual harassment, this time by her new manager.
The incident followed a night out for drinks with her wife and two teammates, including her manager. The next day, during a team lunch, the manager allegedly said Park’s sex life had been discussed the previous evening. Park, who said no such conversation had occurred in her or her wife’s presence, felt “horrified and humiliated” by comments she believed fetishized queer relationships.
A colleague reported the comments to HR as sexual harassment, according to the suit. Weeks later, Park’s manager apologized in a Slack message, saying she didn’t recall what she had said. When Park sought HR’s guidance, she was again told to address the matter directly with her manager.
During their conversation, the manager allegedly became defensive, and the encounter left Park feeling “crushed, anxious, and vulnerable.” The manager also allegedly said she would never make such a comment because she had “a lot of gay friends.”
The manager told HR that they had agreed it was a misunderstanding. HR closed its investigation without interviewing witnesses, according to the suit, even though Park disputed her manager’s account.
“Requiring an employee to confront her harasser as the price of complaining — and then closing her complaint — would dissuade a reasonable employee from complaining at all,” the suit said.
Park alleges her manager retaliated by publicly berating her, sometimes so aggressively that colleagues intervened or checked on her afterward, according to the lawsuit. The suit also alleges that other teammates left the team over concerns about the manager’s behavior.
Park again complained to HR about “escalating retaliation” and expressed concern the manager would “derail her career.” HR allegedly defended the manager’s conduct, saying the manager was “within her reasonable authority” and again instructed Park to address her concerns directly with the manager.
In early 2026, Park received another low performance review and a reduced bonus. The lawsuit alleges that similarly situated men continued to receive promotions, raises, and bonuses. When Park reported the negative performance review to HR in March, she was allegedly told her sexual harassment complaint against her manager could not be “substantiated.”
Park took medical leave in March to receive treatment for PTSD symptoms and generalized anxiety. Cleared to return to work in June, she was prescribed workplace accommodations, including a graduated work schedule and mandatory remote workdays.
Park told TechCrunch that Figma approved the accommodations but had not implemented them at the time of the interview. In July, Park and her lawyers notified Figma of their intent to pursue legal action.
“It’s really scary for me,” she said about taking legal action. “I don’t know what’s going to happen next with this, I don’t know what the outcome is going to be, but at least it feels like this is my chance to do the right thing.”

articles.title: El Tamagotchi que nació en 1996 cumple 30 años y hoy es un accesorio retro
articles.text:
El Tamagotchi cumple 30 años desde que Bandai lo lanzó en Japón el 23 de noviembre de 1996. La mascota digital de tres botones revive como icono retro, impulsada por adultos que crecieron con ella, jóvenes atraídos por la estética de los 2000 y niños que descubren ahora su sistema de cuidados.
El aniversario confirma que el pequeño dispositivo con forma de huevo no quedó limitado a una generación. La compañía japonesa busca convertirlo en un objeto de colección, un accesorio de moda y una puerta de entrada al juego para nuevos usuarios. Las celebraciones incluirán lanzamientos especiales, colaboraciones y una aparición en las pantallas de Times Square, en Nueva York.
El Tamagotchi nació de una idea ligada al cuidado
Taro Tsuji, director ejecutivo de Bandai y responsable de Tamagotchi, explicó que el origen del juguete estuvo en una imagen cotidiana de Japón: un niño que atrapa un insecto, lo guarda en un recipiente y lo cuida.
Esa costumbre se trasladó al mundo digital mediante un aparato pequeño, portátil y con una mascota virtual que exigía atención. El usuario debía alimentarla, limpiarla, jugar con ella y vigilar su estado. Si descuidaba esas tareas, el personaje podía enfermar o desaparecer.
Bandai desarrolló el producto en una etapa de dificultades financieras, cuando la compañía buscaba lanzar algo distinto. La mezcla entre un objeto de bolsillo, una pantalla de cristal líquido y una rutina de cuidado convirtió al Tamagotchi en un fenómeno durante los últimos años del siglo pasado.
Tres generaciones sostienen el regreso de la mascota virtual
Tsuji divide a los compradores actuales en tres grupos. El primero está formado por personas de alrededor de 30 años que recibieron un Tamagotchi durante el lanzamiento original. Para ellos, el juguete funciona como un vínculo con la infancia.
El segundo grupo reúne a jóvenes de 20 años que conocieron la franquicia por la serie animada de 2008 y por el regreso de la moda ‘dosmilera’. El tercero corresponde a niños que se acercan al dispositivo como una experiencia distinta a los teléfonos y las consolas actuales.
La nostalgia retro ayudó a expandir la marca desde 2025. Tsuji vinculó ese impulso con el llamado “boom de las niñas de Heisei”, una tendencia japonesa que recupera la estética, los accesorios y la cultura popular de las décadas recientes.
“Sin este auge de nostalgia retro, no habríamos podido crear una ola tan grande como la actual”, señaló el ejecutivo. Según su explicación, Bandai llevaba tiempo preparando productos y estrategias para conectar con ese interés.
Los adultos compran juguetes para recuperar recuerdos
El aniversario coincide con una tendencia entre adultos que adquieren juguetes vinculados con su infancia. Valerie, una compradora austriaca entrevistada por EFE en Harajuku, contó que su madre nunca le compró un Tamagotchi y decidió obtener uno al ver los productos del 30 aniversario.
Para ella, el objeto comparte una lógica con Furby, Polly Pocket, Playmobil y otros juguetes populares durante los años noventa. Comprar uno en la adultez permite volver, aunque sea por un momento, a una etapa asociada con menos responsabilidades laborales.
Sayran, una seguidora australiana de la franquicia, mantiene varios dispositivos en su bolso y los cuida durante todo el día. Recibió su primer Tamagotchi mientras estudiaba desde casa y lo sintió como “su primer amigo”.
El dispositivo ocupa una posición particular frente al teléfono móvil. No busca reunir todas las funciones digitales, sino concentrarse en una tarea sencilla: cuidar a un personaje virtual. Esa limitación también explica su vigencia como accesorio y objeto de colección.
Bandai busca convertirlo en accesorio de moda
La empresa ampliará esa estrategia con los Tamagotchi Ring, anillos jugables que llegarán a partir de febrero como parte de las celebraciones. La propuesta intenta integrar la mascota virtual en el estilo personal de quienes cuelgan los dispositivos de bolsos, mochilas o llaveros.
Tsuji considera que el pequeño huevo ofrece una alternativa a la frialdad tecnológica del celular. Su formato permite llevarlo visible, tocar sus botones y establecer una rutina breve de interacción con el personaje.
Bandai también busca acercarse a los niños mediante colaboraciones. Una de ellas fue desarrollada con Roblox, plataforma donde los jugadores pueden trasladar avatares y participar en experiencias vinculadas con Tamagotchi.
El modelo original utilizaba una pantalla sencilla de cristal líquido. Durante tres décadas, la franquicia incorporó infrarrojos, pantallas a color, conexión Wi-Fi y nuevas funciones de interacción. Tsuji atribuye parte de esa continuidad a la escucha activa de los seguidores en internet.

articles.title: Tesla change en douce une règle clé de son pilote automatique : les grands excès de vitesse sont terminés
articles.text:
Voilà peut-être la roulette la plus piégeuse de toute l’industrie automobile. Vous la connaissez possiblement, celle qui se trouve sur la branche droite du volant des Tesla. Une fois la conduite autonome activée, il suffit de la manipuler pour augmenter ou réduire la vitesse de consigne. Les effets sont immédiats, et rappelés par le petit cercle bleu englobant l’inscription « Max » indiquant l’allure à ne pas excéder.
Comme tout système, l’ensemble détecte la vitesse maximale autorisée, mais laisse le choix au conducteur de fixer sa propre allure. Si la chose est là encore commune aux autres véhicules, cela pose réellement problème lorsque la voiture est équipée du FSD autorisant une autonomie quasi complète. L’ordinateur de bord a en effet une plus grande emprise sur les commandes, et nombre de propriétaires pourraient donc le pousser à la faute.
Du FSD au TAS : une mise à jour en apparence purement cosmétique
C’est d’autant plus vrai que le FSD peut dépasser jusqu’à 50 % la limite de vitesse détectée si on le souhaite ! Le véhicule peut ainsi en théorie filer à 135 km/h sur une nationale limitée à 90 km/h. Rejeter la responsabilité d’un excès de vitesse sur le constructeur est alors très tentant pour éviter la sanction. Sauf que l’esquive est désormais impossible avec la dernière version du système.
Ce n’est pourtant pas ce que suggère la mise à jour 2026.39.100, qui renomme au passage le FSD (Full Self Driving) en TAS (Tesla Assisted Driving). Le petit texte d’information concernant cette mise à jour précise que « cette modification concerne uniquement le nom de certaines fonctionnalités et certains textes dans votre véhicule, sans en altérer le fonctionnement ». Hormis les réglages d’ordre sémantique, rien ne bouge, vraiment ?
Une marge d’excès de vitesse sabrée à 10 % en toute discrétion
Certains utilisateurs ont tout de même signalé une nette réduction de la vitesse pouvant être excédée par le véhicule. On passerait d’un dépassement de 50 % à seulement 10 %. Pour reprendre l’exemple précédent, le FSD ne pourrait faire rouler la voiture qu’à 99 km/h sur une route limitée à 90 km/h. Et à chaque redémarrage, la marge de dépassement de la vitesse maximale serait réinitialisée à 0 %.
Pourquoi de telles modifications, au-delà d’évidentes raisons de sécurité ? Le but est surtout de répondre aux demandes souhaitées par plusieurs pays de l’Union Européenne, dont l’Allemagne, qui voulait un dépassement de la vitesse autorisée allant à 10 % au maximum. Le pays soutiendra donc le système lors du prochain vote d’approbation à l’échelle de l’Union Européenne. De quoi inciter la France à faire de même ?

articles.title: Jordanian fintech invoiceQ raises $5 million in oversubscribed Series A
articles.text:
Jordanian fintech invoiceQ raises $5 million in oversubscribed Series A
- Jordan-based e-invoicing and tax compliance startup invoiceQ has raised $5 million in an oversubscribed Series A round, led by Manara Ventures and Next Ventures, with participation from Orange Ventures, the Innovative Startups and SMEs Fund (ISSF), and the Jordan Small and Medium Enterprises Fund (SME Fund Jo).
- Founded in 2020 by Mohannad Tobal, Mohammad Bassit, Fadi Al Jabali and Amer Ayyad, invoiceQ provides a SaaS platform that enables businesses to automate, manage, exchange and archive tax-compliant electronic invoices, integrating with existing ERP, POS, accounting, e-commerce, banking and payment systems.
- Headquartered in Amman, Jordan, invoiceQ serves more than 1,400 businesses and operates across Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Oman, Qatar, Egypt, Bahrain and Morocco, in addition to its home market. The company holds regulatory qualifications and accreditations in several markets, including Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Oman.
- The funding will support invoiceQ's next phase of growth as it expands its regional presence and develops its e-invoicing and tax compliance services. The investment also marks SME Fund Jo's second investment in the company.
Press release:
invoiceQ, Inc., a regional e-invoicing and tax compliance technology company, has closed a Series A round that raised $5 million, exceeding the target. The round was led by Manara Ventures and Next Ventures, with participation from Orange Ventures, the Innovative Startups and SMEs Fund (ISSF), and the Jordan Small and Medium Enterprises Fund (SME Fund Jo).
Founded by Mohannad Tobal, Mohammad Bassit, Fadi Al Jabali, and Amer Ayyad, invoiceQ provides a SaaS-based e-invoicing and compliance platform that enables businesses to automate, manage, exchange, and archive tax-compliant invoices through a centralized solution.
From its Jordanian base, invoiceQ has expanded across the region, with operations spanning Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Oman, Qatar, Egypt, Bahrain, and Morocco. Today, invoiceQ helps businesses navigate evolving e-invoicing regulations and maintain compliance across multiple markets. Through seamless integration with ERP, POS, accounting, e-commerce, banking, and payment systems, the platform enables organizations to streamline their invoicing operations and meet regulatory requirements without disrupting or replacing their existing infrastructure.
Commenting on this investment, Mohammad Al-Muhtaseb, CEO of the Innovative Startups and SMEs Fund (ISSF), said: "invoiceQ's successful closing of its Series A funding round is not only an achievement for the company itself, but also a milestone that reflects the maturity and excellence of Jordan's entrepreneurial ecosystem, and a new success story added to the track record of the business environment in the Kingdom.
This achievement underscores the growing confidence in the ability of Jordanian startups to attract quality capital and lead digital transformation. It also proves that funding and venture capital are available to support ambitious companies that possess successful business models and innovative solutions scalable regionally and globally.At the Innovative Startups and SMEs Fund, we are proud to support invoiceQ's journey, which strengthens Jordan's standing as a regional hub for innovation and technology and opens broader horizons for Jordanian entrepreneurs to turn their ideas into regional and global success stories.
Al-Muhtaseb also noted that invoiceQ's early-stage journey was supported by funds within the ISSF portfolio, such as Oasis500, Flat6Labs, and Propeller, in addition to Ahli Fintech. This highlights the pivotal role of the Innovative Startups and SMEs Fund and the importance of its strategic work in providing venture capital across various stages within Jordan's investment environment, empowering startups to grow and access markets."
Commenting on the investment, Manara Ventures said: “E-invoicing mandates are transforming how businesses operate across the region, and what stood out to us about invoiceQ is that the company is not simply responding to this shift but actively helping shape it. Seeing a Jordanian team at the forefront of building the region’s compliance infrastructure is a testament to the depth of talent and innovation coming out of Jordan. We are proud to lead this round and support invoiceQ in its next phase of growth.”
Next Ventures added: “Next Ventures invests in founders who position ahead of regulatory change. invoiceQ identified the e-invoicing opportunity early, secured the key regulatory approvals and built a strong customer base. With an exceptional management team and a scalable platform, invoiceQ is well placed to become the regional standard in e-invoicing SaaS, and we are excited to be part of what they achieve next.”
Orange Ventures commented, "invoiceQ addresses a tangible business need through its e-invoicing and compliance solutions. We are pleased to support its development and regional expansion.”
SME Fund Jo added, "The presence of promising Jordanian companies like invoiceQ, with clear visions, successful business models, and innovative, scalable solutions, reflects the strength of Jordan’s entrepreneurial ecosystem and reinforces investor confidence in the ability of local companies to compete regionally and globally.
invoiceQ’s consistent growth, expansion into new markets, and continuous innovation demonstrate the potential of Jordanian businesses to attract investment and achieve sustainable success.
These achievements motivated us to invest in invoiceQ for the second time, reaffirming our confidence in its vision and future potential. We believe that supporting successful Jordanian companies encourages continued investment and strengthens Jordan’s position as a regional hub for innovation and technology.”
invoiceQ currently serves more than 1,400 businesses across the region and has established a strong regulatory and technical footprint. The company is qualified by Saudi Arabia’s Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA), compliant with Jordan’s Income and Sales Tax Department (ISTD) regulations, accredited as an Approved Service Provider (ASP) by the UAE Federal Tax Authority (FTA) and Oman Tax Authority (OTA), and is a Peppol-certified Access Point (AP) and Service Metadata Publisher (SMP) provider.
The successful close of this Series A round marks a significant milestone in invoiceQ’s growth trajectory and further positions the company within the region’s expanding digital compliance and financial technology ecosystem.
invoiceQ would like to thank its partners and supporters, including Kassim Legal, which acted as legal counsel to invoiceQ.

articles.title: AI agents leaked confidential data in 87 of 100 test runs, Cyberhaven finds
articles.text:
AI agents leaked confidential data in 87 of 100 test runs, Cyberhaven finds
A new report out today from data security company Cyberhaven Inc. finds that artificial intelligence agents will leak confidential company data if doing so helps them get the job done, even after noting that it’s confidential.
The report from Cyberhaven Labs, the company’s research arm, is based on a test in which agents built on five different AI models were given an ordinary marketing task: Write a six-month product report for a company blog, cite the numbers and then publish it.
The user pointed the agents to a confidential board review and an internal customer spreadsheet as sources for the numbers, though no one asked for either file to be shared. The agents also had access to an approved press kit that could have been used instead. Of the 100 test runs, confidential data ended up on the public blog in 87.
The models tested included three open-weight models, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8, along with two closed models in the form of Anthropic PBC’s Claude Sonnet 5.5 and OpenAI Group PBC’s GPT-6.1 Terra.
Confidential data was found to have leaked in 57 of the 60 runs involving the open-weight models, which were also the worst offenders when it came to sharing entire documents. In 16 of those runs, a whole confidential file was made public. In all 16 cases, the agent had flagged the risk in its reasoning before going ahead and doing it anyway. Kimi K3 noted in one run that public links to the board review would expose sensitive data to anyone, calling it “a real-world judgment call” before creating the links regardless.
None of the open-weight models asked before sharing the files, and in 14 of the 16 runs, the user was only told about it after the fact. Per-customer revenue or usage data from the spreadsheet also made it onto the blog in 51 of the 60 open-weight runs, with Qwen3.8 going as far as republishing the entire 63-customer list on two occasions.
It was a different story for Anthropic and OpenAI’s models, which flagged confidentiality to the user before publishing in 38 of their 40 runs. Claude did not share a single file in any of its runs, and GPT shared files in only three, each time after first asking for the go-ahead.
The closed models did, however, publish the numbers contained in those files. Product annual recurring revenue and the exact customer count were among the figures that ended up on the blog in 30 of the 40 closed-model runs, and in 27 of those cases the files themselves never left the drive. Claude Sonnet 5.5 came out of the testing the best of the five, though it still stuck to safe material in only eight of its 20 runs.
In Cyberhaven’s words, the closed models guarded “the container, not the contents.” Any security tool keeping watch over files alone would have missed the leaks entirely.
Nor can most of the leaks be put down to the user giving the green light. The user had been scripted to tell the agents to use their own judgment if asked, but 69 of the 87 leaking runs had already leaked data before the user replied or included material the agent never asked about.
As for what companies should do about it, Cyberhaven suggests checking what an agent is doing at the moment it shares or publishes something. According to the report, a figure copied from a board review “is still board data,” so content derived from sensitive files should be tracked as well.
The study, which tested a single scenario at one fictional company with a scripted user, is still undergoing a human audit of its results.
Earlier this month, Cyberhaven launched Agentic Data Security, a product said to track data from its source through every step an agent takes with it. The company did not use the product in the study.

articles.title: UN human rights watchdog finds Bill C-22 violates human rights
articles.text:
The United Nations’ Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights has said that several elements of the federal government’s lawful access bill (Bill C-22) could violate human rights.
In an assessment of the bill, which was reported on by the Canadian Civil Liberties Association (CCLA), the human rights body noted several issues with the proposal, which include:
- The government’s ability to secretly impose surveillance-by-design mechanisms onto service providers without robust judicial authorization
- The government’s ability to obligate digital service providers to keep metadata indiscriminately on everyone, including in situations where it cannot be linked to a specific investigation or security threat.
- The government’s ability to impose surveillance-by-design obligations that break safeguards like end-to-end encryption
- The government’s need to include individual notice requirements and other safeguards into search provisions
- being able to prevent the federal government from using the surveillance powers to facilitate investigations of any activity that is not criminal here by law enforcement in other countries.
“Bill C-22’s excessive in its breadth of application and its inconsistency with global standards could threaten Canada’s ongoing attempts to integrate digitally with partners in the European Union,” writes the Canadian Civil Liberties Association.
The Canadian Civil Liberties Association also says the assessment raises questions about the government’s assertions that Bill C-22 aligns Canada with its Five Eyes intelligence partners.
Bill C-22 is currently being reviewed by the Senate Standing Committee on National Security, Defence, and Veteran Affairs (SECD).
Now, this isn’t the only organization concerned about the bill. Tech giant Apple warned about the bill’s privacy concerns and said it “will never” add the backdoors. Alongside that, Google, Meta, and Signal all expressed concerns about the bill, with Signal threatening to exit the Canadian market if it passes. Recently, Apple, Meta, and Google made a final lobbying push to rewrite Bill C-22 before it officially goes into law.

articles.title: Nuevo golpe de EEUU a China: también perseguirá los chips más básicos utilizados en televisores o teléfonos móviles
articles.text:
El Departamento de Comercio de EEUU acaba de asestar un golpe más a China. Su nueva regulación endurece los mecanismos de control sobre los circuitos integrados de 16 y 14 nm, así como sobre algunos nodos avanzados. Estas tecnologías de integración son relativamente antiguas, pero continúan siendo muy utilizadas en la fabricación de chips para electrodomésticos, teléfonos móviles y coches. Y son muy importantes para la industria china de los semiconductores.
Las nuevas normas no condicionan solo a las compañías estadounidenses; también afectan a cualquier empresa de semiconductores que utilice tecnologías y patentes desarrolladas en EEUU. Y TSMC, el mayor fabricante de circuitos integrados del planeta, lo hace, lo que lo ha llevado a paralizar una parte de sus envíos de chips a China para cerciorarse de que sus entregas satisfacen los últimos requisitos impuestos por la Administración estadounidense.
Hasta ahora la regulación de EEUU perseguía principalmente limitar la llegada a China de semiconductores avanzados, pero su estrategia a partir de ahora restringe también la venta de chips maduros. Y lo hace porque el Gobierno de EEUU sabe que estos circuitos integrados son muy importantes para China. Tanto, de hecho, que muchos fabricantes chinos de electrodomésticos, televisores, dispositivos electrónicos y coches los usan en sus productos.
No obstante, la dependencia de las empresas chinas de TSMC en este escenario es parcial. SMIC, Hua Hong Semiconductor y otros fabricantes chinos de semiconductores tienen la capacidad de producir circuitos integrados maduros, por lo que no está en juego su desaparición del mercado chino. Lo que todavía no está claro es si los fabricantes chinos de chips serán capaces de responder a toda la demanda de semiconductores maduros que reciben de sus clientes.
Los chips maduros son esenciales para la industria china. Y EEUU lo sabe
Durante los dos primeros meses de 2026 China exportó circuitos integrados por un valor de 43.300 millones de dólares, lo que representa un incremento del 72,6% frente al mismo periodo de 2025. Esta información procede directamente de los registros de las aduanas de China, por lo que presumiblemente es fiable. No obstante, lo más asombroso es que el conjunto de las exportaciones de este país creció un 21,8% durante enero y febrero, por lo que es evidente que la industria de los semiconductores fue estimulada con mucha más intensidad que otros sectores.
Durante los dos primeros meses de 2026 China exportó circuitos integrados por un valor de 43.300 millones de dólares
La demanda interna ha sostenido durante los últimos años el crecimiento de la industria china de los chips, pero las cifras que he recogido en el párrafo anterior demuestran que la demanda externa también es muy fuerte. En ese contexto es razonable que nos preguntemos de qué tipo son los circuitos integrados que están produciendo de forma masiva los fabricantes chinos.
La respuesta es muy reveladora: se trata de chips derivados de tecnologías de integración maduras, habitualmente de 28 nm o menos avanzadas. Buena parte de los fabricantes chinos de chips, como Hua Hong Semiconductor, China Resources Microelectronics o Guangzhou ZenSemi, está fabricando circuitos integrados de 28 nm o con tecnologías aún más antiguas. Y la empresa Beijing Yandong Microelectronics (YDME) va a construir una planta de 4.600 millones de dólares expresamente para producir semiconductores de 28 nm en obleas de 300 mm.
Es evidente que estas compañías no se volcarían de esta forma en la fabricación de chips maduros si no fuese una estrategia rentable, y, sobre todo, necesaria para sostener la industria china de los circuitos integrados en un momento tan crítico como el actual. EEUU es consciente de que esta capacidad de producción es uno de los pilares de la estrategia china para alcanzar la autonomía tecnológica. Este es el motivo por el que ha decidido ampliar sus restricciones a unos semiconductores que, aunque están lejos de la vanguardia tecnológica, son imprescindibles para sostener buena parte de su industria.

articles.title: Google ferme l’application Nest en janvier, voici ce qu’il faudra récupérer avant sa disparition
articles.text:
L’application Nest cessera de fonctionner le 25 janvier 2027, sur mobile comme sur le Web, pour laisser la place à Google Home. Les appareils et leur historique vidéo seront transférés, mais les clips que vous avez sauvegardés manuellement devront être récupérés avant la fermeture.
Si vous ouvrez encore Nest pour regarder vos caméras ou régler le chauffage, il va falloir changer vos habitudes. Comme on le pressentait ces derniers mois, Google a fixé la date de fermeture de l’application, après des années de cohabitation avec Google Home. 9to5Google indique que le basculement commencera dans quelques semaines seulement, plus précisément le 25 janvier prochain. Une échéance qui concerne aussi les utilisateurs restés fidèles au site home.nest.com pour surveiller leur domicile depuis un ordinateur.
Des vidéos à télécharger avant de fermer la porte
La première chose à vérifier se trouve dans votre bibliothèque de clips. Les séquences enregistrées manuellement sur le site Nest ne seront pas transférées dans Google Home. Pour les conserver, Google demande de se connecter à home.nest.com avant le 25 janvier et d’utiliser le bouton « Tout télécharger », qui permet de tout récupérer en une fois.
L’historique récent des caméras, avec les événements détectés et les enregistrements continus associés à votre abonnement, suivra en revanche les appareils vers Google Home. Vos réglages et programmations doivent également être conservés. Le transfert automatique commencera le jour de la fermeture de Nest.
Pour retrouver les commandes à distance et les notifications, il faudra installer Google Home et s’y connecter avec un compte Google. Ceux qui utilisent encore un ancien identifiant Nest devront donc le migrer. Google recommande de le faire avant le 25 janvier pour conserver l’accès aux appareils. À partir du 25 mars 2027, l’entreprise commencera à supprimer les comptes Nest restés sans migration et leurs données associées.
Google Home et Gemini prennent le relais
Google promet de continuer à prendre en charge les appareils actuellement compatibles. Thermostats, caméras, sonnettes, détecteurs et serrures doivent rejoindre son application unique. Les abonnements Nest Aware de première génération basculeront également vers Google Home Premium.
Cette fermeture achève le regroupement engagé avec la refonte de Google Home et l’arrivée de Gemini pour la maison. Pour les propriétaires de caméras, cela signifie retrouver les flux et l’historique dans Home, y compris sur ordinateur à l’adresse home.Google.com.
Le ménage concerne aussi les enceintes et écrans connectés. À partir du 2 août 2027, Google commencera à y retirer Assistant au profit de Gemini pour Home. Le passage à l’assistant de base sera gratuit, mais demandera une validation dans Google Home. Sans cette démarche, les appareils concernés finiront par cesser de répondre à Assistant et inviteront leur propriétaire à effectuer la migration.
C’est donc une page de plus qui se tourne pour Nest. Cofondé par Tony Fadell, ancien dirigeant d’Apple ayant supervisé la création de l’iPod, et Matt Rogers, le constructeur avait été racheté par Google en 2014. Le nom reste présent sur les objets connectés pour la maison, à l’image de Fitbit pour les appareils de santé. Mais pour les piloter, c’est désormais à la porte de Google Home qu’il faudra frapper.

articles.title: Milchstraße mit 5,4 Billionen Teilchen simuliert – wie KI ein altes Rechenproblem löst
articles.text:
5,4 Billionen Teilchen: Wie KI die Milchstraße auf drei Supercomputern nachbildet
Forscher:innen um das Institut Riken im japanischen Wako und die japanische Universität Tokio haben die Milchstraße nun bis auf einzelne Sterne simuliert. Das Team stellte die Studie auf der Supercomputer-Konferenz SC26 in Chicago vor und berechnete mit dem Programm Pheasant bis zu 5,4 Billionen Teilchen.
Damit liegt die Auflösung für Sterne, Gas und unsichtbare Dunkle Materie tausend- bis zehntausendmal höher als in bisherigen Modellen der gesamten Galaxie. Die Software lief dafür getrennt auf drei verschiedenen Supercomputern, benötigte neben reiner Hardwareleistung für diese Detailtiefe aber zusätzlich künstliche Intelligenz.
KI-Modell überbrückt Sternexplosionen in der Milchstraße
Ohne KI-Hilfe scheitern hochaufgelöste Galaxienmodelle an großen Maßstabsunterschieden: Die Milchstraßenscheibe misst bis zu 200.000 Lichtjahre, umgerechnet rund 1,9 Trillionen Kilometer. Während sich die Galaxie in 200 Millionen Jahren einmal dreht, verändern Sternexplosionen das umliegende Gas binnen Jahrzehnten und erzwingen kurze Zeitschritte.
Um diesen Rechenstau aufzulösen, entwickelte der Riken-Astrophysiker Keiya Hirashima ein eigenes KI-Vorhersagemodell, wie aus einer Mitteilung der Universität Tokio hervorgeht. „Mein Modell sagt die Gasverteilung nach 100.000 Jahren voraus“, erläutert Erstautor Hirashima das Prinzip hinter dem Verfahren.
Bei jeder Sternexplosion schickt das Hauptprogramm die Daten des umliegenden Gases an die KI und erhält den berechneten Zustand nach Abklingen der Druckwelle zurück. Weil dadurch viele kurze Zwischenrechnungen entfallen, rückt die Simulation der gesamten Galaxie in Zeitschritten von 2.500 statt rund 30 Jahren vor.
Das KI-Training dauerte auf einem einzelnen Grafikchip einen Tag, während die Vorhersage im Betrieb direkt auf normalen Hauptprozessoren läuft. Die Grafikchips berechnen stattdessen die weitreichende Schwerkraft zwischen allen Teilchen, wohingegen die Hauptprozessoren die lokalen Strömungen benachbarter Gaswolken übernehmen.
Supercomputer Jupiter in Jülich und US-Rechner im Vergleich
Damit die Software unabhängig vom Chiphersteller läuft, passten die Entwickler:innen den Programmcode für Hardware der kalifornischen Unternehmen Intel, AMD und Nvidia an. Erprobt wurde das System auf den US-Großrechnern Frontier und Aurora sowie auf dem Supercomputer Jupiter im nordrhein-westfälischen Jülich.
Aus Deutschland wirkten der Jülicher Informatiker Mathis Bode sowie die Entwicklerin Laura Morgenstern von Nvidia in Würselen mit. Jupiter ist laut dem Forschungszentrum Jülich Europas schnellster Supercomputer und berechnete mit knapp 21.000 Nvidia-Chips 135 Milliarden Teilchen pro Sekunde.
Aurora verarbeitete mit gut 60.000 Intel-Chips 144 Milliarden Teilchen pro Sekunde, während Frontier mit AMD-Chips und mehr Arbeitsspeicher 5,4 Billionen Teilchen berechnete. Gegenüber dem Vorläufermodell von Ende 2025 verzehnfachte sich das Tempo fast: Eine Milliarde Jahre mit 100 Milliarden Teilchen könnte Jupiter in 19 Tagen berechnen.
Abgleich mit dem James-Webb-Teleskop und Grenzen der Simulation
Mithilfe der Detaildaten wollen Astronom:innen untersuchen, wie chemische Elemente aus explodierten Sternen durch die Galaxie wandern und später neue Sterne sowie Planeten bilden. Die Berechnungen lassen sich mit Daten der Raumsonde Gaia und des James-Webb-Weltraumteleskops abgleichen, zudem ist die KI-Methode auf Klimamodelle übertragbar.
Allerdings liefert die Arbeit vorerst nur einen technischen Leistungsnachweis, denn der Spitzenlauf mit 5,4 Billionen Teilchen umfasste lediglich zehn kurze Testschritte. Überdies startet das Modell mit einer bereits geformten Galaxienscheibe und lässt physikalische Faktoren wie Magnetfelder, Strahlung, Staubbildung sowie Schwarze Löcher bislang weg.
Wie aus dem frühen Universum überhaupt erst eine Spiralgalaxie wie die Milchstraße entsteht, kann auch die aktuelle Software noch nicht abbilden. Zwar erreichte das Projekt das Finale des Gordon-Bell-Preises für Höchstleistungsrechnen, unterlag laut dem New Yorker Informatikverband ACM aber einem chinesischen Forschungsteam.
Heiße Mädchen warten auf dich — Miss4.fun

articles.title: IG Defence test-fires counter-drone micro-missile system
articles.text:
IG Defence test-fires counter-drone micro-missile system
The company's indigenously developed micro-missile system JWALA MK-I was successfully tested at Pokhran, Rajasthan.
IG Defence has successfully test-fired JWALA MK-I, an indigenously developed micro-missile system designed to counter unmanned aerial threats, at the Pokhran Test Range in Rajasthan.
The announcement was made by Bodhisattwa Sanghapriya, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of IG Defence. “India’s first indigenous Counter-UAS (CUAS) Micro-Missile System, JWALA MK-I, has been successfully test-fired by IG Defence at the Pokhran Test Range, Rajasthan,” he wrote in a LinkedIn post.
Highlighting the importance of developing domestic defence technologies, Sanghapriya said, “The future of warfare will be shaped by nations that innovate, develop and manufacture their own strategic technologies. India must not merely prepare for the future of warfare. India must build the technologies that will define it.”
The development adds a missile-based approach to India’s expanding counter-drone capabilities, an increasingly important area of defence modernisation as the use of unmanned aircraft in military operations grows.
IG Defence describes JWALA as a short-range surface-to-air missile intended for use against unmanned aerial vehicles, with a claimed engagement range of 2-5 km. It represents a hard-kill approach, in which an incoming drone is physically destroyed. Soft-kill systems, by contrast, use techniques such as electronic jamming or signal spoofing to disrupt a drone’s control or navigation signals.
India already has several counter-drone programmes employing different technologies. Bharat Electronics Limited, in collaboration with the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), has developed the D4 Counter Drone System, which combines drone detection and tracking with soft- and hard-kill capabilities, according to the Department of Defence Production.
Private-sector participation is also growing in this space. Adani Defence and DRDO unveiled a vehicle-mounted counter-drone system at Aero India 2025, integrating radar, electronic jamming and a laser-based weapon.
In July 2026, Zen Technologies announced a man-portable anti-drone system designed for high-altitude operations, using radio-frequency detection and jamming.

Revopoint Launches MIRACO 2 on Kickstarter: Scan in One, Create with Agents
An all-in-one 3D scanner combining high-precision capture, powerful onboard computing, and AI-driven workflows—with Super Early Bird pricing starting at $1,425.

Back MIRACO 2 on KickstarterTruly Standalone Design with Powerful Onboard ComputingWeighing just 960 g, MIRACO 2 integrates depth computation, 3D scanning, point cloud processing, and basic editing into one portable device.
Powered by an 8-core CPU and 6-core NPU, it supports three operating modes:
- Standalone Mode: Scan, preview, process, and make adjustments directly on its 6-inch 2K AMOLED touchscreen.
- Wireless PC Mode: Connect to a computer via Wi-Fi 6 for a flexible scanning workflow.
- Wired PC Mode: Connect via USB-C 3.0 for a stable, high-performance workflow.
When connected to a GPU-powered PC, Multi-Line Laser scanning can reach speeds of up to 120 FPS.
High Precision Meets Versatile Scanning Capabilities
MIRACO 2 delivers single-frame accuracy of up to 0.02 mm in Multi-Line Laser Mode and offers six scanning modes to handle a wide range of objects and applications:

With a maximum capture rate of 10 million points per second in Hybrid HD mode, MIRACO 2 can handle challenging surfaces and geometries, including reflective metals, black objects, intricate structures, and human bodies.
Additional capabilities include:

Revo Agents: An AI-Native Ecosystem for 3D Workflows
Capturing an object is only the beginning. Turning scan data into CAD models or inspection results often means navigating complex software and hours of manual processing.

You define the task. Revo Agents helps execute it.
Full-Color Capture and Physically Scaled 3DGS

AI-powered cleanup tools further simplify model preparation:
- AI Segmentation: Automatically identifies and removes unwanted environmental point clouds.

Together with Revopoint's software ecosystem, these capabilities support an integrated Scan-to-CAD workflow, helping users move from physical objects to usable digital models.
Built for Indoor and Outdoor Work
Designed for both indoor and outdoor applications, it supports ambient lighting conditions of up to 100,000 lux. Its 10,000 mAh battery provides approximately three hours of runtime, with 65 W fast charging.
Two configurations are available:

articles.title: Google va supprimer l’application Nest : voici ce que vous devez absolument faire avant janvier 2027
articles.text:
Google a annoncé la fermeture de l’application Nest pour le 25 janvier 2027. Les clients Nest passeront ainsi sur l’application Google Home. Cette transition sera en bonne partie automatique, mais ceux qui disposent d’un compte Nest doivent tout de même effectuer quelques manœuvres pour pouvoir continuer à profiter de tous les services. Voici ce qu’il faut savoir.
Google va mettre un terme à l’application Nest
C’est officiel, l’application Nest fermera ses portes le 25 janvier 2027. À partir de cette date, l’application ne sera plus disponible sur Android et iOS, sur les téléviseurs ou encore sur le web. Tous les appareils de la marque passeront dans l’application Google Home. L’objectif de Google est bien entendu d’unifier ses services domotiques au sein d’une même application. L’entreprise américaine précise par ailleurs que cette manœuvre permettra de mieux intégrer les nouvelles fonctionnalités de Gemini et d’offrir une meilleure sécurité (l’application Nest a été créée il y a plus de 15 ans). Notons également que Google Assistant cessera de fonctionner sur les appareils Nest pour laisser sa place à Gemini dès le 2 août 2027.
Deux points sont à retenir particulièrement. Le premier : la fermeture de l’application Nest ne signifie absolument pas que les appareils de la marque cesseront de fonctionner. Ceux-ci resteront totalement opérationnels. En revanche, les personnes qui n’auront pas effectué la migration de leur compte vers l’application Google Home ne recevront plus de notifications et ne pourront plus contrôler leurs appareils à distance. Le second point à retenir : Google commencera à supprimer les données des comptes qui n’ont pas été migrés vers l’application Google Home, à partir du 25 janvier 2027. Mais, concrètement, quelles sont les mesures à prendre ?
Que faire si vous disposez d’un compte Nest ?
Tout d’abord, les personnes qui disposent d’un appareil Nest doivent migrer leur compte Nest vers l’application Google Home, avant le 25 janvier 2027. Pour ce faire, il suffit de se rendre dans les paramètres de l’application Nest où un bouton « Migrer vers un compte Google » devrait être disponible.
Ensuite, Google précise que les clips vidéo qui ont été enregistrés manuellement ne seront pas transférés automatiquement. Il faut donc se rendre sur home.nest.com et cliquer sur le bouton « Tout télécharger », avant le 25 janvier 2027. En revanche, l’entreprise américaine précise que « vos appareils Nest, y compris les caméras et l’historique vidéo, seront automatiquement transférés de l’application Nest vers l’application Google Home ».
Enfin, une question se pose : est-ce que tout cela aura un impact tarifaire pour les clients des appareils Nest ? Selon Google, la réponse est non. Ceux qui disposent d’un abonnement Nest Aware (première génération) passeront automatiquement à la formule Google Home Premium Advanced à partir du 25 janvier 2027, sans surcoût ou modification de tarif.

The Gentlemen adds Nvidia to its data leak site
- Ransomware group The Gentlemen claims to have breached Nvidia, and is threatening to leak stolen data unless paid
- Nvidia says it has found no evidence that its systems or networks were compromised and continues investigating
- The incident highlights growing extortion tactics where threat actors publicize alleged breaches before providing proof of data theft
Nvidia has confirmed it is investigating claims of a data breach after a prolific ransomware operator added the company’s name to its data leak website.
On November 18, 2026, threat actors going under “The Gentlemen” added Nvidia to their website, as per International Cyber Digest. They didn’t share any details - we don’t know the nature of the stolen files, or the size of the allegedly exfiltrated archive.
The group only said “DATA INFO - SOON” on the website entry and shared a clock that counts down to November 28 2026 - most likely the date when they plan on leaking everything (unless Nvidia decides to pay the ransom demand in the meantime).
"No indication of a breach"
Cybersecurity professionals and law enforcement generally advise companies not to pay the ransom. There is no guarantee the criminals won’t leak the data anyway, and there is even less guarantee they won’t attack the company again in a few weeks’ or months’ time. Also, in case the data is encrypted, there is no telling if the decryptor works properly, so the company could end up paying and still losing everything.
Instead, they advise organizations to keep an updated backup archive of all crucial information, and to tighten up on security to make sure they don’t get breached. That includes educating the employees on the dangers of phishing, as well as keeping all hardware and software updated with the latest patches and upgrades.
When asked about the claims made by the threat actors, the AI giant told The Register it was looking into it: “We have found no indication that Nvidia systems or networks were affected,” a spokesperson said. “We continue to monitor the situation."
Since the group did not post a sample on its leak site, it is impossible to determine whether the claims are real or not. However, The Gentlemen is a rather prolific threat actor with a history of successful breaches. It first emerged during 2025 and has, since then, made a name for itself by targeting organizations across multiple sectors including healthcare, manufacturing, education, and finance. Notable victims include Puerto Rico’s Caribbean Medical Center, which reported a data breach affecting some 92,000 people. In April this year, the group struck US manufacturer Gator Cases, in which it exposed sensitive data on 1,171 individuals.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The Gentlemen run a ransom-as-a-service (RaaS) operation and offer its affiliates 90% of ransom payments, some sources said. According to Microsoft, its encryptor is built in Go and, besides the traditional encryption features, also allows the actors to move laterally and quickly spread throughout the target network. In its writeup, The Register says its affiliates claimed more than 320 victims as of April, with the majority of these alleged infections (240) taking place in the first half of 2026.
Nvidia's been hacked before
Pointing to a Check Point research, the publication argues that the actual count is likely much higher, since the researchers found an affiliate’s live C2 server while responding to an incident earlier this year. On the server they found telemetry for more than 1,570 victims, most of which were US-based organizations.
Nvidia, best known for manufacturing graphics cards, became insanely popular with the emergence of AI and AI data centers (all of which need Nvidia’s hardware to run). These days it is one of the most valuable companies on the planet but even before the proliferation of AI it was a popular target for cybercriminals. Back in 2022, for example, it suffered an attack in which threat actors made away with a terabyte of sensitive data.
The company was struck by LAPSUS$ which, at the time, was one of the largest and most dangerous hacking collectives in existence.
