articles.title: University of Queensland: Wie ein alter Aufzug erstmals Daten per Schwerkraft sendet
articles.text:
Datenversand per Schwerkraft: Physiker schicken Textnachricht durch eine Ziegelwand
Fünf Physiker der University of Queensland im australischen Brisbane haben erstmals eine digitale Botschaft allein über Schwankungen der Anziehungskraft gesendet. Sie übertrugen das englische Wort „Gravity“ durch eine 27 Zentimeter dicke Mauer, wie ihre Studie im Wissenschaftsmagazin Science Advances beschreibt.
University of Queensland nutzt alten Aufzug als Sender
Als Signalgeber diente ein Aufzug aus den 1950er-Jahren, dessen rund 1,8 Tonnen schweres Gegengewicht aus Gusseisen zwischen zwei Etagen fuhr. Im benachbarten Waschraum stand auf dem Boden ein sogenanntes Gravimeter, also ein empfindliches Messgerät für winzige Veränderungen der örtlichen Schwerkraft.
Während Metallkäfige, Erdreich oder dickes Mauerwerk Funkwellen, Licht und Schall abhalten, kann kein bekanntes Material die Anziehungskraft von Masse blockieren. „Ein Gravitationssignal lässt sich nicht einfach abschirmen, indem man gewöhnliches Material in seinen Weg stellt“, erklärt Mitautor Charles Woffinden in einer Hochschulmitteilung.
Mit kosmischen Gravitationswellen, die erst bei schweren Himmelskörpern wie Schwarzen Löchern messbar durch das All laufen, arbeitet das System jedoch nicht. Stattdessen zog das bewegte Gegengewicht im Schacht lediglich eine kleine Testmasse an einer Feder im Messgerät je nach Etage unterschiedlich stark an.
Ein einzelnes Wort benötigt über eine Stunde Sendezeit
Für den Binärcode bedeutete die untere Position des Gegengewichts rund 70 Zentimeter neben dem Sensor eine Null und die obere Position eine Eins. Jeder Buchstabe von „Gravity“, englisch für Schwerkraft, erforderte sieben Bits, was samt kurzen Start- und Endfolgen 63 Bits in 63 Minuten ergab.
Pro Bit entfielen 25 Sekunden auf die Aufzugfahrt über 5,4 Meter Höhe, zehn Sekunden Wartezeit sowie 25 Sekunden auf die eigentliche Messung. Zwischen beiden Positionen änderte sich die Anziehung nur um 50 Nanometer pro Sekunde zum Quadrat, also um fünf Milliardstel der normalen Erdanziehung.
Aus den Rohdaten rechnete das Team die langsame Dehnung der Messfeder sowie die Gezeitenkräfte von Mond und Sonne heraus. Kontrolltests schlossen Einflüsse von Magnetfeldern aus, und die rechnerische Fehlerquote erreichte mit einem Fehler pro Milliarde Bits das Niveau von Glasfaserkabeln.
Von der Fahrzeugwaage für Lastwagen zu neuen Quantensensoren
Seinen Ursprung hatte der Versuch in einem Verkehrsprojekt, bei dem Erstautor Andrew Groszek schwere Lastwagen berührungslos allein über ihre Anziehungskraft wiegen wollte. Nachdem dieses Messprinzip funktioniert hatte, übertrugen Groszek und seine vier Kollegen denselben physikalischen Ansatz auf das Senden digitaler Nachrichten.
Ein schnellerer Aufzug mit fünf Sekunden Fahrzeit und aktuellere Sensoren könnten die Rate rechnerisch auf rund 15 Bit pro Minute steigern. Für größere Reichweiten messen Quantensensoren ohne mechanische Feder, wie schnell abgekühlte Atome bei fast minus 273 Grad Celsius im Vakuum fallen.
Selbst für eine Überbrückung von 500 Metern müssten Anwender:innen in den Modellen allerdings mehrere schwer umsetzbare Bedingungen gleichzeitig erfüllen. Nötig wären eine kompakte Kugel mit 75 Tonnen Gewicht wie bei einem Kampfpanzer sowie deutliche Abstriche beim Abstand zwischen Nutzsignal und Hintergrundrauschen.
Physikalische Grenzen im Vergleich zu Funk und Voyager 1
Bei doppelter Distanz schrumpft das nutzbare Schwerkraftsignal bereits auf ein Achtel und verliert damit weit schneller an Stärke als Funkwellen. Selbst die über zehn Milliarden Kilometer entfernte Raumsonde Voyager 1 empfängt Funkbefehle mit 960 Bit pro Minute mehr als sechzigmal schneller.
Zudem bleibt der Empfang anfällig für Störungen, weil schon Bodenvibrationen oder nahe Fahrzeuge das schwache Nutzsignal überlagern können. Angreifer:innen könnten die Verbindung außerdem gezielt stören oder verfälschen, indem sie in der Nähe eigene schwere Massen bewegen.
Denkbare Einsätze in versiegelten Schutzbunkern oder abgeschirmten Sicherheitsräumen bleiben daher eng begrenzt, weil sich tonnenschwere Massen weder schnell noch unbemerkt verschieben lassen. Im Alltag nützt solche Schwerkraft-Sensorik eher Ingenieur:innen, etwa bei der Erdbeben-Frühwarnung, beim Orten von Unterwasserobjekten oder beim Wiegen schwerer Fahrzeuge.
~ Heiße Mädchen warten auf dich — Miss4.fun

articles.title: Microsoft commence à tourner la page des applications 32 bits et change ses règles de compatibilité
articles.text:
Microsoft prépare un changement important pour Windows Server 2028. Les logiciels 32 bits ne pourront plus fonctionner par défaut sur le système. Une décision motivée par la sécurité, qui rompt avec des décennies de rétrocompatibilité considérée comme acquise.
Faire fonctionner un logiciel vieux de vingt ans sur un PC récent ? Windows en est toujours capable, même lorsque le programme a été conçu pour une architecture 32 bits, bien que le système d'exploitation n'existe plus qu'en version 64 bits. Une souplesse dont bénéficient aussi les entreprises sur leurs serveurs, mais que Microsoft a décidé de revoir, comme elle l'a annoncé lors de sa conférence Ignite 2026.
Protégez votre entreprise gratuitement pendant 30 jours
Découvrez Bitdefender Ultimate Small Business Security et protégez votre activité contre les cybermenaces. Aucune coordonnée bancaire requise.
Un choix désormais laissé à l’appréciation des entreprises
Pour assurer cette compatibilité, Windows s'appuie sur WoW64 (Windows 32-bit on Windows 64-bit), un sous-système qui permet aux applications 32 bits de fonctionner dans un environnement 64 bits. Il se charge des adaptations nécessaires à leur exécution, en redirigeant par exemple certains accès aux fichiers système et au registre Windows. Jusqu'à présent, Windows Server l'intégrait par défaut, ce qui permettait aux entreprises de continuer à utiliser leurs anciens logiciels métier sans configuration supplémentaire.
Mais avec Windows Server 2028, Microsoft a décidé de changer la donne. Comme l'a expliqué Elden Christensen, membre de l'équipe Windows Server, lors d'Ignite 2026, dans des propos rapportés par Windows Central, WoW64 deviendra une fonctionnalité facultative (Feature on Demand), que les administrateurs pourront installer en cas de besoin.
Les entreprises qui dépendent encore de logiciels 32 bits ne seront donc pas contraintes de les abandonner, mais elles devront s'assurer que WoW64 est bien installé sur leurs serveurs. Un changement de politique de rétrocompatibilité qui nécessitera d'identifier les applications concernées avant de migrer vers Windows Server 2028, sous peine de voir des programmes jusque-là compatibles refuser de démarrer.
La sécurité prend le pas sur la rétrocompatibilité
Microsoft cherche ainsi à réduire la surface d'attaque de Windows Server en limitant les composants installés par défaut. Sans WoW64, les logiciels malveillants conçus exclusivement pour le 32 bits ne pourront plus s'exécuter directement sur les serveurs concernés.
Une décision qui s'inscrit aussi dans une volonté de simplifier la maintenance de Windows, alors que les outils d'analyse fondés sur l'IA accélèrent la découverte de vulnérabilités. Lors de l'Ignite, l'entreprise a ainsi reconnu que plusieurs composants historiques de Windows reposaient sur des technologies trop anciennes pour être sécurisées sans une réécriture complète. Plutôt que de s'acharner à les maintenir, elle préfère désormais se débarrasser des fonctionnalités dont ses serveurs peuvent se passer.
Cette révision des composants historiques ne concerne pas uniquement WoW64. Microsoft prévoit également de supprimer SMBv1 et VBScript de Windows Server 2028, tout en adoptant des configurations plus restrictives dès l'installation, en commençant par Server Core. Redmond inverse ainsi la logique longtemps privilégiée sur ses serveurs : plutôt que de miser sur une compatibilité maximale et de laisser les administrateurs faire le tri dans les fonctions inutiles, elle entend désormais fournir des systèmes plus sécurisés dès leur installation.
À noter, enfin, que Windows 11 n'est pas concerné par cette évolution. WoW64 y est toujours intégré et les applications 32 bits continuent de fonctionner. Microsoft n'a annoncé aucune mesure équivalente pour les PC, même si les deux systèmes partagent une partie de leur architecture.

articles.title: States sue SpaceX to stop Grok from generating child sex images, revenge porn
articles.text:
On Monday, Virginia and Oregon became the first states to sue SpaceX, alleging that Grok continues to sexualize, unchecked, real photos of mostly women and children.
SpaceX acquired xAI in February and now must handle the ongoing reckoning over the controversial rollout of Grok’s “spicy mode”—a model feature Musk hyped but was soon found to generate a flood of non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) and child sex abuse images (CSAM).
Initial safeguards were so lax that Grok sometimes generated nude images without being asked. Although X Safety and xAI (now known as SpaceXSI) were silent at first, Musk’s companies eventually apologized and claimed that additional safeguards were implemented and policies redesigned to block harmful outputs. However, state attorneys general alleged that those statements were “misleading” and that SpaceXSI instead quietly “embraced” sexualized content to seize more AI market share, as Grok continues to generate NCII and CSAM today.
Without intervention, kids in Virginia and Oregon risk a lifetime of distress, as Grok images will likely be impossible to remove online.
“Once created and shared,” Grok-generated CSAM and NCII “can never be fully erased, and it becomes a permanent record of the child’s abuse that may resurface for the rest of the child’s life,” Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones’ complaint said. “Virginia has a profound interest in protecting its children from this harm.”
Millions allegedly harmed
Millions of residents were allegedly harmed, as the attorneys general seek to protect every Grok or X user in their state. Many Grok victims will likely suffer from chronic anxiety, depression, and PTSD, as well as reputational harm, as some viewers may not realize the images are AI-generated, the states alleged. Further—due to Grok’s integration with the social media platform X—users as young as 13 may have been exposed to the AI content and possibly re-traumatized if they, too, are victims of sexual abuse, the states alleged.
“xAI not only knowingly endangered kids and our communities, but they also lied to our faces about non-existent safety measures,” Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield said in a press release.
States alleged that xAI could have conducted rigorous red-teaming to block outputs before the new feature launched. But instead, the X Safety team responsible for Grok red-teaming was reduced to two or three team members, states alleged.
Overall, rather than use industry-standard safeguards, Musk’s firms allegedly put profits over women’s and children’s safety, states alleged, while complaining that SpaceXSI won’t even publicly identify “the officers responsible for safety governance.”
“Industry standard requires not only building guardrails but also vigilantly monitoring whether they hold,” states alleged. SpaceXSI is doing neither effectively, states alleged.
SpaceX responds
Asked for comment, SpaceXSI shared an X Safety post on X, which repeated claims that the company has a “zero-tolerance” policy for “any forms of child sexual exploitation.” X Safety said that the company “acted promptly to tighten” Grok protections, which are supposedly “designed to refuse any request to generate explicit images of minors or real people.” That statement also claimed that X Safety continually tests and adjusts protections when bad actors find ways to avoid filters, while relying on “sophisticated classifiers that screen every prompt” to catch harmful outputs “before an image is generated and check every output after.” Although the statement did not mention whether xAI sues users who break Grok rules to generate CSAM and NCII, it emphasized that xAI reports harmful content generated to police.
“When someone tries to break our safeguards and generate this content, we take appropriate measures, including actioning accounts and notifying law enforcement,” X Safety said. “Attempting to create this material is a serious crime, and the individuals who do it should be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. We will continue to work with the authorities via all available means to pursue these bad actors.”
However, state attorneys general alleged that reports from independent researchers and news outlets this year have shown that Grok is still generating NCII and CSAM. They noted that the chatbot “even advises users how to circumvent its own limited moderation measures to generate those images.” In some cases, a Virginia state probe found that Grok complied “with a user request to draft a prompt designed to avoid moderation.” So, even when filters work, the chatbot helps determined users immediately get around them, states alleged.
Nothing xAI did put a dent in the harmful outputs, least of all putting the feature behind a paywall, states alleged, which only ensured maximum profits. A troubled New York City Council speaker, Julie Menin, confronted SpaceX this October with proof that attempts to digitally undress her own photo still worked for free Grok users, states alleged.
Concluding its probe, Virginia found that moderation remains “inconsistent and ineffective,” with Grok sometimes carrying out prompts “that it later blocked.”
In its complaint, Virginia alleged that Grok protections “were weak, ineffective, sparsely enforced, and easily circumvented.” Oregon agreed that rather than act to protect users, SpaceX entities repeatedly made statements “with the intent to deceive consumers” that Grok was safe. Most egregiously to state attorneys general, in January, Elon Musk denied any harm to real people, claiming that Grok is only “supposed [to] allow upper body nudity of imaginary adult humans (not real ones) and only generated nudity of fake people (not real ones).”
“Contrary to Musk’s representation,” Grok “makes the same sexualizing edits to photographs of real, identifiable people,” states warned. “Defendants intentionally released a product that inundated their platforms with CSAM, NCII, and non-consensual sexualized images,” they alleged, and other “contemporaneous statements by Musk make clear that Grok’s ability to create sexualized material was part of xAI’s business strategy.”
Grok CSAM, NCII may trigger steep fines
It’s also troubling to states that the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) reported to Congress that more than 90 percent of the Grok-generated CSAM that xAI submitted to its CyberTipline was considered a “dead end.”
As NCMEC explained, xAI initially refused to provide NCMEC and police with “basic user information, including location information, that law enforcement needs to act.” To fix the problem, NCMEC had to set up a meeting with xAI and get the reports resubmitted. This, states alleged, confirmed that “the information existed and that xAI had not provided it.” The concerning omission allegedly slowed down police response, just as the average number of Grok CSAM reports jumped by 88 percent from December 2025 to January 2026, then increased by another 66 percent from January to June 2026.
“X users were subjected to the risk that any person, at any time, could use their likeness to create CSAM, NCII, or other non-consensual sexualized images,” states alleged.
Lawmakers have asked state courts for an injunction blocking SpaceX entities from violating consumer protection laws by allegedly operating Grok without industry standard safeguards. If they win, they want SpaceX to pay thousands in civil penalties per violation, as well as disgorge any ill-gotten gains from marketing the chatbot as safe to users.
“Most people who use social media do not want to contribute to the harm caused to victims of CSAM, NCII, and other non-consensual sexualized images by being exposed to those images online,” states alleged.
Although Oregon’s complaint only vaguely estimates the number of users Grok attracted with Musk’s allegedly deceitful marketing strategy as at least “hundreds of thousands,” Virginia’s complaint included more detailed estimates. It said that approximately 6.4 million X accounts were linked to geolocations in the state, while the Grok application was downloaded 986,624 times by users with Virginia-based IP addresses.
“When xAI allowed Grok’s creators to sideline consent to turn a profit, they prioritized growth and engagement over safety, and they deceived the public about it,” Jones said. “Today’s filings are the first step towards holding this company accountable.”
Ashley is a senior policy reporter for Ars Technica, dedicated to tracking social impacts of emerging policies and new technologies. She is a Chicago-based journalist with 20 years of experience.

articles.title: Innovaccer expands Gravity Voice AI agents with SpaceXSI's Grok Voice model
articles.text:
Innovaccer expands Gravity Voice AI agents with SpaceXSI’s Grok Voice model
Healthcare artificial intelligence company Innovaccer Inc. today announced that it has expanded its Gravity Voice AI agents with Grok Voice, the speech-to-speech model from Elon Musk’s artificial intelligence company SpaceXSI, formerly xAI.
The integration is aimed at the routine calls that make up much of a health system’s phone traffic, such as booking a visit, refilling a prescription or asking about a bill.
Grok Voice is a speech-to-speech model from SpaceXSI that is said to offer subsecond time to first audio, native tool use and the ability to reason while it speaks. According to Innovaccer, the model was trained on real phone audio with interruptions, corrections and background noise in it. More than 25 languages are supported. A business associate agreement is available for Grok Voice, which is Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act-eligible.
Coming into the expansion, Innovaccer’s voice business has grown quickly. Patient voice interactions on the platform have gone from roughly 250,000 to more than five million in the six months since the agents went live. Customers using them are said to be booking significantly more appointments, with referral intakes tripled and documentation time per case down 90%.
“Healthcare Voice AI is moving from answering questions to doing work,” co-founder and Chief Executive Abhinav Shashank said. With Grok Voice, he said, the company is extending where its agents work across the healthcare journey.
Innovaccer’s Agents of Care on Gravity approach is designed so that software handles the bulk of administrative calls, such as scheduling and refills. A human stays in the loop on clinical conversations.
Existing customers will get Grok Voice first through upgrades, along with new customer deployments. Innovaccer plans to use it in scheduling, referrals, prior authorizations, refill requests, chronic care check-ins and annual wellness visit outreach, among other tasks.
The integration is set to extend beyond voice over time. Innovaccer says it will bring Grok models to its healthcare data through the Grok API, with plans for SpaceXSI’s Grok Build coding agent and Grok Bot AI agent as well. Healthcare-specific training and evaluation are to follow once the voice integration is live.
The integration comes about six weeks after SpaceXSI released Grok Voice 3.0, the latest version of the model. At the time, SpaceXSI said Starlink uses Grok Voice to answer about 20,000 customer calls a day, with roughly 70% resolved without a human. The SpaceXSI name was adopted earlier in October, following SpaceX’s acquisition of xAI in February and a rename to SpaceXAI in July.
Innovaccer is a venture capital-backed company that has raised about $675 million to date, including a $275 million Series F round in January 2025. Notable customers include Orlando Health, Adventist HealthCare and Banner Health.
Gravity Voice AI agents with Grok Voice capabilities are available now.

articles.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes
articles.text:
Anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship. On Monday, the newly public AI company announced the launch of Claude Ship, a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes.
The latter is the more interesting part of this new set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now. What’s notable about Claude Ship is not just that it can review proposed code changes and identify and address problems, but that it also includes an agent that can approve code changes automatically based on policies set by a development team.
The launch arrives at a time when AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving the code changes before they go live. With Claude Ship, the idea is to automate even more of the work involved in the development process, essentially by delegating approval authority to an AI agent itself.
“Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” a company blog post explains. “On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code, and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too.”
Claude Ship is launching in beta, allowing early adopters to use it to review pull requests (PRs), and then decide what’s ready to merge.
The new offering consists of Code Review, which is already generally available, and two new agents now in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. PR Steward focuses on addressing issues such as failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and feedback from Code Review. It also comments after every push on what it changed and how to roll it back, if needed.
Claude Approvals then applies an approval policy that the team writes as a file in the repository. This approval process can incorporate various signals, including Code Review findings or the company’s own classifiers, with policies written in natural language.
Because the offering is still in beta, Anthropic suggests running the approval functionality in observe-only mode first. Teams can also choose to start with just one repository and set monthly spending limits to have more control over the process.
Anthropic says teams will also still remain in control of where Claude Ship runs, which review settings to use (e.g., Quick, Standard, or Deep), and which changes should be escalated to a human for a decision.
Claude Ship is rolling out to Claude Team and Enterprise plans for repositories on GitHub. Code Review is generally available, while PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in beta.

articles.title: Google Canada axed Pixel protection plans, here are some alternatives
articles.text:
Google has left Canadian Pixel owners in a lurch after it ended its Preferred Care protection plan last month, with no replacement option on the horizon.
Preferred Care offered additional out-of-warranty protections for Pixel phones, but Google stopped offering it for new purchases in Canada at the beginning of October 2026. Notably, existing Preferred Care subscriptions remain active — only new customers are locked out.
The bigger issue, however, is that Google hasn’t launched a replacement, and doesn’t have plans to. In an email to MobileSyrup, a Google spokesperson said “we don’t have anything to share on Pixel Care+ or a new extended protection plan in Canada right now” and that “Canadian customers continue to be covered by our standard hardware warranty.”
Google launched the Pixel Care+ protection plan in August 2025 and said at the time it would migrate Preferred Care customers to the new plan. However, Pixel Care+ never came to Canada, and it seems like it won’t any time soon.
But while Google isn’t offering a protection plan, that doesn’t mean there’s no way to get additional protection for a Pixel phone in Canada. Many retailers and carriers offer their own protection plans, and some credit cards also offer insurance for devices.
Best Buy, for example, offers Geek Squad protection plans for phones. Bell, Telus, Rogers, and Freedom also all offer phone protection plans. And credit cards like the RBC Avion Visa Infinite, Scotia Momentum Visa Infinite, Tangerine World Mastercard, and American Express Cobalt Card offer built-in device insurance, to name a few.
Still, it sucks that Google is no longer offering Canadians its protection plan. Hopefully that changes sooner rather than later.

articles.title: Russia readying nuclear-armed satellite that could destroy every low-Earth-orbit satellite, report claims — Kremlin blasts Sputnik-S claims as ‘unfounded allegations’ and propaganda
articles.text:
Russia readying nuclear-armed satellite that could destroy every low-Earth-orbit satellite, report claims — Kremlin blasts Sputnik-S claims as ‘unfounded allegations’ and propaganda
Western intelligence agencies believe that a launch of Sputnik-S could take place before the end of the year.
Western intelligence agencies believe that Russia could be readying the launch of a nuclear-armed satellite before the end of the year. The satellite, called Sputnik-S, is believed to have been in development for the last several years, with the United States first warning of Russia's plans in February 2023. Now, a German news report believes that the country's armed forces are already "raising the alarm" about the potential impact such a satellite could have. According to one expert, such a weapon could knock out a third of low Earth orbit satellites instantly, eventually disabling all of them with a devastating impact on the planet as a whole. With satellites playing such a vital role for civilian life as well as both military and intelligence operations, it's easy to see why Russia may want such satellite-crippling capabilities.
The report notes that information about Sputnik-S has been exchanged between several NATO member countries, with intelligence agencies having already warned that a launch could happen within 60 days. That report was made in early November, suggesting that Sputnik-S could be in orbit and operational in early December. The Russian embassy in Germany rejected the "unfounded allegations," saying that they are nothing more than "part of a propaganda campaign" against the country.
Perhaps worryingly, the United States Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) published its own report in which it warned that "Russia is developing a satellite designed to carry a nuclear weapon." Such a move would be a violation of the 1967 Outer Space Treaty. The treaty prohibits any country from launching anything carrying nuclear weapons or, indeed, any weapon of mass destruction into Earth orbit. While there has been no suggestion that Russia could turn the nuclear weapons towards the planet, Sputnik-S would still clearly be in breach of the longstanding treaty. One expert cited by the report says that a nuclear explosion in space would knock out one-third of low Earth orbit satellites instantly, with the remaining satellites gradually failing in the following months. The EMP generated could even cause widespread technical carnage on Earth.
As for which satellites could be a potential target for Sputnik-S, there is no shortage of options. SpaceX Starlink satellites are relied upon around the globe for their ability to provide fast, reliable networking to parts of the world not served by traditional connectivity options. Notably, Starlink has been used by Ukraine as it defends itself amid Russian aggression. But amid SpaceX's limiting of performance, Ukrainian officials have chosen to use their own "flying modems" to avoid relying on Elon Musk's company. Russia has been trying to launch its own Starlink rival, with limited success. September saw it lose a batch of 16 satellites during launch.

articles.title: El regreso de Jensen Huang es una victoria para los accionistas, aunque también abre un precedente peligroso
articles.text:
Lo vaticinamos esta misma mañana, apenas unas horas antes de que se conociese el regreso de Jensen Huang al liderazgo de Nvidia: iba a ser casi imposible llenar el vacío que este ejecutivo había dejado en la compañía. Huang estaba involucrado en la mayor parte de los procesos de Nvidia. En las grandes decisiones, y también en los proyectos de corto alcance que a menudo pasan desapercibidos para los directores generales de las grandes compañías de tecnología.
Con toda probabilidad todo va a volver a ser como antes. Los 11 días que ha estado fuera de la dirección ejecutiva de la compañía que cofundó no bastan para cambiar nada. De hecho, si el consejo de administración ha decidido volver a apostar por él es debido a que ha recuperado la confianza tanto en él como en su capacidad de gestión. Durante los últimos años unos 60 altos cargos de Nvidia rendían cuentas directamente ante él, y no hay ningún indicio que nos invite a pensar que esto va a cambiar.
Sea como sea, su regreso no se entiende sin observar la presión que ha tenido que soportar Nvidia desde su salida de la compañía, el pasado 12 de noviembre. Su cotización llegó a caer un 27,7% entre el cierre del 11 de noviembre y el del 20 de noviembre, pasando de 173,73 a 125,53 dólares por acción. No obstante, esto no es todo. Pocos días después de su dimisión nació una campaña pública que exigía su reincorporación. Más de 200.000 personas la firmaron, y entre ellas se encontraban miles de empleados y accionistas de Nvidia.
La presión externa ha movilizado al consejo de administración
Elon Musk y Donald Trump expresaron públicamente su apoyo a Jensen Huang y la necesidad de que regresase a Nvidia. No obstante, según Reuters, los inversores han ejercido un papel determinante en su vuelta debido a que consideran que esta compañía no puede permitirse prescindir de su cofundador y líder en un momento tan delicado para la industria de la inteligencia artificial (IA). Y el mercado ha reaccionado inmediatamente al que sin duda es el acontecimiento del día. Y, posiblemente, de la semana.
Las acciones de Nvidia han subido hasta un 30% en la sesión de hoy, recuperando así buena parte del terreno perdido durante los días de incertidumbre. Este comportamiento expresa hasta qué punto es crucial para los inversores el rol del fundador como un activo fundamental, y también como eje del liderazgo de Nvidia en la carrera de la IA. Sin embargo, este giro también nos invita a hacer otra lectura en el ámbito del liderazgo empresarial que va mucho más allá de Nvidia.
Lo que acaba de suceder con Jensen Huang demuestra que la presión de los accionistas y el miedo a perder valor pueden degradar la supervisión del consejo de administración
Los consejos de administración de las empresas son los responsables de supervisar a sus directivos, defender los intereses de las compañías e investigar posibles incumplimientos de la regulación. Sus decisiones no deben estar ligadas solo a la cotización a corto plazo de la organización cuyos intereses defienden. Lo que acaba de suceder con Jensen Huang demuestra que la presión de los accionistas y el miedo a perder valor pueden degradar la supervisión del consejo de administración.
En este escenario tiene todo el sentido del mundo que nos preguntemos hasta qué punto las grandes empresas tecnológicas son capaces de mantener sus mecanismos de control cuando el directivo cuestionado es, al mismo tiempo, su principal activo. En cualquier caso, la "crisis de Huang" no ha terminado. El consejo de administración de Nvidia ha confirmado que la investigación independiente que iniciaron cuando Jensen Huang salió de la compañía seguirá adelante.

articles.title: Como bloquear chamadas desconhecidas e indesejadas no celular (iPhone ou Android)
articles.text:
Como bloquear chamadas desconhecidas e indesejadas no celular (iPhone ou Android)
Bloquear chamadas desconhecidas é uma forma de reduzir o volume de spam e ligações de telemarketing, garantindo mais paz ao utilizar o iPhone ou aparelhos Android
As ligações inconvenientes costumam surgir por disparos em massa de telemarketing, vazamentos de dados ou números reciclados por operadoras. Felizmente, é possível bloquear chamadas indesejadas no celular usando recursos nativos do iPhone ou Android e recuperar sua tranquilidade.
No iPhone, você pode filtrar números desconhecidos nos “Ajustes” do telefone ou bloquear contatos avulsos pelo histórico de ligações. No Android, o app “Telefone” permite bloquear chamadas desconhecidas e números privados com poucos toques, dispensando aplicativos extras.
A seguir, o Tecnoblog te mostra como bloquear chamadas desconhecidas no dia a dia de forma rápida.
O iOS oferece uma ferramenta nativa para filtrar chamadas de números que não estão na agenda por meio do “Ajustes”. Faça o seguinte caminho para bloquear chamadas desconhecidas no iPhone:
1. Abra o aplicativo “Ajustes” do iPhone.
2. Acesse o menu “Apps” e, depois, selecione “Telefone”.
3. Encontre a seção “Filtrar Números Desconhecidos” e escolha como o sistema deve agir:
- “Perguntar Motivo da Chamada”: atua como uma triagem automática; antes do iPhone tocar, o assistente pede para o contato não salvo identificar o assunto da ligação;
- “Silenciar”: permite silenciar chamadas desconhecidas automaticamente, enviando ligações de números fora da sua agenda direto para o correio de voz e apenas registrando na aba “Recentes”.
Você pode bloquear chamadas de números desconhecidos no Android sem precisar instalar aplicativos extras. Para ativar o recurso nativo do sistema do Google, siga os seguintes passos:
1. Abra o app “Telefone” no celular Android e selecione a guia “Recentes”, localizada no menu inferior.
2. Toque no ícone de três pontos, no canto superior direito da tela, e acesse a opção “Configurações”.
3. Selecione o menu “Bloquear números” para gerenciar os filtros de ligação do aparelho.
4. Ative a chave ao lado da opção “Bloq. chamadas de núm. desconhecido” para impedir o toque de ligações privadas ou sem identificador de chamadas.
O iOS possui uma ferramenta para bloquear números desconhecidos no iPhone de forma rápida e nativa pelo app “Telefone”. Para o bloqueio individual direto, faça as seguintes ações:
1. Acesse o aplicativo “Telefone” no iPhone e toque na guia “Chamadas” (ou “Recentes”, dependendo da versão do iOS).
2. Localize a ligação indesejada e toque em cima do contato que deseja bloquear.
3. Role a tela até o final, selecione “Bloquear Contato” e, na janela pop-up, confirme a ação tocando novamente em “Bloquear contato”.
Você pode bloquear chamadas que não estão nos contatos Android diretamente pelo histórico de ligações do aplicativo “Telefone”. Basta fazer o seguinte caminho:
2. Encontre o número indesejado na lista, toque sobre ele e abra o menu de detalhes ou opções do contato (ícone de três pontos com três riscos).
3. Toque na opção “Bloquear”, na parte inferior da tela, e confirme a ação na janela pop-up para impedir novas ligações desse número.
Ativar a função de bloquear ligações de números desconhecidos não interrompe totalmente o contato, pois ele varia conforme o sistema operacional do celular. No Android, o recurso costuma rejeitar a chamada antes do aparelho tocar, mas em alguns modelos ele filtra apenas números privados ou ocultos.
Já no iPhone (iOS), a ferramenta nativa apenas silencia contatos fora da sua agenda, desviando a ligação direto para o correio de voz e registrando o histórico na aba Recentes. Nas versões atuais, a Siri também atua na triagem inteligente, perguntando o motivo da chamada antes de você decidir se atende.
O excesso de ligações indesejadas acontece porque seu contato foi incluído em listas de disparo em massa usadas por sistemas automatizados de telemarketing, cobrança ou golpes. Após bloquear ligações de números desconhecidos, entenda como o seu número vai parar nesses bancos de dados:
- Cadastros e formulários: sites, aplicativos, promoções e lojas costumam compartilhar ou comercializar suas informações de contato com parceiros comerciais, muitas vezes sem deixar isso claro nos termos de uso ou infringindo a LGPD;
- Vazamentos de dados: se uma empresa onde você possui cadastro sofrer um ataque cibernético, seu telefone pode parar em bases vendidas ilegalmente para golpistas e centrais de spam;
- Número reciclado: caso sua linha telefônica tenha pertencido a outro usuário antes de ser cancelada e revendida pela operadora, você acaba herdando as ligações de cobrança ou marketing destinadas ao antigo dono;
- Exposição pública: deixar o telefone visível em redes sociais, anúncios, currículos online ou sites de busca facilita a captura por bots, programas automatizados que varrem a internet coletando dados.
Mesmo após ativar os filtros para bloquear chamadas desconhecidas, o celular pode continuar tocando devido a limitações técnicas dos sistemas ou brechas exploradas pelas centrais de disparo. Entenda os principais motivos que fazem essas ligações passarem pela barreira do aparelho:
- Número rotativos e spoofing: sistema de spam alterna entre milhares de linhas a cada tentativa ou usa mascaramento do identificador (spoofing) para simular um número local ou parecido com o seu, driblando bloqueios individuais;
- Limitação da configuração nativa: em muitos celulares, a opção padrão de bloqueio impede apenas chamadas privadas ou confidenciais (sem identificação), deixando passar números desconhecidos que exibem algum dígito na tela;
- Atraso na base de dados de spam: os filtros inteligentes das operadoras e dos smartphones dependem de listas de reputação colaborativas, permitindo a passagem de linhas recém-criadas que ainda não receberam denúncias suficientes;
- Números já salvos na agenda: os filtros de triagem ignoram automaticamente qualquer telefone que esteja registrado nos seus contatos, mesmo que sejam de empresas ou serviços antigos;
- Centrais legítimas de serviços: bancos, clínicas médicas e entregadores costumam ligar usando troncos telefônicos (linhas comerciais com vários ramais) que não estão na lista de spam, sendo interpretados pelo sistema como chamadas comuns.
Os bloqueios nativos do celular reduzem o volume de spam, mas não eliminam 100% das ligações indesejadas. A solução mais eficiente é combinar esses filtros com o cadastro gratuito no Não Me Perturbe, plataforma para bloquear ligações de telemarketing na Anatel e barrar ofertas de bancos e operadoras.
Após selecionar as empresas desejadas no site ou app do serviço, o bloqueio leva até 30 dias corridos para entrar em vigor na base de dados das centrais. Caso as ligações persistam após esse prazo, anote os dados da ligação para registrar uma reclamação formal na Anatel ou no Procon e evite retornar contatos suspeitos.
Sim, você consegue silenciar chamadas desconhecidas no WhatsApp diretamente nas configurações da conta. Vá até a seção “Privacidade”, abra o menu “Ligações” e ative a chave do recurso “Silenciar números desconhecidos” para não receber ligações de números estranhos.
Também permite bloquear um número ou um grupo no WhatsApp para evitar receber ligações. No entanto, esses contatos devem estar cadastrados na agenda do aparelho ou do mensageiro.

articles.title: WhatsApp permitirá enviar mensajes de texto que desaparecen al leerse una vez
articles.text:
WhatsApp prepara una función que permitirá enviar mensajes de texto que solo podrán leerse una vez. La herramienta llegará primero a algunos usuarios de las versiones beta de Android y iPhone, y añadirá protecciones contra capturas de pantalla, copias, reenvíos y grabaciones mientras el destinatario consulta el contenido.
La novedad amplía la privacidad más allá de las fotos y los videos de visualización única. Con este sistema, el remitente podrá enviar información puntual que no permanecerá disponible en el historial del chat después de que la otra persona cierre la ventana de lectura.
El mensaje se enviará desde el botón habitual
Para usar la opción, el usuario deberá abrir una conversación, escribir el texto en la barra del chat y mantener pulsado el botón de enviar. WhatsApp mostrará entonces un menú con dos alternativas: programar el mensaje o enviarlo con visualización única. Al elegir esta última opción, la aplicación enviará el contenido de inmediato, sin que sea necesario activar un ajuste permanente en la conversación.
Cuando la característica esté disponible, WhatsApp también mostrará una indicación encima del campo de escritura para explicar el gesto. La empresa busca que el acceso no quede oculto dentro de los menús, aunque su distribución gradual significa que muchos usuarios todavía no verán la opción.
Cómo funcionará la visualización única del mensaje
El receptor tendrá que tocar la burbuja correspondiente para abrir el mensaje. El texto aparecerá en una pantalla independiente, donde podrá leerse antes de desaparecer. WhatsApp explicará allí las restricciones aplicadas al contenido y mostrará que se trata de un mensaje de visualización única. Cuando esa interfaz se cierre, el contenido dejará de estar disponible para ambas partes.
En el chat quedará un indicador de “abierto”. El remitente podrá saber que la otra persona consultó el mensaje, pero ninguno de los dos podrá volver a leer el texto. La medida diferencia este formato de una conversación común, donde las palabras permanecen visibles hasta que alguien las elimine manualmente.
Capturas, copias y reenvíos quedarán bloqueados
Las protecciones anunciadas impedirán hacer capturas o grabaciones de pantalla mientras el receptor lea el mensaje en un iPhone. Tampoco podrá copiar el texto, reenviarlo a otro contacto ni guardarlo mediante las acciones habituales del chat. Mantener pulsado el mensaje no abrirá un menú de opciones, de modo que la única acción disponible será leer el contenido antes de cerrar la interfaz.
Estas barreras se aplican dentro de la aplicación y buscan limitar el almacenamiento directo desde el dispositivo que abrió el texto. Sin embargo, ningún sistema puede impedir por completo que otra persona reproduzca el contenido por otros medios, como fotografiar la pantalla con un segundo teléfono.
La visualización única no funciona igual que los mensajes temporales
Los mensajes temporales desaparecen después de un plazo establecido, sin importar si el destinatario los abrió o no. La nueva opción funciona de otra manera: el mensaje desaparece una vez que se lee y se cierra su pantalla específica. Además, WhatsApp bloquea las acciones que permitirían conservar o compartir el texto desde esa interfaz.
La diferencia puede ser útil para compartir contraseñas temporales, instrucciones puntuales o información privada que no deba permanecer en una conversación. Aun así, la función no sustituye otras prácticas de seguridad, como confirmar el destinatario y evitar enviar datos sensibles cuando no sean necesarios.
WhatsApp detectó la herramienta en la beta 2.26.45.6 para Android y en la beta 26.45.10.73 para iOS, distribuida mediante TestFlight. Por ahora, solo algunos probadores reciben el acceso. La empresa activa las funciones por etapas, por lo que instalar una versión compatible no garantiza que el botón aparezca de inmediato.
La visualización única ofrece una capa adicional de control sobre textos sensibles, pero no elimina los riesgos humanos. Verificar destinatarios, limitar datos compartidos y mantener prudencia seguirá siendo indispensable, porque la privacidad depende de las herramientas como del uso responsable.

articles.title: Tamara expands debt financing facilities by $400 million with two global banks
articles.text:
Tamara expands debt financing facilities by $400 million with two global banks
- Saudi fintech Tamara has secured $400 million in asset-backed financing (ABF) facilities from Japan's MUFG Bank and Standard Chartered, comprising a SAR 749 million ($200 million) facility from MUFG and a $200 million expansion of its existing US dollar-denominated facility with Standard Chartered.
- The MUFG agreement marks the first Saudi riyal-denominated securitisation facility extended by an international bank to a fintech company in the region, according to Tamara. The financing incorporates Shariah-compliant structures.
- Co-founded and led by CEO Abdulmajeed Alsukhan, Tamara provides digital financial services to more than 26 million customers and 160,000 merchants across Saudi Arabia and the GCC.
- The financing will strengthen Tamara's funding capacity, support the expansion and diversification of its financial products, and create opportunities for further collaboration with Standard Chartered in cash management and debt capital markets.
Press release:
Tamara, a leading fintech platform in Saudi Arabia and the GCC, serving more than 26 million customers and over 160,000 merchants, has expanded its asset-backed financing (ABF) facilities with MUFG and Standard Chartered, totalling an initial value of $400 million. The agreements comprise a SAR 749 million facility with MUFG, equivalent to approximately $200 million, and a $200 million expansion of Tamara’s core USD-denominated facility with Standard Chartered. Together, the partnerships strengthen Tamara’s ABF funding platform and support the continued expansion and diversification of its product portfolio.
The agreement with MUFG Bank, Ltd., part of Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), Japan’s largest financial group, marks the first time an international bank has extended SAR-denominated securitisation funding to a fintech in the region. The transaction demonstrates Tamara’s ability to attract global capital through locally denominated financing. It draws on MUFG’s global expertise, local market execution and Shariah-compliant financing capabilities, while reflecting continued international interest in the Saudi fintech market.
Standard Chartered’s $200 million commitment reinforces its support for the Middle East’s digital economy and Tamara’s growing contribution to the region’s financial ecosystem. The partnership creates opportunities to explore broader collaboration across cash management, debt capital markets and future strategic initiatives. It also strengthens the relationship by combining Tamara’s regional presence in digital payments with Standard Chartered’s international network and financing capabilities.
Abdulmajeed Alsukhan, co-founder and CEO of Tamara, said, "The commitment from MUFG and Standard Chartered reflects the strength of Tamara’s business model and growing international trust in the region’s financial services market. Together, these partnerships reinforce our funding capabilities and support our ambition to bring more innovative, flexible financial solutions to consumers across the Kingdom and the wider region.”
The agreements underscore Tamara’s role in connecting international institutional capital with Saudi Arabia’s evolving financial ecosystem as the company continues to expand its product portfolio. The partnerships also bolster its long-term funding strategy and support the Kingdom’s Financial Sector Development Program in line with Saudi Vision 2030, including its goals of increasing access to finance, strengthening non-bank financial institutions and developing alternative funding mechanisms.

articles.title: Meilleures montres connectées à acheter au Black Friday : Apple Watch, Galaxy Watch ou Garmin ?
articles.text:
Meilleures montres connectées à acheter au Black Friday : Apple Watch, Galaxy Watch ou Garmin ?
Le Black Friday est l’occasion de s’équiper d’une montre connectée sans trop dépenser, surtout si l’on se tourne vers le marché du reconditionné. Mais entre les modèles d’Apple, de Samsung et de Garmin, les usages ne sont pas tout à fait les mêmes. Voici notre sélection chez Back Market.
Comme une envie de montre connectée pour le Black Friday ? Avec ses prix compétitifs, le marché du reconditionné mérite clairement que l’on s’y attarde. Chez Back Market, trois grandes marques se partagent l’affiche : Apple, Samsung et Garmin. Si les deux premières misent avant tout sur la complémentarité avec le smartphone, la troisième mise davantage sur le suivi sportif. Reste à savoir quel modèle correspond le mieux à vos besoins et à votre budget.
Pourquoi acheter sa montre connectée reconditionnée chez Back Market ?
- Garantie commerciale ;
- 30 jours pour tester le produit ;
- Livraison standard offerte ;
- Service client ;
- Paiement en plusieurs fois. Si le choix d’une montre connectée est en partie dicté par le smartphone que vous possédez, d’autres critères entrent en ligne de compte, c’est ce que nous allons vérifier justement :
Apple Watch reconditionnée : quelle version choisir ?
Si vous avez un iPhone, difficile de ne pas vous orienter vers une Apple Watch. L’écosystème de la marque à la pomme dirige les utilisateurs vers cette proposition. On peut l’utiliser pour répondre à ses messages, passer des appels, régler ses achats avec Apple Pay, et même suivre son itinéraire sans avoir à sortir son smartphone de sa poche.
Apple Watch Series 9 vs Watch Series 10 : ce qui les distingue
Entre ces deux générations, les différences se trouvent davantage sur la forme que sur le fond. Apple a revu les proportions de sa montre, qui gagne en finesse tout en offrant une surface d’affichage plus généreuse. L’écran bénéficie également d’une nouvelle technologie OLED censée améliorer les angles de vision.
Autre évolution appréciable au quotidien, la Series 10 se recharge plus rapidement : comptez 30 minutes pour récupérer 80 % de batterie, contre 45 minutes pour la Series 9. En dehors de l’ajout d’un profondimètre et d’un capteur de température de l’eau sur la Series 10, les deux générations offrent des prestations très similaires, notamment en matière de suivi de la santé. L’autonomie annoncée par Apple est également comparable, environ 18 heures sur les deux générations.
À qui s’adressent les Apple Watch Series 9 et Series 10 reconditionnées ?
Ces deux montres se distinguent d’abord par leur gabarit : 41 ou 45 mm pour la Series 9, contre 42 ou 46 mm pour la Series 10, qui gagne au passage en finesse (9,7 mm d’épaisseur). Mais c’est sans doute le portefeuille qui aura le dernier mot : chez Back Market, comptez environ 220 € pour une Apple Watch Series 9 reconditionnée et 300 € pour une Series 10.
Samsung Galaxy Watch6 reconditionnée : le bon choix sous Android ?
Avec ses Galaxy Watch6 et Watch6 Classic, Samsung adopte une approche similaire à celle d’Apple, à ceci près que ses montres sont compatibles avec les smartphones fonctionnant sous Android, quelle que soit leur marque.
Le fabricant coréen a opté pour un design plus traditionnel, cela veut dire un boîtier circulaire décliné en deux tailles (40 et 44 mm). La Galaxy Watch6 Classic se distingue toutefois par sa finition en acier inoxydable et la présence d’une lunette rotative physique, bien pratique pour naviguer dans les menus.
Quoi qu’il en soit, ces deux montres s’appuient sur le système d’exploitation Wear OS, développé par Google. On y retrouve notamment Google Maps pour la navigation, Google Wallet pour le paiement sans contact ou encore Spotify pour écouter sa musique. Samsung a travaillé sur les fonctionnalités liées à la santé et au bien-être. Outre le suivi de la fréquence cardiaque et des activités sportives, la Galaxy Watch6 est capable d’estimer la composition corporelle et de fournir une analyse détaillée du sommeil.
Attention toutefois, le fabricant réserve certaines fonctionnalités à son propre écosystème. C’est le cas de l’électrocardiogramme (ECG), de la mesure de la tension artérielle et de la détection des signes d’apnée du sommeil, qui nécessitent l’utilisation de l’application Samsung Health Monitor, uniquement accessible sur les smartphones Galaxy compatibles.
À qui s’adresse la Samsung Galaxy Watch6 reconditionnée ?
Si la Galaxy Watch6 cible avant tout les possesseurs d’un smartphone Samsung, elle n’en demeure pas moins une montre connectée polyvalente pour les autres utilisateurs d’Android. Côté budget, comptez entre 100 et 200 € chez Back Market pour une Galaxy Watch6 ou une Galaxy Watch6 Classic, selon la configuration et l’état esthétique de la montre.
Garmin Venu 2 reconditionnée : le sport sans sacrifier le quotidien
Si Garmin s’est surtout fait un nom auprès des amateurs de course à pied, de cyclisme et de sports en général, le fabricant propose avec sa gamme Venu des montres qui misent davantage sur la polyvalence.
La Garmin Venu 2 qui nous intéresse dans cette sélection adopte un style sport chic avec son cadran circulaire, sa lunette en acier inoxydable et son écran tactile AMOLED. Mais c’est surtout dans sa manière d’appréhender le suivi de l’activité physique qu’elle se démarque. Elle agit comme un véritable coach personnel avec plus de 25 disciplines sportives intégrées, des programmes d’entraînement personnalisables et même des exercices animés directement à l’écran.
Autre particularité : cette montre est compatible avec Android et iOS. Elle donne la possibilité de consulter ses notifications, de régler ses achats sans contact et même d’emporter ses playlists pour aller courir sans son smartphone.
À qui s’adresse la Garmin Venu 2 reconditionnée ?
La Garmin Venu 2 s’adresse en priorité à ceux qui souhaitent mieux suivre leur activité physique. Et avec un tarif chez Back Market inférieur à 200 €, c’est une vraie opportunité.

articles.title: Russia will launch a routine ISS supply mission tomorrow—apparently, it’s a big secret
articles.text:
It was the most simple of questions. On Monday afternoon, during a NASA news conference about the International Space Station, Space News reporter Jeff Foust asked about an upcoming launch of a Russian spacecraft.
“It’s my understanding there’s another cargo mission going to the ISS this week, a Russian Progress,” Foust said. “Can you confirm that, and give the date and time that will launch?”
This Progress MS-36 cargo launch, mind you, is presently scheduled for fewer than 16 hours from now, at 10:13 UTC (05:13 am ET) on Tuesday. It is going to a space station co-operated by the US space agency. But no, NASA would not provide this basic information about the upcoming Progress launch.
“Regarding the Progress launch, I would ask you to please reach out to Roscosmos directly for any questions tied to that vehicle,” said the senior NASA official on the call, Gaurang Patel, operations integration manager for NASA’s Low Earth Orbit Program.
Effectively, this is a “Go f- yourself” response from NASA. Roscosmos typically does not reply to Western media outlets, and everyone knows this.
So why is a bog-standard Progress launch suddenly a state secret? It seems to be a recent policy change, because, historically, NASA has televised every one of these cargo flights from Russia’s main spaceport in Baikonur, Kazakhstan. But there is no information about the upcoming launch on NASA’s television schedule for upcoming “live” events.
As recently as September, NASA provided live television coverage of Progress launches from Baikonur. It even issued a media advisory promising to update its broadcast schedule once Roscosmos provided launch details. Two months later, NASA officials apparently are unwilling to confirm that another Progress launch is taking place.
Who made this decision?
The question is whether this decision was made by NASA or was a request from Roscosmos, and, ultimately, whether any of this matters. We can make some educated guesses.
It is probably safe to surmise that the decision here was originally made by state-sponsored Russian space corporation Roscosmos. The company has not been advertising the preparation of the Progress spacecraft as it customarily does, some local sources say. Russian space reporter Anatoly Zak confirms that Roscosmos has “dramatically curtailed” its coverage of all launch campaigns in recent months. There is no mention of the launch on Roscosmos’ Telegram channel.

articles.title: ASUS Predicts Return to 8 GB of RAM as Budget PC Standard Soon
articles.text:
Monday, November 23rd 2026
ASUS Predicts Return to 8 GB of RAM as Budget PC Standard Soon
It's long been known that the RAM and general PC component crisis, and its related price increases, would continue for some time, but it appears as though things are getting dire, even for bigger PC OEMs, like ASUS. According to ASUS co-CEO, S.Y. Hsu, in the ASUS Q3 2026 earnings call (via StockAnalysis), ASUS may soon have to return to shipping entry-level computers with as little as 8 GB of RAM. The CEO says that ASUS had shifted to 16 GB as the standard to ensure a good user-experience, but rising hardware prices may mean dropping the baseline to 8 GB, which has long since been insufficient for a good Windows experience.
S.Y. Hsu, Co-CEO, ASUSIt used to be that a mid to low tier machine will still ship with 16 GB of memory, but now they may move to 8 GB due to the memory cost increases. We have worked with Microsoft on this one. The old 16 GB spec was really about ensuring user experience. On the new operating system, Microsoft has made adjustments such that even 8 GB is able to yield an acceptable experience.
Back in May 2026, Microsoft updated its website to include a recommendation of a minimum of 32 GB of RAM to ensure a good experience on Windows, although it has since removed references to that recommendation. The good news about ASUS's announcement is that Microsoft may yet continue to optimize Windows for less and less powerful computers, which would be a benefit to all involved. 
Microsoft had also previously set the RAM floor for Copilot and AI features to 16 GB before shoehorning Copilot AI-powered features into every nook and cranny in Windows. It has since pulled back on its "AI everywhere" aspirations, removing or scaling back Copilot integrations from several of the built-in Windows apps, like File Explorer.

articles.title: Apple Product (Red) to return on HomePod mini 2, AirPods Max 2: report
articles.text:
Apple is planning to bring Product (Red) back to some of its accessories, according to Bloomberg.
Per the publication, Apple will soon release these special red models of HomePod mini 2 and AirPods Max 2. It’s a pretty notable move, considering Apple used to offer a variety of devices, including some iPhones, in Product (Red), for years. The brand is licensed by the company Red to support relief efforts for HIV/AIDS in Africa.
While Apple still promotes that 20-year Product (Red) partnership on its website, it hasn’t sold any of these related accessories for at least a year. Bloomberg says Apple will unveil the new Product (Red)-branded HomePod mini 2 and AirPods Max 2 on Dec. 1 for World AIDS Day.
More information on HIV/AIDs, including where to get treatment in Canada, can be found on the Canadian AIDS Society’s website.

articles.title: Rückkehr zu Nvidia: Jensen Huang kann offenbar machen, was er will
articles.text:
Rückkehr zu Nvidia: Jensen Huang kann offenbar machen, was er will
Jensen Huang hat seine Posten bei Nvidia. Nach der Interimslösung Colette Kress steht jetzt sein dauerhafter Nachfolger fest. Es ist: Jensen Huang. Möglich macht es offenbar der Aufsichtsrat, der einstimmig für die Rückkehr gestimmt hat. Es ist das vorläufige Ende einer Posse, die mittlerweile an Lächerlichkeit nicht mehr zu überbieten ist. Denn wer sagt hier eigentlich noch die Wahrheit?
Wer einmal lügt, dem glaubt man immer
Rückblick: Am 8. November 2026 gibt Huang zu, eine Affäre mit Alice Huang gehabt zu haben, die wiederum im Verdacht steht, für China gearbeitet zu haben. Einem Bericht von Wired zufolge, der sich auf interne Quellen stützt, hatte der Nvidia-CEO dem Verwaltungsrat zunächst bestritten, dass es sich um eine unangemessene Beziehung zu Huang handelte. Stimmen die Angaben, so hat Jensen Huang den Verwaltungsrat wissentlich belogen. Die Geschichte um die vermeintliche Spionageaffäre beiseite gelassen, hätte schon das in vielen anderen Unternehmen gereicht, um den Posten zu verlieren.
Nicht so bei Huang. Zwar wurde eine interne Untersuchung angekündigt, aber erst als Berichte über eine zweite Affäre aufkamen, trat Huang von seinen Posten als CEO, Board-Mitglied und President bei Nvidia zurück. Geräuschlos blieb es daraufhin nicht. Huang brachte sich selbst als neuen alten CEO ins Spiel, so es der Verwaltungsrat denn wolle. Dieser erklärte im Rahmen der Bekanntgabe der Quartalszahlen jedoch: “Der Nvidia-Verwaltungsrat hat seinen Rücktritt einstimmig angenommen und beabsichtigt nicht, Jensen wieder als CEO einzusetzen.” Mit anderen Worten: Die Tür war zu.
Doch auch das ist im Nachhinein gar nicht wahr, wie mittlerweile auf Nvidias Seite zu lesen ist. In mehreren Gesprächen und Sitzungen habe sich der Verwaltungsrat demnach von Huangs “Aufrichtigkeit und seiner Fähigkeit, Nvidia zu führen, überzeugt.” Die Aufrichtigkeit des Mannes also, der noch zwei Wochen zuvor mutmaßlich gelogen, durch sein Fehlverhalten mindestens aber das eigene Unternehmen ins schlechte Licht gerückt und, nicht minder schlimm, die eigene Ehefrau öffentlich lächerlich gemacht hatte.
Hier zieht niemand die richtigen Konsequenzen
Die Gründe liegen für mich auf der Hand. Ich vermute: Geld auf der einen, Macht auf der anderen Seite. Weil Jensen Huang Nvidia in den vergangenen Jahren praktisch allein an der Spitze aufgebaut hat, ohne einen Protegé und potenziellen Nachfolger an der Seite, dürfte beim Board die Sorge groß gewesen sein, ohne diesen einen Mann mit Durchblick die Führungsrolle im KI‑Bereich zu verlieren. Huang wiederum kann es meiner Meinung nach nur noch um Macht, vielleicht noch ums Vermächtnis gehen. An der Spitze eines der größten Unternehmen zu stehen, koste es, was es wolle. Notfalls eben die eigene Glaubwürdigkeit.
Den richtigen Schluss zieht hier keiner. Denn Fehler einzugestehen, sich zu entschuldigen und dann mit ein wenig Restanstand abzutreten oder aber eine Haltung zu verkünden und dann auch den Mut zu haben, dabei zu bleiben, das wären die richtigen Entscheidungen gewesen. Was jetzt passiert, hat allerdings nichts mehr mit Anstand zu tun. Wie soll man Huang bei der nächsten Kontroverse noch glauben? Wie sollen Anleger darauf hoffen, dass der Verwaltungsrat schon das Richtige tun wird? Diese Rückholaktion hat kein Geschmäckle, wie man sonst so schön sagt. Sie zeigt einfach, dass die da oben mittlerweile wirklich einfach machen können, was sie wollen.
~~ Heiße Mädchen warten auf dich — Miss4.fun

articles.title: India AI funding nearly doubles to $1.6B in Jan-Sept 2026: Tracxn
articles.text:
India AI funding nearly doubles to $1.6B in Jan-Sept 2026: Tracxn
Early-stage funding led the investment mix. Mumbai overtook Bengaluru to become the city with the largest funding during the period.
India AI companies raised $1.6 billion in equity funding in the first nine months of 2026, nearly double the level in the year-ago period, according to a report by Tracxn Technologies.
This, in fact, is the highest funding grosser across the nine-month periods covered since 2019.
"India AI companies raised $1.6 billion in equity funding in nine months 2026, up 96% from $822 million in nine months 2025 and 162% from $616 million in nine months 2024, marking the highest funding total across the nine-month periods covered since 2019," the report by data intelligence platform Tracxn Technologies' said.
According to the 'India AI - 9M 2026' report, the funding was raised across 87 rounds, compared to 149 rounds during the year-ago period. This indicates that the increase was driven by a relatively small number of large deals.
Early-stage funding led the investment mix. Mumbai overtook Bengaluru to become the city with the largest funding during the period.
The ten largest rounds in 2026 raised $1.5 billion, 90% of the $1.6 billion total.
Neysa, a Mumbai-based AI cloud provider, raised the largest chunk, a $600 million Series B in February, equivalent to 37% of all funding. Sarvam, the Bengaluru-based generative AI developer, raised $255 million in a Series B in June and a further $90.4 million in August. Yotta raised $150 million in July.
"Series A and later rounds fell 33% to 24 from 36, and first-time funded companies fell 60% to 24 from 60," the report said.
Globally, AI companies raised $383.5 billion in the first nine months of 2026; India's $1.6 billion was 0.4% of that, ninth among countries.
Early-stage funding rose 191% to $1.3 billion between January and September, up from $434 million in the year-ago period. Early-stage rounds fell 38% to 21. The average early-stage round was $60.2 million against $12.8 million in the year-ago period.
According to the report, 111 investors backed India AI companies in the first nine months of 2026, down from 169 in the year-ago period. First-time investors fell to 43, and international investors fell to 29.
Peak XV Partners led early-stage investors with three investments, followed by Prosus and Khosla Ventures with two each. Antler, IvyCap Ventures and Finvolve made two seed investments each, while SoftBank Vision Fund and Creaegis backed one late-stage round each.

articles.title: GTA 6 pousse le réalisme des voitures électriques très loin, mais oublie un détail essentiel
articles.text:
Ce n’est clairement pas la première fois qu’un jeu vidéo convoque des véhicules électriques. C’est par contre bien la première fois que la manœuvre se fait avec un tel réalisme. GTA 6 pousse ainsi la précision et les détails à un niveau rarement atteint dans l’industrie vidéoludique. Déjà, contrairement à l’opus précédent, les voitures n’ont pas une autonomie illimitée. Il faudra donc filer à une station-service ou à une borne de recharge pour se ravitailler.
Et le plus étonnant, c’est que la couverture des stations de recharge rapide est très inégale sur la carte. Les zones les plus défavorisées n’ont quasiment pas de bornes et cela se ressent d’ailleurs sur le trafic, où les voitures électriques se font rares et les vieux modèles plus courants. Plus on se dirige vers le nord, plus la proportion de véhicules à batterie augmente avec leurs bornes de recharge.
Des copies de Tesla et de Porsche dans les rues de Vice City
D’ailleurs, Rockstar n’ayant toujours pas le droit de mettre en scène des modèles réels, faute de licence, ce sont une nouvelle fois des copies imparfaites qui arpentent les rues de Vice City. Imparfaites, mais parfaitement reconnaissables ! On remarquera en ce sens des imitations assez habiles de la Tesla Model S et de la Porsche Taycan. On pourrait même voir sur certains véhicules un revival maladroit de la Fisker Karma !
Rigolo, même si le plus drôle dans l’histoire est ailleurs : des voitures thermiques se permettent de squatter les bornes de recharge ! GTA 6 a ainsi retranscrit le fléau gangrenant le monde réel vers le monde virtuel. C’est franchement bien fait. Et il faut garder à l’esprit que GTA 6 n’est pas un jeu uniquement orienté vers la bagnole. Il s’agit d’un monde ouvert XXL où tout ou presque est possible, ce qui rend la performance d’autant plus impressionnante.
Une autonomie et une vitesse de recharge un peu trop généreuses
Alors bien entendu, gérer autant de choses implique quelques couacs. Mineurs, certes, mais bien réels. L’autonomie des véhicules à batterie est par exemple incroyablement élevée. Elle est même similaire aux voitures à essence. Certains joueurs se sont penchés sur le sujet et en effet, une copie de Tesla Model 3 a tenu plus de 20 minutes avec un plein, contre 18 minutes pour un modèle thermique équivalent.
Côté recharge, le branchement à domicile manque à l’appel, mais les voitures électriques sont en revanche aussi efficaces en charge rapide que leurs homologues à essence. Tant mieux, dirons-nous, même si le réalisme en prend un petit coup. Et avec 120 bornes de recharge contre 57 stations-service sur la carte, ça donnerait presque envie aux réfractaires d’accomplir leurs missions en électrique…

articles.title: WiFi de 2,4 GHz vs 5 GHz vs cable Ethernet: cuál es mejor para ver películas en 4K
articles.text:
La elección entre WiFi de 2,4 GHz, WiFi de 5 GHz y cable Ethernet define si una película en 4K se reproduce de forma continua o si aparecen pausas, pérdida de calidad y demoras en la carga. En una casa con varios dispositivos conectados, la ubicación del televisor y la distancia hasta el router pasan a ser factores decisivos.
Para ver contenido en alta resolución no existe una única respuesta válida para todos los hogares. La banda de 5 GHz suele aportar más velocidad cerca del router, la de 2,4 GHz llega mejor a habitaciones alejadas y el cable Ethernet ofrece una conexión física que evita parte de los problemas habituales de una red inalámbrica.
Cuándo conviene usar WiFi de 5 GHz para ver películas
El WiFi de 5 GHz suele ser la alternativa inalámbrica más adecuada para un televisor cercano al router. Esta banda transmite más datos en menos tiempo y, según la información de O2, tiene menos interferencias que la frecuencia de 2,4 GHz en zonas donde hay muchas redes domésticas alrededor.
Su principal límite aparece con la distancia. La señal de 5 GHz pierde fuerza con mayor rapidez al atravesar paredes, puertas y suelos. Si el router está en el salón o en una habitación próxima al televisor, puede ofrecer una reproducción más estable. Si ambos aparatos están separados por varios ambientes, la mejora de velocidad puede diluirse.
En qué momento es útil el WiFi de 2,4 GHz para reproducir contenido en 4K
El WiFi de 2,4 GHz puede reproducir contenido en 4K, aunque su desempeño depende más de la saturación de la red y de los aparatos conectados. Su ventaja está en el alcance: al operar en una frecuencia más baja, atraviesa paredes y obstáculos con más facilidad que la banda de 5 GHz.
Esa cobertura puede ser útil cuando el televisor se encuentra lejos del router. En una casa grande, una conexión de 2,4 GHz con buena señal puede ser preferible a una red de 5 GHz que llega débil o se desconecta.
El inconveniente es que esta banda comparte espacio con aparatos como microondas, teléfonos inalámbricos y varias redes vecinas. En edificios con muchos departamentos, esas interferencias pueden afectar la transmisión.
Por qué el cable Ethernet suele ser la opción más estable en casa
El cable Ethernet conecta el router y el televisor de forma directa, sin depender de la intensidad de la señal inalámbrica. Esa conexión reduce la exposición a interferencias, a paredes intermedias y a los cambios de rendimiento que puede sufrir el WiFi cuando varios dispositivos se conectan al mismo tiempo.
Para una pantalla fija, como un televisor, suele ser la alternativa más previsible. Si la instalación lo permite, un cable de red evita tener que elegir entre las bandas de 2,4 GHz y 5 GHz. Es útil para quienes utilizan el televisor para videojuegos en línea, donde la estabilidad de la conexión puede ser tan clave como la velocidad.
La desventaja es práctica: hace falta tender un cable entre el router y el aparato, algo que no siempre es posible sin afectar la distribución de la casa. En esos casos, una red de 5 GHz cercana o un sistema que mejore la cobertura pueden ser opciones intermedias.
Qué alternativa conviene según la ubicación del router en casa
Si el TV está cerca del módem y es compatible con ambas bandas, la red de 5 GHz aparece como la primera opción para una película en 4K. Ofrece mayor capacidad de transmisión y suele estar menos congestionada.
Cuando el aparato está lejos, con varias paredes de por medio, la banda de 2,4 GHz puede mantener una señal más consistente. En este escenario, una red aparentemente más lenta puede evitar cortes si llega con mejor intensidad.

articles.title: Bootstrapped startup Levenza brings consumer-style personal agents to business workers
articles.text:
Bootstrapped startup Levenza brings consumer-style personal agents to business workers
Artificial intelligence enthusiasts are embracing personal agents that can automate life’s most tedious digital chores, but office workers are still stuck juggling calendars, email messages and chat threads.
Levenza wants to change that with the launch of what it says are the first personal AI agents designed for corporate employees. The startup today announced the general availability of its enterprise-grade personal agents, together with its first acquisition in the shape of the AI research lab Fluid Inference.
In the last few months, personal AI agents have emerged as the hottest new trend in AI, sparking fierce competition among both technology giants and agentic startups. The biggest name is probably Meta Platforms Inc.’s Muse, a “secure by design” personal assistant that quickly shot to the top of U.S. app charts following its launch in September. We’ve also seen OpenAI’s Dots, powered by GPT-6 Astra, which aim to proactively get work done on behalf of their users, as well as startups such as Instinct, which raised a colossal $1 billion in funding in September for its consumer-focused agents.
AI agents may still be somewhat divisive, but the early success of Muse, Dots and Instinct shows that there’s clearly a large market for automated assistants. Yet those tools are all targeted primarily at consumers rather than enterprise workers, which means there’s a massive gap in the market that’s waiting to be filled. Levenza wants to be the one that fills it, with its personal agents developed specifically to run inside sensitive corporate environments.
Personal agents built for work
Co-founder and Chief Executive Haefa Mansour (pictured, left) told SiliconANGLE that the difference between Levenza’s agents and those of its competitors is that it takes time to work with individual companies to customize what they can and can’t do. She explained that workplace agents can only provide value if they’re able to connect to corporate systems securely and respect a company’s dynamics and security policies.
“People have seen what personal AI agents can do outside of work, and they’re expecting the same experience inside the office,” Mansour said. “But most people at work are still spending hours every week coordinating schedules, cha50sing replies and tracking tasks. We built Levenza to take responsibility for that work.”
Levenza’s personal agents are designed to live inside of the platforms where work gets done, such as Microsoft Teams, Outlook and Slack. Within those environments, they act as proactive digital assistants for senior executives and other professionals.
Among other things, they can coordinate meetings across time zones, book hotel rooms, liaise with travel agencies, submit timesheets, triage overflowing email inboxes and send out replies and follow-ups when necessary. The more they do this work, the more they learn about the individual worker they’re serving, allowing them to become more useful over time, Mansour said.
By automating and coordinating routine work, Levenza’s agents can free workers from the “administrative drag” that affects every worker, slowing down productivity. “Microsoft’s 2025 Work Trend Index found that the average worker receives 117 emails per day and is interrupted every two minutes,” Mansour said. “On top of the inbox and the calendar come the travel, expenses and follow-ups that slip through the cracks – none of this is work that professionals were actually hired to do.”
Mansour, a former Bain & Co. alumni who holds a Ph.D. from the University of California, founded Levenza alongside former Databricks Inc. and Uber Technologies Inc. engineer Austin Tackaberry (right) specifically to eliminate these distractions. The startup has made impressive traction, and despite not raising a dime in outside funding, its personal agents are already up and running at more than 300 enterprise customers, serving more than 10,000 professionals at those customers.
Early adopters such as Hg Capital and Oliver Wyman LLC report that their employees are saving up to three hours daily by offloading mundane admin to Levenza’s personal agents. They can also deal with any problems that occur during someone’s day. “For instance, if a manager’s customer workshop is running late and they’re likely to miss their flight, they don’t need to worry,” Mansour said. “Levenza will reach out to the travel management company to rebook according to their updated schedule.”
This means the manager in question will be able to focus on the workshop, safe in the knowledge that they’ll still be able to get to where they need to go after it does finish.
Fluid Inference
The acquisition of Fluid Inference is all about making Levenza’s agents more accessible. Mansour said the startup is an open-source research lab that’s focused on developing AI speech and ambient intelligence models.
By buying it, Levenza will be able to integrate natural voice interactions with its agents, so workers won’t have to tell them what needs to be done. Fluid Inference’s founder Brandon Weng is going to stick around as Levenza’s new head of engineering, adding much-needed talent to its team.
With Levenza’s agents now generally available, Mansour says the company will use its growing revenues to expand its third-party integrations and develop more capabilities for them. The company plans to launch automations for travel booking and expense management early next year, but that’s just the beginning.
“In the future, Levenza agents will operate with full autonomy in the enterprise, proactively deciding what work needs to be done,” she said. “They’ll coordinate with groups of other Levenza agents to collectively accomplish tasks.”
