articles.title: Supertake raises $20M to let AI agents turn your market predictions into stock portfolios
articles.text:
AI investing startup Supertake has an interesting premise: What if your “takes” on the market could make you money without you having to pick stocks yourself? The service lets people turn their ideas into real investment portfolios, using frontier AI models and trading agents.
Now, the company has raised $20 million in seed funding to grow its business. The round was led by venture firm Adjacent (Nico Wittenborn), with participation from Coinbase Ventures and Union Square Ventures (USV). Numerous angel investors also joined, including Nat Friedman, who’s currently head of product at Meta Superintelligence Labs; Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch; renowned product manager Nikita Bier; investor Scott Belsky; and Nemil Dalal, a former Coinbase exec who is now a visiting partner at Y Combinator.
Michael Mignano originally incubated the startup at USV. He is the co-founder and former CEO of the podcasting platform Anchor, which Spotify acquired in 2019 for over $150 million. After leading Spotify’s podcasting business as “Head of Talk” for a few years, he joined the team at Lightspeed as a venture partner, betting on AI companies like Suno and Granola. He also co-founded Oboe, an AI education startup, and joined USV as a general partner in April.
“We really believed there was an opportunity to make investing more democratized…and give everyone and anyone the ability to invest in their own insights and beliefs and ideas,” Mignano said. While he will continue in his role as founder and executive chairman, he’s now brought in a team to run the company day to day.
The team includes co-founders Lincoln Murr (CEO) and John Peterson (CTO). Both joined from Coinbase, where, Mignano notes, they were the heads of AI product and engineering, leading launches like Coinbase advisor, Coinbase for agents, agentic wallets, and others.
The startup arrives as AI continues to make inroads into financial services, but allowing AI to take over people’s actual investments requires a new level of trust. Supertake is betting that people will ultimately be willing to take that leap, given recent improvements in frontier AI models.
Currently, Supertake works with Coinbase and Robinhood, and the company intends to expand to more brokerages over time. The idea is that you can explain, in broad, natural language, what you believe about how the world is going to change, and Supertake’s AI will iterate with you back and forth to turn that idea into a “take” that’s investable.
Under the hood, the startup is leveraging frontier AI technology and tools, combined with its own proprietary software that directs and limits what the AI can do.
Supertake’s users’ ideas are tracked on a leaderboard on the site, so others who agree can invest alongside them. For instance, there’s currently an idea on the leaderboard about looksmaxxing and longevity becoming more of a trend, where the portfolio includes certain pharma and cosmetic companies that could potentially benefit.
For now, these portfolios consist of stock picks, but the team wants to expand the service over time to handle other types of transactions, like shorts, derivatives, perpetuals, long exposure, or even prediction markets — the latter handled through partnerships with companies in that space.
Despite these “takes” seeming like bets on what could happen next in a given market, Murr stresses that this doesn’t make Supertake itself a prediction market.
“We think it’s a novel and very much improved way to create what was previously considered the robo-advisor experience,” he says. “When that came out, it had this amazing vision and direction of allowing people to have digital asset management. We think now is actually the time for that, with AI agents being so widely proliferated.”
“I don’t think this is necessarily a prediction market by any means. The idea of natural language translation into an underlying set of assets feels different in that regard,” he says.
Still, the startup could wade into short-term predictions if a user’s take involves something they believe could happen in the near future, like who might win an election.
“We’re primarily focused on the longer, medium-term holdings today. But that being said, we don’t want to preclude people from building out very hyper short-term strategies that might exist,” Murr adds.
To address people’s concerns over AI managing their money, Supertake’s team says it’s implementing certain guardrails and spend limits. For instance, the AI has no ability to deposit or withdraw funds on a user’s behalf without their explicit consent. There are also drift limits in place so the portfolio stays balanced, plus allow and deny lists (meaning which assets the AI may and may not trade), real-time monitoring for anomalous activity, tools to set trade size limits, and a restriction that keeps agents from seeing the user’s brokerage credentials.
“We view it as somewhat analogous to self-driving cars, actually, where there is a spectrum here of both trust and technological innovations that are happening,” says Murr. “Where a few years ago you may not feel comfortable getting in a car that has lane assist, but today you get in a Waymo, and it’s like nothing. And we think that there’s a very similar progression happening with the agentic finance space, and we’re far further along in the technological spectrum than people think.”
Access to Supertake is still behind a waitlist while in beta, but the founders said they’ve put their money where their mouths are. Murr and Peterson are letting it manage “tens of thousands” and “thousands” of dollars, respectively.
Mignano, meanwhile, says he has Supertake managing “hundreds of thousands” of dollars.
With the new funding, which follows a $2 million pre-seed round, Supertake aims to expand its team in areas like engineering, design, growth marketing, and others. Mignano and Murr are in New York, while Peterson is in the Austin area but commutes to New York at times. The team says it hopes to figure out a hybrid work model as it grows.

articles.title: The RTX 5090’s 16-pin connector just got a free pin-by-pin watchdog — RTX Lens taps Asus Astral, WireView Pro II, and MSI PSU sensors to alert your phone or shut down your PC
articles.text:
The RTX 5090’s 16-pin connector just got a free pin-by-pin watchdog — RTX Lens taps Asus Astral, WireView Pro II, and MSI PSU sensors to alert your phone or shut down your PC
With the right hardware, it compares current at both cable ends and alerts your phone.
A developer known as Codeh4ck released a free, open-source Windows app, RTX Lens, to help assuage melting power connector fears for owners of powerful RTX 5080 and 5090 GPUs. The app can read per-pin current information on Asus Astral cards, the WireView Pro II GPU monitoring device from Thermal Grizzly, and MSI MPG Ai1300TS/Ai1600TS PSUs, enabling an optional shutdown for persistent warnings. It works by reading current at the GPU, PSU, or both ends of the cable, and can even notify you by phone to provide extra protection for your investment.
The project’s README says that the app allows reading of “GPU power, pin currents, and temperatures at a glance.” The per-pin monitoring is the important part here, as the 12V-2x6 connection carries current on six 12V pins with a rating of about 9A, with Asus’s warning at 9.2A, and exceeding the per-pin limit has led to melted connectors. An RTX 5090 is rated at 575W of board power, which is close to the connector’s 600W rating. This led to the app’s construction, the developer says, due to “double paranoia about the 12VHPWR connector melting, since I own 2 5090s.”
For supported Asus ROG Astral RTX 5080 and 5090 GPUs, the app uses the open-source LibreHardwareMonitor library. The WireView Pro II already measures inline at the GPU connector, but the app can read and edit the device’s settings, mirroring the official app’s settings.
The MSI PSUs measure at the PSU side of each connector and reveal per-pin currents for both 12V-2x6 ports, as well as PSU temperature and fan status, although a USB data connection is needed for both the PSUs and the WireView. The project clarifies that “With an Astral or WireView Pro II, you can compare both ends of the cable.” All of the listed hardware has been tested on real devices, the developer says.
| Where RTX Lens gets its readings, per the developer’s README |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Device | Cable end | Per-pin data | Also reads | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Asus ROG Astral RTX 5080, 5090 | GPU | Current | Connector power, current totals | 
| Thermal Grizzly WireView Pro II | Inline at GPU | Current, voltage, power | Cable rating, temps, faults | 
| MSI MPG Ai1300TS, Ai1600TS | PSU (both ports) | Current | PSU temp, fan | 
| Other GeForce RTX cards | None | None | Clocks, temps, usage, VRAM, fans | 
The app allows users to set up warning profiles per device with thresholds and reminders, and optionally a shutdown when a warning persists. This would be used in cases of sustained overcurrent or uneven pin loads on Astral, or WireView device faults. The app’s service initiates a Windows shutdown after a set time, from one second to almost 24 hours. The app can also make performance recordings that are exportable as interactive HTML.
Additionally, it can configure MSI Afterburner Safeguard+ for the MSI PSUs with per-connector alarms and timeouts, emergency low-power profiles, or even a script for delayed shutdowns or optional methods of notification, like email. More customization is available, in this case, as the app can set the PSUs’ fan curves with up to six temperature points.
Phone apps for Android, using a sideloaded APK from GitHub, and the iPhone, through a TestFlight beta or sideloaded with iLoader, are available. The sideloaded iPhone app only shows warnings while it’s open and connected, though. Pairing happens by QR code on the same network, and remote access from outside the network requires a reachable address. The PC also must stay awake, with the service running, for local or remote connections to work. An alternative way to monitor is a read-only iCUE widget for the Corsair Xeneon Edge touchscreen, if you’re so inclined.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The ongoing melting connector problem has led to solutions in the past, including a vibe-coded safeguard that now limits the GPU if a pin current exceeds 9.5A for more than 15 seconds, then shuts down the system if it stays that high. That tool, 12VHPWR Guard, is limited to Asus cards; RTX Lens adds wider device support and more options. Some hardware already works to help here, as MSI’s Ai1600TS cut GPU power after about three minutes in our testing, and Cooler Master’s GPU Shield can scale down an RTX 5090 to 450W, but these are not an option, or the best option, for everyone.
RTX Lens updates have been fast, with five shipped releases in the last week or so, and the maintainer appears motivated to keep development going. The developer says the project is in a “beta-ish phase,” and that “Google Play Store and App Store releases are coming soon, pending approval from Google and Apple.”

articles.title: Windows 11 : Microsoft permet d’additionner la mémoire de plusieurs PC en USB4 pour faire tourner de grosses IA
articles.text:
Microsoft adapte à l’USB4 une technique utilisée dans les centres de données pour accélérer les échanges entre ordinateurs. La fonction sera d’abord proposée en préversion dans le programme Windows Insider.
Trois mini-PC et trois câbles USB4 ont suffi à Microsoft pour faire tourner en local un modèle d’IA de 235 milliards de paramètres. Le moteur d’inférence répartit les poids du modèle et les calculs entre les machines, ce qui permet de dépasser la capacité mémoire d’un seul PC. Pour les faire communiquer, Microsoft utilise leurs ports USB4 et se passe ainsi de cartes réseau spécialisées et de commutateur.
Ce que le RDMA change entre deux PC
Le RDMA, pour Remote Direct Memory Access, permet de transférer des données directement entre les mémoires de deux ordinateurs en court-circuitant une grande partie de la pile réseau. Sous Windows, cette technique passait jusqu’ici par des cartes dédiées, notamment en Ethernet ou en InfiniBand. Microsoft conserve son API NetworkDirect et lui ajoute un module logiciel qui s’appuie sur les anneaux DMA du contrôleur USB4. Ces structures servent à organiser les transferts en limitant les copies effectuées par le logiciel.
C’est surtout le délai de ces échanges qui compte. Avec le parallélisme tensoriel, les machines se partagent les opérations et s’échangent des résultats intermédiaires plusieurs fois par jeton généré. Sur de petits messages, Microsoft mesure un aller-retour de 28 à 50 microsecondes, soit environ le quart du délai observé en UDP sur Ethernet avec la même liaison USB4. En revanche, dans ce type de configuration, passer d’une liaison USB4 à 40 Gbit/s à une liaison à 80 Gbit/s ne réduit pas sensiblement le délai des échanges. Le débit supérieur profite surtout aux transferts plus volumineux.
Ce que donnent les essais de Microsoft, AMD et Intel
Dans son annonce du 19 novembre, publiée à l’occasion de Microsoft Ignite, Microsoft détaille les premiers essais menés dans son laboratoire et chez ses partenaires AMD et Intel. Le géant du logiciel a relié directement trois mini-PC en USB4 à 40 Gbit/s. Chacun embarquait un processeur Ryzen AI Max+ 395, un GPU Radeon 8060S et 128 Go de mémoire unifiée. Sur ce montage, Qwen3-235B-A22B, quantifié sur 4 bits, a réussi à générer environ 18,5 jetons par seconde. Dans ses propres essais sur trois machines, AMD annonce 21,98 jetons par seconde en génération et 117,98 en traitement du prompt.
Côté Intel, c'est GPT-OSS-120B qui a été mis à l'épreuve sur des PC Core Ultra Series 3 équipés de 64 Go de mémoire chacun et reliés en Thunderbolt 4. Dans cette configuration, le modèle ne tenait pas sur une seule machine. Avec un contexte de 1 024 jetons, Intel a mesuré 49,4 jetons par seconde en génération sur trois PC, puis 54,2 sur quatre. La quatrième machine apporte donc un gain de débit inférieur à 10% dans cet essai.
Pour l’instant, Microsoft conseille des PC de test
Microsoft prévoit de proposer RDMA sur USB4 dans le canal Expérimental (plateformes futures) de Windows Insider, sans préciser quand cette préversion sera disponible. La fonction est par contre désactivée par défaut. Pour l’activer, il faudra modifier le registre et passer en mode de signature de test (test signing), ce qui implique de désactiver le démarrage sécurisé du PC (Secure Boot). Microsoft recommande pour l'instant de réserver cette manipulation à des machines de test.
Le montage impose aussi de regarder de près la connectique. Chaque paire de PC doit être reliée par un câble direct, ce qui mobilise déjà trois ports USB4 par machine et six câbles au total dans un groupe de quatre. Le chaînage dégrade nettement les performances. En cas de coupure, c’est à l’application de rétablir la connexion. Encore faut-il qu’elle prenne en charge NetworkDirect. Microsoft a publié une version dérivée de llama.cpp en open source pour montrer comment l’intégrer.
Le projet s’inscrit dans la stratégie de Microsoft pour l’IA locale, déjà engagée avec Project Zenith. Pour passer de la démonstration au bureau, il faudra que d’autres logiciels adoptent NetworkDirect et que la fonction arrive dans une version stable de Windows. Quant à ceux qui veulent déjà tenter l’expérience, ils peuvent commencer par compter les ports USB4 à l’arrière de leurs machines.
Sources : Microsoft et Wccftech

articles.title: British Gas launches new plug-in solar kit starting at £649 offering savings of up to £175 per year, predicting they'll be 'snapped up quickly'
articles.text:
British Gas launches new plug-in solar kit — two 465W panels cost £649 and could save up to £175 per year
Engineer setup is an option for an extra £100
- British Gas is launching a new plug-in solar kit for the UK
- You get two 465W solar panels with a ground-mounted bracket and an inverter for £649
- The kit comes with installation by a British Gas engineer for £749, and you can have an outdoor power socket added for an extra £250 on top of that
British Gas has got on board with plug-in solar with the announcement that it will sell kits starting from £649.
As an alternative to a traditional roof-based installation, plug-in solar has become popular in the UK since the initial batch of kits became legal at the end of the summer. Utility suppliers like Octopus are already on board, and British Gas is now joining the plug-in club.
The base kit with two Perlight PowerPlug 465W solar panels is the most affordable option priced at £649, coming with a ground-mounted bracket and an inverter. You can add a hundred quid on top to buy this kit with setup by a British Gas engineer included (so it's £749).
If you'd like an outdoor power socket to go with your kit, that's also a choice here, and it'll cost £999 to have an engineer visit, which provides the socket alongside installing the plug-in panels.
The Perlight PowerPlug panels measure 176 x 114cm and British Gas claims that a pair of panels represents a chance to save between £147 to £175 on a typical energy bill over the course of a full year.
Analysis: solar boom
It's good to see another energy supplier offering plug-in solar, as not everyone can afford a full rooftop installation, or even has permission for one (some folks are renting, of course). Some roofs don't suit solar panels, too, so it's good to have choices — and I like that British Gas is offering an engineer installation service too, for those who might be less confident on that side of the equation.
The potential savings that British Gas calculates means you could make back the money you paid for a basic kit in around 4.5 years, going by the leanest estimate of solar energy production. Naturally, how much you'll make from your two panels will vary considerably based on their location (ideally south-facing with no shading, which is what British Gas has assumed here), and how much sunlight the panels are getting.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
One caveat about buying plug-in solar panels right now is that it's not exactly the ideal time of year in the UK. We're just entering the three months of winter in which the sun is at its weakest, and the days are shortest, but still, British Gas expects demand to be high and "initial stock [is] predicted to be snapped up quickly". You can't help but think that the timing of the legalization of plug-in solar for the UK could have been better (as in at the start of summer rather than the end of the season).
It'd be no surprise if plug-in solar gained some serious momentum in the UK, mind, in 2027. After all, rooftop solar had a record 2026 with 270,000 installations in the UK, and on the other side of the Atlantic, as a recent Bloomberg report made clear, "plug-in solar is sweeping the US," with a lot of folks adopting these panels due to increasingly expensive electricity — more than 10 states now allow plug-in or 'guerrilla' solar legally. We're seeing electricity prices notching up in the UK as well, alongside all the more recent noises being made about possible power cuts as part of the government's 'Be Ready' campaign.
The attraction of plug-in solar is that it's an investment which is much more readily recouped when compared to a full rooftop installation, and you can also take the panels with you should you move house — making it less of a commitment in that respect, too.
Plug-in solar and battery systems are also waiting in the wings, and should be legal and ready to go on sale in the UK next year, too.

articles.title: iPhone 18e também pode ser lançado antes da versão base
articles.text:
iPhone 18e também pode ser lançado antes da versão base
Apple pode separar modelos mais acessíveis e ter três lançamentos de smartphones no ano.
Neste ano vimos, pela primeira vez, a Apple separar o lançamento dos iPhones base das versões Pro, em evento marcado também pela estreia do iPhone Duo. Agora, rumores apontam que até mesmo o iPhone 18e deve chegar às lojas antes dos demais modelos da linha.
A empresa estaria planejando o anúncio de produtos mais “acessíveis” no começo do ano que vem, numa janela entre fevereiro e março, enquanto o iPhone 18 chegaria em uma segunda leva, ainda que também no primeiro semestre.
A previsão, compartilhada pelo jornalista Mark Gurman, da Bloomberg, encontra eco em vazamentos recentes que indicam que o novo CEO da companhia, John Ternus, pretende quebrar a tradição de um evento gigante em setembro para todos os principais modelos da marca.
Caso o calendário se confirme, o iPhone 18 será o último da linha a estrear: os iPhone 18 Pro e 18 Pro Max, além do primeiro iPhone dobrável da Apple, foram apresentados ainda em setembro de 2026.
Segundo o rumor, a ideia é concentrar os primeiros meses do ano em produtos mais acessíveis. Entre fevereiro e março, a principal novidade seria o iPhone 18e, além de um novo iPad de entrada e a segunda versão do MacBook Neo.
O iPhone 18 tradicional deve aparecer pouco depois, provavelmente em um evento separado. Na mesma janela, deve chegar o MacBook Air, o iPhone Air 2, iPad Air com tela OLED, novos iPad Pro e novo MacBook Air.
O iPhone 18e pode aparecer com o chip A20 e 9 GB de RAM, contra os 8 GB da geração anterior, e trazer melhorias na câmera. As especificações de hardware esperadas para o iPhone 18 são semelhantes, assim como um possível aumento de US$ 100 a US$ 200 no preço nos Estados Unidos.
No iPad a atualização deve ser mais significativa. O modelo atual ainda usa o chip A16 e é o último dispositivo da Apple sem suporte ao Apple Intelligence. A próxima geração deve migrar para o A19, acompanhado por 8 GB de RAM e outras melhorias em conectividade, como suporte ao Wi-Fi 7.
A Apple também prepara dois Macs para o período: um novo MacBook Neo com chip A19 Pro, da geração do iPhone 17 Pro, e um MacBook Air com o chip M7, segundo o GSMArena. O notebook deve estrear a nova geração de processadores da companhia, esperada para o ano que vem, após um lançamento limitado no M6.
Entre os tablets, o primeiro semestre ainda deve trazer um iPad Air com tela OLED e novos iPad Pro. Estes últimos são esperados com o chip M6, sucedendo os modelos com M5 lançados em 2025.
Outro aparelho previsto para algum desses lançamento é o ultrafino iPhone Air 2, que tem a dura missão de corrigir, frente ao público, a péssima bateria do primeiro. O dispositivo também pode receber uma câmera extra ultrawide para complementar o conjunto, que conta com uma principal de 48 MP.
Depois da sequência de atualizações, o foco da Apple deve mudar para a nova geração de iPhones, encabeçado pelo suposto iPhone 20. A geração, que marca também os 20 anos de iPhone, deve trazer uma reformulação mais significativa em design, além de uma tela frontal com as quatro bordas curvas.
Os aparelhos também são esperados com chips produzidos em um processo de 2 nanômetros de segunda geração e uma nova versão do modem desenvolvido pela própria Apple.
Segundo Gurman, a Apple também prepara para o período novos Apple Watch, óculos inteligentes e AirPods equipados com câmeras.

articles.title: Surveillance pricing uses our personal data to make us pay more
articles.text:
“It costs what it costs” is a mindset I’ve found useful when encountering a sizable, but highly necessary or desired, expense. The sentiment encourages me to accept the price because that’s the accepted value of the gadget, app, or service that I really need or want.
But with surveillance pricing, that comfort is no longer a given. I could end up paying more for my TV because of where I am or more for a software subscription because of my age.
Surveillance pricing leverages data collected from our web history, smart devices, and apps with the goal of getting us to pay more. That obfuscates the value of products, challenges smart shopping and budgets, and makes it harder for people to get products and services at a fair price.
Surveillance pricing versus dynamic pricing
Surveillance pricing, according to the nonprofit Electronic Privacy Information Center (EPIC), is an algorithmic pricing practice that charges individuals or groups of individuals different prices “for the same goods or services.”
“The goal of surveillance pricing is to infer the highest price that the customer is willing to pay, based on consumers’ personal data and other market data,” EPIC explains.
Instacart previously practiced surveillance pricing, also called personalized pricing. In 2025, Consumer Reports found that, “based on how much Instacart says the typical household of four spends on groceries, the average price variations observed could translate into a cost swing of about $1,200 per year.” Instacart has since removed its surveillance pricing tools.
Dynamic pricing, or surge pricing, differs from surveillance pricing in that, instead of relying on consumer data, it uses changing market trends, like supply and demand, inventory levels, and competitor pricing, to set prices.
While dynamic pricing may charge you more for an Uber ride when it’s very busy, surveillance pricing can feel less reasonable.
For instance, Target’s app was previously accused of using location data to charge users $100 more for a TV if they bought it while standing inside a Target store. At the time, Target said that it would match lower prices presented by customers, but many customers wouldn’t think to look for pricing discrepancies. In another instance from 2012, Orbitz was found to more prominently feature expensive hotels to people using macOS. Companies often dispute whether their practices truly qualify as surveillance pricing. But these examples all reflect companies using data about their customers to influence the prices they show them.

articles.title: Log out after using WhatsApp Web to prevent account hijacking: MHA advises users
articles.text:
Log out after using WhatsApp Web to prevent account hijacking: MHA advises users
According to an advisory issued by the National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit of the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre, active WhatsApp Web sessions could be misused to access private messages, impersonate users, and carry out cyber fraud.
The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has issued a cybersecurity advisory cautioning users about the potential misuse of authenticated WhatsApp Web sessions to gain access to their accounts.
The advisory, dated November 18, was issued by the National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit of the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), under the MHA.
The advisory warned that leaving accounts logged in on office computers or shared devices could expose them to unauthorised access. This could allow malicious actors to read private messages, send messages while impersonating the account holder, access contacts and group conversations, and exploit trusted identities to carry out fraud, phishing and social-engineering attacks.
The advisory recommends that organisations avoid using WhatsApp Web on office computers, particularly in official and sensitive environments. Users have been advised against exchanging government, financial, confidential or other sensitive information through WhatsApp Web sessions on computers.
The I4C has cautioned that simply closing a browser window or tab should not be treated as logging out of WhatsApp Web. Users must manually terminate their sessions after completing their work and avoid leaving accounts permanently logged in.
If access is unavoidable, the agency recommends using 'incognito' or 'private browsing' mode on a trusted computer, followed by a manual logout. Users have also been advised against accessing WhatsApp Web through cyber cafes, public kiosks, hotel business centres, borrowed computers, or other untrusted systems.
The advisory further recommends keeping devices, operating systems, browsers and security software updated, avoiding suspicious downloads, and monitoring accounts for unexpected messages or unusual activity.
WhatsApp Web sessions targeted in 'Boss Scam'
The latest warning comes amid a rise in WhatsApp-linked account takeover fraud. In an August 7 advisory, the MHA warned corporates and finance professionals about a campaign known as the 'Boss Scam' or CEO impersonation fraud.
According to the ministry's statement published on the Press Information Bureau, fraudsters circulated malicious ZIP files disguised as account statements and regulatory communications, using names such as 'Statement of Account.zip', 'RBI.zip' and 'MCA.zip'.
The files contained malicious Windows executable (.exe) and Dynamic Link Library (.dll) files. Once extracted and executed on a Windows computer, the malware could compromise the device and hijack an active WhatsApp Web session.
Attackers subsequently used compromised accounts to circulate the same malicious files to contacts and groups. In more advanced cases, they impersonated senior executives and instructed finance employees to make urgent transfers to fraudulent bank accounts.
The MHA said it had alerted more than 58,000 potential victims through SMS messages sent under the header 'I4CMHA-G' in the preceding 30 days. More than 10,000 Indians had been protected through coordinated interventions, including the blocking of malicious infrastructure through the government's Sahyog Portal.
The ministry also said it had shared malware-related threat intelligence with the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), Microsoft Defender, and Indian cybersecurity companies, including Quick Heal, K7 Computing and Net Protector.
In its June 22 advisory, the I4C had first flagged the emerging 'Boss Scam' threat, warning that compromised WhatsApp accounts could be used to target employees with fraudulent financial instructions.
The MHA has advised users to regularly review the 'Linked Devices' section in WhatsApp and remove unfamiliar or inactive sessions. It has also urged companies to independently verify urgent payment instructions received through messaging platforms.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: L’écran verrouillé de l’iPhone Duo cache une petite surprise, mais elle est désactivée pour l’instant
articles.text:
L’informateur pdfu a exhumé du code d’iOS 27.1 une fonction baptisée « colonne de complications », pensée pour l’écran verrouillé de l’iPhone Duo. Elle alignerait deux widgets circulaires le long du bord droit, en plus de la rangée déjà disponible en bas de l’écran. Apple l’a testée puis désactivée, et rien n’indique si elle reverra le jour.
Deux pastilles entre la lampe torche et les barres de réseau
La colonne se loge sur la tranche droite de l’écran verrouillé, au-dessus des raccourcis lampe torche et appareil photo, sous les indicateurs Wi-Fi et cellulaire. Ses deux widgets reprennent la taille de ceux du bas de l’écran, et les deux zones pourraient s’afficher ensemble d’après la fuite. Aujourd’hui, l’écran verrouillé du pliable affiche l’heure en haut, une rangée de widgets le long du bord inférieur et deux commandes dans l’angle inférieur droit, qui acceptent déjà d’autres raccourcis que la lampe et l’appareil photo.
 Apple has tested a “complication column” for iPhone Duo’s Lock Screen. It fits two circular widgets along the right edge.
Flag: SpringBoard/Ionic (disabled). First seen in iOS 27.1, with no code changes since. https://t.co/orjOuvM1Xs
— pdfu (@itspdfu) November 22, 2026
Le réglage interne qui pilote la fonction, estampillé « SpringBoard/Ionic », reste désactivé. Le code n’a plus évolué depuis son apparition dans iOS 27.1, la version livrée avec le téléphone puis mise à jour pour lui seul fin octobre. Rien ne permet de trancher entre un chantier en cours et une piste abandonnée. Le même pdfu avait déjà tiré du code cinq cadrans cachés pour le mode En veille du pliable, dont un Snoopy, fin septembre.
Une idée d’horloger pour un écran grand format
Le mot complication vient de l’horlogerie, où il désigne tout ce qu’un cadran affiche en plus de l’heure, et l’Apple Watch l’a fait entrer dans le vocabulaire de la marque. Sur la montre, ces pastilles livrent météo, anneaux d’activité ou prochain rendez-vous d’un coup d’œil. Les widgets de l’écran verrouillé, arrivés sur iPhone avec iOS 16 en 2022, en descendent en droite ligne, au point que les développeurs les fabriquent avec le même outil que les cadrans de la montre. L’iPad, lui, les range dans une colonne latérale depuis iPadOS 17, en 2023.
La fuite ne précise pas si la colonne vise l’écran externe de 5,4 pouces, la dalle interne de 7,6 pouces ou les deux. Le grand écran, largement vide une fois le téléphone déplié, offre l’espace le plus évident, et une colonne de pastilles l’occuperait sans gêner l’heure ni les notifications. De quoi garder la météo, le niveau de batterie ou les prochains rendez-vous du calendrier à portée de regard, sans rien déverrouiller.
Apple retouche son pliable au rythme des mises à jour depuis la sortie du 23 octobre. La deuxième bêta d’iOS 27.3 vient d’ajouter le déverrouillage par le visage via la caméra de l’écran externe et le verrouillage automatique au pliage, deux absents remarqués du lancement. À 2 339 euros l’appareil, chaque fonction dormante compte : celle-ci ne demande qu’un réglage à basculer, et l’écran verrouillé du pliable y gagnerait une disposition encore jamais vue sur un iPhone.

articles.title: GTA 6's First Post-Launch Patch Fixes Crashes, Stuck Weather, and Autosaves
articles.text:
Monday, November 23rd 2026
GTA 6's First Post-Launch Patch Fixes Crashes, Stuck Weather, and Autosaves
Rockstar has released the first post-launch patch for GTA 6. It is quite a small one, weighing 603.8 MB on the PS5 and 1.6 GB on the Xbox Series X|S. The patch started rolling out on November 23, just four days after the game's record-breaking launch. The patch notes have been posted on Rockstar's support site, and they mention some key bug fixes along with other general improvements. The patch shows up as version 01.002.002 on PlayStation and 1.0.2.2 on Xbox.
The update claims to fix several crashes, autosaves that weren't working correctly, as well as a bug that caused weather to stay stuck for long stretches. That last one was making the rounds on X and Reddit recently, as many players were surprised at the lack of rain in the game. Turns out, it was a weather bug that has now been fixed by Rockstar. Other fixes include phone calls that failed to trigger, which often stranded players, unable to progress the story. Rockstar has also sorted out a bug that kept players from losing their Wanted level, and a couple of other fixes related to the gym and fences. Curiously, Rockstar's notes don't mention the infamous red barn money glitch northeast of Hamlet, with players reporting that it still works after the update. Rockstar doesn't list any performance changes for this patch, so all consoles are still stuck at 30 FPS for the foreseeable future.
Source:
				Rockstar Games			
	
	
	
		
	
		
3 Comments on GTA 6's First Post-Launch Patch Fixes Crashes, Stuck Weather, and Autosaves
It's small relative to the total installed size of the game (212GB on PS5, 225GB on Xbox X|S). 600MB represents about 0.26% of the total storage requirement.
CDs debuted in 1982 so 44 years ago.
Obviously videogame titles have increased in size over time. Here's one example:
www.ign.com/articles/2019/10/25/every-call-of-duty-install-size-compared-from-2003-to-modern-warfare
Game site Polygon wrote that recently released CoD: Modern Warfare 4 requires about 300GB.
www.polygon.com/gta-6-storage-size-install-ps5-xbox-series-x/
While GTA VI is big, it's by no means the storage hog champion. I'm sure a judicious web search will give you the answer to that.
Note that Microsoft Flight Simulator with add-ons is considerably larger. The 2020 edition is about 400GB, the 2024 edition (with more streamed content) is still about 300GB.
www.simulatorhardware.com/learn/how-much-storage-does-msfs-2020-need/
The apocryphal story behind the audio CD is that it needed to be 74 minutes to contain the entirety of Beethoven's Ninth Symphony on one disc. Today people are STREAMING lossless audio over the Interweb to their phones. Times have changed...

articles.title: “El error fue corregido”: Elon Musk apoya regreso de Jensen Huang como CEO de Nvidia
articles.text:
Elon Musk afirmó en X que “el error ha sido corregido” después de que NVIDIA restituyera a Jensen Huang como presidente ejecutivo y miembro de su consejo de administración. La decisión, efectiva de inmediato, devuelve al cofundador al mando de la empresa tras una crisis que abrió interrogantes sobre seguridad nacional y gobierno corporativo.
La restitución fue aprobada por unanimidad por el consejo de NVIDIA. La junta explicó que adoptó la determinación después de varias reuniones con Huang y de recibir información de altos funcionarios del Gobierno de Estados Unidos. Con esos elementos, afirmó que su regreso no implica un riesgo para la seguridad nacional.
La publicación de Musk llegó después del anuncio corporativo y se sumó a las expresiones previas de respaldo que había manifestado para el regreso del directivo. El propietario de Tesla y SpaceX había apoyado públicamente la vuelta de Huang en medio del debate por su salida y la posterior conducción interina de la compañía.
El consejo dijo que la restitución beneficia a accionistas y empleados de Nvidia
Harvey C. Jones, presidente del consejo, sostuvo que los directores consideraron que Huang es la persona adecuada para encabezar nuevamente a la empresa. “El Consejo de Administración considera que Jensen es la persona idónea para liderar NVIDIA y que su reincorporación redunda en beneficio de nuestros accionistas, empleados, socios y clientes”, señaló Jones en el comunicado de la compañía.
La decisión devuelve a Huang tres funciones de forma simultánea: presidente, director ejecutivo y miembro del consejo. Jones continuará al frente de la presidencia del órgano de administración, mientras que Colette Kress dejará la dirección ejecutiva interina y seguirá como directora financiera.
Kress había asumido el liderazgo temporal durante el período de ausencia de Huang. El consejo agradeció su trabajo en esa función, en un momento sensible para una compañía que ocupa un lugar central en el mercado de procesadores avanzados destinados a sistemas de inteligencia artificial.
La empresa no precisó qué funcionarios del Gobierno estadounidense aportaron información al proceso ni detalló el contenido de esas conversaciones. Sin embargo, subrayó que la conclusión sobre la ausencia de riesgo para la seguridad nacional fue determinante para el voto unánime de sus directores.
Huang prometió colaborar con la investigación independiente
En su declaración, Jensen Huang calificó su regreso como un honor y dijo que retomaba la responsabilidad con “la mayor humildad y un compromiso renovado”. También agradeció al consejo, a Kress, al equipo ejecutivo, a los empleados, a los accionistas y a los socios de la empresa.
“Estoy deseando volver al trabajo”, afirmó Huang. El ejecutivo vuelve a encabezar una firma cuya evolución se convirtió en un indicador seguido de cerca por inversores, fabricantes de equipos tecnológicos, centros de datos y desarrolladores de modelos de inteligencia artificial.
La restitución, no obstante, no pone fin a las pesquisas abiertas alrededor del caso. NVIDIA recordó que había creado previamente un comité formado solo por directores independientes para investigar reportes según los cuales Huang habría sido blanco de una operación de inteligencia extranjera.
Ese comité contrató asesoramiento jurídico independiente y continuará con su labor, de acuerdo con el comunicado. Huang se comprometió a cooperar plenamente con la investigación, una condición que la empresa incluyó expresamente al informar su retorno al puesto.
La continuidad del proceso marca una separación entre la evaluación que permitió la vuelta inmediata del ejecutivo y la revisión interna de los hechos que motivaron la apertura del expediente. El consejo indicó que había quedado conforme con la franqueza de Huang y con su capacidad para dirigir la compañía, aunque no dio detalles adicionales sobre las conversaciones.
NVIDIA creó un comité para controlar riesgos de seguridad nacional
El consejo señaló la creación reciente de un Comité de Seguridad Nacional y Control de Exportaciones. El nuevo grupo está integrado exclusivamente por consejeros independientes y tendrá la tarea de supervisar el cumplimiento de las reglas comerciales y los riesgos vinculados a la seguridad nacional.
Según la empresa, el comité consulta con abogados especializados en esa materia. Esos asesores, a su vez, podrán contratar a otros expertos para apoyar el trabajo de revisión. La estructura refuerza el control sobre un sector sujeto a restricciones comerciales y geopolíticas por la relevancia estratégica de los chips de alto rendimiento.
Asimismo, NVIDIA inició la búsqueda de un director de Cumplimiento Normativo. La persona elegida deberá supervisar las obligaciones regulatorias en toda la empresa e informar al Comité de Nominaciones y Gobierno Corporativo.
La compañía afirmó que seguirá colaborando con las investigaciones y consultas gubernamentales en curso. La vuelta de Huang, por lo tanto, se produce mientras permanecen activos los mecanismos internos de control y las gestiones con autoridades estadounidenses.

articles.title: Smartphone in der Prüfung: Mit dieser Methode ließ Südkorea Schummler auffliegen
articles.text:
Smartphone in der Prüfung: Mit dieser Methode ließ Südkorea Schummler auffliegen
In Südkorea ist die landesweite Hochschulaufnahmeprüfung nicht nur im Kalender angehender Student:innen ein wichtiger Termin. Für die sogenannte Suneung, eine achtstündige Abfolge aus mehreren Examen, versetzt die Regierung das Land in den Stillstand, wie die BBC berichtet. Demnach dürfen Bauarbeiter nicht arbeiten und sogar Flugzeuge zumindest zwischenzeitlich nicht abheben. Alles, um die optimalen Voraussetzungen für die Prüflinge zu schaffen. Der Hintergrund ist durchaus ernst. Denn das Ergebnis dieser Prüfungen habe „erheblichen Einfluss auf die Verteilung von Chancen und Ressourcen“, wird Präsident Lee Jae Myung von der BBC zitiert. Sprich: Das Ergebnis kann die späteren Berufschancen beeinflussen.
Entsprechend ist es wichtig, dass es während der Prüfung nicht nur ruhig zugeht, sondern auch fair. Das heißt: keine Smartphones und keine Hilfe von KI‑Assistenzen. Weil Vertrauen gut, Kontrolle aber besser ist, hatten südkoreanische Behörden im Vorfeld Maßnahmen angekündigt, um Schummler auffliegen zu lassen.
111 Prüflinge mit unerlaubten Geräten festgestellt
Und dabei waren sie offenbar erfolgreich. Laut Bericht mit Verweis auf das Bildungsministerium habe man 111 angehende Student:innen mit unerlaubten smarten Geräten erwischt. Fünf seien demnach auf frischer Tat bei der Nutzung smarter Geräte ertappt worden. Mit einer neuen Methode wollten die Behörden Schummler auffliegen lassen. So hatten die Behörden kurzfristig angekündigt, zwischen 8:00 und 15:00 Uhr drei landesweite Notfallalarme auszulösen. Hierzulande kennt man das vielleicht vom bundesweiten Warntag. Smartphones spielen dann einen lauten Warnton ab, egal ob sie auf laut geschaltet sind, oder nicht. Ausnahmen gibt es nur, wenn sie – wie es vermutlich bei der Prüfung vorgesehen ist – abgeschaltet werden.
Zudem mussten die Schüler:innen die Knöpfe an ihren Kleidungsstücken verhüllen, um den Einsatz kleiner Kameras auszuschließen. Die Behörden führten zudem Kontrollen der Brillen durch. Smarte Brillen sind schließlich nicht immer auf den ersten Blick von einer normalen Brille zu unterscheiden.
Den Entschluss zu diesen Maßnahmen fassten die Behörden in Südkorea, nachdem der beste Absolvent der Prüfung zum Steuerberater zugab, bei dem Examen mithilfe einer kleinen Kamera, eines Smartphones und eingesetzter KI‑Tools betrogen zu haben. Solche Gadgets stellen das Bildungsministerium vermehrt vor schwierige Aufgaben. Demnach hätte man zuvor bereits vier Schüler:innen der Mittelschule und Highschool dabei erwischt, wie sie mithilfe von KI-Gadgets bei Prüfungen mogelten.
Der Einsatz von KI zum Schummeln bei Prüfungen erschüttere die Grundordnung der Gesellschaft, „indem er Fairness und Vertrauen untergräbt“, so Präsident Lee.

articles.title: Post-quantum cryptography startup Q.security launches with $11.5M in funding
articles.text:
Post-quantum cryptography startup Q.security launches with $11.5M in funding
Post-quantum cryptography startup Q Security Inc. formally launched today with $11.5 million in new funding for a platform designed to take enterprises from discovery through to completion of their quantum-safe migrations.
Founded this year, Q.security offers a remediation platform that runs the move to post-quantum cryptography as one coordinated program. The company argues that security teams need business context to decide which cryptographic findings to address first, since the time and resources available for the work are limited.
At the core of the Q.security offering is a map of an organization’s business structure and applications. Findings from the cryptographic inventory are tied back to that map, with the highest-risk assets put at the front of the queue.
Teams are said to be able to investigate exposure and work through remediation using a conversational artificial intelligence interface. Through integrations with existing cybersecurity and infrastructure tools, the platform drives fixes to completion using AI-guided runbooks, ticketing and automation.
Once a fix is in place, Q.security verifies that it works. Monitoring of the organization’s cryptographic posture then continues as standards and threats change, an approach the company claims lets security teams reduce risk faster and at lower cost.
“Quantum computing is making cryptographic risk an urgent and ongoing business priority,” said Guy Peer, co-founder and chief executive of Q.security, who previously co-founded Unbound Security and led its research and development through its acquisition by Coinbase Global Inc., announced in 2021.
Peer’s co-founder, Nir Steinherz, was director of product at Coinbase and vice president of strategy and product at Unbound Security. He was also a senior vice president at Citigroup Inc.’s Security Innovation Center, where he led secure digital banking initiatives for more than 100 million customers. The pair are said to have led a cryptographic migration protecting hundreds of billions of dollars in assets.
The funding is intended to support Q.security as it brings its platform to enterprise customers through direct sales and channel partners.
Castle Island Ventures led the seed round, with New York Life Ventures, Coinbase Ventures, Fin Capital, SBI US Gateway Fund and Ground Up Ventures also participating.
Matt Walsh, general partner at Castle Island Ventures, said enterprises know they need to prepare for the day quantum computers can break current encryption. With harvest-now, decrypt-later data collection already under way, “the challenge is determining how to prioritize the migration across business and technology environments,” he added.

articles.title: Elon Musk and others rejoice as Jensen Huang is reinstated at Nvidia amid scandal
articles.text:
A handful of tech CEOs, including Elon Musk, are celebrating Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia. Despite being caught in three affairs — including one with an alleged Chinese spy that has triggered multiple congressional investigations over national security concerns — Huang was reinstated as CEO and president of Nvidia on Monday morning.
“The mistake has been corrected,” Tesla and SpaceX leader Elon Musk wrote on X about Huang’s return.
Musk had been among the most vocal tech leaders to advocate for Huang.
“I think it’s like kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak, and it just doesn’t seem like a good thing for shareholders,” Musk said last week at the DealBook Summit.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman had taken a more neutral stance, commenting last week, “It’s hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen.”
Altman had experienced a similar situation when he was ousted as CEO of OpenAI, then reinstated days later. After the announcement that Huang would return, Altman simply posted, “Jensen!” Many other tech CEOs have similarly refrained from commenting on the matter, given the shifting politics surrounding Huang’s ouster and reinstatement, as well as the national security concerns at the center of the controversy.
In addition to Musk, Binance co-founder and former CEO Changpeng Zhao (CZ), who served prison time for failing to stop criminal activity on the Binance crypto exchange, is also supportive of Huang.
“Glad to see @JensenHuang back,” CZ posted on X with a clapping hands emoji.
Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, who had been among 200,000 signatories on an open letter calling for Huang’s reinstatement, wrote on X, “Jensen’s return will be a demonstration of American resiliency to corporate, political and journalistic missteps.”
Another signatory on the open letter, former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick, who had similarly been driven out of the company he founded after scandals, also voiced his support for Huang on X.
When Nvidia’s stock tanked in reaction to Huang’s ousting, billionaire hedge fund manager Bill Ackman said he believes that the Nvidia board was “not acting in the best interest of shareholders nor in a manner consistent with their fiduciary duties.” As Nvidia’s stock began to rebound Monday morning, Ackman wrote, “The wisdom of the crowd prevails.”
The attitude toward Huang’s return is not as celebratory outside of the tech industry. Across the political spectrum, some elected officials are skeptical about President Donald Trump’s claims that Huang’s return does not threaten national security.
“No national security risk? Based on what?” wrote Senator John Cornyn (R-TX).
Senator Pete Ricketts (R-NB) added, “Nvidia’s decision today doesn’t excuse Jensen Huang from testifying before Congress. It also doesn’t absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips. I look forward to Mr. Huang coming to the Senate in December.”
Huang is still expected to testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3, as well as privately before three House committees.

articles.title: MacBook modder turns Apple’s Force Touch trackpad into a speaker using haptic engine — MacBook ‘talks’ using only vibrations from the motor, can play speech, tones, and even music
articles.text:
MacBook modder turns Apple’s Force Touch trackpad into a speaker using haptic engine — MacBook ‘talks’ using only vibrations from the motor, can play speech, tones, and even music
There's a remote chance this could be useful one day, if all your other audio output options failed simultaneously.
The MacBook's Force Touch trackpad is considered one of the crown jewels among Apple's laptop technologies. Now Cody Collier, AKA os6 on GitHub, has devised another way to make use of Apple's trackpad design, albeit an unusual and probably not very useful one. The trackpad's haptic engine can be used to make it work as a speaker using Collier's No Speaker software. Want to see and hear it for yourself before installing? There's a demo video below mixing speech, tones, and music playback through a MacBook trackpad.
As indicated in the intro, Apple's Force Touch trackpad has many fans, largely because of its smooth and solid glass surface with consistent and accurate tactile feedback driven by haptics, making it a step up from traditional clattering 'diving board' mechanical alternatives. The haptics that make it feel so responsive can also produce sounds, Collier found, after its haptic vibration frequencies were manipulated into the human hearing range.
"There's no speaker in a MacBook trackpad, just a small haptic motor that taps the glass so you feel a click," Collier explains on the GitHub project page. "No Speaker drives that motor up to 4,000 times a second, fast enough to make sound you can hear, and turns it into a voice. It talks, sings, raps, and becomes an instrument under your finger."
In the video, Collier shows the trackpad being used to play a melody, and as a simple drum machine with kick, snare, and high hats programmed on a 16-step grid. If for some reason you can't play the demo video for yourself, suffice to say No Speaker audio quality is pretty terrible. The nearest approximation to the trackpad's output quality might be the legendary but ancient Speak & Spell with a severely damaged speaker.
The GitHub page contains links to the Mac software and command-line examples to test on your trackpad. Passing parameters to the installed nospeaker command lets you send text strings for it to speak, adjust the No Speaker voice, play test tones, and switch between various UI modes.
To have some no speaker fun with this project, you can run it yourself and fiddle with the input parameters and settings. It has been tested on a MacBook Pro (Mac17,10) with M5 Max and macOS 27.2.1. The author notes the Force Touch trackpad first appeared in MacBooks starting in 2015, so it may work on anything from then onwards. macOS 12 or later on Apple Silicon, or macOS 13 or later on Intel, are also essentials. The app is smart enough to alert a user that there is no Force Touch trackpad present if they attempt to run it on such a machine.
The MacBook Force Touch trackpad isn't the first device or component that has been coaxed into audio playback duties contrary to its designed purpose. Tech tinkerers have previously played music on floppy drive motors and used hard drive actuators as speakers. Another example of out-of-scope hacking on a modern MacBook was the use of the hidden ‘LidAngleSensor’ API to make opening and closing the lid sound like a creaky door being adjusted.

articles.title: „Man ist als Sicherheitsnetz da“: Was der Job als Fluglotse für Lieferdrohnen mit sich bringt
articles.text:
„Man ist als Sicherheitsnetz da“: Was der Job als Fluglotse für Lieferdrohnen mit sich bringt
Als Trevor Wischnewsky hörte, dass in seiner Nachbarschaft in Texas Pizza und Sushi per Drohne ausgeliefert sollten, stand sein Entschluss fest. „Das war unglaublich faszinierend“, sagt er. „Ich wollte einfach sofort ein Teil davon sein.“ Und es klappte: Mittlerweile trägt Wischnewsky den Titel RPIC, also „Remote Pilot in Command“ und ist bei der Firma FlyTrex tätig.
Was der Job als Fluglotse für Drohnen mit sich bringt
Ein RPIC ist so etwas wie ein Fluglotse. Doch statt Flugzeuge sind diese Art von Piloten für Flotten von Hexakopter-Drohnen zuständig. Die Drohnen liefern Fracht zu Haushalten und Unternehmen in einem Umkreis von knapp fünf Kilometern. Wischnewsky sorgt nicht nur für den sicheren Transport der FlyTrex-Pakete, sondern stimmt sich auch mit den anderen Anbietern wie Zipline, Amazon und Alphabets Wing ab. Sie alle bevölkern mit wachsenden Schwärmen von Lieferdrohnen den Himmel über Dallas.
Ein kleiner Rückblick auf Wischnewskys Einstieg: Als er sich bei FlyTrex bewarb, absolvierte er gerade eine Ausbildung zum Berufspiloten und Fluglehrer. Er war bereits von der Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) als Drohnenpilot zertifiziert. Das Unternehmen verlangt diese Qualifikation. Außerdem ist ein mehrwöchiger, von der FAA anerkannter Schulungskurs erforderlich. Damit soll sichergestellt werden, dass eine Pilotin oder ein Pilot auch darauf vorbereitet ist, bei Bedarf selbst die Drohne zu steuern. Ansonsten überwacht Wischnewsky aber den Lieferprozess vom FlyTrex-Einsatzzentrum aus mithilfe von Daten aus GPS, Lasern und einer Reihe von Sensoren.
Für Drohnenpiloten gilt es, der Automatisierung zu vertrauen
Angesichts seiner Ausbildung als Berufspilot war es für Wischnewsky anfangs die größte Herausforderung, der Technologie zu vertrauen. „Im Bereich der bemannten Flugzeuge sagt man dir: ‚Vertraue der Automatisierung nicht‘“, sagt er. Der Großraum Dallas-Fort Worth ist jedoch ein Testgelände für das Verkehrsmanagement unbemannter Flugsysteme (UTM) – ein Netzwerk, das es autonomen Drohnen von FlyTrex und seinen Mitbewerbern ermöglicht, ihre Koordinaten in Echtzeit auszutauschen. So sollen Kollisionen auch außerhalb der Sichtweite des Piloten vermieden werden. Sobald Wischnewsky sich vergewissert hat, dass eine Drohne flugbereit ist, ihr Flugweg frei ist und die Wetterbedingungen gut sind, übernimmt UTM den Rest.

Die Fähigkeit, unter Druck ruhig zu bleiben
Wenn viel Betrieb ist, hat Wischnewsky bis zu zehn Drohnen gleichzeitig im Blick. „Man ist als Sicherheitsnetz da“, sagt er. Aber auch die beste Automatisierung ändert nichts daran, dass bei den Verantwortlichen ein ausgeprägtes Situationsbewusstsein vorhanden sein muss.
Vor allem das Wetter ist eine Gefahr. Wischnewsky erinnert sich an einen besonders stressigen Tag: Eine Drohne war erst seit wenigen Sekunden in der Luft, als der Wind so plötzlich auffrischte, dass er eingreifen musste. Er brachte sie sicher zurück und verhinderte so, dass die beförderte Eistorte auf den Bürgersteig prallte.

articles.title: Ionic Wealth secures Rs 177 Cr from Angel One, others
articles.text:
Ionic Wealth secures Rs 177 Cr from Angel One, others
The wealthtech platform will use the funds to expand its portfolio of services, technology, and footprint in India and beyond.
Ionic Wealth, a wealthtech platform and a subsidiary of Angel One, has raised Rs 177 crore in strategic funding to accelerate its growth trajectory. The funding was led by Angel One and marquee families.
This takes the company's cumulative funding to Rs 466 crore. According to a statement, all investors from the previous round also participated in the latest round, comprising business families, Bollywood personalities, fintech entrepreneurs, global CXOs, board advisors and media houses.
As part of its growth plans, Ionic Wealth will strengthen portfolio-led proposition, global capabilities, and AI integration in the wealth-tech experience. It will also scale the UHNI business and expand its footprint in India and beyond.
The fresh capital will be used to double down on the company's early bets, leverage technology, advance GIFT City-led global investing, and develop a differentiated UHNI proposition for India's leading families.
Ionic Wealth was founded in 2024 by Srikanth Subramanian, Shobhit Mathur, and Dharmendra Jain. It today has an AUM (assets under management) of over Rs 16,000 crore and more than 2,900 HNI and UHNI clients across 12+ cities.
“As investor needs evolve, our focus is to move beyond traditional product-led offerings towards a more comprehensive platform approach to wealth creation, informed by our institutional-grade investment intelligence across global markets and asset classes,” said Srikanth Subramanian, Co-founder and CEO, Ionic Wealth.
Ionic Wealth attributes its growth to rising HNI numbers, appreciation in asset value, and growing income and savings.
Dinesh Thakkar, Founder, Chairman and Managing Director, Angel One, said, “India’s wealth management industry is at an important inflection point, driven by the growing aspirations of affluent investors and the increasing sophistication of their financial needs.
"Ionic is being built to serve this opportunity by bringing together investment expertise, technology and a client-first approach. We have strong conviction in the founding team and the institution they are building."

articles.title: Amazon fights Delivery Protection Act by putting stickers on its packages
articles.text:
Amazon is placing a sticker on some of its delivery boxes to urge customers to oppose a New York City bill.
This weekend, some Amazon shoppers reported getting a delivery from Amazon with a sticker on it that reads: “NYC Council could add up to $5 per order. Act now to protect low prices.” The sticker reportedly includes a QR code that leads to a link for contacting NYC Councilmembers. The sticker encourages the package’s recipient to “Scan to tell your council member: no increases for New Yorkers.”
Amazon is looking to stoke opposition to Introduction 0518-2026 (518), also known as the Delivery Protection Act. The proposed law would require Amazon and other companies with last-mile delivery facilities in the city, such as FedEx, to directly employ third-party contractors Amazon uses for making deliveries.
Amazon previously sent mailers to NYC residents regarding a new headquarters (which was subsequently scrapped), but political messaging on packages is unprecedented for Amazon, which hasn’t used its delivery boxes to lobby for political causes before.
Last week, Amazon made another uncharacteristic move by showing NYC shoppers a homepage banner ad—which I see when logging in to Amazon as of this writing—and an in-app pop-up that also urges opposition to the bill. The banner and pop-up include a link to a blog where Amazon says the law would force it to consider moving operations outside of NYC and lead to “slower and more expensive delivery for millions of customers in New York City, while also threatening small businesses and their thousands of employees.” Mayor Zohran Mamdani and the Amazon division of the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, however, support the bill.

articles.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO, Board Director
articles.text:
Tech giant Nvidia has announced that it has reinstated Jensen Huang as President, Chief Executive Officer, and board member.
According to Nvidia’s press release, the board of directors voted unanimously to reinstate Huang after what it described as “a series of discussions and meetings,” during which the company was “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s ability to lead Nvidia.”
Nvidia also confirmed that it received input from “senior levels of the United States government” and used that input to determine that Huang’s reinstatement posed no national security risk.
“I am honoured to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Jensen Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the Nvidia board for its confidence and deliberation through this process.”
Huang also added that “I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”
To add some context, Nvidia opened an independent investigation into Jensen Huang after it was revealed that a woman he was having an affair with was an alleged Chinese spy. Eventually, Huang resigned from his position at Nvidia, with current executive vice president and CFO Colette Kress serving as interim CEO.
Interestingly, Nvidia’s stock price is up over 30 per cent since the announcement that he is returning.
Source: Nvidia

articles.title: 'Some people get so excited about ‘free’ software that they forget the risks': New report finds rush to develop software faster with AI is creating a costly new problem
articles.text:
'Some people get so excited about ‘free’ software that they forget the risks': New report finds rush to develop software faster with AI is creating a costly new problem
Vibe coding apps can be costly and complex
- Enterprises are using AI to vibe code their apps and save huge cash vs. buying commercial apps
- They're losing out on the technical support and spending more on maintenance
- Vibe-coded apps can also have major security vulnerabilities
New research from Appian has warned many businesses are rushing into using AI to code software, but despite being able to make software for free, they could actually be exposing themselves to unexpected costs around maintenance and security.
Two in three (64%) enterprise leaders in the UK say that they've had to increase the time spent on testing, troubleshooting and deployment even though AI made the actual software development was faster.
Ultimately, the report reveals that AI coding tools are simply pushing time and costs further down the software lifecycle, where problems could actually be more difficult and expensive to resolve than having just spent the cash on commercial software in the rifts place.
Is expensive commercial software cheaper than free vibe-coded tools?
We might still be in the early days of vibe-coded software, but four in five (79%) UK enterprise leaders say they've already allocated at least 10% of their entire technology innovation budgets to testing, deploying and maintaining non-commercially available software. Two in five (43%) even allocate at least 20% of their budgets to this cause.
Appian is using the term 'aloneware' to describe apps developed using AI, noting the significant speed potential of developing and even deploying them. But the report doesn't hold back on sharing the downsides, including generated code that's hard for developers to understand and maintain, limited documentation, complex integrations, awkward dependencies, and of course the security issues involved with not buying enterprise-grade software that's already been tested and built to stringent standards.
It's these complexities that could be causing the biggest headaches and bills, too. Appian says three in five reported unexpected post-launch costs associated with security or governance, and a further three in five struggle to access the relevant technical support when apps don't come from enterprise-grade vendors.
"The most important applications in enterprises need support," CEO Matt Calkins explained. "If you vibe-code them, there will be nobody to turn to when problems occur."

While many enterprises are looking to ditch conventional software vendors in a bid to cut costs, there are clear benefits to using one over vibe coding software in-house. There is, potentially, a middle ground, though, and Appian implies that using a shared architectural foundation could give enterprises more ownership over their software while maintaining compatibility and security benefits.
"Using AI to build applications on a commercial platform combines the speed of AI with the reliability of supported technology," Calkins added.

articles.title: AI server makers hike prices up to 45% months after contracts are signed as RAM shortage triples memory-heavy CPU node costs — financial firms still pay up as 'the compute is valuable'
articles.text:
AI server makers hike prices up to 45% months after contracts are signed as RAM shortage triples memory-heavy CPU node costs — financial firms still pay up as 'the compute is valuable'
"I am altering the deal. Pray I do not alter it further."
"Prices are really expensive for technology X" isn't truly news anymore, but it seems that even the bigshots who place orders in the magnitude of hundreds of millions of dollars are feeling the pinch. According to the Financial Times (FT), trading and financial service firms are seeing post-contract hikes of up to 45% on their data center servers.
The price upgrades are coming in well after the ink has dried on the respective agreements, often signed months in advance. One unnamed person told the FT that "it is disconcerting when you get a 25, 30, 45 percent" increase, further adding that "there is a significant disparity" between the initial figure and the one that pops up on the final invoice.
However, even this bump isn't deterring well-funded financial firms, which are reportedly buying up as much compute power as they can get their hands on, and are willing to eat the cost. Another informant said "we've never said no," noting that "at the end of the day, the compute is valuable to us and we'll pay for it." The FT asked whether the contacted companies had any clauses in their contracts preventing price volatility, but none confirmed or denied the fact.
The publication predictably points to RAM pricing as the main cause behind the out-of-nowhere hikes, noting that while GPU servers have risen in price by 20-30%, memory-heavy CPU nodes purportedly doubled or tripled in price.
This is arguably more bad news for us peons, as it illustrates the DRAM shortage is alive and well, whether natural or fabricated. Furthermore, it shows if even the big shots are more than willing to pay inflated prices, then mere mortals have little chance of a RAM price reprieve.
Not every firm is taking the price jacking lying down, though. Back in June, XTX Finland Oy took one of Dell's Irish subsidiaries to court, after Dell asked for another $62 to $70 million on top of the previously agreed-on price of $549 million for 1,680 servers. That case is still ongoing and is an interesting watch, as XTX apparently paid $5 million extra for a contract clause specifically to prevent any pricing shenanigans.
Even if XTX wins, though, the firm may find it harder to do future business with OEMs. The supply-demand balance is currently so lopsided that chip fabs and OEMs have all the ability to pretty much set any terms they wish.

articles.title: Coup d'arrêt à Kourou, Ariane 6 reporte son 10e vol, prévu pour Amazon Leo, en raison d'un problème technique
articles.text:
Arianespace a reporté ce lundi le lancement d'Ariane 6, qui devait placer 36 satellites Amazon Leo en orbite depuis Kourou. En cause, un incident sur les installations au sol, qui repousse le dixième vol du lanceur au 24 novembre, au mieux.
Le dixième vol d'Ariane 6 n'aura pas lieu aujourd'hui. Arianespace a annoncé tôt ce lundi 23 novembre avoir interrompu le compte à rebours de la mission qui devait emporter 36 satellites Amazon Leo depuis Kourou. L'opérateur évoque un problème technique sur les installations au sol et assure que la fusée et sa cargaison sont en sécurité. Un contretemps malvenu pour Amazon, dont la poisse semble se poursuivre, qui a perdu 40 satellites dans l'échec de la fusée Vulcan il y a huit jours à peine.
Ariane 6 retenue au sol par ses installations
Le compte à rebours de la mission Ariane 6 VA271 s'est arrêté avant même l'ouverture de la fenêtre de tir, prévue à 8h09 heure de Kourou. Un coup dur pour Arianespace, qui évoque « un événement technique survenu sur les moyens sol de mise en œuvre du lanceur », autrement dit sur les équipements au sol qui servent à préparer et à lancer la fusée. L'opérateur européen n'a, pour l'instant, rien dit de plus sur la nature exacte du problème.
La procédure a été stoppée avant le retrait de la tour mobile, l'imposante structure qui abrite Ariane 6 sur son pas de tir et s'écarte avant le lancement. Les opérations sur les systèmes de la fusée n'avaient pas encore commencé. Ariane 6 et ses 36 passagers restent donc « en configuration stable et en sécurité », assure Arianespace. Ce coup d'arrêt survient au bout d'une campagne de plus de trois mois entre l'arrivée des satellites en Guyane mi-août, leur installation sous la coiffe le 17 novembre, et la revue d'aptitude au lancement, dernier examen avant le vol, qui était programmée le 20.
Reste à savoir quand Ariane 6 pourra repartir. Les équipes analysent l'incident et préparent une nouvelle tentative, avec une prochaine opportunité de lancement « pas antérieure au 24 novembre ». Demain au plus tôt, donc, sans aucune garantie que ce créneau soit tenu. Arianespace promet de nouvelles informations dès que possible, mais n'a encore communiqué aucune fenêtre de tir.
Un dixième vol très attendu par Amazon Leo
Ce report touche un vol assez symbolique pour Arianespace. VA271 (ou LE-04 pour le nom de code donné par Amazon Leo) doit en effet être le dixième lancement d'Ariane 6, dont le vol inaugural remonte à juillet 2024, et le cinquième lancement d'Arianespace cette année. L'entreprise lui a même consacré un dossier de vol en édition spéciale. La fusée décollera dans sa version la plus puissante, Ariane 64, équipée de quatre boosters P160C. Étrennés en juin, ces propulseurs plus chargés en propergol portent sa capacité d'emport à environ 22 tonnes en orbite basse.
Du côté d'Amazon Leo, chaque lancement compte double. Le 15 novembre, la fusée américaine Vulcan a échoué avec 40 de ses satellites à bord, définitivement perdus, et les 37 autres vols réservés sur ce lanceur sont suspendus le temps de l'enquête. Un gros coup de frein pour une constellation de 396 satellites, encore loin des plus de 3 000 prévus, et dont le service commercial, promis pour 2026, se fait toujours attendre. Ariane 6, elle, affiche un parcours sans faute pour Amazon, avec trois lancements réussis cette année, et 100 satellites livrés en orbite basse.
Pour cette quatrième mission au profit d'Amazon, il faudra en théorie 2 heures et 4 minutes à Ariane 6 pour libérer ses 36 satellites vers les 460 km d'altitude de l'orbite basse. Amazon les fera ensuite grimper entre 590 et 630 km pour étoffer sa constellation, concurrente du mastodonte américain d'Elon Musk, Starlink. À l'issue de la mission, on atteindra les 136 satellites Leo lancés par Arianespace, dans le cadre d'un contrat désormais porté à 24 lancements. Mais le compteur reste, pour on ne sait combien de temps, encore figé.

articles.title: Another GTA VI Glitch Unlocks Frame Rates on Xbox
articles.text:
Monday, November 23rd 2026
Another GTA VI Glitch Unlocks Frame Rates on Xbox
Since the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI, which has so far been a commercial smash-hit, as expected, gamers have seemingly been trying their best to break the game as much as possible, despite the limitations of modern gaming consoles. The latest GTA VI hack, following the prior first-person hack and DLSS 5 implementation, is a framerate unlock on Xbox Series X|S consoles that can apparently get the game running well beyond its 30 FPS limit. 
The hack appears to take advantage of a bug in Xbox's quick resume functionality to trick GTA VI into running at up to 60 FPS instead of the typical 30 FPS limit. This hack was recently tested by Digital Foundry on YouTube, who showed that the Xbox Series X reaches 60 FPS in certain scenarios while running GTA VI. The biggest framerate jump occurs in less dense areas and when the camera is pointed at areas like the sky box, where not much is happening. In dense areas, the framerate typically hovers around 40-45 FPS, and when driving fast through a dense area, for example, the framerate will drop to as low as 30 FPS again.The framerate unlock hack can be triggered by following these steps:
- The GTA VI framerate unlock hack is triggered by doing the following:
- Change the console to 60 Hz output in settings
- Boot the game and exiting the game with the Xbox button once the loading screen with the stars appears
- Go back into settings and change the system output to 120 Hz
- Boot another game and close it again with the Xbox button once it has passed its initial splash screen
- Switch back to GTA VI
It was previously confirmed that Rockstar deemed GTA VI too demanding to run beyond that 30 FPS cap on current-gen gaming consoles, and, although there is evidence to support that the PS5 may be running into some issues—mainly caused by aging liquid metal, it seems—it looks like the Xbox Series X can fairly consistently run the open-world game somewhere between 35 and 50 FPS during most situations, although there are still instances where the frame rate will drop below 30 FPS. This inconsistent performance above 30 FPS, as described by Digital Foundry, may be part of the reason why the framerate was locked. Additionally, the testing outlet reports that the game's engine appears to be tied to that 30 FPS cap, meaning that the game actually runs faster when the framerate is unlocked.
Hilariously, as demonstrated in the video, doing the inverse of the hack—that is, switching from 120 Hz output to 60 Hz output while GTA VI is suspended—will result in the game running at a locked 15 FPS.

articles.title: Rebondissement chez Nvidia : Jensen Huang est de retour comme PDG
articles.text:
Ce lundi 23 novembre, Nvidia a annoncé le retour de Jensen Huang au poste de PDG « avec effet immédiat ». Le milliardaire reprend ses fonctions de président, de directeur général et de membre du conseil d’administration. Pour rappel, le cofondateur de Nvidia avait démissionné le 12 novembre, soit onze jours plus tôt. Il avait préféré quitter son poste à la suite de la révélation de plusieurs aventures extraconjugales. Jensen Huang a notamment entretenu une relation avec une femme d’affaires soupçonnée de travailler pour les services secrets de la Chine.
À lire aussi : « 0 % de chance » – Nvidia ne croit pas à l’apocalypse de l’IA
« Aucun risque pour la sécurité nationale »
Le conseil indique avoir voté le retour de Huang à l’unanimité, après « une série de discussions et de réunions » avec le principal intéressé. Le conseil assure avoir consulté « les plus hauts niveaux du gouvernement américain » avant de prendre sa décision, et se dit désormais « convaincu » que ce retour « ne présente aucun risque pour la sécurité nationale ».
« Le conseil estime que Jensen est la bonne personne pour diriger Nvidia », déclare Harvey Jones, le président du conseil d’administration, remerciant au passage Colette Kress, qui a assuré l’intérim pendant l’absence forcée du cofondateur.
« J’ai hâte de me remettre au travail »
Dans un billet publié sur X, Jensen Huang se dit « honoré de revenir chez Nvidia ». Il précise assumer cette « responsabilité avec la plus grande humilité et un engagement renouvelé », et indique avoir « hâte de se remettre au travail ».
La semaine dernière, quelques jours après sa démission, Jensen Huang s’était dit prêt à reprendre les rennes de l’entreprise, mais le conseil avait aussitôt refusé. Le conseil de Nvidia s’était même lancé à la recherche d’un successeur, en approchant notamment le patron d’un autre géant des puces, Arm.
Le retour de Jensen Huang à la tête de Nvidia devrait ravir énormément de monde. Des salariés, Elon Musk et plus de 157 000 personnes avaient en effet réclamé son retour dans une pétition. Donald Trump avait également appelé Nvidia à réintégrer Huang, qu’il qualifie de « brillant » dirigeant. Elon Musk a d’ailleurs salué ce retour sur X d’un simple message : « L’erreur a été corrigée ». Sur Truth Social, Donald Trump a, lui, évoqué une décision « juste et appropriée » et qualifié Jensen Huang de « grand patriote et trésor national ».
 The mistake has been corrected
— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 23, 2026
Une enquête toujours en cours
L’affaire n’est pas close pour autant. L’enquête interne lancée après les révélations se poursuivra « jusqu’à son terme », précise Nvidia. Les investigations s’intéressent particulièrement au fait que Jensen Huang a peut-être été « la cible d’une opération de renseignement étranger ».
