articles.title: Beyond tickets: How LightSprint.ai is building a multiplayer software factory where PMs and designers ship with engineers
articles.text:
NetApp Excellerator
View Brand Publisher
Beyond tickets: How LightSprint.ai is building a multiplayer software factory where PMs and designers ship with engineers
AI made writing code faster. It did not make it easier for the people closest to customers to change the product. LightSprint.ai, part of NetApp Excellerator's Cohort 15, is changing that.
It is Monday morning. A product manager has a customer escalation, a designer has spotted exactly where users drop off, and both know what should change. They write a ticket. It joins a backlog waiting on an engineering team that is already stretched. Weeks later, the change ships, often not quite as intended.
AI coding agents have made individual engineers dramatically faster, yet the way most companies build software has barely changed.
Enter LightSprint.ai, which is building a multiplayer software factory, one shared place where engineers, product managers and designers plan, build and ship together on the codebase they already have, with engineering approving every merge.
The problem: AI made coding single-player
Today's coding agents live in one developer's editor or terminal. One person drives, and everyone else falls out of sync. Planning stays buried in documents, context lives in someone's head, and reviewers approve large batches of AI-written code with little shared understanding of why it was written.
Prototyping tools showed non-engineers they could create software, but on a blank canvas. Real companies depend on complex codebases with years of conventions and review rules. A prototype can ignore all of that; a production change cannot, so the prototype gets rebuilt and the speed is lost.
The bottleneck has moved. Writing code is no longer the slowest step. Coordination is.
Why enterprises feel it most
For large organizations, every change needs to be traceable: which requirement it came from, which acceptance criteria it meets, and which tests prove it works. Teams must follow approved packages and design systems, and security teams want to know where code and
data live and who approved what. Opening AI coding to more people without that structure creates risk; withholding it leaves the backlog where it is.
LightSprint.ai's approach
LightSprint.ai sits on top of the coding agents teams already use and turns them into a shared workspace for the whole product team. It rests on three pillars.
- Spec first, with traceability built in. Anyone can describe a change in plain language. LightSprint.ai asks clarifying questions, drafts a spec with acceptance criteria, and the team agrees on the plan before any code is written, while it is still cheap to change. Each change stays traceable from requirement to spec to tests and the final pull request.
- Multiplayer by default. Product managers, designers and engineers work in the same live session. Anyone can join an agent, steer it, and review a live preview of the change. Shared skills and memory capture the team's conventions, so every teammate and agent builds the way the organization already works.
- Engineering in control. Engineers set up the environment once, and nobody else needs a local development setup. Agents work in isolated cloud sandboxes, credentials stay out of AI-written code, automated verification checks each change, and engineers approve every merge through the GitHub workflow they already use. Teams can bring their own models and LLM gateway.
The result is not fewer engineers. It is engineers spending their time on the decisions that need their judgment, while the people closest to customers ship the changes they understand best.
Building with NetApp
Through NetApp Excellerator, LightSprint.ai is working with NetApp teams on evaluating how a multiplayer software factory fits an enterprise environment: spec-driven development, traceability from requirement to test, adherence to approved packages and UI standards, and a security model that meets enterprise review.
"Coding agents made engineers faster, but most software teams are still single-player. The people closest to customers write tickets and wait," said Ben Ong, Co-founder and CEO of LightSprint.ai. "Working with NetApp through the Excellerator program has sharpened what enterprises need for a multiplayer model to work at scale: clear specs, end-to-end traceability and security built in from day one."
Early signs of a shift
Since starting with early users in April 2026, LightSprint.ai now works with over 100 companies, and non-engineers have shipped thousands of pull requests on the platform, with an aggregate merge rate averaging above 80%. Companies are adopting a "coding for all" strategy, where product, design and operations build alongside engineering.
And that Monday morning? The product manager and designer open a shared session, agree on the plan with an engineer, click through a live preview together, and the engineer approves the merge the same week. No ticket left waiting.

articles.title: Black Friday Apple : idéal pour installer une IA locale, ce Mac mini M6 profite de 160€ de remise chez Amazon
articles.text:
Le Mac mini M6 permet de profiter d’une configuration solide, adaptée au travail et à l’utilisation des IA, le tout dans un boîtier très compact. Amazon le propose à 889 € pour le Black Friday, au lieu de 1 049 € en temps normal.
Vous pensez qu’il faut disposer d’une énorme tour, voire d’un serveur, pour faire fonctionner une IA en local ? Pas nécessairement. Le Mac mini M6 disponible à 889 € chez Amazon est tout à fait adapté à la découverte de petits modèles d’IA exécutés directement sur la machine, mais aussi au travail quotidien et à la création. Il embarque une puce M6 avec CPU et GPU à 12 cœurs, accompagnée de 16 Go de mémoire unifiée et d’un SSD de 256 Go. Si vous disposez déjà d’un écran, d’un clavier et d’une souris Apple, c’est un achat qui peut très vite révéler son potentiel.
Le Mac mini M6 avec 16 Go de mémoire et 256 Go de SSD est proposé à 889 € au lieu de 1 049 € chez Amazon durant le Black Friday.
Pourquoi choisir le Mac mini M6 ?
- Pour ses capacités en IA : la puce M6 intègre des accélérateurs dédiés qui bénéficient à différents modèles de langage compatibles.
- Pour son format compact : son boîtier de 12,7 cm de côté trouve facilement sa place sur un petit bureau.
- Pour sa connectique : les ports Thunderbolt 4, USB-C, HDMI et Ethernet permettent de raccorder plusieurs écrans, mais aussi des supports de stockage et différents périphériques.
Une machine pour travailler et découvrir l’IA locale
Le Mac mini M6 permet d’utiliser les fonctions d’Apple Intelligence, mais aussi d’expérimenter des modèles locaux avec des logiciels comme LM Studio. Si vous ne désirez pas être totalement dépendant des IA en ligne, c’est un usage intéressant. Notre test du Mac mini M6 souligne les performances de sa puce et son efficacité énergétique. Ce modèle a reçu la note de 8 sur 10 et si son prix compte parmi ses défauts, la remise proposée par Amazon permet de le gommer.
Un ordinateur polyvalent, avec une configuration à bien choisir
Ce Mac mini constitue une base intéressante pour découvrir l’IA locale tout en conservant un ordinateur de travail compact. Il faut tout de même prendre en compte le fait que ses 16 Go de RAM peuvent s’avérer limités pour certains modèles de langage, et qu’il n’est pas possible d’en ajouter par la suite. Il en va de même pour son SSD, qui est soudé.
✅ Les points forts
- Puce M6 adaptée aux applications créatives et d’IA compatibles.
- Boîtier de seulement 12,7 cm de côté.
- Connectique Thunderbolt 4, HDMI et Ethernet 2,5 Gbit/s.
❌ Les limites
- Mémoire unifiée de 16 Go non extensible.
- SSD de 256 Go rapidement limité par les applications et modèles téléchargés.
Proposé à 889 € par Amazon, le Mac mini M6 bénéficie d’une réduction de 160 € et sa livraison est offerte.
Le Mac mini M6 en promotion chez Amazon s’avère donc adapté à la découverte et à l’usage d’IA locales, mais son intérêt ne se résume pas à cela : il peut tout à fait vous accompagner dans votre quotidien de créatif ou de télétravailleur, tout en limitant l’encombrement de votre station.
Néanmoins, les projets d’IA lourds ont tendance à nécessiter une configuration plus généreuse : il faut donc vous assurer que les outils que vous désirez utiliser pourront tourner efficacement sur cette machine avant de valider votre commande.

articles.title: How LinkedIn Built a View-Agnostic Analytics System for Modern iOS UI Architectures
Jensen Huang vuelve como CEO de Nvidia y la accion sube 31,8%
articles.text:
Jensen Huang volvió a la dirección de Nvidia como presidente y consejero delegado, tras la decisión unánime del consejo de administración de restituirlo con efecto inmediato.
El anuncio impulsó las acciones de la compañía un 31,8% en las operaciones previas a la apertura de Wall Street. El fabricante de chips informó que la reincorporación se produjo después de varias conversaciones con el ejecutivo de origen taiwanés, en las que los directores evaluaron su continuidad al frente del grupo y descartaron que su regreso suponga riesgos para la seguridad nacional de Estados Unidos, según Nvidia.
“El Consejo de Administración considera que Jensen es la persona idónea para liderar NVIDIA y que su reincorporación redunda en beneficio de nuestros accionistas, empleados, socios y clientes … Tenemos plena confianza en Jensen y esperamos colaborar con él en su regreso al frente de la compañía. Agradecemos a Colette Kress su excelente labor como Directora Ejecutiva interina, además de seguir desempeñando sus funciones como Directora Financiera de NVIDIA”, afirmó Harvey C. Jones, Presidente del Consejo.
El regreso llega después de una salida marcada por un escándalo. Huang había renunciado a sus cargos luego de admitir una relación extramatrimonial con una exejecutiva de una empresa de centros de datos en Singapur, cliente de NVIDIA, señalada por autoridades estadounidenses por presuntos vínculos con espionaje chino y desvío de chips restringidos.
El caso se agravó cuando The New York Times reportó una segunda relación extramatrimonial del ejecutivo, esta vez con una empleada de NVIDIA bajo su supervisión directa.
La controversia derivó en investigaciones del FBI, una indagación independiente dentro de la compañía y caídas en las acciones de NVIDIA, mientras Pekín negó las acusaciones de espionaje y no se estableció públicamente que Huang hubiera entregado información confidencial de forma deliberada.
Cómo se mueven las acciones del sector tecnológico
La subida de NVIDIA se dio en medio de un rebote generalizado del sector tecnológico y de inteligencia artificial este 23 de noviembre, tras las fuertes caídas de la semana pasada.
Anthropic también se recuperó después del desplome registrado tras su salida a bolsa, presentando un aumento de más de 4% durante la jornada. Zscaler lideró las subas de la jornada, con un avance cercano al 13%, impulsado por el acuerdo de CrowdStrike para adquirirla por 43.900 millones de dólares en acciones.
AMD subió alrededor de un 5%, beneficiada por el optimismo hacia el hardware y los semiconductores de inteligencia artificial. Oracle avanzó cerca de un 5% después de reafirmar su objetivo de superar los 30.000 millones de dólares en flujo de caja libre para el año fiscal 2029.
Micron Technology y CoreWeave, ligadas a la cadena de suministro de centros de datos, también avanzaron de forma notable.
Cómo queda Nvidia con el regreso de Huang y su investigación
El regreso de Huang se produjo once días después de que renunciara a sus tres cargos y no cierra los procesos internos que la compañía sigue tramitando.
El consejo recordó que, tras conocerse que Huang había sido blanco de una presunta operación de inteligencia extranjera, había formado un comité integrado exclusivamente por consejeros independientes, asistido por asesoría legal externa, cuya investigación continuará hasta su conclusión.
NVIDIA informó además la creación de un Comité de Seguridad Nacional y Control de Exportaciones, también compuesto solo por directores independientes, encargado de supervisar el cumplimiento comercial y los riesgos de seguridad nacional con apoyo de abogados y asesores especializados en la materia.
La compañía anunció que inició la búsqueda de un director de cumplimiento (Chief Compliance Officer), un cargo nuevo que reportará ante el comité de nominaciones y gobierno corporativo, y reiteró que continuará cooperando con las investigaciones y consultas de las autoridades estadounidenses.
Harvey C. Jones, nombrado presidente del consejo el 12 de noviembre, el primero de ese tipo en la historia de la empresa, conserva el cargo. Mientras que Colette Kress, que ejerció como directora ejecutiva interina, vuelve a concentrarse en su rol como directora financiera de NVIDIA.

articles.title: Math's biggest open problem may have fallen to AI, but the proof is unreadable to humans
articles.text:
What just happened? Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, has published a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, a 167-year-old conjecture about the distribution of prime numbers and one of mathematics' most famous unsolved problems. He developed the proof with the help of Anthropic's Claude AI model. The organizations responsible for maintaining the field's leading proof-checking software verified it within a day of its release. It is the second of the seven Millennium Prize Problems to be solved with AI in roughly three months.
Alpöge did not release the proof as a traditional research paper. Instead, he posted it on his personal website in a formal programming language that allows computers to check every logical step. Within a day, reviewers from the Lean Focused Research Organization and the Mathlib Initiative had checked 17 million lines of code.
"We have full confidence that Alpöge's proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct," the two groups said in a joint statement. "We congratulate him on this achievement."
The speed of the verification came down to the format. A paper tackling a problem this difficult would normally face months or even years of expert review. A formal proof, however, can be checked mechanically. The software doesn't need to understand the reasoning or be convinced by it. It only needs to confirm that each step follows logically from the previous one.
The downside is that humans can't easily read it. Alpöge said the argument draws on "an astounding amount of mathematics" that he is still working to absorb. When he tried a version written in natural language by the AI, he found "some massive, unreadable travesty of 'slop.'" That document ran to more than 250,000 pages. He plans to write a proper version once he can simplify the argument.
Bernhard Riemann first proposed the hypothesis in 1859. It makes a precise prediction about how prime numbers are distributed along the number line. For generations, the problem resisted the efforts of leading mathematicians, eventually becoming one of the best-known open questions in number theory. In 2000, it was named one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems. In the 26 years since, only one of the seven has been solved by humans working without AI.
AI has changed that picture quickly. In September, an internal OpenAI model solved the Navier-Stokes problem, a fundamental question about how liquids and gases move, at a cost of millions of dollars in computing power. In October, OpenAI released hundreds of major proofs at once. Among them was work on the quasi-Riemann Hypothesis that would have been worthy of a Fields Medal had a human produced it. Alpöge called that release "obviously the most significant moment in mathematical history."
Terence Tao, a Fields Medalist, described the quasi-Riemann result as the "biggest advance on the subject in 50 years" during an appearance on the Numberphile podcast. He predicted that a team of humans and AI might solve the full hypothesis by 2050.
Alpöge already had a track record of using AI to tackle difficult mathematical problems. Over the summer, he reported that Anthropic's Fable model had found a counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture, an 87-year-old problem in algebraic geometry. His post about the discovery attracted 40 million views.
He said the Riemann Hypothesis was the problem he had dreamed of solving since childhood. He and Claude worked on it for months, with the proof finally coming together late on a Sunday night, just days before Anthropic's IPO, the largest in history. Alpöge called the timing "horrible." He messaged CEO Dario Amodei to ask whether he could announce the result, then published it the morning after the company went public.
"I just could not live if I waited even longer," he said.
He described the model's work near the end in vivid terms. "Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line," he wrote.
As mathematicians around the world rushed to examine the work, Anthropic declined to comment. Meanwhile, the company's stock fell sharply. At least one investor was more enthusiastic. Deedy Das, a Menlo Ventures partner who works on the firm's Anthropic investment, called it "a landmark moment in history where we can truly say: the AI is smarter than the human."
Alpöge said he expects more results like this one. "In a time of revolution in mathematics, I hope the argument provides a glimpse towards the miracles that lie ahead, and shows us the joy and wonder we are about to find in the simplest things," he said.
He also doesn't see the proof as an ending. "It is natural to feel that this is an end," he wrote. "But what I saw during the course of progress so amazed me that I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater."

articles.title: Marvel crams every superhero ever into Avengers: Doomsday final trailer
articles.text:
Rumors have been swirling for days that we would be getting a final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday, the penultimate film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe’s Phase Six, heralding the end of the so-called “Multiverse Saga.” The rumors were true: Marvel just released the trailer, featuring pretty much every superhero ever represented in the MCU. And it looks like the Avengers will face consequences for messing with the timeline to reverse the blip in Endgame.
As previously reported, the film takes place 14 months after the events of Thunderbolts*. Per the official logline: “Beloved heroes from three distinct universes will be set on a deadly collision course and face an existential threat unlike anything they’ve ever encountered.” Those universes are Earth-616 (the Avengers, Wakandans, and New Avengers), Earth-828 (Fantastic Four), and the “original” X-Men.
Cast-wise, we have Avengers favorites Thor (Chris Hemsworth), the new Captain America (Anthony Mackie), Bucky Barnes (Sebastian Stan), Ant-Man (Paul Rudd), Falcon (Danny Ramirez), and Loki (Tom Hiddleston). Then there’s the Wakandan contingent: Shuri as the new Black Panther (Letitia Wright), M’Baku (Winston Duke), and Namor (Tenoch Huerta Mejia), as well as Alex Livinalli as Namor’s ally, Attuma. And, of course, Robert Downey Jr. as Doctor Doom.
We also have the Thunderbolts* (aka New Avengers): John Walker/US Agent (Wyatt Russell), Yelena Belova (Florence Pugh), Bob/Sentry (Lewis Pullman), Red Guardian (David Harbour), and Ghost (Hannah John-Kamen). And the Fantastic Four: Reed Richards (Pedro Pascal), Sue Storm (Vanessa Kirby), Ben Grimm (Ebon Moss-Bachrach), and Johnny Storm (Joseph Quinn). We’ll also see Charles Xavier (Patrick Stewart), Beast (Kelsey Grammer), Magneto (Ian McKellen), Mystique (Rebecca Romijn), Nightcrawler (Alan Cumming), and Cyclops (James Marsden).
For good measure, Marvel threw in Gambit (Channing Tatum) and Xu Shang-Chi (Simu Liu). There will be plenty of cameos, like Steve Rogers (Chris Evans), revealed in one of four sneak teasers last year. We can also expect to see (at least briefly) Peggy Carter (Hayley Atwell), Spider-Man (Tom Holland), Hawkeye (Jeremy Renner), Doctor Strange (Benedict Cumberbatch), Thor’s adopted daughter, Love (India Rose Hemsworth), and Scott Lang’s daughter, Cassie (Kathryn Newton).

articles.title: Bell reports some customer information accessed in data breach
articles.text:
Bell and its subsidiary Virgin Plus suffered a data breach earlier this month that exposed some customers’ personal information.
According to a notice published by Bell on its website, an “unknown party gained unauthorized access to an internal Bell system” on Nov. 17, 2026. Bell says it started informing impacted customers as soon as it confirmed that their data had been impacted.
The unknown party may have accessed personal information, including names, mailing addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, and account details like account numbers, product information, business names, and the date and amount of customers’ last payment.
“We have confirmed that no highly sensitive personal information such as credit card number or bank account information was impacted,” Bell said.
The telecom said that it “immediately removed the threat actor and initiated emergency protocols.” It also continues to monitor all systems closely and has engaged the RCMP’s cybercrime unit to help investigate.
Bell also shared some best practices for impacted customers. That includes being wary of any unsolicited requests from people posing as Bell, especially if they’re asking for personal information. Bell says it will never contact customers asking for bank account information, passwords, or PINs.
The company also warned against clicking on links or downloading attachments delivered from suspicious emails or text messages. Customers should also review accounts for suspicious activity.
Notably, Bell is the latest telecom to suffer a breach this year. Telus also suffered a breach between Feb. 2025 and June 2026. Cogeco’s Oxio suffered a data breach as well, as did Rogers and Fido. And Freedom Mobile suffered a breach in January.
And security issues extend beyond carriers, with Loblaw and Canada Computers also reporting breaches this year.
Source: Bell, Virgin Plus

articles.title: President Trump says Nvidia board rehiring Jensen Huang would be best for the company and US — Treasury Sec Bessent walks back outsider CEO comments, claims Huang is technically an outsider now
articles.text:
President Trump says Nvidia board rehiring Jensen Huang would be best for the company and the US — Treasury Sec Bessent walks back outsider CEO comments, claims Huang is technically an outsider now
Bessent had argued that Huang's replacement should "come from outside the company," but now argues that the former CEO fits that description.
After saying just days ago that any new Nvidia CEO should "come from outside the company" following the resignation of Jensen Huang after he admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has now backtracked by saying that Huang is on the outside, seemingly paving the way for his return. At the time, Bessent's assertion was in stark contrast with that of the U.S. President, with Trump calling for Huang to be reinstated. Trump earlier today doubled down, writing of his "hope" that Nvidia's board would rehire Huang in a post on his Truth Social account. Now, Bessent has fallen in line despite having previously called for a "dramatic shake-up" at Nvidia.
Bessent's latest comments came on CBS' Face the Nation show. When asked about whether Nvidia should look beyond its current payroll when looking for a new CEO instead of bringing Huang back, Bessent argued that he "said they should go to the outside, but he's on the outside now." Bessent also said that he would "assume [Huang] didn't know that [Alice Huang] was an alleged spy." That has, to date, not been publicly confirmed.
Bessent's latest statement may be semantics to realign himself with Trump, but it's unclear whether either of them will sway an Nvidia board that has already said it has no intention of double-dipping with Huang. That's despite some members of the same board angling for Huang to be allowed back into the company. Predictably, Huang has made it known that he would be "honored" to return, but the situation has now moved beyond a simple affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. The fact that multiple affairs may now have been uncovered won't help his case, nor will being dragged before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence, and China Select Committees in early December. Nvidia's top lawyer will also have to make an appearance following the news that a criminal investigation has been launched into whether Megaspeed — a previous client of Nvidia, and the company where Alice Huang worked — was involved in the bypassing of AI chip export controls.
Megaspeed has long been accused of being involved in a chip smuggling operation. An investigation found in October 2025 that it had helped move around $2 billion worth of Nvidia chips into China via an import and re-export process. The alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, was a Megaspeed executive and was reportedly instrumental in the import of more than $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia AI GPU imports during a three-year relationship with the then Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

articles.title: Kein Kabelfrust zu Weihnachten: So machst du den Weihnachtsbaum smart
articles.text:
Kein Kabelfrust zu Weihnachten: So machst du den Weihnachtsbaum smart
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Den Tannenbaum zum Leuchten zu bringen, ist manchmal gar nicht so einfach. Zwar gibt es längst Lichterketten in allen möglichen Farben, das heißt aber nicht, dass die passende Steckdose immer gut erreichbar ist. Dann kann es auf Dauer nerven, den Stecker ein- und auszustöpseln. Es gibt aber auch Hersteller, die sich des Problems angenommen haben – etwa in Form smarter Lichterketten. Aber auch mit anderen Gadgets könnt ihr nicht nur Weihnachtsbaumbeleuchtung bequem mit dem Smartphone oder via Sprachbefehl an Siri, Alexa oder Gemini steuern.
Smarte Lichterketten von teuer bis günstig
Dabei kommt es natürlich darauf an, wie viel ihr für diesen Komfort ausgeben wollt. Am oberen Ende des Spektrums befindet sich etwa die Lichterkette Festavia von Philips Hue*. Die lässt sich über die App des Anbieters steuern. So ist etwa möglich, die Beleuchtung in drei Zonen einzuteilen, eigene Effekte zu erstellen oder die Lämpchen passend zur Musik auf Spotify leuchten zu lassen.
Grundsätzlich könnt ihr die Lichterkette per Bluetooth bedienen. Das volle Potenzial entfaltet sie aber erst in Verbindung mit der Hue-Bridge. Dann ist es möglich, sie mit anderen Lampen des Herstellers zu synchronisieren, in Szenen einzubinden und über Smarthome-Lautsprecher und -Displays zu steuern. Günstig ist die Festivia nicht. Online zahlt ihr derzeit rund 170 Euro für die 20 Meter lange Lichterkette. Die 40 Meter lange Ausgabe kostet 273 Euro.
Erschwinglicher sind die Govee Christmas String Lights 2* für rund 75 Euro. Diese Lichterkette lässt sich ebenfalls per Bluetooth steuern. Über die Govee-App habt ihr Zugriff auf 130 Szenen und einen KI-Assistenten, der die Beleuchtung nach euren Wünschen anpassen soll. Über das sogenannte Shape Mapping kann das System außerdem erkennen, wo sich welche LED am Baum befindet. Damit sollt ihr die Effekte optimieren können. Eine Musikerkennung ist ebenfalls integriert. Einziger Wermutstropfen: Um die Lichterkette ins Smarthome einzubinden und per Sprache steuern zu können, benötigt ihr einen Matter-fähigen Hub. Der ist allerdings schon vielen smarten Lautsprechern von Amazon, Apple oder Google eingebaut.
Eine dritte Alternative ist die smarte Lichterkette von Nanoleaf*, die ebenfalls diverse Szenen und animierte Farbverläufe bietet und auf Wunsch passend zur Musik leuchtet. Wie die anderen beiden Modelle könnt ihr das Exemplar von Nanoleaf per Bluetooth steuern. Alternativ ist die Einbindung ins Smarthome per Matter möglich. Auch hier braucht ihr dafür einen kompatiblen Hub. Zusätzlich könnt ihr die Lichterkette über ein integriertes Steuerelement am Kabel bedienen. Darüber lässt sie sich ein- und ausschalten. Einige vorprogrammierte Szenen könnt ihr auf diese Weise auch aktivieren. Die Nanoleaf-Lichterkette ist etwa bei Amazon für rund 66 Euro zu haben.
Smarte Steckdosen als günstige Alternative
Wollt ihr nicht gleich 100 Euro oder mehr in eine Lichterkette investieren, ist eine smarte Steckdose eine günstige Alternative. Die dient als Zwischenstück zwischen der normalen Steckdose und der Lichterkette. Der Vorteil: Ihr müsst eure bestehende normale Lichterkette nur einmal einstöpseln und könnt die Steckdose danach via Smartphone steuern. Bei Integration ins Hue- oder Samsung-Smarthings-System klappt es sogar über smarte Lautsprecher. Auf besondere Effekte müsst ihr dann zwar verzichten. Ihr erkauft euch über die Lösung aber etwas Komfort.
Und: Eine solche Steckdose muss im Vergleich zu den smarten Lichterketten gar nicht so teuer sein. Die Modelle aus der Tapo-Reihe von TP-Link starten etwa bei rund acht Euro* für die einzelne und 27 für die Mehrfachsteckdose*. Beide sind mit Alexa und Google kompatibel, unterstützen allerdings nur WLAN, aber kein Zigbee.
Habt ihr schon ein Smarthome-System, etwa von Philips Hue, solltet ihr darauf achten, dass die Steckdosen den Standard Zigbee unterstützen. Dann lassen sie sich einfach einbinden. Solche gibt es etwa von Hue selbst* für rund 27 Euro. Etwas günstiger (20 Euro) ist das Modell von Innr*, das aber auch mit dem Hue-System kompatibel ist.
Speziell für Apple-Nutzer:innen hat Eve mit dem Energy Strip* eine Mehrfachsteckdose im Angebot. Diese könnt ihr entweder über die App des Herstellers steuern oder sie in Homekit integrieren. Neben einem iPhone oder iPad braucht ihr dazu allerdings einen Homepod (Mini 2) oder ein Apple TV. Dazu kommt, dass die Steckleiste in der Regel um die 100 Euro kostet. Derzeit ist sie allerdings auf rund 70 Euro reduziert. Zusätzlich verzichtet Eve auf eine Cloud und die Registrierung in der App. Eure Daten bleiben also bei euch.

articles.title: 'Outrageous,' 'reckless,' 'wow': Here's what politicians are saying about Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia
articles.text:
Jensen Huang is back. The Nvidia CEO and founder, who was ousted from his company a little over a week ago after revelations of extramarital affairs (including, critically, a dalliance with a suspected Chinese spy), has apparently been deemed too big to fail.
Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and subsequently grew the chipmaker into one of the most powerful companies in the world, has now been reinstated by the company’s board. The move was one that President Trump lobbied for. On Monday, after Huang’s return was announced, the president posted an AI-generated meme of the CEO holding a woman’s bra, an image that recalled the famous photo from Trump’s own assassination attempt.
Just how and why all of this has happened is a question that everybody is still scrambling to figure out. Because Nvidia is an economically important company, it is also a politically important one. Yet there’s a lot of disagreement over just how important Huang, himself, is — and whether his importance outweighs the alleged dangers of Chinese espionage to which his affair with Alice Huang may have exposed the company.
Even if Huang is back for now, the Nvidia founder may face an uphill battle given the changing political landscape wrought by the “blue wave” of Democratic victories that swept the U.S. midterms. Huang, now aligned with Trump, will face increased scrutiny from congressional Democrats — starting with a public Senate appearance scheduled for next week. He is also expected to testify privately before several House committees next month, including the Intelligence Committee, the Foreign Affairs Committee, and the China Select Committee.
If initial responses from current political leaders are any indication, Huang has his work cut out for him. As news of his return broke on Monday, politicians and public figures from across the political spectrum weighed in — and many didn’t seem too pleased.

articles.title: GrapheneOS diz que Google ameaça fabricantes para barrar sistema
articles.text:
GrapheneOS diz que Google ameaça fabricantes para barrar sistema
Projeto afirma que licenças dos serviços Google vêm sendo usadas para impedir parcerias. Motorola já confirmou suporte ao GrapheneOS no Signature 27.
Os desenvolvedores do GrapheneOS acusaram o Google de ameaçar fabricantes de celulares para impedir parcerias com o projeto. No X, a equipe afirma que a big tech questiona fabricantes sobre possíveis acordos com o sistema e ameaça impor condições mais restritivas de licenciamento de seus serviços.
O grupo também acusa o Google de desencorajar o desbloqueio do bootloader, procedimento necessário para instalar outro sistema operacional no aparelho. As declarações foram publicadas em meio à preparação para a chegada do sistema, baseado no Android e focado em privacidade e segurança, aos aparelhos da Motorola.
O projeto atribui as supostas pressões à área comercial do Google, mas não divulgou documentos nem identificou fabricantes. A equipe, porém, manifestou interesse em procurar autoridades e reguladores dos Estados Unidos.
A Motorola anunciou uma parceria com a fundação responsável pelo GrapheneOS em março e já confirmou o Signature 27 como seu primeiro aparelho com suporte previsto ao sistema. Isso não significa que o telefone chegará às lojas com o GrapheneOS pré-instalado.
A marca ainda divulgará detalhes sobre a disponibilização. Por enquanto, a lista pública de aparelhos com versões prontas para uso continua restrita aos Pixels. O suporte depende de adaptações ao hardware e requisitos de segurança definidos pelo projeto, razão pela qual a parceria não garante que o sistema possa ser instalado em qualquer celular da Motorola.
A disputa envolve uma diferença importante no Android. O Android Open Source Project (AOSP) reúne o código aberto que terceiros podem usar para criar seus próprios sistemas. Já o Google Mobile Services (GMS), pacote com aplicativos e serviços como a Play Store, depende de licença comercial.
Para considerar um aparelho compatível, o Google exige requisitos técnicos e testes. Essa aprovação não concede a licença dos aplicativos, que segue um processo separado. Esse controle já esteve no centro de uma disputa com a Acer. Em 2012, a fabricante cancelou a apresentação do CloudMobile A800 com Aliyun, desenvolvido pela Alibaba, após a oposição do Google.
A Amazon fez um movimento em outra direção. Após anos usando o Fire OS, derivado do Android e sem a loja do Google, a empresa lançou recentemente novos tablets com Android e acesso à Play Store. Esses aparelhos possuem a Alexa+ e permitem acessar aplicativos como Gmail, YouTube e Google Docs, aproximando os tablets da Amazon do ecossistema de aplicativos e serviços licenciados pelo Google.
No GrapheneOS, os serviços do Google são opcionais. Quem precisa deles pode instalá-los como aplicativos comuns, sem os privilégios que costumam ter em outros celulares Android. Essa abordagem permite usar parte do ecossistema Google, mantendo o controle de permissões do sistema.

D’ordinaire, l’Europe découvre les nouveautés de l’intelligence artificielle avec une mention frustrante en bas de page : « réservé aux États-Unis ». Pour une fois, le drapeau change de camp, on passe à « Europe uniquement » au lieu de « US uniquement ».
La start-up parisienne offre un mois complet de Vibe Pro, la formule payante de son assistant (l’ex-Le Chat) taillée pour le développement, grâce au code promo MISTRALVIBE.
La semaine dernière déjà, Mistral lançait le code LECHONK pour offrir trois mois de Vibe Pro aux développeurs européens, mais dans la limite des stocks disponibles. L’opération célébrait l’intégration de Large 4, son modèle phare présenté début octobre, ainsi que le lancement d’une application de bureau dédiée sur macOS et Windows.
Les places s’étant envolées en moins d’une heure, Mistral élargit le tir tout en réduisant la durée : l’abonnement Pro étant facturé 14,99 euros HT par mois (soit 17,99 euros TTC en France), le cadeau passe d’environ 54 euros à 18 euros.
    Pour aller plus loin
« On a accompli des miracles » : Mistral annonce Large 4, sa nouvelle IA surpuissante qui défie les cadors chinois
            
Un modèle européen, mais avec un colocataire chinois
Derrière le « modèle européen » vanté par la marque se cache Mistral Large 4, surnommé en interne Le Chonk. Ce mastodonte totalise environ 1 000 milliards de paramètres (les réglages internes acquis durant l’entraînement), dont seuls 49 milliards s’activent réellement à chaque mot généré grâce à une architecture en mélange d’experts (mixture of experts) qui réduit drastiquement le coût de calcul.
Ses poids sont téléchargeables librement depuis le 29 octobre, et Mistral prépare déjà une déclinaison allégée capable de tourner sur PC portable. Petite ironie toutefois : Vibe donne aussi accès à GLM 5.3, un modèle conçu par le laboratoire chinois Z.ai et hébergé sur les serveurs de Mistral, que l’entreprise française avait même placé par défaut dans la version web de Vibe Code cet automne.
Si Mistral assure que son tandem Vibe et Le Chonk surclasse GLM et DeepSeek en programmation, les benchmarks indépendants dressent un bilan plus nuancé. Sur l’indice d’agents de code d’Artificial Analysis, Vibe propulsé par Large 4 décroche 48 points contre 49 points pour GLM 5.3 dans l’outil open source Opencode, loin derrière Claude Code (62 points) et Codex d’OpenAI (55 points).
La véritable force de Mistral se joue en réalité sur la rentabilité : une tâche de développement revient en moyenne à 1,26 dollar au tarif API (facturé aux développeurs), contre 5,23 dollars pour son rival chinois. De quoi confirmer que Large 4 a bien rattrapé les meilleures IA chinoises en code sur le rapport performances-prix.
    Pour aller plus loin
Mistral Large 4 rattrape les meilleures IA chinoises en code, et tout le monde peut le télécharger
            
    Pour aller plus loin
Mistral Large 4 est-il surcoté ? Voici ce que disent les benchmarks indépendants
            
Comment activer votre mois gratuit (et les précautions à prendre)
Pour profiter de l’offre, il suffit de créer un compte Mistral puis de se rendre sur la page d’échange de code, où le coupon MISTRALVIBE est déjà prérempli. 
Une fois activé, Vibe s’utilise au choix dans le navigateur, via l’application de bureau macOS et Windows ou directement en ligne de commande dans le terminal (où l’agent lit vos fichiers, exécute des commandes et modifie le code), avec des extensions disponibles pour VS Code, JetBrains et Zed.
Avant de tester l’outil, pensez à vérifier dans le menu quel moteur est actif afin de sélectionner Large 4 plutôt que GLM 5.3; sachant que pour exécuter l’IA 100 % en local sur votre machine, il faudra encore patienter jusqu’à la sortie de la version allégée de Large 4 promise par Mistral.
Côté conditions, Mistral promet de pouvoir coder toute la journée dans la limite d’un « usage raisonnable » dont aucun quota chiffré n’est précisé, sans détailler non plus les frontières exactes de l’« Europe » (un utilisateur @andacgvn demande ainsi si la Turquie est éligible).
Une carte bancaire est exigée à l’inscription : pensez donc à programmer un rappel avant la fin des trente jours pour résilier si vous ne souhaitez pas être prélevé de 17,99 euros par mois.
    Pour aller plus loin
« Il tournera sur PC portable » : Mistral nous confirme un Large 4 allégé

articles.title: Piratage de frigos de supermarchés : une opération secrète a évité une catastrophe au Royaume-Uni
articles.text:
Pendant environ trois semaines, une opération de cybersécurité menée dans le plus grand secret a permis de sécuriser des dizaines de milliers de frigos et de congélateurs au Royaume-Uni, révèle la BBC. Seuls les frigos de supermarchés, d’entrepôts, de restaurants, ou de stations-service, sont concernés.
L’opération, qui vient d’être révélée par la presse britannique, devait permettre d’éviter une vague de cyberattaques similaire à celle enregistrée dans plusieurs pays européens le mois dernier. Début octobre, près de 700 supermarchés ont été visés par des pirates. En pleine nuit, ils ont déréglé les frigos, poussant les enseignes à jeter des montagnes de nourriture. Dans certains cas, les frigos en surchauffe ont même provoqué des incendies.
La France a attribué l’attaque aux Gardiens de la révolution iraniens, une unité secrète de l’armée iranienne. Quelques semaines plus tard, une deuxième vague a touché des supermarchés de sept pays européens, dont la Belgique et le Luxembourg. Le même jour, des congélateurs de banques de sang situés en France ont été visés par des cybercriminels, mais le pire a été évité.
« Un problème de mot de passe faible »
Jusqu’ici, le Royaume-Uni semblait épargné. Les magasins britanniques s’appuient en effet sur des équipements différents de ceux du reste de l’Europe. Fin du mois dernier, un employé du cabinet Omega Solutions, spécialisé dans la réfrigération, a voulu savoir si des pirates pouvaient également s’en prendre aux supermarchés britanniques. Il a donc examiné les boîtiers de contrôle de frigos les plus répandus au Royaume-Uni. Ceux-ci sont fabriqués par Resource Data Management (RDM), une société britannique.
 The UK may have narrowly avoided the refrigeration cyberattacks seen across Europe, but its systems weren’t without vulnerabilities.
We were approached by Neil McCourt at Omega Solutions about a significant vulnerability in RDM refrigeration controllers widely used across the UK. @cybergibbons and the rest of our hardware security team subsequently validated the findings and discovered several additional vulnerabilities similar to those affecting Danfoss controllers, but not identical.
What followed was a coordinated effort involving Pen Test Partners, Omega Solutions, RDM, NCSC, and organisations across the food supply chain to identify exposed systems and reduce the risk.
Much of this work took place quietly to avoid alerting potential attackers while remediation was underway.
We’re publishing now to help reach smaller operators further down the supply chain who may still be exposed. We’ve deliberately withheld technical exploitation details while remediation continues.
Organisations should ensure their refrigeration controllers aren’t directly accessible from the public internet and apply RDM’s latest security updates.
Our @TheKenMunroShow and Andrew Tierney explain how it unfolded, how the industry responded, and why there’s still some work to do.
📌 https://t.co/PpQH3ZnfVF
#CyberSecurity #OTSecurity #UKFridges #VulnerabilityDisclosure #FridgeHacks #BBC
— Pen Test Partners (@PenTestPartners) November 20, 2026
Dans les boîtiers, il a rapidement découvert une faille de sécurité. La vulnérabilité a été rapidement confirmée par les hackers éthiques de Pen Test Partners, une entreprise britannique spécialisée dans la cybersécurité. Interrogé par la BBC, Ken Munro, de Pen Test Partners, assure que « ces contrôleurs très répandus avaient un problème de mot de passe faible similaire à celui des appareils Danfoss et des autres contrôleurs attaqués avec succès ». L’expert fait référence aux contrôleurs de la société Danfoss, qui sont à l’origine de l’attaque contre les supermarchés français des 11 et 12 octobre. Une grande partie des installations compromises étaient protégées par des mots de passe faibles et faciles à deviner.
Selon le chercheur, il ne fallait probablement « plus que quelques jours avant que des criminels ou des pirates d’État » ne découvrent la faille, et cherchent à l’exploiter pour lancer des cyberattaques, similaires à celles enregistrées en France. Pour Garry Turner-Smith, d’Omega Solutions, un cabinet de conseil britannique spécialisé dans la réfrigération, des pirates « auraient pu prendre le contrôle total » des boîtiers vulnérables et « perturber les systèmes de réfrigération sur plusieurs sites », rapporte le Guardian. Il ajoute que « cet incident devrait servir de signal d’alarme pour toute l’industrie de la réfrigération ».
À lire aussi : Cyberattaques en cours dans le « monde entier » – le FBI alerte sur une vague d’intrusions menées par ARTEX, une redoutable IA
« Une course contre la montre »
Peu après la découverte de ce problème de mots de passe, le NCSC (National Cyber Security Centre), l’agence britannique de cybersécurité, a été alerté. C’est aussi le cas des ministères de l’Agriculture et de la Sécurité alimentaire du Royaume-Uni. L’alerte a été émise dans le plus grand secret pour éviter que des pirates ne soient mis au courant avant que le problème soit corrigé.
« Nous devions travailler discrètement pour ne pas alerter des hackers moins éthiques et des États comme l’Iran, qui sont actifs dans ce domaine », raconte Ken Munro.
Des milliers de boîtiers ont été déconnectés d’Internet de toute urgence, que ce soit à distance par le biais de panneaux de contrôle, ou à la main. Des employés ont en effet dû débrancher les câbles réseau et surveiller les températures manuellement le temps de colmater les vulnérabilités. Au sein d’une grande enseigne britannique, l’équipe informatique a mis hors ligne des centaines d’appareils chaque jour pendant une semaine.
« On avait l’impression d’une course contre la montre, car nous nous attendions à une nouvelle vague d’attaques », confie un employé à la BBC.
De son côté, Resource Data Management, la société à l’origine des contrôleurs vulnérables, conteste la gravité de la faille. Selon la firme, il faut se procurer un équipement bien précis pour prendre le contrôle des dispositifs mal protégés. C’est pourquoi Resource Data Management estime qu’une attaque était peu probable. À l’inverse de la société, les chercheurs assurent que les hackers pouvaient facilement profiter de la situation. Selon eux, le matériel nécessaire à une cyberattaque s’achète facilement sur eBay. Quoi qu’il en soit, Ged Evans, le patron de Resource Data Management, assure que son entreprise a agi « rapidement pour régler ce problème » et que des « premiers correctifs » ont été colmatés.
« Des efforts considérables ont été déployés en très peu de temps, ce qui a obligé les équipes des enseignes à travailler le soir et le week-end », explique Pen Test Partners.
Des milliers de frigos toujours en danger
En dépit des efforts des chercheurs et de Resource Data Management, la menace n’est pas totalement écartée. Ken Munro estime que « des milliers de petits magasins sont toujours exposés ». Il faut encore du temps pour couper ces boîtiers d’Internet et installer la mise à jour. En attendant que tous les frigos soient à l’abri des pirates, les chercheurs ont soigneusement gardé le secret sur les détails des failles, et sur les méthodes d’exploitation.

articles.title: Mouse gamer barato: 10 modelos a partir de R$ 100 para comprar em 2026
articles.text:
Mouse gamer barato: 10 modelos a partir de R$ 100 para comprar em 2026
Selecionamos os melhores mouses gamer com preço baixo e bom custo-benefício para comprar sem medo; lista inclui modelos Logitech, Redragon, Attack Shark e mais
Quem busca um mouse gamer barato, encontra modelos com boas taxas de polling rate e alta sensibilidade numa faixa de preço entre R$ 100 e R$ 500.
Modelos mais avançados como o Delux M900 Pro se destacam pela latência baixa de 0,125 ms. Mas também existem mouses mais básicos focados em faixas de sensibilidade mais ampla e custo mais acessível, a exemplo do Redragon Neva Standard.
A seguir, o Tecnoblog lista 10 opções de mouse gamer baratos para otimizar o seu setup. Confira prós e contras de modelos da Delux, Redragon, Rappo, Attack Shark, Logitech e Havit.
Flutuação de preço 💸
Esta lista foi montada em novembo de 2026 e os preços dos produtos podem variar conforme disponibilidade no varejo. Para obter as melhores ofertas em tempo real, acesse o Achados do Tecnoblog.
O Redragon King Pro 1K é o mouse mais leve da lista, pesando apenas 49 g. Seu design simétrico se adapta a usuários destros ou canhotos, e os switches Huano Blue dot Blue têm cliques mais rígidos e durabilidade estimada de 50 milhões de cliques.
O periférico traz o mesmo sensor PAW3395 visto no Delux M900 Pro, com sensibilidade de até 26.000 DPI. Já o polling rate de 1.000 Hz tem atraso de resposta de aproximadamente 1 ms, sendo ideal para jogos competitivos que exigem rastreamento de mira preciso.
Você pode usar o mouse via cabo, conexão wireless de 2,4 GHz ou Bluetooth 5.1. Mas o ponto negativo é que a recarga completa da bateria de 400 mAh leva aproximadamente 4 horas.

Dentro da carcaça está o sensor avançado PAW 3398, com sensibilidade de até 26.000 DPI e velocidade máxima de deslocamento de 650 IPS. O polling rate alcança até 4.000 Hz, mas somente se você comprar o receptor V2M 4K separadamente. Com o dongle que acompanha a caixa, a frequência fica em 1.000 Hz.
A bateria é um dos destaques, com autonomia de 160 horas. Não há suporte para conexões Bluetooth, embora você ainda possa usar o mouse sem fio via conexão wireless de 2,4 GHz.

O Delux M900 Pro é um mouse sem fio ultraleve voltado para mãos médias ou grandes, com design assimétrico. Ele chega com microswitches Huano Blue dot Pink, com força de acionamento de 50 gf a 60 gf e vida útil estimada de 80 milhões de cliques.
O polling rate de até 8.000 Hz reduz a latência para até 0,125 ms, o que garante respostas rápidas para jogos competitivos. Já o sensor PAW3395 garante sensibilidade de até 26.000 DPI e velocidade máxima de deslocamento de 650 IPS para movimentos rápidos e com precisão.
A bateria promete até 65 horas de duração e a embalagem acompanha uma dock para carregamento magnético. O mouse funciona com ou sem fio (2,4 GHz), mas não é compatível com conexões Bluetooth.

O Attack Shark X11 é um mouse gamer com boa relação custo-benefício, projetado para mãos grandes ou médias e uso ambidestro. Sua vida útil é mais baixa que outros modelos da lista devido aos switches Huano Blue dot White, com durabilidade média de 20 milhões de cliques.
O mouse conta com o sensor PAW3311 que, apesar de não ser dos mais avançados, tem até 22.000 DPI e velocidade máxima de rastreamento de 400 IPS. E o polling rate de 1.000 Hz tem atraso de 1 ms para boa performance em jogos.
A bateria dura até 65 horas e a embalagem acompanha uma dock para carregamento magnético. Falando de conexões, o mouse funciona no modo cabeado ou sem fio, via wireless 2,4 GHz ou Bluetooth 5.2.

O periférico tem polling rate de até 1.000 Hz e usa o mesmo sensor PAW3311 visto no modelo X11. No entanto, a sensibilidade máxima é de 18.000 DPI. Ainda é uma faixa ampla, mas com um teto menor comparado ao Attack Shark X11.
A bateria também tem autonomia de até 65 horas e suporta carregamento apenas via cabo USB-C. Por falar nisso, o mouse funciona no modo cabeado, via conexão wireless de 2,4 GHz ou por Bluetooth 5.2.

O mouse é alimentado pelo sensor Hero, com sensibilidade de até 12.000 DPI e velocidade máxima de deslocamento de 400 IPS. Já o polling rate é de 1.000 Hz, que representa uma frequência mais básica com intervalo nominal de 1 ms.
Não há Bluetooth integrado ou suporte para uso cabeado, já que a conexão é restrita ao modo wireless de 2,4 GHz. O periférico também não conta com bateria interna e requer uma pilha AA. A autonomia pode chegar a 250 horas, dependendo do uso e da qualidade da pilha.

O Redragon Invader Pro é um mouse sem fio ideal para quem joga com várias macros, já que ele chega com nove botões personalizáveis. Um dos pontos negativos é que não há informações precisas sobre os switches usados e nem em relação à durabilidade de cliques.
O mouse traz o sensor PMW3325 e tem sensibilidade de até 10.000 DPI, que é uma boa faixa para jogos ou usos gerais. Já o polling rate de 1.000 Hz alcança uma latência de comunicação do periférico de apenas 1 ms. E isso significa comandos responsivos durante as gameplays.

O Logitech G203 é um mouse com fio e design simétrico, sendo boa opção para usuários destros ou canhotos. O periférico tem durabilidade próxima a 10 milhões de cliques, embora a marca não divulgue informações sobre os switches utilizados.
Você pode encontrar o mouse nas versões Prodigy ou Lightsync, ambos com polling rate de 1.000 Hz. Porém, vale apostar no segundo modelo, já que ele é mais atualizado e possui uma faixa mais ampla de sensibilidade, de até 8.000 DPI.
O mouse funciona exclusivamente via cabo, sem depender de bateria ou pilhas. E caso esteja acostumado com mouses com fio, ele é uma escolha segura e com preço mais acessível.

O Redragon Neva Standard é um mouse ultraleve que pesa apenas 54 gramas. Ele apresenta um shape ambidestro e ergonômico, que se adapta a diferentes tipos de pegada. E ainda conta com seis botões programáveis.
O periférico traz o sensor PAW3311, com rastreamento preciso para jogos e até 12.000 DPI. Enquanto isso, o polling rate de até 1.000 Hz garante um intervalo de comunicação rápido de apenas 1 ms.
O dispositivo de entrada ainda conta com bateria interna de 400 mAh e três modos de conexão: via cabo USB-C, wireless de 2,4 GHz e Bluetooth.

O Havit MS966SE é um mouse sem fio voltado para destros, por conta do seu design assimétrico. Ele possui seis botões programáveis e durabilidade estimada em 20 milhões de cliques, apesar de a marca não identificar os switches adotados.
No interior do mouse está o sensor de entrada PMW3325, com sensibilidade máxima de 10.000 DPI para adaptação em diferentes tipos de jogos. Já o polling rate de 1.000 Hz mantém o tempo de comunicação de 1 ms para um delay mínimo de comandos.
O periférico funciona via conexão Bluetooth 5.2 e também pode operar no modo wireless (2,4 GHz) ou com cabo. E ainda inclui uma bateria com 300 mAh de capacidade.
| Características | Especificações | 
|---|---|

| Peso | 68 g | 
| Pegada recomendada | Claw ou fingertip | 
| Orientação | Destro | 
| Cores disponíveis | Preto, branco e branco com azul | 
A escolha pelo melhor mouse gamer barato deve considerar suas preferências de uso e as especificações do periférico. Vale ficar de olho em aspectos como:
- Dimensões e peso: confira as dimensões e peso do mouse e veja se as medidas batem com suas preferências de uso. Essa questão é puramente pessoal, já que o modelo ideal varia de usuário para usuário.
- Design do mouse: prefira mouses recomendados para seu tipo de pegada (claw, palm ou fingertip). Não esqueça também de olhar se o periférico tem design assimétrico (para destro ou canhoto) ou simétrico (ambidestro).
- Sensor adotado: verifique a velocidade (IPS) e aceleração (medido em G) do sensor adotado. Essas duas métricas indicam a capacidade de acompanhar movimentos rápidos sem perder o rastreamento. E quanto maiores os números, maior a rastreabilidade para movimentos intensos.
- Tipos de switches: pesquise sobre os switches adotados, já que eles têm sensações táteis e durabilidade diferentes. A sensação de clique é questão de gosto pessoal, mas se possível, escolha modelos com vida útil prolongada para evitar problemas no curto e médio prazo.
- Polling rate: polling rate é a frequência com que o mouse envia dados de posição e cliques, medida em hertz (Hz). Taxas de 1.000 Hz já são ótimas para games, mas índices mais altos como 4.000 Hz ou 8.000 Hz garantem comandos ainda mais responsivos.
- Faixa de sensibilidade: a sensibilidade (expressa em DPI) determina o quanto o cursor se desloca em relação ao movimento físico do mouse. Jogos de tiro não precisam de DPI elevado, mas altas taxas de sensibilidade podem ser úteis em games de outros gêneros que exigem grandes deslocamentos do cursor.
- Número de botões: o número de botões é importante para jogadores que configuram macros de atalho durante as jogatinas. E caso jogue títulos que se beneficiam disso, aposte em mouses com vários botões personalizáveis.
- Conectividade: mouses com mais conexões oferecem mais versatilidade de uso. A conexão wireless de 2,4 GHz é ideal para jogos pela latência mais baixa, mas modelos com Bluetooth também permitem que você use o mouse em dispositivos com suporte a essa conexão.
- Autonomia de bateria: priorize mouses com autonomias prolongadas, caso vá optar por modelos sem fio. Os periféricos suportam carregamento via cabo enquanto você joga, porém, modelos mais duradouros garantem mais autonomia longe de cabos.
Mouses gamer oferecem várias faixas de sensibilidade para adequação a diferentes usos e tipos de jogo. Além disso, eles têm polling rate mais elevados para diminuir o intervalo de atraso e garantir comandos mais responsivos, e costumam ter vida útil prolongada.
Já mouses comuns focam apenas em ser um periférico funcional. Por isso, eles costumam ter mais delay e não oferecem faixa de sensibilidade ampla. E geralmente são menos duradouros, porque não foram projetados para atender à alta demanda de cliques de jogos.
Sim. Mouses gamer baratos e importados se destacam pela boa relação custo-benefício, com especificações interessantes a custos mais baixos. Vale apostar em marcas confiáveis como Attack Shark, Delux ou Rappo, que já têm certa notoriedade no mercado.
No entanto, você pode enfrentar dificuldades para suporte ou políticas de troca e reembolso — algo comum em compras internacionais. E certifique-se de fazer a compra em marketplaces ou importadoras confiáveis para evitar de receber um modelo divergente do escolhido.
Não é obrigatório, mas trata-se de uma prática altamente recomendada, especialmente em mesas de vidro ou com acabamento brilhante.
Mousepads oferecem uma superfície mais uniforme para que o sensor óptico consiga rastrear os movimentos com mais precisão. Os materiais usados nesses acessórios também oferecem deslize mais suave e maior controle do mouse.
Além disso, usar um mousepad ajuda a diminuir o desgaste dos pés de deslizamento do mouse, que podem se deteriorar mais rapidamente devido ao atrito direto em mesas ou superfícies mais ásperas.
Sim. Mouses sem fio pareados via Bluetooth têm atraso perceptível, com latências de até 20 ms. Já mouses que usam conexão wireless de 2,4 GHz costumam ter latência em torno de 1 ms a 2 ms, e o atraso tende a ser imperceptível comparado a um mouse com fio.
Importante mencionar que monitores com taxas de atualização mais altas ajudam a diminuir essa sensação de atraso do mouse, já que atualizam a imagem em intervalos menores. E a boa notícia é que existem monitores gamer baratos que oferecem essa sensação de comandos mais fluidos.

articles.title: How Toronto is making it easier for actors and indies to collaborate on games
articles.text:
Canadian film and TV productions are having a bit of a moment. Crave’s Heated Rivalry and Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie. CBC’s North of North. Netflix’s Below. Over the past year, all of these titles, among others, have been glowingly received around the world, not just here at home.
But something that historically hasn’t gotten nearly as much attention is Canada’s video game industry. Despite being one of the largest game development hubs in the world thanks to over 800 studios bringing in $5.1 billion to our GDP, there isn’t all that much awareness about, well, any of it.
ACTRA Toronto, the trade union representing more than 15,000 of the city’s performers, is hoping to help with that. Over the past few years, the organization has been making a concerted effort to bring together its members and our many local developers to make games. Most prominently, this includes a recently ratified three-year agreement with publishing giant Ubisoft, which records many of its AAA titles in Toronto. But of course, that’s only one part of the equation, given that so many other games are made here, especially on the indie front.
To address that, ACTRA Toronto has recently come forth with a new low-budget video game agreement aimed at making it easier for smaller teams to work with union talent.
“This all came about through a very passionate conversation at a union picnic a couple of summers ago, where I literally was like, ‘I was a lead in a video game. Why am I not auditioning for things?'” says Elana Dunkelman, ACTRA Toronto councillor and vice president who was also nominated for a Canadian Game Award for playing the titular lead role in Ubisoft Quebec’s Immortals Fenyx Rising. She says some peers she knows were going years without work, which is a particular problem since, contrary to popular belief, the majority of actors are far from millionaires.
On the video game front, specifically, conversations with those in the industry led the union to realize that there wasn’t much information readily available for developers interested in working with actors.
“Let’s say you’re a developer and it’s 3 a.m. and you’re like, ‘Hey, you know what? I actually want to do voice,’ and you Google ‘voice actors Toronto,’ and ACTRA Toronto pops up. And then you go to the website, and there’s no rate chart. You’re just going to automatically assume that it’s way too expensive and way too difficult, and you’re going to close the browser and pick a different route,” says Dunkelman. “So we made the recommendation that ACTRA Toronto build our own low-budget indie video game agreement to make rates transparent and accessible to developers, and then […] it was developed and brought forward to members for input.”
As ACTRA Toronto director of contracts and production Gail Haupert explains, the previous lack of such an agreement created a “lot of hurdles” for developers and performers alike.
“So our performers do have to be under a contract; they have to work on an ACTRA contract of some kind,” she says. “We’re generally able to work out some terms with producers, but without having a specific agreement to point to say, ‘These are the rates, this is how our performers can work,’ there wasn’t anything for our performers to turn to if they were approached by a video game company saying, ‘We want to work with you.’ And we wanted to be able to change that. We’re all about creating opportunities both for the indie producers as well as our performers.”
With this new agreement, developers can clearly see different rates for actors depending on the budget of their game, which Haupert says will provide flexibility.
“In all honesty, we heard from a bunch of producers. We had letters of understanding in place with some smaller video games before we had a bigger agreement in place to encompass it all, so some of the feedback we heard is their budgets were too low for a specific rate, or budgets that were offered, say, to a AAA game company, the performer rates they couldn’t afford because they don’t make the kind of revenue that a AAA game does to put into their video games,” she says. “So we decided to tier our rate system. We have tiers one through six. So based on the budget you’re working with, you have a different rate of what you would pay the performer.”
View this post on Instagram
This includes options for developers who may not necessarily have the budget to fully buy out an actor (an “in perpetuity” deal). Dunkelman says this structure will help developers go into a project with a clearer sense of budget.
“I think having the rate charts ahead of time, and getting a rough estimate of how much money you’re going to need to be able to hire actors and incorporating that into your funding application, is going to be a game-changer,” she says.
That sentiment is shared by Lindsey Gardner, a veteran Toronto-based freelance casting director, voice director and voice performer. When it comes to video games, she’s voice directed on such big titles as Ubisoft’s Assassin’s Creed Shadows and Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora, alongside extensive work in animation, audiobooks, commercials and more.
For Gardner, ACTRA Toronto’s new agreement allows developers to tap into a vast talent pool that might otherwise have been overlooked.
“A lower budget does not mean lower quality in the performances. You still want the best. You might not be able to get high level A-listers, but the talent pool, especially with the new actor agreement, is phenomenal,” she says. “So you’re not compromising on the talent that you’re accessing. You’re just sort of accessing them in a different way — in a possibly more secure way as well, knowing that they have a resume as a performer.”
In particular, she notes that many of the actors in Toronto are trained in theatre, allowing them to bring a level of gravitas to gaming projects.
“Performers that have spent the volume of their time studying those types of performance are in the union for the most part. Those are our theatre actors. Those are our performers that are on film and television,” she says. “And so, by having this agreement, you’re getting access to the people that know not just how to use their voice, but know how to use their voice to create a character, to create depth, to create realism […] When you give direction to try something different, they have the range to try something completely different, even with that same line.”
And, of course, a lot of actors are themselves gamers, and that passion can naturally be funnelled into a game to great results. Look no further than ACTRA member Jon McLaren, whose lead role as Star-Lord in Eidos Montreal’s Marvel’s Guardians of Galaxy landed him a coveted BAFTA nomination. Notably, the Ottawa native is a lifelong gamer and regular streamer in between acting gigs, and because of that, he’s long wanted to work on more games. The previous lack of a uniform indie agreement, however, has made that difficult.
“With this new agreement, that’s hopefully going to allow us to participate more and have these conversations with indie developers. Because there’s nothing more exciting than meeting someone at a level of passion that you have, and I’m sure it goes both ways with the developers,” says McLaren. “It’s about that passion that is in some of us who just love video games and want to contribute and want to be a part of them more than anything.”
For him, the goal is to be more involved in video games, regardless of their size.
“I just want every single opportunity that I can get to be in the next video game. And it doesn’t matter if you’re a AAA developer or you’re an indie developer. I just want to work with really great people who are telling awesome stories,” he says. To demonstrate this openness, he even asked to share his personal email here for developers: hello@jonmclaren.com.
“We’re in constant conversation about how we can formulate a plan to raise awareness with indie developers, this article included. I hope we can get this out to as many people and hit developers to help educate them to know that there are options out there. Because I’ve been to a few things around Toronto, like Toronto Game Expo and stuff like that. We’ve talked to people, and they’re like, ‘Oh, I didn’t know you could do that!'” he says.
“If people have been hesitant or think that it’s not possible — anything is possible! And certainly, from my perspective, especially with these new agreements, I’m happy to help do some of the groundwork if it means we get to bring your idea and your game to life. I’m so excited to be a part of it.”
Blessing of Resthaven
So far, the first indie game to incorporate ACTRA Toronto’s new low-budget agreement is Curse of Resthaven, a recently released narrative roguelite about a governor who has to manage a cursed island while searching for his missing niece. It was developed by Toronto-based Hilltop Studios, the team behind 2024’s acclaimed Lil’ Guardsman that also has deep ties to Canada’s arts scene.
That’s because the studio’s founder, Scott Christian, is a veteran musical director, composer, arranger and pianist who’s performed across Canada, a prolific artistic background that he wanted to leverage on his burgeoning game development journey.
“We make relatively low-budget indie games, and I’m always thinking about how to bring a level of polish and production value that lifts us above the pack. With both Lil’ Guardsman and Curse of Resthaven, we had wonderful artists, but very small teams and no dedicated animators. So the creative math became: let’s go all-in on full voice acting to compensate a little,” says Christian.
“And that gamble really paid off. I know firsthand that people’s memories of our games often suggest there’s more animation than there actually is! I think a lot of that is the power of voice acting. Great performances give characters a sense of life and personality that can literally trick your brain as you lose yourself in the experience.”
Given that Christian’s network of friends now consists of many folks in both the game development and acting scenes, he says he was inspired to help come up with a way to better combine those two fields. This led him to work closely with ACTRA Toronto to develop the new low-budget agreement and incorporate it into Curse of Resthaven, his sophomore game.
“He was just so supportive and just a huge champion for this agreement, and he provided his input. And then when he was ready, he actually piloted it, and he’s been very vocal online about the amazing actors that he has cast in his game, and the fact that he had piloted the agreement,” says Dunkelman. “I think having such a strong voice in the indie space like Scott is so important because a lot of what I’m learning as [someone who is] not a developer is that word of mouth is just so important. Because people talk to each other and learn from each other, and it’s such a strong community. And having Scott champion it has been so, so amazing.”
“I think one of the real benefits of the new agreement is that it’s something that’s been developed with input from ACTRA membership, so actors can take it to their agents and it feels very solid and legit,” explains Christian. “That’s a lot easier than presenting an agent with a Frankenstein’d, one-off contract that’s been cobbled together for the individual project. In our case, the voice cast were all people who were excited about working on the game, and having the agreement in place made it a really smooth process to make that happen.”
Certainly, Curse of Resthaven speaks for itself with its impressive assortment of seasoned Canadians actors from across the film, TV and, yes, gaming spaces. This includes Wade Bogert-O’Brien (Beacon 23), Raoul Bhaneja (Star Trek: Starfleet Academy), Jan Alexandra Smith (Mass Effect), and Alana Bridgewater (Cuphead).
For Bogert-O’Brien, a longtime friend of Christian, Curse of Resthaven presented the special opportunity to lead the sort of narrative adventure game he adored as a kid while doing something uncommon in the space.
“So many indie games don’t have voice acting at all. Even narrative-heavy visual novel-style games often don’t have full voice acting. My guess is that this largely comes down to cost, but I think voice acting really adds a lot to the experience and immersion of a game,” he says. “It’s been really cool to see how excited so many players are that Curse of Resthaven is fully voiced. Without this agreement I probably wouldn’t have been able to be involved at all. Either Hilltop wouldn’t have been able to afford to do voice acting or they would have hired non-union performers.”
He adds that it’s a good deal for both performers and developers, especially in the long-term. “The structure of this agreement seems to allow the studios to engage ACTRA performers under an affordable day rate, but ensures those actors will be compensated additionally if the game becomes a big hit,” he explains. “This seems like a fair compromise for the studios to be able to afford to engage union performers, while ensuring performers will get a fair share of the proceeds from their work.”
Curse of Resthaven is out now on Steam!
Congratulations to @playhilltop.bsky.social on launching Curse of Resthaven, the first game made under the ACTRA Toronto Low Budget Video Game Agreement.
— ACTRA Toronto (@actratoronto.bsky.social) October 29, 2026 at 1:24 PM
Bhaneja, who plays General Oliver Bolingbroke in Curse of Resthaven, says he enjoys the transformative nature of gaming work and was “thrilled” to channel that in an independent Canadian project with longtime theatre collaborator Christian.
“I need to work on union projects. I am a member for 30 years and many decades with SAG-AFTRA as well, so it’s important to me,” he says. “A new agreement that supports independent Canadian developers and with roles I am interested in playing makes it a no-brainer. These guys wrote some intelligent story and dialogue so it wasn’t just grunts, yells and other efforts!”
He says union talent is a “great boon” for indie developers, and Curse of Resthaven is the perfect example of that.
“The quality of some of the performers is very high, as they recruited some of the best theatre actors in Toronto and around to contribute, particularly for a period/fantasy game. It’s nice to have that weight behind it,” he says. “I hope this allows for more collabs in the future between union actors and creators. As long as we are compensated for our work and have a slice of future profits, it’s fair to me.”
And best of all, Hilltop’s success proves that indies don’t need extravagant equipment to produce results. By Christian’s own admission, voice recordings for both of his games were done with actors in his basement studio under the direction of him and co-writer Matt Bernard.
“There are options at pretty much every scale and budget. If you have the money, you can bring in an external team, rent a beautiful recording studio, and get some absolutely stunning results. But if you have someone on your team who handles sound or audio, a half-decent microphone and a reasonably quiet space can get you surprisingly far,” says Christian.
“We’ve won awards for the voice work in our games, and I can tell you that our recording setup is much, much closer to the latter than the former! You don’t need a AAA production pipeline to get wonderful performances. You need good actors, someone who can give them direction, and a little bit of care and attention to the process. Start with what you have and don’t let the lack of a fancy setup scare you off.”
Next steps
Of course, the low-budget agreement is just one part of ACTRA Toronto’s wider gaming push.
For Dunkelman, a key focus is spreading the word about working in games in general. Those efforts are clearly on display, as she’s frequently been with fellow ACTRA Toronto member Myles Dobson (The Next Step), Samy Osman (Rainbow Six Siege) and other colleagues at events like the XP Game Summit and Toronto Game Expo throughout their outreach efforts. Dunkelman says she’s heartened to see the community start to recognize actors at these shows and ask for more information about the union, and she has hopes to take that even further.
“My dream is that we get into schools to start not only providing information about the union and the agreement, but also skills sharing where we can share tips and tricks on working with actors, so that they feel more confident about actually incorporating voice into their games. Because I think sometimes developers don’t even consider that, and that’s okay. Obviously, some games don’t have voice, and that’s totally fine,” she says.
“But if there are any barriers in terms of someone maybe being nervous about working with an actor or unsure, I want them to feel so confident and have the skills to be able to direct actors, to put out a casting call that they know that they’re going to get the the right voice for that character because they know how to create a breakdown. I want it to be so second nature by the time that they get into the workplace that they’re excited to work with actors. They are already thinking about voice as opposed to adding it on at the end or not even considering it.”
So far, Haupert says she’s optimistic based on ACTRA’s conversations with studios.
“In all honesty, we’ve seen a lot of games come forward. We had one game from around 2020 that came forward. We told them the rates. They said, ‘Sorry, we can’t afford it,’ tried to go off and do it non-union, came back to us and said, ‘We couldn’t find the voices to do it non-union,” she says. “[They] turned the whole thing into an ACTRA production, got the voices banged out in one session, and the game — I don’t think I can name the game right now — went on to be pretty successful after that. And then this company wanted to keep working with us because of the caliber of the voices that they were able to get.”
Christian wholeheartedly agrees.
“I hope that five years from now, we can look back and say this agreement helped encourage more indie teams to embrace voice acting in their games, and gave more professional actors opportunities to get into the medium. So many of them are hungry to!” he says. “It was really cool to have a handful of recognizable names in the cast of Curse of Resthaven, but there’s also an enormous wealth of underexposed and under-utilized talent here in Toronto. We have so many phenomenal performers who haven’t become household names, but are absolutely attainable at an indie budget level.”
While this might all seem like “inside baseball,” Dunkelman brings it all back to the average gamer with a relatable anecdote of recently playing through the Mass Effect trilogy, which stars Canadian actors Mark Meer and Jennifer Hale. In the wake of the closure of Edmonton-based Mass Effect developer BioWare, we’ve seen Meer and Hale back hundreds of thousands of fans who have passionately called for the return of the beloved sci-fi series.
“You spend more time with a video game character than you do for any character for a TV show or movie — hundreds of hours. No wonder people get extremely attached to characters!” she says. “And I think that’s something I’m really trying to reiterate to performers and tout why it’s important to have experienced actors and what we bring to a game.”
More information on ACTRA Toronto can be found on the union’s website.
The organization is also hosting a free panel on Monday, Nov. 23 at George Brown Polytechnic Waterfront to discuss bringing voiceover to games and share more about the new low-budget agreement.
Curse of Resthaven is now available on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2 and PC.
