articles.title: Una hoja de papel tiene 0,1 mm de grosor, pero al doblarla 27 veces se forma una pila más alta que el Everest. 15 pliegues más la elevan más allá de la Luna
articles.text:
El doblez de una hoja de papel es una acción muy común. Sin embargo, si tratamos de hacerlo muchas veces seguidas, nos encontraremos con algunos problemas. Por ejemplo, cuantos más dobleces hacemos, menos superficie queda. También se va engrosando el paquete. Hasta aquí son problemas físicos. Pero, si dejamos de lado esto último, podemos seguir calculando. Es decir, podemos pensar en cómo sería el tamaño de una hoja de papel doblada muchas veces.
Con 27 pliegues por la mitad, tenemos un grosor teórico de unos 13,42 km. Esto quiere decir que el Everest está por debajo (su altura sobre el nivel del mar es de 8.848,86 metros). Además, bastaría con 15 pliegues más (42 en total) para tener un tamaño de unos 439.805 km, que es superior a la distancia media de la Tierra a la Luna. Estos cálculos están hechos en el caso ideal (sin limitaciones de una hoja real).
Simplemente vamos doblando por la mitad. Es decir, en cada paso multiplicamos el grosor por dos. Empezando con 0,1 mm, tenemos: 0,1 mm × 2 = 0,2 mm (primer doblez); 0,2 mm × 2 = 0,4 mm (segundo); 0,4 mm × 2 = 0,8 mm (tercer doblez)… En general, el grosor tras N dobleces es 0,1 mm × 2^N.
Estos primeros números los podemos manejar en nuestro entorno. Por ejemplo, 10 pliegues nos darían 1.024 capas (grosor de 10,24 cm). Con 10 pliegues más tendríamos 1.048.576 capas (unos 105 metros). En cada paso multiplicamos por dos.
De esta forma podemos entender por qué saltamos el Everest. Con 24 pliegues tenemos unos 1,68 km. Con 25, unos 3,36 km y con 26, unos 6,71 km. La siguiente doblez nos añade 6,71 kilómetros de golpe. De esta forma superamos la cumbre.
De igual forma llegamos a la Luna. Con 40 dobleces tenemos cerca de 110.000 km. Con 41 dobleces tenemos cerca de 220.000 km. Con 42 dobleces llegamos a casi 440.000. Hemos hecho solo 15 dobleces desde que superamos el Everest. La distancia media a la Luna es de 384.400 km (NASA).
Esta es una de las dificultades que tenemos a la hora de manejar cantidades que se van multiplicando. Se trata de un sesgo del crecimiento exponencial. Como describen los investigadores Martin Schonger y Daniela Sele, hay una tendencia a subestimar el crecimiento exponencial. No es fácil imaginar cómo son los incrementos exponenciales.
La estudiante que consiguió doblar el papel 12 veces
Además de estos problemas de tipo geométrico, también tenemos que pensar en que, conforme vamos engrosando el paquete, necesitamos cada vez más material para poder hacer el siguiente pliegue (hay que envolver el conjunto). Durante mucho tiempo se pensó que era imposible pasar de 7-8 pliegues.
Sin embargo, en 2002 Britney Gallivan (que entonces era estudiante de secundaria en California) rompió este techo. El reto era doblar algo 12 veces por la mitad. Se trataba de un reto académico. Ella probó con hojas y periódicos. Y otros materiales. Pero fue acumulando fracasos. Al final llegó a plantear las ecuaciones correspondientes. Dependiendo de la dirección de los pliegues, la longitud necesaria varía según el grosor.
Guinness documenta que consiguió doblar 12 veces una misma pieza. Para ello utilizó una tira de papel tisú continua (de unos 1.219 m). Trabajó durante unas 8 horas. Las ecuaciones que desarrolló relacionaban las dimensiones del material con el número de pliegues posibles (tanto en una dirección como alternando). Para superar este techo es necesario utilizar una tira mucho más larga que una hoja normal.
A partir de ahí podemos seguir con la progresión matemática. Por ejemplo, con 69 pliegues llegamos a la escala de años luz. Con poco más de un centenar tenemos un tamaño parecido al del universo observable. Todos estos casos siguen siendo extensiones de este modelo ideal (fuera de las posibilidades físicas del papel).
Antes tenemos otro umbral. Con 51 pliegues tenemos unos 225,2 millones de km. Es decir, superamos los 150 millones de km que de media separan a la Tierra del Sol.

articles.title: Black Friday : un 65 pouces 4K QLED Dolby Vision à 499 € chez E.Leclerc
articles.text:
Black Friday : un 65 pouces 4K QLED Dolby Vision à 499 € chez E.Leclerc
Du 20 au 29 novembre, E.Leclerc propose le téléviseur Hisense 65E7S à 499 € au lieu de 699 €. Une offre intéressante pour cette TV 4K QLED de 164 cm compatible Dolby Vision IQ. Envie de savoir pourquoi elle mérite – ou pas ! – de trôner dans votre salon ? Suivez le guide.
Vous cherchez une TV 65 pouces abordable sans renoncer aux formats HDR récents ? À 499 €, le Hisense 65E7S revient à moins de 7,70 € le pouce de diagonale. L’intérêt de l’offre tient pourtant moins à ce ratio qu’à la fiche technique qui l’accompagne. Le modèle 2026 ne se limite pas à afficher de la 4K. Sa dalle QLED à points quantiques élargit la palette de couleurs, sa prise en charge couvre les deux grands formats HDR dynamiques, du Dolby Vision IQ au HDR10+ Adaptive, et ses trois entrées HDMI 2.1 laissent de quoi brancher plusieurs sources. Son terrain, ce sont les grands salons et les soirées qui passent du film à la série, avec une partie de console en invitée occasionnelle.
Qualité d’image : un grand format compatible avec tous les HDR
Avec 164 cm de diagonale et une définition de 3840 × 2160 pixels, le 65E7S supporte un recul de 2,5 à 3 mètres sans que vous perdiez le détail d’un visage ou la netteté d’un sous-titre. La technologie Hi-QLED ajoute à la dalle une couche de points quantiques (Quantum Dot) qui, selon Hisense, produit des couleurs plus saturées qu’un téléviseur LED classique. Les chaînes de la TNT et bon nombre de flux restant en HD, l’AI 4K Upscaler se charge de les mettre à l’échelle de l’écran, un traitement dont l’utilité grandit avec la diagonale.
Le traitement HDR est l’autre argument de ce modèle. Le 65E7S gère à la fois le Dolby Vision IQ et le HDR10+ Adaptive, deux formats dynamiques qui ajustent l’image scène par scène. Vous n’avez donc pas à vérifier lequel convient à votre plateforme de streaming. L’ajustement est automatique. Tous deux s’appuient parallèlement sur un capteur de luminosité, l’AI Light Sensor, pour adapter le rendu à l’éclairage de la pièce. Pour les puristes, le Filmmaker Mode désactive les traitements ajoutés par le téléviseur et restitue l’œuvre telle que le réalisateur l’a voulue.
Connectique : un équipement complet
Les trois entrées HDMI 2.1 accueillent en même temps votre box et votre console, la prise eARC restant disponible pour une barre de son. Deux ports USB complètent l’ensemble.
Côté jeu, le Game Mode Plus réunit le VRR, qui synchronise l’affichage avec la console jusqu’à 60 Hz, et l’ALLM, qui active automatiquement le mode à faible latence. Hisense annonce un retard à l’affichage de 10 ms au maximum, ainsi que la compatibilité Dolby Vision Gaming. Pour une partie de temps en temps, vous ne percevrez pas de décalage entre la manette et l’écran.
Au quotidien, l’interface VIDAA Smart OS regroupe les applications de streaming et se pilote à la voix. AirPlay 2 et le Bluetooth se chargent de relier votre smartphone ou un casque. Quant aux deux haut-parleurs de 10 W, compatibles Dolby Atmos, ils offrent selon Hisense un rendu plus large qu’une simple stéréo, suffisant pour un journal télévisé ou une série.
Les limites à connaître avant d’acheter
Trois concessions expliquent le tarif du 65E7S. La première concerne les joueurs assidus. Avec sa dalle 60 Hz native, ce téléviseur n’exploite pas les modes d’affichage à haute fréquence des consoles récentes. Si le jeu compétitif occupe l’essentiel de votre temps d’écran, ce modèle n’est peut-être pas le bon candidat. La deuxième porte sur le contraste. Le rétroéclairage DLED éclaire la dalle de façon uniforme, sans gradation locale par zones. Les noirs sont donc moins profonds que sur les téléviseurs capables d’atténuer une partie de leurs diodes, et le HDR demeure mesuré dans ses pics lumineux, malgré la compatibilité Dolby Vision IQ et HDR10+ Adaptive. Vous le remarquerez surtout dans une pièce plongée dans une vraie obscurité.
La dernière, enfin, porte sur le son. Les 20 W conviennent à un usage courant, mais une soirée cinéma gagnera à s’appuyer sur une barre de son, que la prise eARC permet de relier avec un seul câble. Ces réserves posées, le 65E7S répond à ce que son positionnement annonce, celui d’un grand écran bien équipé pour les films et les séries, proposé à 499 €.

articles.title: OpenRouter drops AI providers over leaked prompts and secrets
articles.text:
OpenRouter removed three AI providers from its platform after discovering that they had violated their stated data-handling policies and exposed sensitive data.
The company also revoked Zero Data Retention (ZDR) eligibility for 125 endpoints as a precaution and notified all potentially affected customers.
OpenRouter is an AI model broker that lets developers access AI models from different companies using a single API key.
When an app sends a request, OpenRouter forwards it to a provider that runs the selected model and passes the answer back.
Operational technology security company Dragos alerted OpenRouter after sending two million test prompts through the platform, each containing a unique tracking link or decoy credential, and detecting "activity indicating that data from at least three AI providers was exposed."
Dragos discovered that, in some cases, those credentials were leaked to outsiders and used in the wild, indicating that the test prompts had escaped.
“We observed activity indicating that data from at least three AI providers was exposed. Our seeded test prompts were used in attempts to access our controlled test systems and canary AWS accounts,” Dragos says.
OpenRouter says there was no breach on its own systems, making the leak point at the provider level and leading to the decision to remove the three leaking inference providers: Together AI, Phala, and Novita.
Another provider, Atlas Cloud, said it would voluntarily withdraw its models from OpenRouter pending security testing, following a third-party security incident.
The other three published separate announcements responding to Dragos’ findings and explaining how the leaks occurred.
Together AI said an AI coding agent exposed a repository credential on GitHub, allowing an unauthorized party to download stored prompt samples from June and July involving MiniMax M3, GLM-5.2, and Kimi K2.6.
Phala said an attacker compromised a server processing DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 requests routed through OpenRouter between October 21 and 22, and possibly up to November 8, and obtained application credentials from affected virtual machines.
Novita said a routing misconfiguration forwarded some MiniMax requests, including those sent through OpenRouter, to MiniMax’s official API between May 28 and November 11.
All four providers are tightening security controls, strengthening their zero data retention or data deletion policies, and advising potentially impacted users to rotate any secrets that may have been exposed in the leaked requests.
OpenRouter is also adapting Dragos’ tests for ongoing use to check whether AI providers forward or leak user requests/responses to third parties, and will require validation before restoring ZDR eligibility.

articles.title: AI is doing to programmers what mechanisation did to farmers, weavers: Vembu
articles.text:
AI is doing to programmers what mechanisation did to farmers, weavers: Vembu
Sridhar Vembu argues AI could transform intellectual work just as mechanisation transformed traditional trades, citing examples of AI tackling complex coding and engineering tasks with striking speed.
What mechanisation and automation did to farmers, weavers, carpenters and ironsmiths could now be happening to mathematicians and programmers, according to Zoho co-founder Sridhar Vembu.
He believes artificial intelligence (AI) is beginning to displace work traditionally associated with highly skilled intellectual professionals, just as earlier technological advances transformed occupations built around manual skills and craftsmanship.
In a post on X, Vembu backed an observation by AI researcher Subbarao Kambhampati that the intellectual class had largely been spared the loss of purpose experienced by workers displaced by previous technological revolutions. He illustrated the shift with two examples from his own experience.
Vembu said he asked AI to optimise code while travelling, a task he estimated would take a very capable programmer at least a month. “AI understood my high level intent very clearly and came up with a detailed plan and cleanly executed it and tested it against very detailed and exhaustive test cases it had constructed itself. The whole thing cost about $4 in tokens,” he wrote.
His second example is a colleague with no engineering background who used a personal AI account to create a mechanical CAD design for a motor housing. Vembu said the AI operated newly released, low-cost CAD software installed on the colleague’s computer, adding that he doubted the tool had been part of the model’s training. The point, in his telling, is that AI can help people attempt technical work previously beyond their reach.
Vembu quoted AI researcher Subbarao Kambhampati’s observation that “The intellectual class never quite experienced the loss of purpose in their lives that many other classes of humans experienced.”
Kambhampati argues that earlier mechanisation displaced weavers and craftspeople, but AI now threatens mathematicians, programmers and other knowledge workers. The anxiety, he suggests, reflects a newly affected class mistaking a loss of individual purpose for a crisis of humanity. Future generations may adapt to AI doing much of today’s intellectual work.
The tools are moving in that direction. Anthropic’s analysis of about 400,000 Claude Code sessions found that users typically made planning decisions while AI handled much of the execution. It also noted that people across occupations completed coding tasks at rates close to software engineers. Microsoft added its MAI Code 2 models to GitHub Copilot on November 17 for tasks such as making changes across several files and complex debugging.
Vembu sees both displacement and democratisation. AI may erode the market value of specialised skills while widening access to technical work.

articles.title: Quatre mois de Deezer Premium pour 4 € : l’offre Black Friday à connaître
articles.text:
Les amateurs de musique en streaming qui auraient envie de tester Deezer Premium peuvent profiter de l’offre Black Friday de la plateforme. Du 23 novembre au 2 décembre, l’abonnement est proposé à seulement 1 € par mois pendant 4 mois.
Les promotions du Black Friday déferlent sur le Web depuis plusieurs semaines, mais plus on s’approche de la fin du mois de novembre, et plus les bons plans deviennent intéressants. La preuve avec l’offre de la plateforme de streaming Deezer, qui propose 4 mois d’abonnement à sa formule Premium pour seulement 4 € au total.
L’offre est valable jusqu’au mercredi 2 décembre et s’adresse aux nouveaux clients du service.
Que propose l’offre Deezer Premium du Black Friday ?
La proposition de Deezer porte sur son abonnement individuel Premium, destiné à être utilisé par un seul utilisateur à la fois. Pendant quatre mois, le tarif de la formule est fixé à un euro par mois au lieu de 11,99 €. C’est ce montant qui vous sera facturé ensuite, si vous désirez rester abonné au bout des quatre mois à prix réduit.
Durant cette période, vous avez accès à l’ensemble des fonctions de Deezer Premium, dont les suivantes :
- Un accès illimité au catalogue musical, sans coupure publicitaire, avec la possibilité de passer les titres sans limite ;
- La possibilité de créer des playlists pour retrouver vos favoris et préparer vos prochaines soirées ;
- Le téléchargement des albums, des playlists et des podcasts dans l’application ;
- Un son Haute Fidélité pour des millions de morceaux compatibles ;
- L’affichage des paroles et l’identification des morceaux via SongCatcher, qui reconnaît aussi les airs que vous fredonnez.
Si vous voyagez régulièrement ou que vous prenez souvent les transports en commun, le mode hors connexion peut s’avérer très utile. Il permet d’écouter les contenus téléchargés sur votre smartphone, y compris lorsqu’aucun réseau mobile n’est disponible.
Une qualité audio sans perte plus ambitieuse que jamais
Deezer Premium donne accès à la qualité HiFi sans avoir besoin de payer un supplément. Et depuis octobre 2026, la plateforme propose également des fichiers FLAC sans perte allant jusqu’à 24 bits et 192 kHz, et ce pour des dizaines de millions de titres.
Si le rendu dépend de l’enregistrement en lui-même et du matériel d’écoute utilisé, il n’est cependant pas indispensable de posséder un équipement audiophile de pointe pour apprécier la proposition de Deezer Premium. L’absence de publicité, la possibilité d’écouter n’importe quel morceau de musique quand vous le désirez ou encore les suggestions d’écoute générées par Flow rendent l’expérience de plus en plus agréable au fil du temps.
L’application Deezer est également disponible sur un vaste choix d’appareils qui comprend les smartphones et tablettes Android et iOS, les ordinateurs, ainsi que de nombreux téléviseurs et autres appareils connectés compatibles.
Une promotion qui vous accompagne jusqu’à l’année prochaine
Un mois d’essai est souvent trop court pour réellement apprécier le travail de suggestion des algorithmes des plateformes de streaming musical. En quatre mois, vous devriez avoir le temps d’évaluer concrètement la proposition de Deezer Premium, afin de déterminer si la proposition peut vous convenir plus durablement. Il faut d’ailleurs noter que Deezer Premium est une offre sans engagement.
La promotion à 4 € pour quatre mois est valable jusqu’au 2 décembre à 9h59 en passant par le lien dédié. Vous serez alors invité à vous créer un compte Deezer afin d’en bénéficier de manière immédiate. Si vous ne désirez pas rester abonné au terme des quatre mois au tarif préférentiel, il vous suffit d’annuler le renouvellement de l’abonnement depuis votre espace client, au moins 48 heures avant sa date effective.

articles.title: GTA 6 : ne vous précipitez pas, vous pourriez le regretter
articles.text:
Il y a des jeux qui encouragent la contemplation, à tel point que l’on aimerait que certains moments soient suspendus dans le temps. Un coucher de soleil sur les plaines d’Hyrule dans The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild ou simplement une après-midi passée à pêcher dans Stardew Valley : ces instants, qui ne font parfois avancer aucune intrigue, constituent pourtant le cœur même de l’expérience.
Je ne m’attendais plus à trouver cette idée de contemplation et de routine du quotidien dans un épisode de GTA, même si la saga nous y avait pourtant déjà habitués. San Andreas se prêtait en effet bien à la flânerie, mais le cinquième épisode avait un peu perdu cette magie du quotidien. Je ne pensais donc pas que GTA 6 nous redonnerait autant le goût de cette vie ordinaire.
Contre toute attente, plus que n’importe quel autre épisode, GTA 6 nous pousse à savourer ces petits riens. Au point de créer un phénomène inattendu sur les réseaux sociaux : la « post-chapter 1 depression », ou « dépression post-chapitre 1 », chez les joueuses et les joueurs qui regrettent déjà cette tranquillité du début du jeu.
Sur X, un joueur prénommé Sani a particulièrement bien résumé ce sentiment dans un message publié le 22 novembre : « La dépression post-chapitre 1 me frappe tellement fort que je suis tenté de recommencer le jeu », explique-t-il. Ce qui lui manque ? Tout simplement sa petite routine : rentrer à la maison, faire de la musculation et nourrir Dolores, le serpent de Jason. Son message a rapidement suscité des réactions d’autres personnes qui partagent sa nostalgie. Certains racontent qu’ils aimeraient retrouver cette vie simple, tandis que d’autres regrettent déjà les moments passés dans la maison de Jason.
Une vie bien plus simple dans le chapitre 1 de GTA 6
Derrière cette idée, un peu dramatique, de dépression post chapitre 1 se cache surtout une grosse dose de nostalgie. Car le premier chapitre de GTA 6 propose une ambiance assez particulière, loin de l’agitation de Vice City. Dans les Keys, on finit en effet par s’attacher bien vite à nos routines, si tant est que l’on prend son temps pour découvrir le jeu.
Ce sentiment se retrouve aussi sur Reddit. Dans une discussion intitulée « Does anybody else have a routine in this game? » (Quelqu’un d’autre a une routine dans ce jeu ?), un joueur raconte avoir développé de véritables habitudes après l’arrivée de Lucia chez Jason. Chaque matin, il prenait son café avec elle, la regardait consulter son téléphone sur le canapé, avant d’aller prendre une douche. Le reste de la journée était consacré aux petits boulots, à la pêche ou à quelques sorties au bar. Il explique même ne pas avoir l’habitude de jouer de cette manière, mais vouloir savourer chaque instant après avoir attendu si longtemps GTA 6.
Un autre joueur, désormais au chapitre 3, explique aussi sur Reddit qu’il conserve des sauvegardes manuelles des deux premiers chapitres pour retrouver leur ambiance. Il regrette le début du jeu, où quelques centaines de dollars représentaient une somme importante, où réparer sa voiture faisait mal au portefeuille et où les journées semblaient beaucoup plus tranquilles. Un autre internaute explique même qu’il pourrait facilement recommencer le jeu pour passer une centaine d’heures dans les Keys.
Mieux vaut donc prendre son temps
Ce qui est intéressant dans ces témoignages, c’est que les joueuses et les joueurs ne regrettent pas nécessairement une mission ou un événement particulier, mais une atmosphère. Rockstar Games a pris le temps de donner une existence à Jason et Lucia, à leur quartier et à leurs habitudes.
C’est aussi ce qui rend le changement d’ambiance difficile pour certains. En passant plusieurs heures à profiter de cette petite vie dans les Keys, on finit presque par oublier que l’on joue à un épisode de Grand Theft Auto, et que l’essence de la série finit par nous rattraper
Alors, si vous êtes encore au début de GTA 6, un conseil : ne vous précipitez pas dans les missions principales. Prenez le temps d’explorer les Keys, de profiter de la maison et de ces petites activités qui paraissent parfois secondaires. Promenez-vous la nuit, prenez en photo la faune locale, allez pêcher, parlez à vos voisins, faites du vélo et discutez avec Lucia. Certains auraient visiblement aimé en profiter un peu plus longtemps s’ils avaient su.

articles.title: First Circle Capital’s $26 million pre-seed playbook
articles.text:
Fintech remains the biggest recipient of venture capital in Africa’s tech ecosystem, but it is not immune to the sector-wide funding slowdown. In the first half of 2026, African fintech startups raised $488 million across 45 deals, according to TechCabal Insights’ State of Tech in Africa report, a 23.7% drop from the $639 million raised in the same period in 2025.
First Circle Capital, a female-led venture capital firm focused on African fintechs, is positioning itself for the sector’s next phase with what it calls Fintech 2.0, which is a generation of businesses that build on the financial infrastructure established over the past decade, using technology to improve how financial institutions operate and serve customers.
“Ten years ago most fintechs in Africa were payments businesses, focused on building bridge-to-cash distribution networks, aggregating remittance flows or enabling online and in-store payments,” Selma Ribica, co-founder and managing partner at First Circle Capital, told TechCabal in an email on Friday. “The next wave of fintech winners will not simply be existing financial businesses with AI features added on top, but companies built from day one around automation, intelligent decision-making, software-led operations, and radically lower-cost distribution.”
Fifteen years ago, Ribica worked at M-Pesa, which helped bring mobile payments to the mass market and build crucial payment infrastructure on the continent. She co-founded First Circle Capital in 2021 with Agnes Aistleitner and Robert Smith. Now, the firm operates across Kampala, Nairobi, Casablanca, and Cape Town, with a pan-African investment mandate covering markets including Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, Egypt, Morocco, Uganda, Ghana, and Francophone Africa.
In 2025, First Circle Capital began building its Africa Fund I with a $6 million commitment from the International Finance Corporation (IFC). It announced the fund’s close at $26 million on Wednesday, with subsequent commitments from Bpifrance and Stellar Foundation. Ribica explained that First Circle Capital’s strategy focuses on six sub-segments within fintech, which include insurtech, alternative lending models, interoperability and infrastructure, climate fintech, fintech software-as-a-service (SaaS), and regulatory technology (RegTech). It is also looking for companies that build with artificial intelligence (AI) from the outset, rather than adding AI features to existing financial products.
In this conversation, Ribica explains how First Circle Capital’s Fintech 2.0 thesis differs from the payments era, why First Circle Capital is betting on AI-native businesses, what it looks for in founders, and the deals the firm walks away from. She also discusses the firm’s approach to follow-on investments and who it expects to buy its portfolio companies.
This interview has been edited for length and clarity.
You started with $6 million from IFC about a year ago and closed at $26 million. Your hard cap was $30 million. Why stop at $26 million?
First Circle Fund I team is here for carry, not management fees. I started investing my personal money in African fintechs in 2017 and had great returns from companies like Expensya, THNDR and more. The goal is to optimise performance, not AUM. At the time our most recent LPs committed, BPIFrance and Stellar Foundation, we already had built a well-performing portfolio, and $26 million is to execute our strategy for optimal returns.
You call this “FinTech 2.0.” How is a company you’ll back today different from the payments companies of the last ten years? Why did you select six core areas?
At the time we launched First Circle, the opportunities shifted to building solutions on top of those rails, leveraging technology to deepen financial inclusion for businesses and consumers, and helping African financial institutions leverage lower costs of operations and manage risk, bridging the gap across the industry with new technologies and accelerating digitisation.
First Circle I is a thesis-led fund focusing on six key sub-segments within fintech: Insurtech, Alternative Lending Models, Interoperability & Infrastructure, Climate Fintech, Fintech SaaS, and RegTech. While we believe these areas still represent substantial opportunities for economic and impact returns in Africa, it is important to note that in markets where financial innovation came later, like Morocco, we still back Fintech 1.0 opportunities, as those will be the most lucrative opportunities at the given stage of fintech innovation maturity.
In African markets, where legacy financial infrastructure is often incomplete or inefficient, AI-native fintech companies have the opportunity to leapfrog traditional models and build more scalable, accessible financial services from the ground up.
Describe the founder you’d write a cheque to.
We spend a lot of time understanding founders’ quality of motivation, as well as certain personal characteristics that we believe are highly correlated with success. Founders we back are ambitious yet humble, have a growth mindset and strong ability to self-reflect; they display a track record as top operators, networkers and thinkers who plan for the long-term.
What makes you walk away from a deal even when the numbers look good? Tell me about one deal you passed on and why.
The greatest number of deals we walked away from had one thing in common: founders who want to get rich quick. Building a successful company takes a decade or more, and we never back teams who prepare themselves for less.
You say you want companies that use AI from day one. What does that look like for a pre-seed fintech?
One example is Orca Fraud, a South African AI-native SaaS platform that we backed in 2023. We were the company’s first investors, supporting the founding team at the MVP stage as they developed an AI-powered solution for real-time transaction monitoring and fraud detection.
Apart from money, what do you do for a founder in their first year?
As mentioned previously, we began investing at the onset of the venture capital downturn, which made us particularly conscious of the importance of deploying our capital efficiently and maximising the value we could create for our portfolio companies beyond financial investment alone.
From the outset, we asked ourselves two fundamental questions: what truly moves the needle for fintech businesses at the pre-seed and seed stages, and which unique assets, capabilities and relationships could the First Circle Capital team leverage to make a transformational difference to our portfolio?
Today, we track progress we have made across three key areas: catalysing additional investment, unlocking commercial opportunities and strengthening the operational foundations of our portfolio companies.
We have helped our portfolio companies attract follow-on investment equivalent to 2.2 times the amount of capital we originally invested. On average, our involvement has helped catalyse 50% of each subsequent funding round, rising to 56% when First Circle Capital’s own participation is included.
To date, we have supported 13 portfolio companies in their fundraising efforts, introducing 23 unique investors and helping them secure the additional capital needed to scale their businesses.
Beyond fundraising, we have focused heavily on helping our portfolio companies establish commercial relationships with enterprise customers and high-growth businesses across Africa and internationally. We have facilitated 80 business development introductions, generating 33 active commercial conversations and nine contracts that are already producing revenue.
Collectively, these efforts have created a potential commercial pipeline worth $18.8 million, comprising $1.3 million in contracted revenue, $2.4 million in contracts undergoing final negotiations and a further $15.1 million in advanced discussions. These figures represent cumulative potential contract values over the 2026–2029 period.
Finally, we support our portfolio companies in recruiting senior executives and accessing experienced operators and advisers. Our network includes professionals with experience at organisations such as RedMart, Lazada, Alibaba and Expensya, alongside alumni communities from leading international business schools, including INSEAD, London Business School, Harvard Business School and Wharton.
How much do you put into a first cheque? With 18 companies already backed and about 24 planned, how much of the $26 million is left for new deals, and how much is set aside for follow-on rounds?
We aim for 10% at entry at the pre-seed and seed stages, so our ticket varies from $250,000 to $1.2m. We hold a 40% follow-on reserve.
Most of your money comes from development finance institutions. How do their goals affect which deals you do?
DFI mandates are aligned with our goals: returns and impact come simultaneously and not at the expense of one another. Therefore our investors do not dictate our investment strategy nor deals we chose to do. The decision to invest is based on the company’s ability to transform financial services for the better and generate top decile returns for our investors.
Who do you expect to buy your companies: banks, telcos or bigger fintechs?
We plan for exits from day 1, and work on improving exit chances for our portfolio continuously. We expect the bulk of exits will come from secondary and strategic acquisitions in the financial services industry, while there is also a possibility of a few IPOs.

articles.title: Lenovo se lleva el mejor portátil convertible del año con una apuesta que le ha salido muy bien: Nvidia Spark
articles.text:
Apostar por un chip de primera generación es arriesgado para un convertible. Bueno, es arriesgado para cualquier dispositivo, sobre todo si tienes otras opciones mucho más establecidas en el mercado. Pero también es cierto que el NVIDIA Spark ha suscitado la expectación de toda la industria al ser una plataforma todoterreno que apuesta por impulsar el rendimiento del equipo sea cual sea la tarea (productividad, IA, gaming, etc).
Los convertibles son una categoría que durante mucho tiempo han tenido que equilibrar movilidad frente a potencia. Intel y AMD ya cuentan con plataformas bastante sólidas en este segmento, pero eso no ha impedido a Lenovo a explorar otras alternativas entre toda su oferta de productos. Por ello, igual su Yoga 9n 2-en-1 de 11ª generación es el más interesante. Y es que está construido en torno a la plataforma RTX Spark de NVIDIA, que reúne una CPU con arquitectura Arm, una GPU Blackwell y memoria unificada en un solo chip.
Este equipo ha sido nuestro ganador en los Premios Xataka Verisure 2026 dentro de la categoría de “Mejor portátil convertible”, superando al ASUS ProArt GoPro Edition PX13 y a la Microsoft Surface Pro de 13 pulgadas de 12ª generación con chip Snapdragon. Y te contamos por qué.
La movilidad y flexibilidad como alma
El Yoga es un portátil creativo grande y flexible. Tiene una pantalla táctil OLED de 16 pulgadas, resolución 2.880 x 1.800 y una bisagra de 360 grados, y admite entrada con lápiz tanto en la pantalla como en el panel táctil. Spark es la carta más fuerte que tiene en la mano. El chip viene con hasta 20 núcleos de CPU, hasta 6.144 núcleos de GPU y hasta 64 GB de memoria unificada. El portento es tal que este modelo de Lenovo en cuestión se convierte por méritos propios en el escaparate perfecto para la plataforma de NVIDIA.
Spark tiene la capacidad de ofrecer a los equipos gran rendimiento para ejecutar modelos de IA en local, pero también el potencial de ser una gran plataforma para ejecutar videojuegos en formatos más reducidos, con una mejor gestión térmica. Este chip, junto a todas las virtudes del Yoga 9n 2-en-1 que Lenovo trae casa, hacen que se convierta (jeje) en una de las propuestas más completas del segmento y, para nuestro jurado, el mejor convertible de este año.
Protege tu hogar frente a robos y ocupaciones con las cerraduras inteligentes de Verisure, disponibles como parte del sistema de alarma Verisure. Al margen de permitir abrir la puerta usando las llaves o desde el móvil, alertan ante cualquier intento de manipulación y transmiten la información a la unidad central de la compañía para generar un salto de alarma. Descubre la solución que mejor se ajusta a las necesidades de tu vivienda o negocio.
Englobar potencia y flexibilidad no suele ser barato, y este equipo es el perfecto ejemplo de ello. Los precios superan los 3.000 euros, por lo que todavía se encuentra en un segmento nicho.

El ASUS ProArt GoPro Edition PX13 también es una gran máquina. Aunque es más chiquitito en dimensiones, con pantalla OLED de 13 pulgadas, monta un chip Ryzen AI Max+ 395 de AMD y hasta 128 GB de memoria. Eso sí, que su pantalla tenga una frecuencia de refresco de 60 Hz igual es un punto difícil de encajar en un portátil Windows que sale al mercado sobre los 3.000 euros. En líneas generales, es más portátil que el Yoga, pero menos cómodo para dibujar o presentar.
Lo interesante de esta edición del PX13 es que en el paquete también se incluye una funda protectora de GoPro, un lápiz compatible con carga inalámbrica, una suscripción a GoPro Premium+ de 12 meses y una bonita caja reutilizable con correas para proteger tus accesorios. Si no te interesa esta edición, siempre puedes optar por el modelo estándar del ProArt PX13.
Asus ProArt PX13 GoPro Edition
En cuanto a la Surface Pro de 13 pulgadas, está un peldaño por debajo en cuanto a especificaciones técnicas. Eso no significa que necesariamente tenga que ser peor para ti según el uso que quieras darle, pero sí nos encontramos ante un equipo con menos ambiciones en cuanto a potencia, es una tablet desmontable (y no un portátil con bisagra ampliada), y cuenta con cifras de autonomía algo mejores que sus rivales. Se sitúa en unos 1.300 euros, por lo que es bastante más asequible que el resto.

articles.title: Tech-packed cars are driving up repair bills and insurance costs, wasting $12 billion a year
articles.text:
Winners & losers: The more technology that gets packed into something, the more things can go wrong. That old adage is especially true with vehicles. According to a new investigation, the time US mechanics lose trying to access and use automakers' repair software is worth an estimated $12 billion a year. Drivers can feel it in their wallets, too, as higher repair bills can push up insurance premiums.
The report, titled Closing Shop, highlights the reality of repairs on today's heavily computerized vehicles. Its authors, from the US PIRG Education Fund, iFixit, and FULU, note that finding a failed sensor, releasing an electronic parking brake, or getting a car to recognize a replacement part can require plugging a laptop or tablet into the vehicle.
This modern problem illustrates the irony of the service light on a dash showing a hand tool. As the authors put it, "it should be a laptop." On some jobs, the mechanic has to pay the manufacturer for software access before the wrench work can start.
As for where that $12 billion figure comes from, the researchers estimate that about one in five repairs at independent shops requires manufacturer software. On those jobs, the median estimate from mechanics was 75 minutes spent buying access, downloading software, logging in, and waiting.
Across the US, that works out to 83 million hours a year, roughly the annual workload of 42,000 full-time technicians. The authors valued those hours at a typical shop rate of $140. The subscription fees themselves are a separate expense.
Buying the software doesn't always get you very far, either. One Ford Ranger Raptor owner cited in the report replaced a faulty anti-lock brake module, bought Ford's diagnostic software, and picked up a new adapter. Then the software asked for professional security credentials to reset the anti-theft system. With the replacement part already fitted, the owner said the truck would either refuse to start or cut out when shifted into drive.
There's also the question of how many subscriptions independent shops can justify. A Nissan dealer can spread the cost of one brand's software across the cars coming through its doors, but a neighborhood mechanic might see five different makes before lunch.
Of the mechanics surveyed, 88% had turned away at least one repair in the past year because they couldn't get or afford the software. For more than a million Americans who live over 100 miles from the nearest Nissan dealer, that could mean quite a tow.
That trip to the dealership can mean a bigger repair bill, too. A 2020 study cited in the report found that Massachusetts dealerships charged 36% more than independent shops for the same work. So if your usual mechanic has to turn you away because they can't access the software your car needs, you could end up paying more for exactly the same fix.
Even drivers whose cars never see the inside of a repair shop can feel it when their insurance comes up for renewal. When a car costs more to fix after a crash, the insurer faces a bigger claim, and those costs can feed into premiums for everyone. The report points to federal figures showing that US auto insurance prices rose 122% since 2012, compared with a 40% rise in consumer prices overall.
Carmakers have backed down over unpopular tech before. BMW dropped its heated-seat subscription after owners objected to paying extra to use hardware already in their cars, while Volkswagen pledged to bring back physical controls for essentials such as volume and heating. The report's authors want lawmakers to go further by making basic diagnostic software and service information free and capping what manufacturers can charge for their other repair tools.

articles.title: AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death
articles.text:
AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death
- Date:
  November 14, 2026
- Source:
  University of California - Berkeley
- Summary:
  Scientists have uncovered a hidden warning sign in routine heart scans that could predict sudden cardiac death before it strikes. The AI-powered discovery outperformed conventional screening methods, potentially revealing thousands of people at risk of a fatal heart malfunction that doctors might otherwise miss.
- Share:
More than 300,000 people in the United States die from sudden cardiac arrest each year. This deadly emergency occurs when the heart's electrical system suddenly fails, causing the heart to stop pumping blood. It can strike older adults with known heart conditions as well as seemingly healthy young athletes. Although implanted defibrillators can prevent some of these deaths, doctors have long struggled to determine which patients need them most.
Now, researchers at UC Berkeley have identified a previously overlooked warning signal in routine heart scans that could make it easier to recognize people at risk before a fatal event occurs.
The discovery was made using artificial intelligence trained on more than 440,000 electrocardiograms, or EKGs, collected in Sweden. By comparing the electrical patterns recorded in these scans with information from death certificates, the researchers taught an AI system to recognize subtle differences between healthy individuals, patients with known heart risks, and people who eventually died from sudden cardiac causes.
The team then evaluated the technology using thousands of additional patient records from the United States and Taiwan, testing whether the patterns could reliably identify people at heightened risk in different populations.
AI Detects Hidden Heart Risks That Standard Tests Miss
The results suggest that AI can identify vulnerable patients more effectively than the conventional tests doctors typically rely on. Current screening methods largely focus on how much blood the heart pumps with each contraction, a measurement used to assess whether someone might benefit from an implanted defibrillator.
Using these traditional measurements, doctors can identify a group of patients with an annual sudden cardiac death rate of 4.6%. The AI system, however, identified a group with an annual death rate of 7%, demonstrating a greater ability to distinguish patients facing serious danger.
Importantly, the algorithm also recognized a broader population of people at elevated risk, including thousands who would not normally raise concerns under existing medical guidelines. Most of these individuals would have been classified as relatively low risk using conventional methods.
Another major advantage is that the AI system works with ordinary EKG images, which are already routinely collected in hospitals and medical centers around the world. This means the technology could potentially improve screening without requiring an entirely new type of medical test.
The findings, published in Nature, could eventually help physicians make more informed decisions about who should receive an implanted defibrillator. They also raise an intriguing scientific question about what changes inside the heart produce the electrical patterns that AI has learned to recognize.
"Medical decisions are really hard, and I think that's why AI is so exciting for me," said Ziad Obermeyer, an associate professor at UC Berkeley's School of Public Health and the study's lead author. "We can not only make better decisions, but also start to understand what's actually going on with these patients before their heart stops."
Why Sudden Cardiac Death Is So Difficult to Predict
Sudden cardiac arrest is different from a heart attack. A heart attack happens when blood flow to part of the heart becomes blocked or severely restricted. Cardiac arrest, by contrast, results from a failure of the electrical signals that coordinate the heartbeat.
Immediate CPR and an electrical shock from an automated external defibrillator can sometimes restore the heart's rhythm. However, roughly 90% of people who experience sudden cardiac arrest outside a hospital die within minutes, making early recognition of those at risk especially important.
For Obermeyer, an emergency physician whose research combines artificial intelligence, medicine, and health policy, sudden cardiac death remains one of medicine's most frustrating unsolved problems.
Because victims often die without warning, researchers have limited opportunities to observe what happens inside the heart immediately before it stops. An autopsy may uncover blocked blood vessels, hardened tissue, or other structural abnormalities, but it cannot fully reveal how the heart was functioning in the moments leading up to death.
"One thing that makes the problem very tragic, but also very well suited for AI, is that we have the cure for this problem," Obermeyer said. "If you knew you were one of the people who was going to drop dead, you would go to a cardiologist and you'd get a defibrillator implanted. The problem is that doctors can't figure out who needs one before it's too late."
The Problem With Current Heart Risk Screening
Doctors currently rely heavily on a measurement of how effectively the heart pushes blood out with each beat. Patients whose hearts pump below a specified threshold may be considered candidates for an implantable cardioverter defibrillator, a device that can deliver an electrical shock when a dangerous heart rhythm develops.
But obtaining this measurement generally requires a more extensive medical evaluation. Many people who eventually experience sudden cardiac arrest never receive such testing because they have no obvious reason to suspect they are in danger.
The approach also has limitations for patients who are identified as high risk. About two-thirds of implanted defibrillators in these patients never need to deliver a shock. As a result, many individuals undergo expensive, invasive procedures for potentially fatal emergencies that may never occur.
At the same time, thousands of people who are not recognized as being at risk die unexpectedly each year.
"In some fraction of those people, we could have prevented those deaths if we had just known it in time," Obermeyer said. "There are a lot of lives being lost from people who are dropping dead of sudden cardiac death that are preventable if we just had better AI tools to find these things."
The researchers hope that identifying more accurate warning signs could help doctors direct preventive treatments toward the patients most likely to benefit.
How Researchers Trained AI to Recognize Deadly Heart Patterns
Developing the algorithm required three independent collections of medical data gathered from different parts of the world.
The researchers began with six years of EKG recordings from Sweden's unified healthcare system. By linking these scans to death certificates, they could examine the electrical patterns of patients who later experienced sudden cardiac death and compare them with those of other patients.
The AI learned to identify combinations of spikes, waves, and other characteristics in the recordings that appeared to be associated with increased risk. Once the system had been trained, the team tested it against two additional datasets: two years of anonymized EKG records from a San Diego hospital system and a separate collection of patient data from Taipei.
This international testing helped researchers evaluate whether the algorithm's predictive abilities extended beyond the Swedish population used to develop it.
"Good AI starts with good data," said Obermeyer, who is also part of the joint UCSF-UC Berkeley Computational Precision Health program. "Unfortunately, data like the ones we used for this study are incredibly hard to access. It's a big part of why there's so little clinical AI in use today."
Obtaining and organizing the information was itself a massive undertaking. According to Obermeyer, assembling the datasets took approximately 10 years and involved contributions from two organizations he helped establish, Dandelion Health and Nightingale Open Science. Both organizations work to advance medical research through better access to data and artificial intelligence.
"It's one of the tremendous luxuries of being at Berkeley," Obermeyer said. "You can pursue these projects that just are a slow burn and then have -- hopefully -- a big return when they get over the finish line."
From Hidden Heart Signals to Lifesaving Treatments
The researchers have already begun exploring how the system might be used in actual healthcare settings.
Obermeyer is collaborating with medical systems in Sweden, Taiwan, and the United States to introduce the algorithm into hospital EKG databases. The goal is to examine existing heart scans for signs of elevated risk and identify patients who may benefit from additional monitoring.
Under the proposed approach, physicians would contact patients whose EKGs receive a high-risk assessment and offer them the opportunity to wear a patch that continuously records their heart's electrical activity.
These longer recordings could provide valuable clues about the biological processes responsible for the warning signals detected by the AI. Understanding those processes could help researchers explain why certain hearts are more vulnerable to suddenly developing fatal electrical disturbances.
For some patients, the additional information might ultimately support a recommendation to receive an implanted defibrillator, potentially preventing a sudden and otherwise unexpected death.
Obermeyer has also created a website where people interested in learning about their own risk can provide basic personal information and an email address. The research team can then contact them about EKG analysis when the technology becomes more widely available.
Could AI Reveal New Secrets About the Human Heart?
Beyond its potential to improve the prevention of sudden cardiac death, the discovery highlights how artificial intelligence could help scientists investigate medical mysteries that have resisted conventional approaches.
Rather than simply identifying patients who might need treatment, the algorithm has uncovered patterns in heart activity that researchers do not yet fully understand. Studying those signals could lead to new insights into the electrical disturbances responsible for sudden cardiac death and potentially reveal additional opportunities for prevention.
Obermeyer believes this ability to uncover previously unrecognized biological patterns could become one of AI's most important contributions to medicine, opening new directions for research while helping physicians make better decisions.
"There is also going to be a new way of doing science that comes out of these tools," Obermeyer said, "and it's fun to think about how that starts happening."
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of California - Berkeley. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Ziad Obermeyer, Alexander Schubert, James Ross, Sendhil Mullainathan, Markus Lingman. An ECG biomarker for sudden cardiac death discovered with deep learning. Nature, 2026; 655 (8121): 210 DOI: 10.1038/s41586-026-10674-6

articles.title: Jensen Huang retorna ao comando da Nvidia
articles.text:
Jensen Huang retorna ao comando da Nvidia
Executivo assume os cargos de presidente e CEO.
Só durou 11 dias: a Nvidia reconduziu Jensen Huang ao cargo de presidente e CEO nesta segunda-feira (23/11). O conselho diretor aprovou a volta por unanimidade e disse ter ouvido altos escalões do governo dos Estados Unidos. Também disse estar confiante de que o retorno não representa risco à segurança nacional.
A investigação interna sobre alegações de que Huang foi alvo de uma ação de inteligência estrangeira continuará até o fim, e ele afirma que vai cooperar. A empresa também criou um comitê de segurança nacional e controle de exportações e vai contratar um diretor de compliance (Chief Compliance Officer).
Huang também volta a assumir uma cadeira no conselho diretor da Nvidia.
Na semana passada, a companhia chegou a descartar o retorno do executivo. Durante a sua ausência, a diretora financeira Colette Kress assumiu como CEO interina, enquanto a Nvidia passou a buscar uma nova liderança.
Jensen Huang nasceu em 17 de fevereiro de 1963, em Taiwan, e passou a infância na Tailândia antes de emigrar para os Estados Unidos. Formou-se em engenharia elétrica na Universidade Estadual do Oregon em 1984, tendo entrado no curso aos 16 anos, e concluiu o mestrado em Stanford em 1992. Antes disso, trabalhou como garçom e lavador de pratos na rede de restaurantes Denny’s, e depois projetou microprocessadores na AMD e chegou ao cargo de diretor na LSI Logic.
Em 1993, fundou a Nvidia com os engenheiros Chris Malachowsky e Curtis Priem, e assumiu a função de CEO desde o início. Sob sua gestão, a empresa deixou de ser uma fabricante de placas de vídeo e passou a fornecer os processadores gráficos usados para treinar modelos de inteligência artificial, o que a levou ao clube do trilhão. Com cerca de 4% das ações da companhia, Huang tem fortuna estimada em US$ 190 bilhões pela Forbes, cerca de R$ 1,1 trilhão, o que o coloca entre as dez pessoas mais ricas do mundo.

articles.title: Theseus Robotics secures €455k to put robots to work in supermarkets across Europe and US
articles.text:
Theseus Robotics, a Swiss startup developing AI-powered robots to automate shelf restocking and online grocery order picking, has secured €455k ($500k) from Y Combinator and will be launching in a grocery store in Silicon Valley.
The investment follows earlier backing from Founderful Campus, S2S Ventures, Earthling VC and Berlin-based Caesar Ventures, as the company prepares to introduce its robot, Theo, into its first grocery stores in the EU and US in November 2026.
“Robot hardware is turning into a commodity, so we build the brain,” said Samarth Malhotra, co-founder and CEO of Theseus Robotics.
Theseus’ software-led approach has parallels with other European robotics financings announced in 2026.
Paris-based Bleu Robotics secured €5 million to develop humanoid learning software, while Inbolt raised €11 million for robot vision and intelligence. In warehouse automation, Poland’s Nomagic raised €8.3 million and Germany’s Sereact secured €93 million. Closer to home, Swiss Physical AI companies Enact Intelligence and Exclaim Robotics secured €26.68 million and €4.29 million respectively, with mutual investor Founderful co-leading Exclaim’s round.
Together with Belgium’s Motion (€1.7 million) and Theseus’ €455k investment, these 2026 financings total approximately €150.4 million.
Founded in 2026, Theseus Robotics is the first spinoff from the ETH Robotics Club and focuses on automating one of the remaining manual processes in grocery retail: moving individual products from storage areas onto supermarket shelves.
The startup is targeting a sizeable operational challenge. According to figures provided by Theseus, Europe and the US together have more than 100k large grocery stores, with supermarkets spending over €54 billion ($60 billion) annually on manual shelf replenishment. While warehouses have adopted automation extensively, shelf replenishment and in-store order picking continue to rely heavily on human workers.
The startup’s robot, Theo, is designed to address both tasks, with a reported capacity to restock up to 400 units per hour and pick up to 40 units per hour for online orders. Its operating schedule allows it to switch between functions, picking customer orders until 9 p.m. before moving to overnight shelf replenishment until stores reopen at 9 a.m.
Rather than developing its own robotic hardware, Theseus Robotics purchases existing wheeled, two-armed robots and focuses on building the software and AI models that enable them to operate in retail environments.
Theo operates using a proprietary operating system and AI models trained by the company to recognise, grasp and place products across different shelf configurations. The technology is designed to handle thousands of product types, ranging from fragile yoghurt cups to heavier items such as cases of water.
Force sensors help Theo adjust its grip to avoid damaging delicate packaging, while its software can compare shelf conditions against planograms, the layouts retailers use to determine where individual products should be placed.
This functionality provides retailers with information about stock availability and shelf organisation, potentially helping them identify missing products and improve replenishment decisions. When Theo encounters a situation it cannot resolve autonomously, a human operator can intervene remotely.
The company reports that its technology has already been deployed in two stores, with pilots involving supermarket and pharmacy retailers in Europe and the US, alongside two major American online delivery platforms.
The recent Y Combinator investment is expected to support Theseus Robotics’ first US grocery store deployment in Silicon Valley. The startup is also preparing a broader programme of pilots across Switzerland, Germany and the US during the first quarter of 2027.

articles.title: Apple-Deals zum Black Friday: 6 Angebote, die sich wirklich lohnen
articles.text:
Apple-Deals zum Black Friday: 6 Angebote, die sich wirklich lohnen
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Ein iPhone Duo günstiger schießen? Das klappt nicht einmal am Black Friday. Das Gerät ist nach wie vor zu begehrt und vielfach vergriffen. Apple-Fans können aber trotzdem von mehreren Angeboten rund um iPads, Apple Watches und Airpods profitieren. Wir haben bei gängigen Angeboten die Preise gecheckt und zeigen, welche Deals sich wirklich lohnen.
Airpods Pro 3 unter 200 Euro
2025 hatte Apple die neuen In-Ears Airpods Pro 3 vorgestellt. Sie können nicht nur Musik abspielen und als Hörhilfe dienen, sondern über integrierte Sensoren und LEDs erstmals auch die Herzfrequenz messen. Praktisch für Sportler:innen. Darüber hinaus sollen sie eine längere Akkulaufzeit als die Vorgänger bieten. Bei Apple kosten die In-Ears 249 Euro. Amazon hat sie für 189 Euro im Angot. Das ist aktuell der beste Preis. In den vergangen Wochen gab es die In-Ears immer mal wieder günstiger. Idealo gibt aber etwa den Durchschnittspreis der vergangenen Monate mit rund 195 Euro an. Amazon liegt darunter.
Apple Watches zum Black Friday im Angebot
Apple Watch SE 3 für 220 Euro
Sparfüchse auf der Suche nach einer Smartwatch werden bei Amazon fündig. Dort gibt es die kleinere 40-Millimeter-Variante der Apple Watch SE 3 für 219 Euro. Im Vergleich mit den ähnlich aussehenden Apple Watches der Series-Reihe müsst ihr aber auf ein paar Dinge verzichten. So sind die Bildschirme etwas kleiner und nicht so hell wie bei der neuen Series 12. Außerdem fehlen ein paar Features, wie die Möglichkeit, ein EKG zu schreiben. Die Erfassung von sportlichen Leistungs- und Schlafdaten ist aber möglich. Nachrichten vom iPhone zeigen die Uhren ebenfalls an.
Apple Watch Series 12 bei Amazon und Otto
Auch die aktuelle Series 12 bieten Amazon, aber auch Otto, Saturn und Mediamarkt, zum Black Friday günstiger an. Bei der Uhr handelt es sich um das größere 46-Millimeter-Modell, jeweils mit Sportarmband. Das aktuelle watchOS 27 ist auf den Geräten schon vorinstalliert. Mit Ausnahme einiger weniger Apple-Watch-Ultra-Features sind die Uhren also mit allen neuen Funktionen kompatibel. Dazu gehören grundsätzlich auch KI-Features, die zunächst aber nicht in der EU verfügbar sind.
- Apple Watch Series 12 bei Amazon*
- Apple Watch Series 12 bei Mediamarkt*
- Apple Watch Series 12 bei Saturn*
- Apple Watch Series 12 bei Otto*
Kein Deal ist hingegen die Apple Watch Ultra 3. Amazon listet sie bei 689 Euro. Anderswo ist sie schon für 649 Euro erhältlich.
Mac Mini mit M6
Mit der Einführung des M6-Prozessors hat Apple den Preis des Mac Mini auf 1.049 Euro gehoben. Wer beim Einkauf sparen will, schaut deswegen auf Amazon. Hier kostet der kleine Desktop-Rechner derzeit nur 835 Euro. Ihr spart also über 200 Euro. Dabei handelt es sich derzeit um den besten Preis im Internet.
iPad Air mit viel Speicher
Zum Black Friday haben Amazon und Notebooksbilliger.de das aktuelle iPad Air mit M4 im Angebot. Allerdings nur mit viel Speicher. Das heißt: Richtig günstig wirkt der Preis von 1.419,99 Euro nicht. Für dieses Modell ist es aktuell aber tatsächlich der beste Preis. Die Leistung des M4 reicht dabei für alle gängigen Aufgaben und Gaming. Durch den großen Speicher und den Multitasking-Funktionen, die Apple mit iOS 26 eingeführt hat, kann das Tablet unter Umständen sogar einen Mac ersetzen.
- Apple iPad mit M4 und 1 Terabyte Speicher bei Amazon*
- Apple iPad mit M4 und 1 Terabyte Speicher bei Notebooksbilliger.de*
Amazon hat zudem die ältere M3-Variante reduziert. Allerdings haben kleinere Händler laut etablierten Preisportalen mittlerweile nachgezogen und Amazon zum Teil sogar unterboten, sodass ihr das Angebot getrost ignonieren könnt. Dasselbe gilt auch fürs iPad Mini mit A17-Pro-Prozessor, das ihr anderswo günstiger erhaltet.
Apple Pencil mit USB-C: Zubehör für iPads und das iPhone Duo
Es muss ja gar nicht immer der teure Apple Pencil Pro sein. Wer einfach nur Notizen festhalten will, kann das auch mit dem Apple Pencil mit USB-C-Anschluss machen. Wie der Name schon sagt, wird der Stift nicht via Induktion am iPad sondern über die USB-C-Buchse geladen. Er ist auch mit dem iPhone Duo kompatibel, das über kein Induktionsfeld für den Stift verfügt. Normalerweise kostet er 89 Euro, ist bei Amazon aber auf 69 reduziert.

articles.title: Militantes de un partido opositor de India irrumpieron en oficinas de Meta por cuentas de Instagram restringidas
articles.text:
Militantes de la rama juvenil del Partido del Congreso, principal fuerza de oposición de India, protestaron el 20 de noviembre frente a oficinas de Meta en Hyderabad, Bombay y Gurugram, y en algunos casos ingresaron a los edificios. Reclaman que Instagram levante las restricciones impuestas a cuentas de sus dirigentes y de críticos del Gobierno.
Según informó The Indian Express, el 19 de noviembre la red social restringió las cuentas del presidente nacional de la organización, Uday Bhanu Chib, y de Manish Sharma, responsable de su área nacional. El grupo sostiene que la medida respondió a órdenes del partido gobernante, el BJP, del primer ministro Narendra Modi.
The Times of India precisó que el grupo no presentó pruebas de que el BJP ordenara la medida. La organización afirma que ambas cuentas fueron restituidas unos 15 minutos después de las protestas. El mismo medio advierte que esa secuencia no demuestra que las visitas causaran la restitución.
Qué pasó en cada ciudad
En Hyderabad, unos 25 militantes entraron a un edificio con acceso controlado, según la policía citada por The Times of India, y rompieron macetas en un pasillo. Entre 20 y 22 personas quedaron detenidas de forma preventiva y fueron liberadas unas tres horas después.
La versión sobre el ingreso difiere. La policía dijo a The Indian Express que los manifestantes no llegaron al edificio principal de Meta y que la compañía no presentó denuncia. El presidente del grupo en Telangana, Jakkidi Shiva Charan Reddy, afirmó que fueron a entregar una petición y que no los dejaron pasar.
En Bombay, manifestantes pintaron consignas en las paredes del edificio donde funciona la oficina de Meta, según Gadgets Now, sitio de tecnología en The Times of India. En Gurugram levantaron carteles, y las fotos de la agencia Reuters los muestran frente al edificio, con un detenido por la policía.
Ultimátum de siete días y respuesta política
Un día después, el 21 de noviembre, el grupo dio a Meta siete días para responder cuatro reclamos. Pide saber cuántas cuentas indias se bloquearon por orden del Gobierno en los últimos seis meses y cuántas siguen bloqueadas, y que se retiren las restricciones a opositores, periodistas y creadores. También exige explicaciones sobre el bloqueo automático de publicaciones que mencionan a Rahul Gandhi o critican a Modi.
Manu Jain, a cargo de las redes de la organización, dijo a Reuters que “miles de cuentas de periodistas, creadores e influencers críticos con el Gobierno siguen restringidas”, según The Verge. El grupo amenazó con llevar el caso a los tribunales, a las calles y de nuevo a las oficinas de la empresa.
El BJP condenó los hechos. Según Moneycontrol, el vocero Pradeep Bhandari calificó al Congreso de “partido de matones” y lo acusó de promover el vandalismo contra empresas privadas. El jefe del Partido Samajwadi, Akhilesh Yadav, también criticó a Meta, a la que dijo que debía “hacer negocios, no política”.
El conflicto ocurre después de que India endureciera en febrero las reglas de eliminación de contenido considerado ilegal: las plataformas pasaron de tener 36 horas a tres para actuar tras recibir una notificación oficial, según The Verge.
Meta no respondió de inmediato a la consulta de The Verge ni emitió una declaración detallada sobre las protestas, según Gadgets Now. La empresa ha dicho antes que restringe contenido en India para cumplir las leyes locales. El plazo de siete días del ultimátum vence en torno al 28 de noviembre.

articles.title: phpAfterShell Vulnerability Revives PHP2Shell’s Attack Path
articles.text:
PHP last week patched a critical-severity vulnerability residing in the same dangerous state as the PHP2Shell flaws, cybersecurity firm Depthfirst says.
Dubbed phpAfterShell, the security flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-126714 (CVSS score of 9.2), and was resolved on November 19 alongside six other critical issues.
According to Depthfirst, the bug could allow an attacker who can control data written to a session file and interrupt the session write operation to trigger an object deserialization and achieve remote code execution (RCE).
It exists because PHP overwrites the session file from the start without emptying it first. If the operation is interrupted mid-write, or before the subsequent truncation operation removes old trailing data, the file is left with mixed content: fresh session data followed by remnants of the old session.
“We discovered reliable methods to interrupt the file operation during session upload-progress updates, allowing us to splice the prefix of one valid session with the suffix of another. A subsequent session operation treats the corrupted data as legitimate server-side state, giving attackers control over session values and the ability to trigger object deserialization,” Depthfirst notes in its technical write-up.
An attacker could arrange the new and old data so that the combined file would be interpreted differently from the original sessions, and parts of ordinary strings would become serialized object data. A future session would create the objects and invoke their deserialization.
“Session upload progress provides one way for a remote client to influence stored session data through multipart uploads. The same underlying problem can arise when an application stores large user-controlled strings in a session. In threaded PHP builds, a hard memory-limit failure in another thread can terminate the process while the session write is in progress,” PHP notes in its advisory.
phpAfterShell, Depthfirst explains, is related to PHP2Shell, which occurred because, during the parsing of an unauthenticated multipart request, PHP’s upload-progress callback could open and decode a file-backed session before the target script would begin.
Because objects would become active during the callback, PHP added restrictions to which objects could be created in memory, but did not modify the underlying file update behavior.
“Even with the new restrictions in place, the callback still reads the existing Session, adds upload-progress state, serializes the whole thing, and writes it back to the same file,” Depthfirst explains.
Successful exploitation of phpAfterShell requires certain conditions to be met: default session storage to be active, an exploitation route (the easiest is upload progress tracking), the PHP process to stop mid-write, a request to call session_start() on the corrupted file, and a deserialization-to-code-execution path.
Patches for the vulnerability were included in PHP versions 8.6.0, 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, and 8.2.36. There appear to be no reports of phpAfterShell’s in-the-wild exploitation.

articles.title: Dutch privacy authority urges consumers not to buy 'pervert glasses'
articles.text:
The Dutch Data Protection Authority is urging consumers not to buy AI-enabled camera glasses, warning that they compromise the privacy of nearby bystanders and risk the safety of their users.
The authority, whose recent statement falls just short of an outright ban, said that use of the internet-enabled and always-on glasses to record people in public is “almost always prohibited.”
Critics have dubbed these smart wearables as “pervert glasses” for their propensity to be used to video people without their permission, particularly to harass women. While some glasses have warning lights when users are recording, privacy advocates have argued that these alerts are not clear enough. Some people have even made phone apps capable of detecting nearby smart glasses wearers.
The Dutch data protection authority warned that the glasses also produce wrong results and unsafe results. In one test carried out by the Dutch authority, a pair of unnamed glasses “gave dating advice to an adult who indicated that they are interested in a minor.” The glasses also incorrectly read a medicine label and claimed to have called an ambulance when it had not.
The Dutch government’s advice follows a similar move by the Norwegian government, which in September said it was considering a ban on camera-enabled devices.

articles.title: Ataque hacker à Binance: governo dos EUA busca recuperar fortuna bilionária
articles.text:
O Departamento de Justiça dos Estados Unidos entrou com ação civil para recuperar mais de US$ 1 bilhão (aproximadamente R$ 5,4 bilhões) em criptomoedas roubadas por hackers norte-coreanos durante ataque à Binance, maior plataforma de negociação de ativos digitais do mundo. A iniciativa foi anunciada nesta segunda-feira (23).
O ataque aconteceu em 30 de outubro e movimentou aproximadamente US$ 6,3 bilhões (cerca de R$ 34 bilhões), segundo o material analisado por especialistas em rastreamento de criptomoedas. A maior parte dos recursos foi desviada em intervalo de apenas 20 minutos.
A ação judicial busca recuperar parte dos ativos envolvidos no roubo. O Departamento de Justiça não detalhou, no comunicado, quais criptomoedas estão incluídas no processo nem como os valores foram localizados.
Como aconteceu o ataque à Binance?
- Segundo análises das empresas TRM Labs e Chainalysis, especializadas em rastrear transações de criptomoedas, os responsáveis pelo ataque seriam hackers ligados à Coreia do Norte;
- Os criminosos conseguiram comprometer o sistema responsável por autorizar transferências de ativos digitais. Com isso, foram capazes de movimentar grandes quantidades de criptomoedas sem a autorização legítima da plataforma;
- A operação aconteceu de maneira extremamente rápida. Registros das transações analisados por especialistas indicam que a maior parte dos recursos foi movimentada em aproximadamente 20 minutos, por volta das 17h (horário de Brasília);
- Depois do desvio, os invasores começaram a transferir os valores entre diferentes endereços digitais para dificultar o rastreamento e impedir que as autoridades bloqueassem os recursos;
- Uma das hipóteses sobre o início da operação envolve uma entrevista de emprego. O ataque pode ter começado com abordagem relacionada a uma oportunidade profissional, utilizada pelos criminosos para comprometer sistemas da empresa.
Leia mais:
- Clientes da Binance sacam bilhões em criptomoedas após ataque hacker
- Binance: Coreia do Norte rebate EUA após FBI atribuir roubo ao país
- Falsa entrevista e IA: Binance detalha invasão de US$ 6,3 bilhões
Binance cobriu prejuízos dos clientes
Após identificar o incidente, a Binance suspendeu temporariamente saques e depósitos para conter os efeitos do ataque.
A empresa também garantiu que os recursos dos clientes estavam protegidos e se comprometeu a cobrir integralmente as perdas. Em 13 de novembro, a plataforma informou que já havia compensado os prejuízos relacionados ao episódio.
A corretora também passou a colaborar com autoridades policiais de diferentes países, incluindo o FBI, agência federal de investigação dos Estados Unidos, e o Serviço Secreto estadunidense.
O trabalho conjunto busca rastrear as movimentações dos criminosos e identificar possíveis caminhos para recuperar os ativos desviados.
Hackers norte-coreanos são suspeitos de roubos bilionários
A participação de grupos ligados à Coreia do Norte em ataques contra empresas de criptomoedas é uma preocupação recorrente para autoridades internacionais.
Essas operações são associadas a estratégias de obtenção de recursos financeiros para o país, que enfrenta sanções econômicas internacionais.
No caso da Binance, a identificação dos responsáveis foi atribuída por empresas especializadas à análise das movimentações registradas na blockchain.
A ação apresentada pelo Departamento de Justiça representa nova etapa dos esforços estadunidenses para recuperar o dinheiro. Mesmo com a compensação dos clientes pela Binance, a tentativa de reaver os ativos pode ajudar a interromper a circulação dos recursos obtidos ilegalmente e dificultar o financiamento de novas operações criminosas.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Why Canada invested in Cohere
articles.text:
Today we have another edition of what is becoming a quarterly accountability check-in with Canada’s AI Minister, Evan Solomon.
“Simply put, Canada is not gonna wait for others to build the AI—maybe people we don’t know or don’t trust. We’re gonna build it now.”
The last time the minister was on the podcast, it was shortly following the release of Canada’s AI strategy. This time, we’re checking in right after Budget 2026, and we talk through some of the budget components the minister is most passionate about in their support of entrepreneurs. We also cover how some of those steps are designed to help prevent more AI companies like Taalas and Tenstorrent from being acquired or fleeing south—for his part, Minister Solomon said it’s his job to give those companies reasons not to leave.
But we also talk about the big news that dropped right before the budget: the federal government’s investment in AI champion Cohere. If you’ve seen the minister on The BetaKit Podcast before, or are familiar with BetaKit’s coverage generally, this news should not surprise you.
But public investments in private companies are relatively novel in Canada, and now that every Canadian has skin in the game, they’re coming armed with a lot of questions. As Build Canada’s Lucy Hargreaves put it, “Ottawa is becoming the owner, the funder, the customer and the regulator of the same companies.” How is that going to work?
