articles.title: ‘La Bola Negra’ destrona a ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ como la película más taquillera de 2026 en España: sus cifras son históricas
articles.text:
La taquilla de España tiene un nuevo rey en este 2026. Y es que, después del último fin de semana (20-22 de noviembre), La Bola Negra ha destronado a Spider-Man: Brand New Day y se ha convertido en la película más taquillera del año en nuestro país. Un hito que parecía imposible para la película de los Javis pero que, a pesar de llevar ya dos meses en cartelera, no deja de sumar alegrías.
Con su recaudación más reciente, La Bola Negra acumula ya 40,5 millones de euros en la taquilla de España. Son unas cifras con las que ha superado los números de Spider-Man: Brand New Day y de La Odisea, los dos mayores blockbusters del año a nivel mundial. De hecho, la película del arácnido es la tercera más taquillera de todos los tiempos, por lo que el triunfo de los Javis tiene todavía más mérito.
Además, los datos domésticos de La Bola Negra son especialmente increíbles porque se encuentra a apenas dos millones de euros más de superar a Lo imposible (42,4 millones). Si lo consigue, se encumbraría como la segunda película más taquillera de la historia de España, solo por detrás de los 56 millones de euros de Ocho apellidos vascos. Ya no cabe duda de que el filme ha hecho historia para siempre.
Por otro lado, a nivel internacional La Bola Negra acumula otros 50 millones de dólares más. unos datos muy sólidos teniendo en cuenta que su distribuidora en Estados Unidos es Netflix, por lo que allí los espectadores están esperando a verla en streaming. Con una recepción tan positiva y con la temporada de premios a la vuelta de la esquina, solo queda soñar con todo.
Los Juegos del Hambre dominan la taquilla mundial
Al margen de La Bola Negra, la película que ha dominado claramente la taquilla de los cines estos últimos días es Los Juegos del Hambre: Amanecer en la cosecha. La cinta ha conseguido 3,7 millones de euros en nuestro país, lo que supone más de la mitad de la recaudación de este fin de semana. Y a nivel mundial sus números son todavía más impresionantes.
Los Juegos del Hambre: Amanecer en la cosecha ha alcanzado, en total, los 225 millones de dólares en solo tres días. En Estados Unidos ha tenido un mejor estreno que Sinsajo - Parte 2 y, por supuesto, que Balada de pájaros cantores y serpientes, el lanzamiento más flojo de la franquicia a nivel de taquilla. En las próximas semanas se demostrará si esta nueva entrega tiene piernas para aguantar sus buenas cifras.

articles.title: Building AI in Africa is expensive. Selling it is harder
articles.text:
This is Follow the Money, our weekly series that unpacks the earnings, business, and scaling strategies of African fintechs, financial institutions, companies, and governments. A new edition drops every Monday.
Nigeria and South Africa are more optimistic about artificial intelligence than the global average of 53%, according to a 2025 Google and Ipsos report. But turning that enthusiasm into a viable business is expensive.
Every diagnostic assistant, predictive model, or automated business tool comes with an infrastructure bill. Companies need computing power to train and run models, data to make those models useful in local markets, and specialised engineers to develop and maintain the technology.
Much of the infrastructure is priced in dollars, while these businesses largely operate in markets with significantly lower purchasing power.
A new report by German development agency Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) and research firm Briter Bridges, which mapped 311 AI businesses across Africa and surveyed 85 of them, found that 65% of surveyed businesses identified cloud computing, graphics processing units (GPUs), and AI infrastructure as their largest research and development spending category.
Another 61.1% identified high cloud costs as their biggest infrastructure bottleneck.
African AI companies must pay global prices to develop products for markets where customers are often unwilling or unable to pay global prices.
Between 2016 and 2025, African AI businesses raised $1.3 billion. However, the median funding ticket was just $225,000. This means that although the ecosystem has attracted investment, the typical company is operating with relatively limited capital to fund an expensive technology business.
In March 2026, OpenAI closed a funding round with $122 billion in committed capital at a post-money valuation of $852 billion.
For African founders, the challenge is building technology that can compete in an increasingly AI-driven world without the financial resources available to their global counterparts.
The AI Cost Trap
How much does it actually cost to serve your AI customers?
Model A: API Renting
Model B: In-House AI
The economics of building AI
The International Monetary Fund estimates that AI could increase sub-Saharan Africa’s economic output by as much as 4% over the next decade.
But capturing that opportunity requires more than developing a useful product. AI businesses have different cost structures depending on how they develop their products.
Some build their own models, others use open-source models or third-party application programming interfaces (APIs), while some combine these approaches. Each option comes with different financial implications.
Building an in-house model gives a company greater control over its technology but requires investment in computing infrastructure, data, and specialised engineers. Using an existing model through an API reduces the initial development burden, but introduces recurring charges whenever the business uses the service.
Open-source models can reduce licensing and API expenses, but companies still need computing resources, technical expertise, and data to adapt them to their markets. Open-source does not mean cost-free.
AI Infrastructure Cost Simulator
Should your startup pay for APIs, host open-source, or build proprietary models?
A. Third-Party API
B. Hosted Open-Source
C. Proprietary Build
Consider a hypothetical Nigerian AI startup that develops a customer service assistant for small businesses. It has 500 business customers, each paying $40 monthly for access to the product. That gives the company monthly recurring revenue of $20,000.
Now assume each customer generates 4,000 AI requests monthly. Across its customer base, the startup processes two million requests every month.
If the company relies on a third-party AI provider and pays an illustrative average of 1.5 cents per request, its monthly API bill reaches $30,000. This is already $10,000 more than its entire subscription revenue, before accounting for salaries, marketing, internet connectivity, and other operating expenses.
The company is effectively losing money every time it serves its customers at that price. AI businesses accumulate between $20,000 and $50,000 in monthly API expenses, according to the report.
The AI startup could switch to an open-source model and host it on its own infrastructure. This would change the economics. Instead of paying an API provider for every request, the company would bear the cost of running its own computing infrastructure and maintaining the model.
For illustration, assume hosting and computing cost $12,000 monthly, while specialised engineering salaries cost another $12,000. Add $8,000 in other operating expenses, and the company’s total monthly expenditure becomes $32,000.
It would still lose $12,000 monthly, but its cost structure would be different. More importantly, its computing costs would not necessarily increase at the same rate as customer usage.
At 1,500 customers paying the same $40 monthly subscription, revenue would rise to $60,000. Under the same assumptions, its API expenses could reach $90,000 if usage tripled. By contrast, its in-house infrastructure would need to expand, but its costs might rise to approximately $42,000 monthly, including additional computing capacity and operating expenses.
The company could now generate an operating surplus of $18,000. This calculation shows how difficult it can be for African AI businesses to make their products generate enough revenue to cover the cost of serving customers.
Roughly one in five surveyed African AI businesses are pre-revenue, and about 40% are not yet profitable. Only 15% have reached profitability. The report also found that 60% of profitable companies operate beyond Africa, compared with 40% that operate exclusively on the continent. This suggests that access to international markets, where customers may have greater purchasing power, could improve the economics of building AI businesses.
But finding customers willing and able to pay remains a challenge. About 56% of surveyed businesses charge less than $2,500 annually per customer, equivalent to roughly $208 a month. Meanwhile, 88% target businesses, 62% serve retail consumers, 44% target government, and 43% operate business-to-business-to-consumer models.
Pricing
Subscription pricing is the dominant monetisation model. But businesses serving price-sensitive markets also rely on freemium, grant-supported, and subsidised pricing to encourage adoption. This creates a difficult relationship between what customers can afford and what it costs to serve them.
Can Your Customers Afford AI?
The gap between what African businesses can pay and what AI companies need to charge.
1. The Customer’s Wallet (SME)
2. The AI Startup’s Costs
The problem is particularly pronounced among smaller enterprises, whose average annual turnover is often below $10,000. These businesses must already pay for internet connectivity, fuel for backup generators, and staff salaries before accounting for the infrastructure required to run AI.
For many AI startups trying to solve some of the continent’s deepest problems, the dilemma is how to make the economics work. The customers who stand to benefit most from these solutions are often the least able to pay for them, while the cost of developing, running, and maintaining the technology remains high.
Raising enough capital to sustain these businesses is another challenge. About 30% of surveyed companies are bootstrapped, while a quarter have raised less than $500,000. Just under a quarter have raised between $1 million and $10 million. Only one company has raised between $10 million and $50 million, while fewer than 10% fall within the $500,000 and $1 million funding bracket.
How Long Can Your AI Startup Survive?
Calculate how much runway remains after paying for computing, talent, and operations.
Building an AI product requires computing power, data, and specialised talent. Investment in one area often creates additional costs in another. African AI startups are therefore building with globally priced infrastructure while trying to sell to customers with locally constrained purchasing power.
Whether they build their own models or rent existing ones, they must find a way to cover these costs and remain profitable. But it is still relatively early for many of these businesses. The report puts the median age of surveyed companies at between five and nine years, suggesting that many are still working to find a sustainable business model. Their ability to do so will depend on whether they can grow revenue fast enough to cover the cost of building, running, and maintaining their products.

articles.title: En 2016, Marruecos construyó esta extraña torre que hoy abastece de energía a más de un millón de personas
articles.text:
A las puertas del Sáhara y a unos 200 kilómetros de Marrakech se encuentra la ciudad de Ouarzazate, cuya aridez y peculiar orografía le han llevado a ser el escenario de algunas grandes producciones audiovisuales como Gladiator o Juego de Tronos. Pero, Hollywood aparte, si hay algo sorprendente de este enclave es una gigantesca construcción artificial, que se extiende por 500 hectáreas y que baña la vista aérea de un reflejo metálico muy curioso.
Se trata del complejo Noor, una macroplanta de energía que se construyó hace ya diez años en una de las regiones con mayor recurso solar de Marruecos y que hoy en día abastece a más de un millón de personas del país. Pero no es solo un parque solar a gran escala: lo que Noor esconde es mucho más.
La mayor central de energía solar de concentración del mundo. Con cuatro instalaciones diferentes y más de 500 hectáreas de extensión, el complejo solar Noor Ouarzazate se inauguró en febrero de 2016 y hoy cuenta con 580 MW en total de potencia instalada. Ha costado más de 3.000 millones de euros que se han financiado internacionalmente y forma parte del Programa Marroquí de Energía Solar, cuyo objetivo es impulsar la transición energética del país.
Espejos que reflejan la luz. Este macrocomplejo de energía concentrada está formado por cuatro instalaciones que entraron en funcionamiento entre 2016 y 2018. Se trata de Noor I, con una potencia de 160 MW, que empezó a funcionar desde el comienzo y que emplea colectores cilindroparabólicos; Noor II, con 200 MW; Noor III, con 150 MW mediante tecnología de torre y Noor IV, con 70 MW.
La más espectacular, por su apariencia, quizá sea Noor III. Esta planta de energía solar de concentración utiliza 7.400 heliostatos para funcionar: son unos espejos motorizados que siguen la trayectoria del sol a 12 metros de altura para reflejar la luz y concentrar la radiación solar en un receptor en lo alto de una torre de 250 metros, situada en el centro de la instalación. Este calor calienta un fluido térmico que permite generar vapor y accionar las turbinas de la instalación.
Energía gracias a la sal fundida. Otra de las curiosidades que se encuentra tras esta instalación es que tanto Noor II como Noor III cuentan con capacidad de almacenamiento gracias a sales fundidas a 600 ºC, como explican desde DW. El calor almacenado en las sales se utiliza para calentar agua y producir vapor, que mueve las turbinas encargadas de generar electricidad con una duración de unas siete horas cada una.
Esto significa que la producción de electricidad en este complejo no se detiene cuando el sol se pone, sino que sigue funcionando más allá de las horas de luz.
Sin embargo, los combustibles fósiles siguen dominando. A pesar de que Marruecos sigue contando con buenos recursos tanto solares como eólicos y que es uno de los que lleva la avanzadilla en la transición energética en su continente, el país sigue dependiendo en gran medida de los combustibles fósiles, y, como apunta DW, del carbón especialmente. Esto hace que, a pesar del potencial de este proyecto, la mayoría de las familias sigan pagando una electricidad cara: de los 550 dólares que son el ingreso promedio de un hogar, 110 van dirigidos a pagar la factura de la electricidad.
Intissar Fakir, investigador principal y director fundador del programa para el Norte de África y el Sahel en el Instituto de Oriente Medio en Washington, señala a DW que el problema está en que Marruecos sigue importando casi toda su energía. Además, aunque cuenta con la tecnología suficiente para generar el 46% de su electricidad de forma renovable, las cifras reales siguen siendo mucho más bajas, ya que la capacidad real para integrar la energía de plantas como Noor sigue siendo muy limitada, según el mismo experto.

articles.title: E-Beam Stitching Errors Increase Loss In SOI Waveguides (AMO GmbH, RWTH Aachen)
articles.text:
Researchers at AMO GmbH and RWTH Aachen University published “The Impact of Field Stitching on Optical Losses in SOI Waveguides Fabricated via Electron Beam Lithography.”
Abstract
“Electron-beam lithography (EBL) is widely used for prototyping photonic integrated circuits (PICs) because of its direct-write capability and sub-50 nm resolution. However, due to limited beam deflection capability, large-circuit designs require multiple write fields that are stitched together. The resulting stitching errors at the write-field boundaries can substantially impact optical waveguide losses. The researchers investigated controlled lateral stitching offsets in straight waveguides and complemented the experimental measurements with finite-difference time-domain simulations based on geometries reconstructed from SEM images. The simulations reproduce the approximately quadratic relationship between stitching-induced loss and offset magnitude, with predicted losses in the same order of magnitude as the experimental results. Stitching offsets as small as 2.5 nm measurably contribute to propagation loss, highlighting stitching accuracy as an important consideration for large-scale photonic integrated circuits.”
Find the technical paper here. November 2026.
Maksim Lipkin, Jashanpreet Kaur, Grigory Vydrevich, Michael Möller, Lisa Ehlert, Jens Bolten, Rijil Thomas, Stephan Suckow, and Max C. Lemme. “The Impact of Field Stitching on Optical Losses in SOI Waveguides Fabricated via Electron Beam Lithography.” *IEEE Transactions on Semiconductor Manufacturing*, 2026. articles.title: The Sovereign AI Paradox: Who Controls the Compute?
articles.text:
On Nov. 20, President Trump threatened penalties on American companies building data centers overseas. The announcement came one day after new U.S. export controls took effect, restricting certain shipments of advanced computing equipment to data centers that provide remote processing capacity to entities in restricted jurisdictions.
The measures address different issues, but together they create a difficult question for the semiconductor industry. If Washington wants the world to depend on American AI technology while placing tighter conditions on where and how that technology can be deployed, how will foreign customers respond?
Saudi Arabia is already providing one answer.
The architecture behind sovereign AI
In August, AMD, Cisco, and Saudi Arabia’s HUMAIN announced that AI infrastructure built around AMD Instinct MI355X accelerators and Cisco Silicon One networking was operational. For a sovereign computing operator, the choice of suppliers carries implications well beyond processor performance.
Nvidia’s CUDA ecosystem has a substantial advantage in software maturity, optimized libraries, and developer adoption. AMD’s ROCm provides an alternative, although migrating workloads between the two involves testing framework compatibility, adapting specialized kernels, and retuning performance. Those engineering costs matter when governments expect infrastructure investments to remain productive for a decade or longer.
Networking introduces another set of decisions. Nvidia’s NVLink and InfiniBand technologies provide tightly integrated communication capabilities for large accelerator clusters. Ethernet-based architectures offer alternative approaches to scaling, equipment sourcing, and interoperability.
The Ultra Ethernet Consortium’s specification 1.1, released in October, extends the industry’s efforts to improve Ethernet for demanding AI and high-performance computing workloads.
For operators building sovereign infrastructure, the ability to introduce new hardware generations without replacing an entire networking or software environment has financial as well as technical value.
Two different markets for sovereign inference
The distinction between training and inference makes these choices more consequential.
Training frontier models requires large clusters, high memory bandwidth, and fast communication among accelerators. These requirements favor tightly integrated systems capable of handling enormous computational workloads.
Inference is creating two distinct infrastructure requirements. At one end, large language models with long context windows, substantial key-value caches, and demanding throughput requirements still benefit from high-end accelerators with large amounts of high-bandwidth memory.
AMD’s MI355X illustrates this category. With 288GB of HBM3E memory and up to 8TB/s of theoretical memory bandwidth, it is designed for demanding AI training and inference workloads. Its memory capacity can help accommodate large model weights and growing context requirements, while bandwidth remains critical to token-generation performance.
At the other end, governments and enterprises are deploying smaller, specialized, and quantized models for applications such as document processing, industrial monitoring, and customer services.
These workloads can favor smaller accelerators, systems using conventional DRAM or hybrid CPU-GPU configurations, provided they meet the required latency and throughput targets.
The distinction matters because the economics are different. A large sovereign AI cluster may justify expensive HBM-equipped accelerators, while a regional inference deployment must balance model accuracy, utilization, power consumption, memory requirements, and cost per delivered token.
The result is a broader hardware market, spanning high-end AI systems and more economical regional deployments. Each creates different opportunities for processor, memory, networking, and power management suppliers.
Export controls reach the infrastructure design
The U.S. Commerce Department’s Nov. 19 rule adds a further complication.
Under specified circumstances, exports, reexports, or transfers of covered advanced computing items require authorization when data centers provide access to more than 12 million aggregate Total Processing Performance (TPP) to companies headquartered in Macau or Country Group D:5 jurisdictions, or whose ultimate parent companies are headquartered there.
The threshold can apply across linked data centers, including digitally connected facilities. The regulation defines these as facilities connected through networking infrastructure that enables resource sharing, workload balancing, and data replication as a unified system. In practice, data center interconnects, often using high-capacity optical networks, can support such arrangements. The regulatory definition focuses on how the facilities share computing resources, rather than prescribing a particular network technology.
For operators, this makes the allocation and accessibility of computing capacity across multiple facilities relevant to compliance. Customer verification, access controls, and reliable records of resource allocation become part of infrastructure design.
Hardware security technologies can support this effort. Nvidia’s confidential computing capabilities, combined with CPU technologies such as AMD SEV-SNP or Intel TDX, enable hardware-backed isolation and attestation of supported execution environments.
These mechanisms help protect sensitive workloads and verify aspects of the environment in which they run. Regulatory compliance also depends on customer due diligence, applicable licenses, and operational controls.
Securing a workload and establishing who is legally entitled to access computing capacity are related engineering and governance challenges, but they require different safeguards.
The supply chain remains global
Even locally owned infrastructure depends on an international semiconductor supply chain. Advanced AI accelerators rely heavily on TSMC’s manufacturing capabilities, sophisticated packaging technologies such as CoWoS, and a concentrated ecosystem of HBM suppliers.
Europe’s efforts to develop processor technologies through initiatives involving RISC-V and domestic high-performance computing reflect a growing interest in controlling more of that value chain.
Yet designing an accelerator is only part of the challenge. Manufacturing, packaging, memory integration, system software, and developer tools determine whether it becomes a viable commercial platform.
For many governments, the immediate objective is operational control: owning the infrastructure, governing access to data and workloads, and securing dependable technology supply. Over time, those priorities could influence which processor architectures, software environments, and networking technologies receive investment.
Washington’s unintended incentive
American semiconductor companies have spent years building technology ecosystems that attract customers worldwide. Their competitive advantages extend from accelerator performance to software, networking, and system integration.
Sovereign AI customers bring a different set of purchasing priorities. They want competitive performance, but they also need predictable access, long-term support, and confidence that their infrastructure can adapt to changes in technology or regulation.
Trump’s proposed restrictions on American companies building data centers overseas introduce another consideration.
If U.S. hyperscalers face new barriers to expanding their infrastructure abroad, governments and regional operators may have stronger incentives to develop and own that capacity themselves, potentially purchasing American processors and networking equipment directly.
Saudi Arabia’s HUMAIN illustrates how locally controlled infrastructure can be built around American semiconductor technology. This creates a tension for Washington. Restrictions intended to preserve American technological leadership may also encourage overseas customers to invest in alternative architectures, software ecosystems, and domestic engineering capabilities.
That is the sovereign AI paradox. American processors may continue to power much of the world’s advanced computing infrastructure. But the decisions surrounding those processors, from software and interconnects to security and system ownership, could increasingly be made by customers seeking greater independence from their suppliers.
For chipmakers, the next competition may be as much about giving customers control over their computing future as about delivering the fastest processor.

articles.title: Nanoleaf's Smart Cordless Circulator Fan cools your entire home and offers cordless freedom to use anywhere
articles.text:
The hot weather is here on the eve of another summer but thankfully we’ve been reviewing the Nanoleaf Smart Air Circulator Fan have easily managed to keep our cool.
As I write this, I am in my home office, which because of all the TVs, monitors, computers, devices and 3D printers, easily runs around 5-degrees Celsius warmer than the rest of the house.
I have the Nanoleaf Smart Air Circulator trained on me at the highest fan speed (which is 9) and staying as cool as a cucumber.
What’s impressive about this relatively small fan is its reach, with a powerful airflow that can reach more than 30m.
It is 11 inches wide and has three 8-inch blades.
The Nanoleaf Smart Air Circulator Fan also has vertical and horizontal oscillation. We like to get it moving horizontally to spread the cool air around in our office.
If you want to go the whole hog, you can have both horizontal and vertical working at the same time so it’s literally covering the entire room.
There are four modes of operation – normal natural, sleep, and turbo.
For us it’s go big or go home so Turbo has been our favourite.
But it’s good to know that there is a sleep mode that operates at just 21 dB so you’re able to easily fall asleep on a hot summer night.
It even has a night light which offers a soft 3000K glow
But one of the best features is the fact that it has a rechargeable battery so you can move it room to room. Forget about looking for a power point to plug it in – you don’t need it.
And when it is plugged in, it is recharging the internal battery. Users can also charge it quickly through the built-in USB-C port.
And you can use it outside, or in a tent, or on your travels. But it’s not waterproof it just needs to be kept out of the rain.
What’s even more impressive is the fact the battery can run for up to 70 hours (with the night light and oscillation off) before it needs to be plugged back into the wall to recharge.
It also has a sleep timer which can be easily set up within the app so you’re able to delay its shutdown by up to 9 hours.
Part of this efficiency comes down to the 24W motor which really punches above its weight and yet it provides so much runtime when it’s unplugged operating from the battery.
Being a Nanoleaf product, it naturally works efficiently through the Nanoleaf app.
It also has Matter connectivity so it could also work with Alexa, Apple Home, and Google Home for easier control.
Nanoleaf Smart Cordless Circulator Fan is usually priced at $199.99 but is available at the special price if you act now for $159.99.

articles.title: Qué es Artex, la IA principal sospechosa del ciberataque a la Comisión Europea que tiene en alerta al FBI
articles.text:
Con el avance de la IA generativa, son cada vez más los usuarios, empresas e instituciones que utilizan herramientas basadas en esta tecnología en sus procesos cotidianos. Sus virtudes también han destacado especialmente en el sector de la ciberseguridad, pues los modelos de IA más punteros también pueden ser tremendamente eficaces a la hora de detectar vulnerabilidades.
Esa es precisamente la necesidad que pretende satisfacer a nivel empresarial e institucional la herramienta de Artex, un programa gratuito y de código abierto que permite que un modelo de IA sondee sistemas informáticos en busca de puntos débiles por su cuenta. Fue diseñado para pruebas de seguridad, pero ya hay grandes empresas que están haciendo uso de esta herramienta. El problema es que su nombre está ahora vinculado a varios incidentes informáticos. Te contamos todos los detalles.
Qué es. Artex es una herramienta que sirve como marco de pruebas de penetración de código abierto, el tipo de software que los equipos de seguridad utilizan para simular un ataque y encontrar agujeros antes de que lo hagan los atacantes reales. Lo que lo distingue es que delega gran parte del trabajo en la IA. La herramienta puede conectarse a cualquier modelo de lenguaje, desde modelos comerciales que ofrecen plataformas como Claude o ChatGPT hasta modelos de código abierto o chinos como DeepSeek, GLM o Kimi.
La herramienta fue publicada en Github este mismo verano bajo el alias “Autumn-27”. Su autor es el ingeniero chino Li Puhua.
Cómo funciona. La peculiaridad de esta herramienta es que permite al usuario describir su objetivo y hacer consultas en lenguaje natural sin la necesidad de escribir código o hacer uso de comandos. Una vez descrita la tarea, los agentes de IA se ponen manos a la obra para buscar servicios expuestos, detectan fallos como contraseñas débiles o configuraciones incorrectas e intentan utilizarlos para adentrarse más en una red.
Por qué se ha vuelto popular. Las organizaciones encargan pruebas de penetración porque encontrar un fallo uno mismo es mucho más barato que descubrirlo después de una brecha. Y claro, contar con la promesa de que una herramienta pueda automatizar esa tarea (y gratis), es bastante atractivo. Pero precisamente esas mismas funciones también pueden ser aprovechadas por los atacantes, y ahí radica parte de las preocupaciones.
La otra cara. El 13 de noviembre, el FBI emitió una alerta afirmando que los ciberdelincuentes y gobiernos extranjeros están utilizando Artex contra agencias gubernamentales y otros sectores en todo el mundo. Según el medio The Record, la agencia señaló que la herramienta puede llevar algunas intrusiones “desde el objetivo inicial hasta el acceso con privilegios en menos de tres horas”. También indicó que el marco permite a personas con poca experiencia técnica ejecutar operaciones complejas contra muchos objetivos a la vez. Las empresas de seguridad han vinculado Artex con ataques a instituciones financieras surcoreanas y japonesas, y Microsoft lo ha relacionado con un ataque contra la empresa de software ConnectWise.
Por qué es difícil de contener. El 8 de octubre, el desarrollador afirmaba que los delincuentes estaban abusando de la herramienta, negó su responsabilidad y posteriormente eliminó el repositorio de GitHub. Pero eso no impidió que se propagara. El FBI asegura que siguen existiendo copias a través de bifurcaciones, versiones archivadas y hasta una edición comercial. TechCrunch cuenta que los investigadores de seguridad han encontrado cientos de servidores de Artex expuestos a internet. Muchos de los ataques vinculados a la herramienta, añadió, se basaron en debilidades básicas como contraseñas débiles o falta de sistemas de autenticación multifactor.
Ciberataque a la Comisión Europea. La Comisión dijo el 19 de noviembre que había sufrido un ciberataque. El portavoz Thomas Regnier indicaba que los primeros indicios aparecieron el 22 de octubre, calificándolo como una “campaña cibernética generada por IA”. Según se informaba, el ataque interrumpió los sistemas del personal durante más de diez días, incluidas las nóminas, las solicitudes de baja y los reembolsos médicos. El medio Politico informó de que el servicio de ciberseguridad de la UE, CERT-EU, había identificado el uso de Artex en el ataque.
Regnier no mencionó la herramienta utilizada ni el aparente motivo de los atacantes. La Comisión también dijo que los investigadores no habían encontrado pruebas de una filtración de datos que afectara de forma generalizada al personal y que no tenían constancia de ningún ransomware, y que la investigación sigue abierta.

articles.title: « Welcome to Vice City » : Miami se met aux couleurs de GTA 6, et tout le monde n’apprécie pas
articles.text:
La série de jeux vidéo Grand Theft Auto a pour habitude de se dérouler dans une version parodique et satirique des États-Unis et GTA VI ne fait pas exception. Le dernier opus de Rockstar Games se déroule à Leonida, une Floride à peine déguisée dont la ville principale, Vice City, reprend largement les traits de Miami. Plutôt que de prendre ses distances avec une série connue pour ses braquages et ses fusillades, la métropole a choisi d’en profiter. Comme le rapporte l’Associated Press, le comté de Miami-Dade a conclu avec Rockstar Games un accord de 3,9 millions de dollars, qui comprend notamment un immense panneau « Welcome to Vice City » sur le toit du Kaseya Center, la salle des Miami Heat.
L’enceinte a d’ailleurs accueilli mercredi dernier, à la veille de la sortie du jeu, une soirée « A Night in Vice City ». Les joueurs du Heat ont évolué sur un parquet blanc, rose et bleu orné d’un « I love Vice City », vêtus d’un maillot spécial, tandis que les fast-foods fictifs du jeu, Cluckin’ Bell et Burger Joint, s’invitaient aux buvettes. Les villes de Miami et de Miami Beach ont aussi signé leurs propres accords de promotion, Rockstar a commandé des fresques dans le quartier de Wynwood, et le club E11EVEN s’est rebaptisé NINE1NINE, comme son double virtuel.
 Introducing the Vice City hardwood 🏀
See it for one night only, tomorrow vs Milwaukee. https://t.co/ZBpxND08hO
— Miami HEAT (@MiamiHEAT) November 17, 2026
Un jeu qui récompense le crime ?
Cette lune de miel ne fait toutefois pas l’unanimité. La shérif du comté, Rosie Cordero-Stutz, s’est opposée à l’utilisation de ressources publiques pour promouvoir un jeu qui récompense le crime, y compris la violence contre les forces de l’ordre. Conseiller municipal de Miami Beach, ville qui a dépensé des millions de dollars pour reprendre le contrôle du Spring Break, David Suarez refuse lui aussi d’« associer notre marque à quelque chose dont nous essayons si désespérément de nous éloigner depuis quelques années ». Sa collègue Monica Matteo-Salinas juge au contraire ces craintes exagérées : selon elle, la ville « peut miser sur ce matériel promotionnel, qui ne dure que six semaines, sans pour autant cautionner le jeu vidéo lui-même et les actions qui s’y déroulent ».
« Je ne peux peut-être pas faire ça dans la vraie vie, mais je peux clairement le faire dans GTA. » Un fan de la série à Miami, cité par l’AP
Une Floride reproduite avec soin
Si Miami se reconnaît autant dans Vice City, c’est que Rockstar a fait ses devoirs : ses équipes ont sillonné la ville et les Keys, survolé les Everglades et interrogé des habitants, dont d’anciens policiers et d’anciens membres de gangs. Un travail salué par Julie Fornary, guide pour la Miami Design Preservation League, pour qui aucune concession n’a été faite sur les néons et les façades Art déco d’Ocean Drive. « Nous avons le clinquant, mais aussi le crasseux. […] C’est le Miami que nous connaissons tous, nous qui vivons ici », résume-t-elle.
À lire aussi : GTA 6 : voici la façon la moins chère d’y jouer
L’engouement est tel aux quatre coins du monde qu’il se mesure aussi côté voyage. Selon Expedia, les recherches d’hébergement à Miami ont bondi de 55 % depuis la diffusion de la bande-annonce, le 15 octobre, par rapport à la même période l’an dernier, et celles pour Panama City, la station balnéaire qui a inspiré la ville de Port Gelhorn, de 65 %. Le groupe rattache ce phénomène à l’une des tendances de son rapport Horizons 2027, les séjours placés sous le signe du « retour à l’enfance », où les voyageurs troquent les programmes millimétrés contre des escapades ludiques et sans obligation. « Avec la sortie d’un titre aussi culte, on voit à quel point le besoin de déconnecter du quotidien et de retrouver une forme d’insouciance est fort chez les adultes », explique Xavier Rousselou, porte-parole d’Expedia.

Le diable est dans les détails, a fortiori sur un jeu aussi méticuleux que GTA 6, et force est de constater que Rockstar a apporté un soin tout particulier au pad de Sony.

Le meilleur exemple pour parler des gâchettes adaptatives, c'est leur utilisation lors des phases de conduite. L'autre grande force de la DualSense, ce sont ses moteurs de vibration, exploités avec talent par les équipes de Rockstar. Du détail toujours, certes, mais c'est le genre de petit plus qui tend à pousser l'expérience au-delà des attentes, comme le soulignait Kelmazad dans son test dithyrambique pour Gamekult.

articles.title: Anatel quer antecipar autenticação de chamadas
articles.text:
Anatel quer antecipar autenticação de chamadas
Proposta em consulta pública prevê antecipar para 2027 as novas regras contra fraudes e chamadas abusivas.
A Anatel pode antecipar para outubro de 2027 a implantação da autenticação de chamadas no Brasil, atualmente prevista para novembro de 2028. A alteração está em consulta pública e depende de uma decisão definitiva da agência.
A antecipação integraria a proposta aprovada em 19 de novembro, que também trata do bloqueio de comunicações irregulares, da identificação de empresas nas ligações e de uma base centralizada de números telefônicos.
A Consulta Pública nº 52 foi publicada nesta segunda-feira (23/11) e busca regulamentar a medida provisória publicada pelo governo em outubro, que estabeleceu novas exigências para enfrentar fraudes e chamadas abusivas.
A autenticação permite verificar se a ligação realmente partiu do número apresentado ao destinatário, dificultando o spoofing, fraude em que criminosos adulteram essa informação para simular chamadas de bancos, empresas ou outras instituições conhecidas.
A Anatel já havia decidido tornar a autenticação obrigatória, com prazo de três anos para adaptação. A proposta atual é encurtar esse calendário. Pelas regras da MP nº 1.396/2026, a operadora de origem deve autenticar a chamada, enquanto as redes intermediárias precisam preservar essa informação. A prestadora que entrega a ligação ao destinatário fica responsável pela verificação antes de completar o contato.
O texto também prevê o bloqueio de chamadas não autenticadas, com exceções a serem definidas, como serviços públicos essenciais. Para ligações de pessoas jurídicas, está prevista a apresentação do nome empresarial e logotipo. A proposta dispensa dessa identificação as empresas que não excederem 100 mil chamadas mensais.
Uma base de numeração integrada às soluções de autenticação e identificação de chamadas reunirá os telefones e titulares. As operadoras deverão fornecer e manter os registros atualizados, sob supervisão da Anatel. O sistema proposto também permitirá consultar qual empresa é titular de um número. O usuário também poderá contestar aqueles que não reconhecer.
Enquanto a proposta segue em discussão, outras medidas contra o uso abusivo da telefonia já estão em vigor. Os responsáveis podem ficar impedidos de fazer ligações por 15 dias. O bloqueio exige realizar, no mesmo dia, mais de mil chamadas por linha ou mais de 10 mil no conjunto de linhas.
Além disso, pelo menos 85% das chamadas precisam ser curtas (ligações não completadas, destinadas à caixa postal ou atendidas com duração de até seis segundos).

articles.title: Microsoft Azure flaw exploited to steal customers' API credentials
articles.text:
Microsoft is warning customers that a security vulnerability in Azure API Management (APIM) Classic tiers was exploited to steal stored API credentials, with Norwegian authorities linking the flaw to cyberattacks against energy companies.
Azure API Management is a cloud service that lets organizations publish, secure, monitor, and manage APIs that connect applications, services, and data.
In an Azure Service Health security advisory (Tracking ID: MZK9-GH0) sent to customers and shared with BleepingComputer, Microsoft said it identified the vulnerability on November 18, 2026, and deployed a mitigation the following day.
"Our investigation found that customers were exposed and an unauthorized party could have used the issue to access secrets stored in Azure API Management Classic instances before Microsoft identified the security issue," Microsoft said in the advisory.
According to Microsoft, the vulnerability allowed unauthorized access to certain management functionality when APIM Classic instances were not configured according to recommended security best practices.
This access could have allowed attackers to perform administrative operations, including accessing secrets stored in the service.
Microsoft said the following information may have been exposed:
- Secrets stored in Named Values
- Client secrets associated with identity providers
- Client secrets associated with OpenID Connect providers
- Subscription keys
- Tokens used to call direct management APIs
These credentials could potentially allow attackers to access additional applications, services, or backend systems, depending on their permissions.
Microsoft said it closed the unauthorized access path on November 19 and rotated Microsoft-controlled keys and credentials where appropriate.
However, the company warned that its remediation would not invalidate customer credentials that may have been compromised before the fix was deployed.
"This remediation blocks the unauthorized management-plane access path that could allow an actor to perform administrative operations, including secrets management, against Azure API Management services," Microsoft warned.
"However, it does not automatically invalidate credentials that may have been accessed before the fix was deployed."
The vulnerability affects Azure API Management Classic tiers, while Microsoft said APIM v2 tiers are not impacted.
Microsoft urged affected customers to immediately rotate potentially exposed credentials, investigate suspicious activity in systems accessible through those credentials, and review available logs for signs of unauthorized access.
In a Reddit post, an administrator claimed their organization discovered the vulnerability after detecting unauthorized access to Azure Key Vault using a valid administrator token.
"Our company has been fighting this for days, after discovering that someone logged into our keyvaults using a valid administrator token and not following the normal access pattern," the administrator claimed.
The administrator alleged that attackers exploited a zero-day authentication bypass in a deprecated legacy API to gain access to a privileged system account on APIM instances.
According to the administrator, the legacy API did not generate logs that customers could use to detect the unauthorized access. They also alleged that Microsoft initially attributed the suspicious activity to leaked customer credentials before deploying a global fix.
BleepingComputer has not independently verified these allegations.
The vulnerability has also been linked to attacks affecting Norwegian organizations, including energy companies Equinor and Skagerak Energi.
In a security advisory, Norway's National Security Authority (NSM) said an unknown threat actor targeted access tokens, secrets, and named values stored in Azure API Management.
The agency said Norway's energy sector first discovered the vulnerability and that organizations in other countries and industries were also affected.
Equinor disclosed an ongoing cyberattack on November 17, a day before Microsoft says it identified the APIM vulnerability. The company later announced that it had stopped the attack and found no indication that data had been stolen or altered.
Skagerak Energi also reported an attempted cyberattack but said it had no impact on its operations and no evidence that information was compromised.
While Microsoft says it deployed a remediation on November 19 that required no customer action, NSM's advisory warns organizations to verify that their APIM instances have received the security update.
The agency warns that instances running below specific runtime versions remain vulnerable and advises customers to contact their "service provider" if they have not received the update.
It is unclear whether the runtime updates are separate from Microsoft's initial mitigation.
Cloud security researcher Anders Kristiansen shared threat-hunting queries to help organizations investigate potential exploitation and identify credentials stored in their APIM instances.
BleepingComputer contacted Microsoft with questions about the attacks but has not received a reply yet.
This Azure API Management incident comes just days after Microsoft confirmed another security breach involving its Entra Connect Health service, where attackers exploited a vulnerability to steal tenant configuration information and administrator email addresses.

articles.title: GrapheneOS s'attaque à Google Messages avec sa propre messagerie RCS chiffrée
articles.text:
GrapheneOS a mis au point un prototype de messagerie RCS chiffrée. Cerise sur le gâteau, elle peut fonctionner sans passer par Google Messages.
L’agenda des développeurs de GrapheneOS est bien rempli. Il y a une dizaine de jours, l’équipe a confirmé que le Pixel 11 aurait droit à son système alors qu’elle avait initialement prévu de le snober. Elle a également annoncé en septembre dernier une compatibilité avec le Motorola Signature 27. Une autre nouveauté pourrait bien faire grincer des dents chez Google. On vous explique.
Une messagerie RCS chiffrée compatible avec l’iPhone et Google Messages
Le moins que l’on puisse dire, c’est que GrapheneOS ne manque pas d’ambition : « Nous avons développé une application de messagerie RCS servant de preuve de concept », ont annoncé les développeurs du système d'exploitation dans un message paru sur X.
La démonstration, qui montre un échange entre un Pixel 7 Pro et un Pixel 9, permet d’en savoir plus sur les fonctionnalités : accusés de réception et de lecture, indicateurs de saisie, partage de photos et de fichiers, mais aussi réactions par emojis. De quoi faire frémir Google, dont l’application Messages était jusqu’ici le seul moyen d’accéder au RCS sur GrapheneOS.
Et en parlant de Google Messages, l’équipe précise également que son prototype comprend un chiffrement de bout en bout qui repose sur MLS et fonctionne aussi bien avec Google Messages qu’avec iOS. L’application enregistre notamment seule le numéro auprès du service RCS, récupère les réglages nécessaires et achemine les messages.
Un prototype qui passe encore par les services Google Play
Ce prototype doit permettre à l'équipe d'intégrer le RCS à l'app Messaging de GrapheneOS, mais les utilisateurs ne vont pas pouvoir faire leurs adieux à Google tout de suite. La plupart des opérateurs confient, en effet, la gestion du RCS à Google et exigent un jeton délivré par Google Play pour valider les numéros. Le prototype de messagerie passe donc encore par ces services, qui tournent actuellement dans un bac à sable. Une version autonome est prévue, mais seulement chez les opérateurs qui accepteront de se passer de Google. Autant dire qu’il va falloir s’armer de patience.
Un autre bémol, et pas des moindres : le prototype fonctionne uniquement avec le RCS et ne prend pas en charge les SMS et les MMS. Quant au chiffrement, il garantit bien la confidentialité du contenu des échanges, mais les messages sont toujours acheminés via les infrastructures de Google ou des opérateurs. L’objectif n’est donc pas de remplacer un outil comme Signal.
Pour l’instant, le service Google Messages a encore de beaux jours devant lui : aucune date de déploiement global n’a été annoncée et le résultat sera, quoi qu'il arrive, réservé à GrapheneOS.

articles.title: Major hack sees attackers steal credit card numbers, CVVs from ecommerce firm Cleverbridge
articles.text:
Major hack sees attackers steal credit card numbers, CVVs from ecommerce firm Cleverbridge
"Notify your issuer and possibly replace your card," Cleverbridge warns customers
- Cleverbridge discloses breach exposing payment card data, including card numbers, expiry dates, and CVV security codes
- The incident affected customers who made purchases through the company's ecommerce and subscription platform
- Users are urged to monitor card activity, consider replacing affected cards, and watch for phishing or fraud attempts
Cleverbridge has disclosed suffering a rather worrying cyberattack in which cybercriminals took, among other things, payment card data and CVV numbers (used to verify payment card transactions).
In a breach notification published on its website, Cleverbridge said it spotted the attack on November 4 2026 and immediately moved to address it. The company took down parts of its infrastructure, contained the incident, and launched an investigation. The analysis is still ongoing, it said, but preliminary results have shown payment card data that was stored on the platform was copied and taken away.
“We worked diligently to identify individuals whose personal information may have been involved and began notifying affected individuals on 20 November where appropriate,” Cleverbridge said.
What is Cleverbridge and what happened to it?
Based in Germany, Cleverbridge operates a global ecommerce and payment platform that helps software and SaaS companies sell subscriptions. It handles payment processing, subscription management, taxes, billing, and other tasks across more than 240 markets, and servers a few major companies including Red Hat, Sony, Dassault Systemes, Dell, Malwarebytes, and Corel, with its platform having apparently processed more than $10 billion in transactions so far.
The breach notice does not mention a few key details. For example, we don’t know exactly how many records were taken. We also don’t know which card details were stolen, since the company is referring affected customers to their individual notifications for more details. We also don’t know if any of its large clients were affected, and in which measure.
“If you have purchased a product or service from one of the businesses supported by Cleverbridge, Cleverbridge may have processed or managed that transaction,” the notice reads.
The company also spoke briefly with BleepingComputer, confirming that customers who made purchases through Cleverbridge are affected.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
"Based on our investigation to date, the information involved includes the payment card details you used to make a purchase through Cleverbridge, notably your card number, expiry date, card security code (CVV/CVC)," the company told the publication. "Note however that no other personal data (for example your name, contact or billing details) were copied. The affected card ends in XXXX,” BleepingComputer wrote, stressing that it redacted the last four digits of the affected payment card.
Finally, we also don’t know who the threat actors are, how they managed to break in, or how long they dwelled inside Cleverbridge before being spotted and ousted.
Was Cleverbridge hit with ransomware?
Elsewhere in the notice, the company said this was not a ransomware attack since none of its systems were encrypted. However, major ransomware players such as ShinyHunters often skip the encryption part altogether and just focus on data theft and exfiltration. Apparently, it’s equally as lucrative while being faster and more simple to achieve.
So far, no threat actors claimed responsibility for the attack, and the data has not yet surfaced anywhere on the dark web.
Cleverbridge now recommends all users check their card statements carefully and notify their card issuer about any unrecognized transactions. “You may also wish to contact your card issuer to tell them about this incident and follow any advice they give, as they may decide to replace your card,” it said.
Finally, users are advised to follow best online security practices, remain vigilant, and be aware of possible phishing attempts. That means treating every incoming email as a potential attack, especially those claiming to be from Cleverbridge, and those carrying a threat or similar sense of urgency.
“Cleverbridge will never ask you for your card details, passwords, or security codes by email, phone, or text message,” the company concluded.

articles.title: La carte Avantage de la SNCF tombe en promo dès aujourd’hui pour le Black Friday
articles.text:
Il y a encore quelques années, le Black Friday rimait avec carte Avantage à moitié prix : la SNCF la vendait elle-même autour de 25 €, au lieu de 49 €. Ce temps-là est révolu. La compagnie ne fait presque plus de promotions sur sa carte de réduction, à une exception près cet été, quand la carte Avantage Jeune, réservée aux 12-27 ans, est descendue à 39 € pendant une semaine.
Pour le Black Friday, c’est Trainline qui prend le relais, comme chaque année à la même période. Cette fois, la plateforme de réservation retire 5 € au prix de la carte avec le code BLACKFRIDAY26. La carte Avantage passe ainsi à 44 €, que vous preniez la version Jeune (12-27 ans), Adulte (27-59 ans) ou Senior (60 ans et plus). L’offre démarre aujourd’hui et s’arrête mercredi 25 novembre 2026, deux jours avant le vrai Black Friday, vendredi 27. Surtout, elle est limitée à 6 000 codes.
À quoi sert la carte Avantage de la SNCF ?
La carte Avantage est le programme de réduction de la SNCF. Elle se décline en trois versions : Jeune (12–27 ans), Adulte (27–59 ans) et Senior (60 ans et plus). Dans tous les cas, elle offre –30 % sur vos trajets en TGV Inoui et Intercités, en 1ʳᵉ comme en 2ᵈᵉ classe. Jusqu’à trois enfants de 4 à 11 ans qui vous accompagnent ont droit à –60 %. Les trajets TER sont aussi moins chers, de 25 à 50 % selon les régions. La carte fonctionne vers plusieurs destinations européennes (Belgique, Espagne, Suisse, Allemagne, Italie…), mais pas sur les Ouigo.
Seule la version Adulte impose une condition. La réduction ne s’applique que pour un aller-retour comprenant une nuit du vendredi, du samedi ou du dimanche, pour un aller simple le week-end, ou pour un trajet avec un enfant. En contrepartie, elle profite aussi à un adulte qui vous accompagne.
Mais son principal avantage, et celui qui a fait son succès, ce sont les prix plafonnés en 2ᵈᵉ classe sur les trajets directs :
- 49 € maximum pour un trajet de moins d’1h30 ;
- 69 € maximum pour un trajet entre 1h30 et 3h ;
- 89 € maximum pour un trajet de plus de 3h.
Ces plafonds sont toujours appliqués, même si la SNCF se garde désormais de les garantir : sur sa page dédiée, elle indique seulement qu’ils restent en vigueur « pour le moment ». En principe, ils vous évitent les billets à plus de 100 € sur les grandes lignes en période chargée (Noël, vacances scolaires…).
La carte donne également 15 % de réduction au bar TGV et sur certains services (Mes Bagages, Junior & Cie, location de voiture). Les billets au tarif Avantage restent enfin échangeables et remboursables sans frais jusqu’à 7 jours avant le départ.
Est-ce que ça vaut le coup ?
Sur le papier, la SNCF promet que la carte est amortie dès le troisième trajet. C’est cohérent sur beaucoup de lignes, même si la réalité varie selon les destinations. Lors de notre comparatif publié au printemps 2024, nous avions constaté que la réduction de 30 % n’était pas toujours atteinte : environ 18 % des trajets observés affichaient une baisse inférieure. Il y a toutefois une réduction dans tous les cas, et la carte fait très souvent passer les billets sous la barre des 100 €. Pour qui prend régulièrement le train, l’affaire reste bonne.
La carte vendue par Trainline est une carte Avantage SNCF classique, valable un an, avec les mêmes réductions et les mêmes conditions. Vous la retrouvez dans votre compte Trainline, et vous la présentez au contrôle en PDF ou en QR code, avec une pièce d’identité. Vous n’êtes pas non plus obligé de réserver tous vos billets sur Trainline.
Bon à savoir : l’an dernier, nous n’avons pas réussi à dématérialiser dans l’application SNCF Connect une carte Avantage achetée sur Trainline. Si vous profitez de l’offre, il sera donc plus facile de faire vos futures réservations de billets via Trainline.
En théorie, la carte fonctionne sur toutes les plateformes qui vendent des billets SNCF, y compris SNCF Connect. Il suffit d’y saisir le numéro de la carte (il commence par 290901) et votre date de naissance, dans votre compte ou au moment de la recherche. Contrairement aux cartes achetées directement auprès de la SNCF, elle ne s’y ajoute toutefois pas toute seule.
Si vous avez déjà une carte Avantage encore valable, vous pouvez quand même en profiter. Au moment de l’achat, Trainline vous laisse choisir la date de début de validité, jusqu’à six mois plus tard. Il suffit de la caler sur l’expiration de l’ancienne pour enchaîner sans perdre un seul jour.

articles.title: London-based Acorda raises €2.15 million to help banks detect payment scams before money moves
articles.text:
Acorda, a London-based FinTech startup helping payment providers stop financial scams through shared risk data, has raised €2.15 million (£1.8 million) in a pre-Seed funding round.
The round was led by Concept Ventures, the first venture capital firm to back AI unicorn Eleven Labs, with participation from NFG Ventures, the firm founded by early Monzo investor and non-executive director Eileen Burbridge. A cohort of angel investors with experience across Monzo, Revolut, Coinbase and OakNorth Bank also participated in this round.
“Scam prevention is becoming an increasingly expensive problem for all banks and payment providers. Very few, if any, teams will have more experience addressing this challenge than the Acorda team,” said Burbidge, founder of NFG Ventures.
Founded in October 2026 by Jhamat Mahbubani, Sam Kelsey, and Robert Parrish, the three former leaders of Monzo’s scam prevention, Acorda was built around a problem the trio experienced first-hand. They spent three years at Monzo building machine-learning models that monitored payments from customer accounts to prevent scams, saving millions of pounds in the process.
They realised that banks know their own customers well, but know almost nothing about the recipients of funds being transferred out. The founders of Acorda call this the blind spot, which makes scams nearly impossible to detect. To banks, a victim handing money to a scammer looks almost identical to someone paying a friend back for dinner.
Acorda addresses this by acting as a single integration point for payment companies. Rather than requiring each firm to build bilateral data-sharing arrangements with each other, Acorda connects them all, enabling risk signals to be shared on both sides of a payment, often before money moves at all. The company says it is already running trials with three major global payment companies, and targets banks and cryptocurrency exchanges alike.
Mahbubani, co-founder and CEO of Acorda, said, “Banks have talented engineers and data scientists who are motivated to stop scams, but are missing the data they need. We want to provide better data in a way that they genuinely love to use.”
The fundraising comes as fraudulent payments globally reached an estimated €537 billion in 2025, a 9% year-on-year jump driven largely by AI-powered scam operations.
Acorda plans to use the new capital to demonstrate strong results with its initial cohort of payment company partners before broadening its reach. The company aims to prove that any payment provider, whether its a traditional bank or a cryptocurrency exchange, can meaningfully reduce scam activity by accessing better, shared data.
“The best founders are the ones who have lived the problem, and Jhamat, Sam and Rob have spent years on the front line of scam prevention at Monzo, building the models that protected customers and saved millions of pounds. They saw first-hand that the missing piece isn’t talent or intent, it’s data. They’ve spent years earning the trust of the industry and understand how banks actually work. That makes them uniquely placed to build the shared data layer payment providers have been missing,” said Oliver Kicks, GP at Concept Ventures.
As AI is increasingly used to create sophisticated scams and fraud, Acorda says the shared data layer, rather than siloed in-house data, will become the infrastructure the payments industry has long lacked.

articles.title: OLED ou Micro RGB : à 1 199 €, quelle TV Samsung choisir pendant le Black Friday de la Fnac ?
articles.text:
Avant de choisir un nouveau téléviseur, il est important de vous interroger sur vos usages. Ce sont eux qui vont dicter la taille de l’écran, la technologie d’affichage et les fonctionnalités dont vous avez vraiment besoin. Vous aimez regarder vos films ou vos séries dans le noir ? Privilégiez les noirs profonds de l’OLED. Vous rêvez d’avoir une image vibrante et lumineuse en plein jour ? Le Micro RGB vous convient sans doute mieux.
Reste la question du budget. Et c’est là que le Black Friday de la Fnac rend le choix intéressant. Avec 400 € de remise, le Samsung 55S92H OLED passe de 1 599 € à 1 199 €, soit le même prix que le Samsung 55R85H Micro RGB. Même diagonale, même prix, technologie d’affichage différente : le choix dépend donc uniquement de vos besoins réels.
Si vous trouvez qu’une dalle 55 pouces est un peu étriquée ou que le son de votre installation manque d’ampleur, la Fnac propose aussi des réductions sur une sélection d’écrans et de barres de son Samsung.
Notre sélection de produits Samsung pour le Black Friday :
- Le téléviseur Samsung 55S92H OLED (TQ55S92H) à 1 199 € au lieu de 1 599 € ;
- Le téléviseur Samsung 55R85H Micro RGB (TMR55R85H) à 1 199 € ;
- Le téléviseur Samsung 65R95H Micro RGB (TMR65R95H) à 2 499 € au lieu de 2 999 € ;
- La barre de son Samsung HW-Q995H à 890 € au lieu de 1 490 €.
À 1 199 €, qu’est-ce qui change entre l’OLED et le Micro RGB ?
La principale différence entre l’OLED et le Micro RGB se joue sur la source de lumière et l’affichage des couleurs. Sur une dalle OLED, chaque pixel émet sa propre lumière et peut s’éteindre complètement pour produire un noir pur, sans lumière résiduelle, même à côté d’un pixel lumineux. Sur un téléviseur Micro RGB, la dalle est rétroéclairée par de minuscules LED rouges, vertes et bleues, qui permettent d’afficher une palette de couleurs plus étendue. L’un se démarque dans les scènes sombres tandis que l’autre brille durant les scènes colorées.
Si votre cœur penche du côté obscur de l’affichage, le Samsung 55S92H avec sa dalle OLED 4K de 55 pouces est tout indiqué. Grâce à elle, vous pouvez profiter pleinement des scènes les plus sombres de vos films ou de vos séries sans avoir à subir cet effet de halo qui a tendance à griser les noirs. Ce téléviseur reste aussi à l’aise dans les pièces lumineuses grâce au traitement antireflet Glare Free, qui limite les reflets d’une fenêtre ou d’une lampe sans ternir les noirs.
Pour le Black Friday de la Fnac, le Samsung 55S92H est à 1 199 € au lieu de 1 599 €, soit 400 € de remise.
Si vous aimez surtout les images riches en couleurs, tournez-vous vers le Samsung 55R85H. Son écran Micro RGB 4K de 55 pouces couvre 100 % de l’espace colorimétrique BT.2020, une couverture certifiée par le VDE (Verband der Elektrotechnik).
Sur un film d’animation en HDR, par exemple, l’écran peut restituer une palette de teintes plus étendue que la moyenne si le film en tire parti. Le Samsung 55R85H est proposé à 1 199 € à la Fnac.
Côté jeu, les deux modèles acceptent la 4K à 120 Hz sur PS5 et Xbox Series X, dans les jeux compatibles. Sur un PC capable de suivre, le Samsung 55S92H monte jusqu’à 165 Hz en 4K avec VRR, contre 144 Hz pour le Samsung 55R85H.
Quand privilégier un écran de 65 pouces ?
Si un 55 pouces vous paraît un peu juste depuis le canapé, pensez au 65 pouces. Avant de vous décider, regardez à quelle distance vous vous asseyez et quelle place vous avez sur le meuble TV.
Sur le papier, passer de 55 à 65 pouces peut sembler anodin. L’image passe d’environ 122 à 144 cm de large, hors cadre. Mais comme elle grandit aussi en hauteur, ces 22 cm de plus représentent environ 40 % de surface d’affichage supplémentaire. De quoi donner plus d’ampleur à un film en Cinémascope ou mieux suivre l’action lors d’un match entre amis.
Le Samsung 65R95H reprend la technologie Micro RGB du 55R85H dans un écran 4K de 65 pouces. Il bénéficie du traitement antireflet Glare Free, comme le 55S92H OLED. Le reflet d’une baie vitrée gênera donc beaucoup moins un match en pleine journée. Ce modèle embarque aussi le processeur Micro RGB AI Engine Pro et le traitement Micro RGB HDR Pro. Branché à un PC compatible, il monte jusqu’à 165 Hz en 4K avec VRR.
Pour le Black Friday, le Samsung 65R95H passe de 2 999 € à 2 499 € à la Fnac, soit 500 € de remise.
Qu’est-ce qu’une barre de son change à vos soirées cinéma ?
Si la taille de l’image joue un rôle important dans l’appréciation d’un film, d’un jeu ou d’une retransmission sportive, un son plus ample rend l’expérience bien plus immersive. C’est ce que propose Samsung avec l’ensemble HW-Q995H. Composé d’une barre de son, d’un caisson de basses et de deux enceintes arrières, il cumule 23 haut-parleurs qui contribuent à créer une véritable bulle sonore autour du canapé.
Ce système 11.1.4, compatible Dolby Atmos et DTS:X, utilise notamment des haut-parleurs orientés vers le plafond pour donner de la hauteur aux effets sonores. Dans une scène de poursuite, une voiture peut ainsi donner l’impression de vous dépasser. Et quand il se met à pleuvoir à l’écran, l’averse semble tomber au-dessus de vous.
Partie intégrante de l’écosystème Samsung, ce système sonore est compatible avec la technologie Q-Symphony qui permet d’intégrer et de synchroniser les haut-parleurs du téléviseur au reste de l’installation.
Pour le Black Friday, le HW-Q995H bénéficie d’une réduction de 600 € qui permet de faire tomber son prix à 890 € au lieu de 1 490 € habituellement. Avec l’un des deux téléviseurs 55 pouces présentés plus haut, l’ensemble home cinéma revient à 2 089 €, soit 410 € de moins que le 65R95H seul.

articles.title: Far Eye helps reduce Flipkart logistics expenses by 6%
articles.text:
Far Eye helps reduce Flipkart logistics expenses by 6%
Far Eye says its logistics platform has helped Flipkart Wholesale cut logistics costs by 6%, reduce vehicle deployment by 8% and lower vehicle idle time by 10% through better routing, dispatch and fleet optimisation across its pan-India operations.
AI-powered enterprise SaaS Far Eye on Sunday said it has helped ecommerce major Flipkart's B2B cash-and-carry market place, Flipkart Wholesale, slash its logistics spend by 6% besides an 8% reduction in vehicle deployment pan-India.
This has enabled Flipkart Wholesale to improve fleet productivity without compromising delivery efficiency, reducing vehicle idle time by 10%, Far Eye said in a statement.
The improvements come from digitising and connecting dispatch, routing, compliance and payment collection processes across a network comprising 26 stores and one cross-dock, it said.
Flipkart Wholesale's network processes more than 200,000 orders and about 195,000 vehicle assignments a month.
The platform said it now supports the movement of goods across this network through a unified digital workflow, replacing largely manual and fragmented dispatch processes.
Far Eye said it also brought optimisation to match vehicle deployment to operational need, along with automated e-way bill generation, thus removing manual work from a compliance-heavy step.
All these initiatives resulted in 8% fewer vehicles across pan-India operations, with no impact on delivery efficiency, 6% lower total logistics spend, through better routing, dispatch discipline and fleet optimisation and 10% lower vehicle idle time, as planning and deployment improved fleet productivity, among others, it said.
India's general trade ecosystem of more than 1.4 crore kirana stores accounts for an estimated 75-80% of the country's FMCG sales. Procurement in this market is moving online.
The government-backed DigiDukaan initiative on ONDC has already connected more than 21,000 retailers with over 450 brands across three cities. As ordering gets easier, the pressure moves to what happens after the order is placed, the platform said.

Speaking of firsts, TC Mzansi launches TODAY! 🇿🇦 At 12 PM WAT, the very first edition of our Southern African tech newsletter lands in inboxes. We’ve spent a week telling you what’s coming. Today, you get to see what we’ve been cooking.

Capital Markets
Dangote considers selling his personal shares as refinery IPO demand surpasses supply
Aliko Dangote, the Nigerian billionaire and founder of the Dangote Group, is in talks with Nigeria’s Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the country’s capital market regulator, about selling part of his personal stake in Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE, Bloomberg reported on November 19.
Explain like I’m new here: Dangote opened the refinery’s initial public offering (IPO) on September 14, offering investors a chance to own a piece of the business. The refinery initially offered about 4.1 billion shares at ₦525 ($0.40) per share, targeting ₦2.15 trillion ($1.6 billion). However, applications reached ₦5.85 trillion ($4.3 billion), with nearly 4 million investors.
In the original IPO, investors were buying shares offered by the refinery. In a secondary sale, an existing shareholder sells some of the shares they already own.
The IPO also included an option to sell up to 30% more shares if demand justified it. Dangote currently owns about 87.3% of the refinery. After the original offer, his stake would fall to roughly 84.4%. If the full additional share option is used, it would drop further to about 83.6%. A separate sale of his personal shares could provide another way to accommodate demand without requiring the refinery to issue more shares.
What does this mean for investors? The proposed sale could give investors who applied for shares but received fewer than they requested another chance to buy into the refinery. However, the discussions do not mean the sale has been approved or that every investor who applied will receive the shares they requested. The SEC still has to review the proposal and approve the final allotment.

Funding
Baobab raises $50 million in bonds to expand small business lending in West Africa
Baobab, the microfinance group owned by Egypt’s Beltone Holding, has raised CFA 30 billion ($50.2 million) through two sustainability-linked bond issues in Côte d’Ivoire and Senegal. The group raised CFA20 billion ($33.5 million) in Côte d’Ivoire and CFA10 billion ($16.8 million) in Senegal. Both bonds mature in five years, with a one-year grace period before principal repayments begin.
Explain like I’m new here: Baobab is in the business of lending money to people and businesses that traditional banks may overlook. In 2025, Baobab had a €957 million loan portfolio and €555 million in customer deposits. It disbursed €1.2 billion in loans during the year and reported a net profit of €1.47 million. By raising CFA francs in the markets where it operates, Baobab would not have to rely on foreign-currency borrowing, which can cause a mismatch between the currency it borrows and the currency in which it lends.
A new chapter: The fundraising comes about ten months after Beltone completed its $197.6 million acquisition of Baobab in January 2026. The deal gave the Egyptian financial services group an established microfinance network across seven African countries, including Senegal, Côte d’Ivoire, Mali, Burkina Faso, Madagascar, the Democratic Republic of Congo and Nigeria.
What it means: African small businesses face an estimated $331 billion shortfall in financing. Baobab bets its microfinance model can serve some of these businesses. The new money could help it extend more loans, particularly to women-led enterprises, while supporting private education providers and green projects.

Banking
Kenya’s big banks want more time
Kenyan banks and the central bank are already arguing over one capital deadline. Now, the country’s biggest lenders want to push it back further.
Top Kenyan banks have asked the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) to delay new capital requirements by at least 12 months, arguing that implementing them during the 2027 election year could slow lending to businesses and households.
The rules are scheduled to take effect on January 1, 2027.
Explain like I’m new here: The CBK wants stricter rules for banks considered too important to fail. These are large, highly connected lenders whose collapse could disrupt the wider economy.
Under the proposed rules, these banks would have to hold additional capital buffers of 0.5% to 2.5% of their loan books. Banks falling below a specified capital ratio of 8.625% would also face restrictions on paying dividends to shareholders.
The idea is to ensure Kenya’s biggest lenders can absorb losses without risking the financial system.
Why the pushback? Kenya’s banks are worried about losing momentum. Private-sector credit growth recovered from a 2.9% contraction in January to 10.6% growth in September 2026.
The Kenya Bankers Association (KBA) argued that requiring banks to hold more capital could limit lending, particularly to small businesses and farmers, just as credit demand is recovering.
Another disagreement already exists: The CBK and Kenya’s Treasury are at odds over when all commercial banks must meet a KES 10 billion ($77 million) minimum capital requirement.
The CBK is sticking to December 2029, while Treasury wants to extend the deadline to 2032. The industry’s request for a one-year pause concerns different rules aimed specifically at the biggest banks.
Zoom out: Kenya’s smaller banks are fighting for more time to raise their minimum capital. Now, the largest lenders want more time to build additional buffers. The CBK wants a banking system strong enough to withstand a crisis. Banks want enough room to keep lending through an election year.
Venture Capital
South Africa returns from Silicon Valley with a $5.7 million AI plan
South Africa went to Silicon Valley with 300 delegates and big AI ambitions. It returned with a R100 million ($5.7 million) startup fund proposal, and the man who put the first money on the table wasn’t a Silicon Valley billionaire.
President Cyril Ramaphosa has announced plans for a venture capital fund to support South African AI and technology startups, with the government promising to match contributions from private investors.
Explain like I’m new here: South Africa wants to build a stronger AI industry, but developing AI products can be expensive. Startups need access to powerful computers, particularly graphics processing units (GPUs), to train and run AI models.
Between November 14–21, Ramaphosa led a week-long delegation of ministers, entrepreneurs, researchers, and students to California, the United States, to attract investment and learn from the world’s biggest AI companies. The delegation met executives from Google, Microsoft, and Cisco, although critics questioned the absence of some of Silicon Valley’s most prominent CEOs.
State of play: During the visit, Andile Ngcaba, founder of investment firm Convergence Partners, proposed the fund and offered to contribute R25 million ($1.4 million), provided other investors joined him.
Ramaphosa backed the proposal and said the government would match private-sector contributions. However, the government hasn’t specified its contribution, and no foreign investors have been confirmed as funders.
Between the lines: South Africa went looking for international AI investment, but the fund’s first named backer is a local entrepreneur. Ngcaba’s offer is also conditional; the R100 million ($5.7 million) remains a fundraising target.
Zoom out: AI startups need more than investment capital. They need expensive computing power, skilled workers, and customers willing to pay for their products. The proposed fund could help with some of those costs, but its immediate challenge is getting investors to commit the remaining money.
