articles.title: Hace 12 años, la exmujer de Elon Musk dijo que una de las mejores técnicas del multimillonario es saber usar sabiamente la psicología de la oposición
articles.text:
Los dos grandes hábitos que observó Justine Musk en su exmarido durante su explosión profesional fueron el de trabajar mucho y el de decir “no”. “Me di cuenta de que detrás de cada no hay un sí más profundo a lo que realmente quieres”, explica en la charla que ella misma transcribió.
Es decir, que cada vez que decía no, estaba diciendo que sí a algo más profundo. Porque en realidad lo que estaba haciendo era bloquear el tiempo y la energía para poder dedicarlos a lo que había decidido que iba a hacer. Se trata de un sí que tiene que ver con lo que uno tiene derecho a querer para sí mismo.
Lo que cuesta decir “no”
Por ejemplo, en el caso de sus hijos. Cuando querían afirmar su independencia, decían que no. A ella le costaba más. ¿Y esto? Justine se preguntó si le costaba porque no se sentía con derecho a defender lo que quería. Lo relacionó con lo que había aprendido de pequeña. De hecho, terminó minimizando sus ambiciones en un mundo que esperaba de las mujeres que fueran modestas.
Esta escena coincide con lo que se ha visto en un estudio sobre autonomía infantil. Los investigadores han seguido a 51 niños con sus madres en dos momentos diferentes. Primero, cuando tenían entre 16 y 51 meses, y luego a los 5 años. En esta última fase aumentan las respuestas negativas verbales sin enfado y las que buscan llegar a algún tipo de acuerdo. Disminuyen los desafíos abiertos.
Temer que nos encontremos con enfados puede llevarnos a aceptar por compromiso. La psicóloga Ahona Guha describe ese miedo entre sus pacientes. También señala que tenemos en cuenta qué piensan los amigos y familiares y que nos preocupa que se nos considere egoístas. Hay que pensar a qué nos vamos a comprometer. Es decir, si tenemos tiempo o no para ello.
La agenda de Buffett y las prioridades de Jobs
Bill Gates también observó en Warren Buffett un modo similar de proteger su tiempo. En una entrevista con Charlie Rose, habló de cómo había aprendido viendo la agenda de Buffett. Gates dijo que era de los que llenaban cada minuto. Creía que era la única manera de hacer las cosas. Pero, viendo cómo organizaba su tiempo Warren, entendió que sentarse a pensar podía ser más importante que muchas de las cosas que ponemos en nuestro calendario.
Steve Jobs también asociaba los “no” con el enfoque. En una conversación con desarrolladores en una conferencia de Apple en 1997, comentaba cómo, para poder concentrarse en determinados proyectos, había que renunciar a otros. Recordó que en Apple había equipos trabajando en ideas interesantes de manera independiente. Sin embargo, juntas no ofrecían una dirección clara para la empresa. También había planteado este principio de priorización en relación a las reuniones de trabajo. En una nota interna de 1986 para el equipo de NeXT, planteaba que todos los jueves se dedicarían a trabajar sin reuniones.

articles.title: Jeff Bezos donó acciones de Amazon por USD 198,9 millones en solo dos días
articles.text:
Jeff Bezos donó 198,9 millones de dólares en acciones de Amazon durante dos días, incluidos títulos que poseía desde 1994, y elevó a más de 600 millones de dólares sus aportes declarados en acciones durante el año.
Las transferencias se producen cuando al Fondo para la Tierra le quedan cerca de cuatro años para cumplir la promesa de distribuir 10 mil millones de dólares antes de 2030, según Fortune.
La fortuna filantrópica de Bezos y su esposa, Lauren Sánchez Bezos, había alcanzado aproximadamente 4.700 millones de dólares a fines de 2025, una cifra que los ubicó en el décimo puesto de la lista de mayores donantes de Estados Unidos. Ese año, sus contribuciones se estimaron en unos USD 600 millones, de acuerdo con Forbes.
El compromiso del Fondo para la Tierra exige acelerar el ritmo de las entregas. Bezos lanzó esa iniciativa en 2020 y, hacia fines de septiembre, había aportado cerca de 2,4 mil millones de dólares, por lo que necesitaría donar un promedio de USD 1,8 mil millones anuales para llegar a la meta.
Las últimas transferencias se sumaron a dos rondas anteriores: más de 1,25 millones de acciones donadas en mayo y 415.580 en agosto de 2026. Al cierre del 16 de noviembre, esos paquetes estaban valuados en torno a USD 323 millones y USD 107 millones, respectivamente.
En conjunto, Bezos entregó al menos 2,44 millones de acciones de Amazon durante el año, con un valor aproximado de USD 629,1 millones a ese precio. Los documentos presentados describen una parte de los destinatarios como organizaciones sin fines de lucro.
A qué destinatarios van las donaciones de Jeff Bezos
Day 1 Academies, la organización sin fines de lucro que administra la red Bezos Academy de preescolares gratuitos, recibió al menos 450.837 acciones: 220.200 en mayo y 230.637 en agosto de 2026. Las dos entidades sin fines de lucro creadas por Bezos concentraron aproximadamente el 22,5% de las acciones donadas en el año.
Asimismo, el Fondo para la Tierra anunció el 19 de noviembre que destinaría más de USD 100 millones. Su enfoque será la protección de la selva amazónica mediante 15 nuevas subvenciones en Sudamérica.
Cristián Samper, director general del fondo y responsable de soluciones para la naturaleza, explicó a Fortune que la organización utilizará informes de los beneficiarios y análisis satelitales independientes para seguir la conservación de los bosques y la reducción de la deforestación.
Day 1 Academies gestiona 38 preescolares gratuitos basados en la metodología Montessori en comunidades desfavorecidas de Arizona, Florida, Hawái, Kentucky, Texas y Washington. Su informe anual registra 2.456 alumnos matriculados para el ciclo lectivo 2026-27.
La red educativa surgió del compromiso de USD 2 mil millones que Bezos anunció en 2018 para respaldar la educación infantil temprana y a las familias sin hogar.
La otra vertiente de aquella promesa, el Fondo Familias del Día 1, financia organizaciones locales que ayudan a familias a salir de refugios o de la calle para acceder a una casa estable. En 2025, ese fondo otorgó USD 102,5 millones a 32 grupos de 20 estados, el Distrito de Columbia y Guam.
Bezos declaró a CNN en 2022 que planeaba donar la mayor parte de su fortuna durante su vida. El fundador de Amazon sostuvo en se momento: “Lo difícil es encontrar la manera de hacerlo de forma estratégica”, al comparar ese desafío con la creación de la compañía. “Así que estamos desarrollando la capacidad para poder distribuir este dinero”.
Cómo es la participación de Jeff Bezos en las acciones de Amazon
Incluso después de las donaciones, Jeff Bezos conservaba más de 878 millones de acciones de Amazon. Esa participación estaba valuada en aproximadamente USD 226.400 millones al cierre del 16 de noviembre de 2026 y las transferencias del año representaban menos del 0,3% de ese total.
Su exesposa, MacKenzie Scott, tenía un patrimonio neto estimado en USD 27.100 millones al 20 de noviembre de 2026. Scott donó USD 7.200 millones solo en 2025, lo que llevó sus aportes acumulados desde el divorcio de Bezos en 2019 a USD 26.400 millones, según Forbes.

articles.title: Intel "Bartlett Lake-S" CPUs Reportedly Boot Natively on MSI Z690/Z790 Motherboards
articles.text:
Monday, November 23rd 2026
Intel "Bartlett Lake-S" CPUs Reportedly Boot Natively on MSI Z690/Z790 Motherboards
Intel's "Bartlett Lake-S" CPU series are reportedly booting natively without modifications on select MSI motherboards. Initially, Uniko's Hardware shared tests of the Intel Core 9 273PE with 12 P-cores and the Core 7 253PE with 10 P-cores on an MSI Z790 MPOWER motherboard, using a modified BIOS to boot and utilize the P-Core only SKUs. However, X user LovK2X successfully booted and operated a Core 9 273PE qualification sample without any modifications on the MSI MEG Z690I motherboard, demonstrating that these CPUs can run without modifications and with minimal restrictions. Reportedly, all MSI motherboards from the Z690 and Z790 series support "Bartlett Lake-S" with the latest BIOS version, with the only limitation being a DRAM frequency lock. Every other aspect can be tuned and customized.
Built on the Intel 7 node and designed for Socket LGA1700, "Bartlett Lake" is a non-hybrid chip featuring up to 12 "Raptor Cove" P-cores without any E-core clusters. It was not intended to be compatible with consumer Intel Z790 chipset motherboards. However, the main issue was never the socket itself. "Bartlett Lake" shares the same physical LGA 1700 layout as Intel's "Raptor Lake" chips, but that doesn't automatically make it compatible with consumer boards. Typically, there was no official BIOS and microcode support to allow proper CPU initialization. However, MSI's latest BIOS update makes it possible to run these CPUs natively, and the second-hand market will likely value them for their potential gaming performance.The flagship "Bartlett Lake" Core 9 273PQE is also notable for its P-core-only design, featuring 12 performance cores and 24 threads. This sets it apart from Intel's more common hybrid desktop CPUs that combine performance and efficiency cores. It requires no intervention from Thread Director or the Windows 11 kernel to manage the threads, which could significantly enhance gaming performance. This uniqueness makes it appealing to enthusiasts, especially those curious about its performance compared to chips like the Core i9-13900K or Core i9-14900K. However, this setup is experimental, as these CPUs are circulating as qualification samples instead of regular consumer SKUs.
Sources:
				LovK2X on X, 				via VideoCardz			
	
	
	
		
	
		
6 Comments on Intel "Bartlett Lake-S" CPUs Reportedly Boot Natively on MSI Z690/Z790 Motherboards
I do, but unfortunately it doesn't seem to be working anymore. I've disassembled and cleaned it, there was a bug under the heatsink - but it doesn't POST and the code reader says "--"No, production units are available. What is called "Bartlett Lake-S" is in fact referring to the Raptor Lake-S A0-type silicon, which replaces the 16 E-cores by four additional P-cores (12P0E configuration).
These were only released for the embedded segment and no microcode update was issued to support them on consumer motherboards, rendering them unbootable unless added manually somehow. Normally this would not be a problem, but since no A0-type Core i9 exists (only B0-type configs), you normally cannot use them on an unmodified say, Z690 or Z790 motherboard.
The 10P+0E should perform pretty close to a 8P+6E setup. I would like that instead of the 8P+8E if possible.

articles.title: GrapheneOS accuses Google of anti-competitive pressure as it expands to Motorola hardware
articles.text:
The takeaway: One of the better known security-focused versions of Android says Google is trying to steer phone makers away from it. GrapheneOS developers claim Google has been asking Android manufacturers whether they work with the project, citing its Google Mobile Services licensing terms in the process. The accusation comes as GrapheneOS moves onto Motorola hardware, its first step beyond Google's own Pixel phones.
The team made the claims on X and described Google's outreach as a threat to the brands involved. It also said Google might eventually take a range of steps meant to block GrapheneOS and other Android forks. Its leaders said they want to speak with US Attorney General Todd Blanche and others to stop what they called "Google's escalating anti-competitive behavior."
GrapheneOS is built on Android's open-source code and hardens the operating system to improve security and privacy. For most of its existence, Pixel phones were its only officially supported hardware. That made it dependent on the same company it now accuses of working against it.
That dependence is starting to loosen. GrapheneOS partnered with Motorola last year, and the Motorola Signature 27 is being offered in a GrapheneOS variant. People who want the operating system will no longer have to buy a Pixel. A second hardware source protects the project if its relationship with Google gets worse. It also creates the kind of manufacturer relationship that licensing pressure could affect.
The project has also kept adding features. Recent work includes a secure paste feature merged into the operating system, part of a steady stream of changes aimed at limiting what apps can see and access.
The GrapheneOS team did not portray everyone at Google as an opponent. It credited Google's engineers and said many have helped the project at a technical level.
"There are a lot of engineers at Google who support what we're building and have directly worked with us," the team said. "People there have repeatedly helped us and even explicitly added support for GrapheneOS to Google software including supporting Vanadium for Play services FIDO2 and passkeys."
 – GrapheneOS (@GrapheneOS) November 20, 2026
That last detail shows how closely GrapheneOS and Google's software remain connected. Vanadium is the GrapheneOS browser. FIDO2 and passkeys are the authentication standards that let users sign in without passwords, using cryptographic keys stored on the device. When Google's Play services support those standards in Vanadium, GrapheneOS users can use passwordless sign-in through the project's own hardened browser. That kind of compatibility work happens at the engineering level, and the project says it has received that help.
According to GrapheneOS, the problem is Google's business division, not its engineers. The project's argument depends on that split. Technical teams at Google have made room for the fork, while the commercial side is now pushing manufacturers on licensing.
The licensing question has a legal history. Google has already lost court battles over its agreements with Android manufacturers, including terms that limited their ability to ship devices running Android forks. If Google is now using Google Mobile Services licensing to discourage manufacturers from working with GrapheneOS, it would be returning to a kind of restriction that courts have already examined.
For now, the claims come from one side. GrapheneOS has not publicly named the manufacturers it says Google contacted or shared the wording of any communications. Google and Motorola have not publicly responded to the allegations.
The outcome could affect more than one project. GrapheneOS's move onto Motorola hardware tests whether a hardened Android fork can survive outside the Pixel line. If manufacturers decide that working with the project puts their Google licensing at risk, other Android forks could find it harder to get onto new hardware.

articles.title: GL.iNet Routers, KVMs Compromised via Remote Management Service Flaw
articles.text:
GL.iNet has warned customers that a threat actor exploited a vulnerability in its cloud-based remote management service to deliver malware to some routers and KVM devices.
China-based networking hardware maker GL.iNet is well known for its pocket-sized travel routers and Comet KVM devices. The devices can be managed remotely through its GoodCloud platform.
The vendor discovered the remote management service vulnerability leveraged by the attacker on November 20 and has since patched it.
However, it noted that the fix doesn’t remove the malware from infected devices — customers need to install a separate “security firmware” for that. GL.iNet recommends installing the security firmware on all devices, even those with no signs of infection.
It remains unclear who is behind the attack and how many devices were compromised.
It’s also unclear whether the attackers reached the computers connected to compromised KVM devices.
“As a precaution, check for unfamiliar programs, browser extensions or user accounts; unexpected startup items or scheduled tasks; and unusual settings changes or network activity. Run a full scan with up-to-date security software,” the company recommends for KVM devices.
Security and networking firm RemoteToHome Consulting, which manages a large number of GL.iNet routers, has been investigating the incident. Based on its code analysis, the attack worked because the GoodCloud software on the routers ran commands from cloud messages without checking them. GL.iNet has not confirmed this information.
RemoteToHome reported that most of the nearly 200 routers it checked appeared to be impacted, either by this new attack or an older backdoor that appears to date back to September 2025. RemoteToHome says it doesn’t know how that older backdoor was installed.
SecurityWeek has reached out to GL.iNet for additional information and will update this article if it responds.

articles.title: EUA colocam empresa ligada a escândalo da Nvidia em lista comercial restrita
articles.text:
O governo dos Estados Unidos colocou a empresa singapurense Megaspeed em sua lista de restrições comerciais nesta segunda-feira (23). A medida impede que companhias estadunidenses forneçam chips avançados, softwares e outras tecnologias à organização sem licença do governo. A decisão ocorre em meio à investigação sobre o suposto envio ilegal de semicondutores da Nvidia para a China.
A Megaspeed está no centro de escândalo envolvendo Jensen Huang, CEO da Nvidia, e Alice Huang, empresária chinesa que controlava a companhia. Autoridades estadunidenses suspeitam que ela tenha ligação com a inteligência da China e investigam se a empresa ajudou clientes chineses a obter chips de inteligência artificial (IA) sujeitos a controles de exportação.
A inclusão na chamada Entity List, administrada pelo Departamento de Comércio dos EUA, dificulta o acesso da companhia a produtos e tecnologias de origem estadunidense. Empresas que aparecem no cadastro precisam obter autorização do governo para receber esses materiais, e as licenças costumam ser negadas.
Empresa é investigada por possível envio ilegal de chips à China
- A investigação contra a Megaspeed começou em 2024 e envolve possíveis violações das regras estadunidenses de exportação de semicondutores;
- O Departamento de Justiça e o Departamento de Comércio dos EUA investigam suspeitas de que a companhia tenha participado do envio de chips de IA da Nvidia para clientes na China;
- Alice Huang, que controlava a empresa, também está no centro de acusações relacionadas à inteligência chinesa. Segundo informações anteriormente divulgadas pelo The New York Times, autoridades estadunidenses concluíram que ela seria uma agente de Pequim (China) e teria repassado informações ao governo chinês enquanto mantinha relacionamento próximo com Jensen Huang;
- A China classificou as acusações como infundadas;
- A Megaspeed afirmou anteriormente que Alice Huang deixou a companhia em agosto de 2025 e que seus negócios foram conduzidos de maneira legal;
- A empresa também aparece no diretório de parceiros oficiais de nuvem da Nvidia, segundo a Reuters.

Decisão expõe divergências dentro do governo Trump
A inclusão da Megaspeed na lista de restrições ocorreu depois de semanas de divergências entre integrantes do governo estadunidense sobre como lidar com o caso.
De acordo com o Times, o secretário do Tesouro, Scott Bessent, defendia ação mais rápida contra a empresa e a adoção de regras mais rigorosas para controlar a exportação de chips de IA. Já o secretário de Comércio, Howard Lutnick, defendia medidas mais específicas e cautelosas. Seu departamento é responsável pela administração das regras de exportação de tecnologia.
Em entrevista neste mês, Bessent criticou a demora na implementação das restrições e afirmou que o Departamento do Comércio tinha o poder de conduzir o processo.
O Tesouro, a Defesa e o Departamento de Estado, além do representante comercial dos EUA, apoiavam a inclusão da Megaspeed na lista havia meses, segundo o secretário.
Lutnick, por sua vez, enfrentou críticas de integrantes do próprio governo e de parlamentares, que questionaram suposta proximidade excessiva de seu departamento com a Nvidia e Jensen Huang.
Na semana passada, o Departamento de Comércio publicou novas regras para restringir o acesso da China a data centers de IA em diferentes partes do mundo. Na ocasião, a pasta tomou a medida incomum de informar que havia agido sob orientação do Departamento do Tesouro.
Restrição coincide com retorno de Jensen Huang à Nvidia
A decisão contra a Megaspeed foi anunciada no mesmo dia em que Jensen Huang retornou ao cargo de CEO da Nvidia. O executivo havia deixado temporariamente a posição após a divulgação de informações sobre relacionamentos extraconjugais, incluindo seu envolvimento com Alice Huang. A empresária também foi apontada por autoridades estadunidenses como possível agente de inteligência chinesa.
A Nvidia anunciou o retorno de seu CEO depois de receber garantias de autoridades estadunidenses de que ele não representava risco à segurança nacional.
A inclusão da Megaspeed na lista comercial também marca mudança na postura recente de Washington. Segundo a Reuters, o Departamento de Comércio não adicionava novas empresas ao cadastro desde outubro de 2025.
A pausa ocorreu em meio aos esforços do governo Trump para evitar o agravamento das tensões comerciais com Pequim.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Tiny flaws in diamonds could unlock a quantum computing revolution
articles.text:
Tiny flaws in diamonds could unlock a quantum computing revolution
By treating qubits like individual molecules, scientists can now predict their behavior faster and more accurately
- Date:
  November 13, 2026
- Source:
  Princeton University
- Summary:
  Scientists have discovered a faster way to identify diamond-based materials that could power quantum computers and sensors at room temperature. The breakthrough has already revealed promising new quantum building blocks that could help unlock computing capabilities far beyond those of today's supercomputers.
- Share:
A new computational technique could accelerate the search for diamond materials capable of powering future quantum computers and highly sensitive sensors. Developed by a researcher at the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory (PPPL), the method makes it much easier to identify promising materials for quantum technology, potentially opening the door to advances across many areas of science.
The approach has already revealed new candidates for quantum computing and sensing applications. The findings were recently published in ACS Central Science and have attracted attention from other researchers in the field.
One of the biggest challenges in developing quantum technology is finding materials that can maintain delicate quantum states under practical conditions. Many candidates require extremely low temperatures to function reliably. Diamond materials stand out because certain quantum properties can remain useful even at room temperature.
This capability could help advance technologies that are important to national research priorities and the development of next-generation computing. Quantum sensors promise levels of sensitivity and precision beyond those of conventional instruments, while quantum computers could eventually solve certain extraordinarily complex problems much faster than today's most powerful supercomputers.
Why Imperfect Diamonds Could Be the Key to Quantum Computing
Although diamonds are made of carbon atoms, a flawless diamond crystal is not enough to create a useful quantum computing system. The key lies in tiny irregularities within the crystal structure.
These imperfections, known as defects, can occur when a carbon atom is absent from its normal position, when another element replaces a carbon atom, or when both changes occur together. The atoms surrounding these defects can form qubits, the basic units used to store and process quantum information in quantum computers and sensors.
Finding the most useful defects, however, has been difficult. Accurately modeling their quantum behavior traditionally requires enormous computational resources, making it challenging to evaluate large numbers of possible candidates.
A Simpler Way to Discover Better Diamond Qubits
Mark Martirez, a staff research scientist at PPPL, developed a way to dramatically reduce the complexity of these calculations. Instead of simulating a much larger diamond structure, he isolates a small region containing just 16 to 30 atoms around a defect.
By "carving out" this tiny atomic cluster and treating it like a separate molecule, Martirez can use powerful computational methods that chemists have spent decades refining. These established techniques make it possible to analyze the quantum properties of diamond defects much more efficiently without sacrificing the high level of accuracy needed for the calculations.
"Because we're treating the qubits as molecules, the cost of calculating these defects is equivalent to the cost of just modeling a simple molecule," Martirez said. "This method really opened the floodgates" in terms of how qubits can be assessed.
The new technique allows researchers to calculate how different qubits respond to laser light and microwave pulses far more quickly than before. Using this approach, the team identified promising defects involving boron and oxygen that could serve as new types of qubits.
New Diamond Defects Reveal a Spectrum of Quantum Colors
Light plays an important role in how scientists interact with diamond qubits. Researchers use lasers and microwave pulses to manipulate their quantum states and retrieve stored information.
Much of the previous work in this area has centered on a defect known as the nitrogen-vacancy center. This structure forms when a nitrogen atom takes the place of a carbon atom in a diamond crystal, while an adjacent position that would normally contain another carbon atom remains empty.
Under laser illumination, this type of defect can emit red light when it occupies a particular quantum state.
The newly investigated defects offer different optical properties. Oxygen defects can produce blue light, while those involving boron emit ultraviolet light.
These differences could make it possible to combine several types of qubits within a single quantum device. Because each type responds differently to light, researchers might be able to interact with one group of qubits without disturbing another.
"One could imagine, then, combining different qubits of different responses, so you can basically probe one qubit but not the other," Martirez said.
Beyond identifying new candidates, the findings suggest a broader change in how researchers approach quantum technology. Diamond qubits have traditionally been studied primarily through physics, but understanding their underlying chemistry could provide additional ways to design them.
Martirez believes that researchers could eventually engineer qubits for particular functions using principles similar to those applied when chemists create specialized molecules, including compounds designed for new medications.
How Quantum Chemistry Could Transform Future Research
The potential benefits extend well beyond the development of quantum computers themselves. Martirez sees an intriguing possibility in which advances made possible by quantum chemistry eventually lead to quantum technologies that help improve the field of chemistry.
In other words, quantum chemistry could develop the very tools needed to "enrich itself" in the coming decades.
A practical quantum system containing multiple qubits could make molecular calculations substantially more accurate. That would allow scientists to study increasingly complex chemical structures, including large biological molecules and proteins, with a level of detail that is difficult to achieve using conventional methods.
"We could describe larger molecules, biomolecules, proteins and everything like that in a more accurate way, and that could improve all the chemical-adjacent industries, such as pharmaceutical science and materials science. Even our fundamental understanding of molecular systems could be enriched."
Such improvements could have far-reaching implications for pharmaceutical development, materials research, and the fundamental study of how molecules behave.
Martirez also hopes the research will encourage more chemists to explore solid-state physics. Although building advanced quantum computers is often viewed as a challenge primarily for physicists, he argues that chemistry offers valuable expertise that could help accelerate progress.
"At this moment in time, there's a great emphasis on building the first state-of-the-art qubit computer," he said. "But it's not just physicists who should be participating in this research. Chemists have decades of developed intuition about chemical systems that could be easily translated into understanding defects in solids as well."
By bringing these disciplines together, scientists may be able to develop more effective ways to discover, understand, and eventually engineer the quantum materials needed for future technologies.
The research was funded through PPPL's Laboratory Directed Research and Development program under prime contract number DE-AC02-09CH11466, with additional support from the DOE Office of Science, Office of Fusion Energy Sciences.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Princeton University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- John Mark P. Martirez. A Chemist’sGuide to Solid-State Qubits: DiamondColor Centers as Embedded Vacancy-Centered Molecules. ACS Central Science, 2026; 12 (10): 1578 DOI: 10.1021/acscentsci.6c00548

articles.title: BDC to manage Canada’s $100-million contribution to NATO Innovation Fund
articles.text:
Two years after earmarking the funds, Canada has finally joined the NATO Innovation Fund, and the Business Development Bank of Canada (BDC) will manage its stake.
The news: Canada became the 25th Allied nation to back the NATO Innovation Fund this past weekend, making an investment of 64.6 million euros ($100 million CAD). BDC will hold and manage Canada’s investment in the fund through its Defence Platform, working alongside the Department of National Defence and Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada.
The NATO Innovation Fund, which has now courted more than 1.1 billion euros ($1.7 billion CAD, is a multi-sovereign venture capital fund investing in technologies with defence, security, and resilience applications. By joining the fund, Canada is giving its defence tech companies another avenue for customers and capital.
From the source: “Defence is about much more than financing companies. It’s about connecting them to opportunity,” BDC senior vice-president of defence strategy Peter Dawe said in a statement. “BDC can help bridge the gap between Canadian businesses and the organizations buying, building and investing, whether that opportunity is here at home or across NATO.”
The context: The NATO Innovation Fund launched in 2022 and invests three to 15 million euros in deep tech, dual-use companies from the seed to Series B stages. The United Kingdom, Germany, and Türkiye are among the 24 other participating members, but not the United States. Canada pledged to join the fund in 2024, even earmarking the funds to do so, but it hadn’t actually joined until this week.
By managing Canada’s stake in the fund, BDC takes on even more responsibility in seeing through Prime Minister Mark Carney’s pledge to “rebuild” the Canadian Armed Forces and increase its defence spending commitments under NATO. In March, BDC expanded the investing and financing capacity of its Defence Platform up to $6 billion. This past September, BDC became Canada’s sole entrant in an investor network for NATO’s defence accelerator.
Final thought: The extra responsibility comes as the Crown corporation faces some uncertainty about its future. The 2026 budget revealed that the government is launching a transition process to merge BDC with Export Development Canada (EDC) to create a single federal development bank, with few details and no timeline for the merger to be completed.
Image courtesy Madison McLauchlan for BetaKit.

articles.title: Schlechte Nachrichten für Thermomix-Nutzer:innen: Vorwerk passt die Preise für Cookidoo an – wer davon betroffen ist
articles.text:
Vorwerk erhöht den Preis für Cookidoo: Was Thermomix-Nutzer jetzt wissen müssen
Der Thermomix von Vorwerk ist beliebt. Das Gerät ist eine multifunktionale Küchenmaschine, die Zutaten nicht nur zerkleinert und mixt, sondern auch wiegen, erhitzen, rühren und dampfgaren kann. Eine Schritt-für-Schritt-Anleitung führt Nutzer:innen durch die Zubereitung und soll so den Aufwand reduzieren. Mit Cookidoo bietet Vorwerk zudem eine digitale Rezeptplattform. Sie umfasst weltweit mehr als 100.000 Rezepte für den Thermomix sowie Funktionen wie Wochenplanung und Guided Cooking. Viele Cookidoo-Nutzer:innen müssen allerdings künftig tiefer in die Tasche greifen, wie aus einer Mitteilung des Unternehmens hervorgeht.
Wer von der Preiserhöhung betroffen ist
Der neue Thermomix TM7 ist seit April 2026 erhältlich. Bis zum Jahresende verkaufte das Unternehmen weltweit über eine Million Geräte. Zudem hatten bis Ende 2025 mehr als sechs Millionen Kund:innen ein Cookidoo-Abonnement abgeschlossen. Das geht aus dem Geschäftsbericht des Unternehmens hervor. Seit Juli 2024 zahlen Neukund:innen für die Rezeptplattform fünf Euro pro Monat beziehungsweise 60 Euro pro Jahr. Bestandskund:innen mit älteren Abonnements zahlen teilweise noch 36 oder 48 Euro jährlich. Das soll sich ändern: Vorwerk gleicht alle Tarife an den Preis von 60 Euro an. Die Anpassung gilt für alle Kund:innen mit einem TM7 oder dem Vorgängermodell TM6. Sie greift bei der ersten Verlängerung ab dem 10. Dezember 2026.
Vorwerk hat die Kund:innen über die Änderungen informiert. Wie Inside Digital berichtet, steht in der E-Mail, dass ihr Cookidoo-Abo zur nächsten Verlängerung nicht mehr verfügbar sei. Sie müssten den neuen Konditionen zustimmen – ansonsten laufe das Abo aus. Die Preissteigerung bezieht sich laut Angaben von Vorwerk explizit auf Kund:innen, die einen TM7 oder TM6 besitzen und „in den vergangenen sechs Monaten mindestens ein Guided-Cooking-Rezept gestartet haben”. Auf Nachfrage von Inside Digital stellte der Hersteller klar, dass Besitzer:innen eines TM5 oder älterer Modelle ausgenommen sind, weil einige Cookidoo-Funktionen auf ihren Geräten nicht verfügbar sind. Wer in den vergangenen sechs Monaten kein Guided Cooking nutzte, zählt in den Augen des Herstellers zu den inaktiven Kund:innen.
Nicht alle wollen den höheren Preis zahlen
Inhaltlich ändert sich am Cookidoo-Abonnement nichts. Mit dem höheren Betrag will Vorwerk künftige Innovationen finanzieren, wie es in der Mitteilung heißt. „Für 60 Euro pro Jahr, also 5 Euro pro Monat, umfasst das Abo ein sich kontinuierlich weiterentwickelndes digitales Koch-Ökosystem mit immer neuen getesteten Rezepten und Übersetzungen, gesicherter Qualität sowie dem Betrieb und der stetigen Weiterentwicklung der Plattform und neuer digitaler Services“, so das Unternehmen hier. Zuletzt fügte Vorwerk auch neue KI-Funktionen hinzu, etwa den Cookidoo-Assistenten und Rezeptübersetzungen.
Cookidoo-Nutzer:innen haben jetzt zwei Optionen: Entweder sie stimmen der Preisanpassung aktiv zu – oder sie reagieren nicht und lassen ihr Abo auslaufen. Viele Bestandskund:innen reagieren verärgert auf die Preiserhöhung. Einige von ihnen müssen künftig zwölf Euro mehr im Jahr für Cookidoo zahlen. Laut Inside Digital wird die Preisanpassung insbesondere auf Facebook diskutiert. Demzufolge würden manche Nutzer:innen es als „absolute Frechheit“ empfinden, dass auch Bestandskund:innen künftig mehr zahlen sollen. Andere wiederum finden den Preis von 60 Euro pro Jahr berechtigt. „Wir reden hier von einem Euro im Monat! Allein der digitale Assistent und die Übersetzungsfunktion sind mir das wert“, so eine Userin laut Inside Digital.
! Heiße Mädchen warten auf dich — Miss4.fun

articles.title: Trump endorses Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, says US has no evidence of wrongdoing
articles.text:
President Trump praised Nvidia’s decision on Monday to reinstate founder Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, saying on his social network Truth Social that “the United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.”
The Nvidia board’s statement had also referred to consultations with “senior levels of the United States government” as informing its decision. It said that, based on that input, Mr. Huang’s reinstatement was deemed not a national security risk.
In his comments on Monday, Trump claimed that U.S. Attorney General [Todd Blanche] had found no evidence that Mr. Huang had engaged in unlawful conduct. It’s an unusual statement for a U.S. president to make, as the attorney general typically conducts those investigations independently. Notably, Attorney General Blanche has not yet made a formal statement on the case.
There’s also indication that President Trump may have been aware of the decision before the announcement by the Nvidia board. Speaking to a PBS journalist over the weekend, he said of Huang “he’s back where he should be and we see he did absolutely nothing wrong.” Asked to clarify about whether he meant Huang would be reinstated, Trump said, “I hope so, I hope so.”
Huang was accused of having multiple extramarital relationships, including one with a direct report at Nvidia and another unnamed employee. However, the affair of most concern was the one with the alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang (no relation). Ms. Huang was an executive at a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed, which had purchased billions in Nvidia chips over the past couple of years. This relationship had raised national security concerns about whether the CEO ties to Ms. Huang could have compromised sensitive information or facilitated China’s access to advanced U.S. AI chips, which are subject to export restrictions.
Trump said last week that he believed this relationship didn’t threaten the U.S.’s national security, and instead said that no one had proven she’s a spy. “She may not be a spy,” the president said, adding that “China plays games with us, and we play games with China.”
Trump’s full statement on Huang’s return, released on Monday, is below.
The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO. The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy. The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct. On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure. Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company’s compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security. Congratulations to Jensen, the NVIDIA Board, to the People of the United States — and, indeed, the World! Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DONALD J. TRUMP

articles.title: Ladybird, the first new browser engine in years, is now available to test
articles.text:
Ladybird, an independent web browser with a built-from-scratch engine, is finally available for testing. On Monday, Ladybird developer Andreas Kling announced that the browser is launching in alpha on macOS and Linux following more than four years of development.
Ladybird, the first new browser engine in years, is now available to test
Looking for a web browser without Google Chrome underneath? You can try this independent web browser now on macOS and Linux.
The release makes Ladybird the first browser in years to arrive with an entirely new engine. We’ve seen many engines emerge over time, but the most popular browsers use just three today: Gecko, Blink, and WebKit. While Gecko, now used in Mozilla Firefox, first appeared in Netscape 6 in 2000, Apple’s WebKit arrived in Safari in 2003 as a fork of KDE’s KHTML. A decade later, the Google-backed Chromium project forked WebKit to create Blink, which now powers Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Opera, and more.
Ladybird is backed by a nonprofit organization with the goal of creating “an independent, fast and secure browser that respects user privacy and fosters an open web,” according to its website. Though Ladybird development initially began as part of a C++ project, its developers eventually began porting the code to Rust using AI.
In his post announcing the alpha, Kling notes that the browser built around the Ladybird engine “is modest but functional,” adding that “some websites won’t work” during the alpha. A Windows version of Ladybird will arrive during a “later stage” of the project.

articles.title: 80er-Jahre-Nostalgie: Sony bringt den legendären Walkman-Kopfhörer zurück
articles.text:
Sony bringt seinen Kopfhörer-Klassiker MDR-3 aus der Walkman-Zeit als MDR-3R zurück. Die Standardversion kostet 59 Euro, eine Sonderausgabe im Design der Serie Stranger Things 69 Euro. Beide sollen noch in diesem Monat in den Handel kommen. Das „R“ im Namen steht je nach Lesart für „Retro“ oder „Relaunch“. Sony will damit das Aussehen des Originals mit aktueller Technik verbinden.
Warum ausgerechnet dieser Kopfhörer
Der MDR-3 kam Anfang der Achtziger passend zum 1979 eingeführten ersten Walkman auf den Markt und blieb dort viele Jahre. In Erinnerung geblieben ist er weniger wegen seines Klangs als wegen der bunten Schaumstoffpolster in Hellblau, Orange und später Schwarz – und wegen des Verstellmechanismus, dessen Metallbügel gern in die Finger piksten.
Den Anstoß für die Neuauflage gab die US-Serie Stranger Things. Dort trägt die Figur Max Mayfield, gespielt von Sadie Sink, den MDR-3 samt Walkman WM-8 in entscheidenden Szenen und hört darüber Kate Bushs ikonisches „Running Up That Hill“.
USB-C statt Klinke
Technisch hat sich beim MDR-3R einiges getan: Statt des 3,5-Millimeter-Klinkensteckers gibt es nun USB-C. Der Kopfhörer arbeitet mit Geräten zusammen, die USB-Audio-Klasse 1.0 unterstützen – etwa iPhones oder Android-Smartphones. Neu ist außerdem eine Fernbedienung im Kabel mit eingebautem Mikrofon. Damit lassen sich Telefonate führen oder Videos vertonen.
Einen Akku braucht der MDR-3R nicht, Bluetooth gibt es nicht. Den Strom liefert das angeschlossene Gerät über das Kabel. Die 23-Millimeter-Treiber sollen laut Sony „dieselben“ sein wie beim Original. Zur Standardversion legt Sony zwei Sätze Ohrpolster bei, einen in Orange und einen in Hellblau. Ob es die Polster auch einzeln zu kaufen gibt, ist bislang offen. Die Sonderausgabe zur im vergangenen Jahr beendeten Serie Stranger Things bringt schwarze und rote Polster mit sowie das eingravierte Serienlogo.

articles.title: Sierra doubles valuation to $30B within six months as demand for AI in CX takes off
articles.text:
Enterprise customer experience company Sierra, co-founded by former Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor, said on Monday that it has raised $1.75 billion in a Series F round that doubles the company’s valuation to $30 billion. The new raise comes within six months of its previous round, which valued the company at $15 billion.
The new round was led by Greenoaks and Lightspeed Venture Partners, with participation from existing investors who have led previous rounds, including Benchmark, Sequoia, Greenoaks, GV, and Tiger Global.
Enterprise automation is among the few areas where AI has seen rapid adoption. Sierra said that it currently serves almost 50% of Fortune 50 companies, and its clients include BNY, HSBC, Singtel, Wells Fargo, JPMorganChase, Pearson, Next, and Cox Automotive. The company late last month said its outcome-based pricing model has helped it double its run-rate revenue to $400 million within five months.
That said, Sierra is working along similar lines as other customer experience players in the market, which is creating a platform to build agents and partner with model developers to provide choices to enterprises. As personal and work agents interact with enterprise systems, Sierra is also working on creating protocol definitions for agents with companies like Meta, Stripe, and Walmart.
Sierra will use the fresh cash build to its technology stack to layer agents for servicing and hire more sales folks to sign and maintain enterprise contracts faster than its rivals.
Startups operating in the CX space have seen multimillion-dollar rounds come their way with soaring valuations. Voice AI company ElevenLabs is now valued at $22 billion; Decagon is valued at $4.5 billion; Wonderful is valued at $5 billion; and Parloa is valued at $3 billion. Multiple other startups have scored investments of more than $100 million.
During the HumanX conference in Amsterdam in September, Sierra co-founder Clay Bavor argued that despite the popular belief that AI-powered CX companies are replacing humans in contact centers, a majority of its customers are reassigning roles to existing employees.

articles.title: The Enigma of SoftBank’s $1 Trillion SK Hynix Buyout Attempt
articles.text:
SK Hynix, the world’s second-largest memory chipmaker, is in the news again, this time for being the target of a trillion-dollar buyout attempt by the Japanese tech conglomerate SoftBank. According to a report published in The Information on Friday (Nov. 20), SoftBank CEO Masayoshi Son recently explored a $1 trillion buyout of SK Hynix.
A SoftBank spokesperson responded in a short statement: “SoftBank explores many opportunities, and this one is no longer under active consideration.” SK Hynix said the company had no knowledge of the matter and that any outreach happened entirely on the SoftBank side.
Apparently, Son sounded out a $1 trillion buyout of SK Hynix and then shelved it. The most likely hurdles could be financing, chaebol governance, and the Korean Government’s view of the memory industry as a strategic asset. The latter makes it a deal that could never close anyway. And there were no negotiations or a term sheet.
But that’s only half the story. Especially when the report didn’t establish Son’s specific rationale for choosing SK Hynix. For starters, the trillion-dollar figure is far higher than SK’s $577 billion market valuation recorded on Friday, Nov. 20. So, the floated trillion-dollar price is 1.7× SK Hynix’s current market value.
The largest tech industry acquisition on record is SpaceX’s $250 billion takeover of xAI in 2026, combining aerospace, satellite, and AI operations. Moreover, SoftBank’s balance sheet is already stretched by its AI bets on OpenAI and Stargate; it recently sold its entire Nvidia stake to raise cash. It’s also mobilizing its stake in Arm to secure funding for investments in OpenAI and Stargate.
So, the question is how SoftBank would arrange the sheer scale of this trillion-dollar funding. In retrospect, it looks more like a financing inquiry. There were no price negotiations and no indications of commitments from Wall Street banks. In other words, it wasn’t a takeover attempt, but an early-stage exploration.
More importantly, there is literally no chance that the Korean Government would approve such a deal. Furthermore, while Korean Government approval is almost unimaginable, SK Hynix has no reason to sell either. That makes this whole episode a non-starter. So, what’s this fuss all about? If Masayoshi Son didn’t actually want to buy SK Hynix, what would he gain from this buyout story, for which he paid nothing?
What Son wants
Industry observers believe this buyout attempt signals Son’s grand plan to build an AI empire, which requires owning every layer of the value chain. Start with Arm, which sits at the semiconductor design IP layer. It controls chip designs that underpin a range of AI processors; furthermore, Arm’s neutral licensing platform effectively serves the entire chip design industry.
Next, SoftBank snapped Graphcore in 2024 and Ampere Computing in 2025, the two upstarts developing AI processors. The Japanese conglomerate has also acquired a significant stake in Intel. At the model layer, powered by AI processors, SoftBank has committed a massive investment in OpenAI.
At the AI infrastructure level, SoftBank has poured nearly $500 billion into the Stargate joint venture and the acquisition of data center investor DigitalBridge. The Japanese giant is also the largest shareholder in SB Energy, which runs data center and power businesses.
What’s missing here is memory, which has become a chokepoint in the AI buildout. In fact, memory suppliers have become more important to the companies designing AI accelerators and building data centers to run them. And on SoftBank’s AI buildup map, one layer is empty: memory.
It’s worth mentioning that SK Hynix is a pioneer in high-bandwidth memory (HBM), which enables processors to handle the vast volumes of data required for AI computing. In 2025, SK Hynix’s HBM revenue more than doubled year on year. Nvidia is SK Hynix’s largest customer, accounting for 14.8% of its revenue in the first quarter of 2026, and according to TrendForce, Nvidia is expected to place about two-thirds of its HBM4 orders with SK Hynix.
Apparently, by owning a major memory chipmaker, SoftBank could extend its reach across the AI supply chain. So, it’s probably a precursor to SoftBank buying a partial stake in a memory chipmaker or buying the whole company outright.
SK Hynix isn’t up for sale, and Son doesn’t need to buy it because even a hostile takeover bid isn’t realistic. But Son tested the financial appetite for bankrolling an acquisition of a memory chipmaker and then walked away. After this free due diligence, if he buys a partial stake in a memory company or buys the whole company for much less, it will look like a concession.

articles.title: Spanish LaLiga confirms hackers stole soccer fans’ personal data
articles.text:
LaLiga, Spain's top men's professional football league, disclosed a data breach that exposed personal information belonging to users of its services and those of some affiliated clubs.
According to the organization, the incident occurred between November 14 and 16, and the attacker extracted data from compromised systems.
LaLiga organizes Spain’s top two men’s professional football divisions.
The top league is one of the world’s most prominent football leagues, where clubs with a global audience, such as Real Madrid, FC Barcelona, and Atlético Madrid, play.
On November 16, the organization’s security team identified the source of the unauthorized access and implemented measures to block the attack and stop the data extraction.
“LALIGA was the target of a cyberattack on one of its technology platforms for fan services,” reads the announcement.
“Between November 14 and 16, a cybercriminal gained unauthorized access to the platform and extracted personal data belonging to users registered for digital services offered by LALIGA and some clubs.”
LaLiga underlined that the incident was confined to a specific platform and did not extend to other systems that support the running of the competitions.
After implementing containment measures, LaLiga launched an investigation to determine the scope of the incident and introduced more thorough monitoring to detect future attempts to breach its systems.
The football organizer also reported the incident to the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD) and filed a complaint with the National Police’s Central Cybercrime Unit.
Impacted clubs were also directly notified, and actions to inform impacted fans are being coordinated.
At the time of writing, no ransomware group has claimed responsibility for the attack on LaLiga.
BleepingComputer has contacted the organization to learn more about the attack and which clubs were impacted, but we have not received a response as of publication.

articles.title: Measuring Verification Gaps In LLM-Generated Post-Quantum Hardware (Lucid, EYL)
articles.text:
Researchers at Lucid Motors and EYL Inc. published “From FIPS to FPGA with LLM Agents: Measuring What Tests and Reviews Miss in Post-Quantum Cryptographic Hardware.”
Abstract
“As LLM agents increasingly generate RTL alongside the tests and reviews that validate it, self-generated evidence is a weak foundation for trustworthy hardware. We present our seven-stage verification-gated workflow, evolved during a post-quantum design port, in which a gate counts only if shown able to fail on negative controls and fault mutants, and reviewer agents audit work before commit. We then audit this evidence with tool-selected netlist mutants, flaw replays, and formal checks. The flow ported an ML-KEM-768/ML-DSA-65 accelerator to a 300 MHz Zynq UltraScale+ key-custody card: all six operations are byte-exact on the board, and it passes all 85 interface-applicable NIST ACVP cases (of 285) and 484 ML-DSA known answers. However, passing module tests overstate the verification strength. Across three RTL modules, existing simulation gates kill only 76% of 399 tool-selected netlist mutants; specification-derived tests guided by the survivors raise the fresh-draw decapsulation kill rate from 48% to 74%. In pre-registered single-model replays on flaws invisible to known-answer tests, undirected whole-design review catches two verifier flaws in only 3/6 and 1/6 sessions, whereas module-scoped review catches every known flaw in all 54 sessions. Even scoped review detects planted key-custody flaws in only 3/20 sessions, whereas formal checks (one added for the replay) flag every one. In this study, trustworthy agentic hardware needed author-independent mutants for test gates, module-level scoping for LLM review, and formal checks for custody invariants.”
Find the technical paper here. November 2026.
Jungmin Park, Eunha Kim, Wooseop Kim, Seongjoon Cho, and Byungho Cha. “From FIPS to FPGA with LLM Agents: Measuring What Tests and Reviews Miss in Post-Quantum Cryptographic Hardware.” arXiv:2611.25339, November 19, 2026. https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25339.

articles.title: ApplyBoard co-founder’s startup Passage deepens its admissions push with Kira acquisition
articles.text:
The talent recruitment startup from the co-founder of ApplyBoard is bolstering its university admissions automation platform.
The news: Passage calls itself an “applied AI lab” that’s building tech to connect international students to schools and talent to job opportunities. The company announced on Thursday that it has acquired Toronto-based Kira Talent, an admissions assessment platform that’s majority-owned by the private equity arm of US non-profit Educational Testing Service (ETS).
Kira Talent’s AI-powered product will be combined with Lectoris, Passage’s admissions operating system, to help institutions assess prospective students and manage acceptances more efficiently, the companies said in a news release. A Passage spokesperson told BetaKit that Kira Talent’s entire team is joining Passage, bringing its headcount to around 60 employees.
From the source: Passage founder and CEO Martin Basiri told international education news site The PIE News that its product will help admissions officers dealing with AI-assisted applications and inflated grades. “Getting to know the students, and seeing how they react and who the real person behind the resume is, is very important—and I think that’s only becoming more important,” Basiri said.
The context: Basiri founded Passage in 2023 after leaving ApplyBoard, the edtech startup and former unicorn he co-founded with his younger brothers. While ApplyBoard helps international students apply to Western schools, Passage was meant to financially support foreign workers looking to move to Canada to fill skilled labour gaps.
Passage raised $40 million CAD to fuel these plans, but a federal clampdown on international students and immigration starting in 2024 forced the company to pivot, Basiri told The Globe and Mail. It landed an exclusive partnership this August to provide technology to ETS, the main US developer of standardized admissions tests like the Graduate Record Examinations. Now, Passage has acquired Kira Talent from ETS; according to its website, Kira has been used by more than 1,100 academic programs.
Final thought: Passage’s partnership with ETS saw it lean into the educational admissions tech space, which ApplyBoard CEO Meti Basiri told the Globe now puts the two startups in competition. With its new acquisition of Kira Talent, Passage appears to have further boosted its AI offering in educational admissions.
Feature image courtesy Passage.

articles.title: ¡Confirmado! Hailee Steinfeld vuelve en ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ como Kate Bishop: ¿llegan los Jóvenes Vengadores al UCM?
articles.text:
Después de muchos meses suplicando por esta noticia, Marvel por fin ha correspondido a sus fans. La actriz Hailee Steinfeld, que interpretó a Kate Bishop en la serie de Ojo de Halcón, volverá en Avengers: Doomsday. Se trataba de uno de los personajes más queridos de esta Saga del Multiverso, pero hasta ahora no había noticias sobre su regreso al UCM en ningún proyecto a la vista.
Por fortuna, todo ha cambiado hace solo unas horas. Y es que, durante la campaña promocional de su próxima película de animación para Disney, Hechizo: Bienvenidos a Hexe, ha sido la propia actriz quien ha anunciado la buena nueva. En un vídeo publicado en redes sociales, Hailee Steinfeld ha desvelado que vuelve en Avengers: Doomsday.
"Hola, pues estoy aquí con mi película Hechizo: Bienvenidos a Hexe, pero parece que me han traído una silla de otra película", sugiere, enfocando una de las sillas con las que Marvel anunció el reparto completo de la próxima película de los Vengadores. "No te pierdas a Hailee Steinfeld en Hechizo: Bienvenidos a Hexe, de Disney, antes de que vuelva a la gran pantalla en Avengers: Doomsday, reza también la descripción del post.
Hailee Steinfeld debutó en Marvel como Kate Bishop en Ojo de Halcón allá por 2021. Un par de años más tarde, en 2023, también tuvo un cameo en The Marvels al unirse a Kamala Khan para un nuevo equipo. Pero desde aquella aparición, nunca más habíamos vuelto a verla. Ahora, volverá en Avengers: Doomsday y las teorías sobre su papel en el filme no ha tardado en aparecer.
¿Aparecerán los Jóvenes Vengadores en Avengers: Doomsday?
Con la presencia confirmada de Hailee Steinfeld como Kate Bishop en Avengers: Doomsday, los fans de la saga ya solo piensan en una cosa: los Jóvenes Vengadores. Este equipo de los cómics reúne a varios de los héroes más novatos y de menor edad para luchar contra diversos villanos. Durante años se ha rumoreado con su llegada al Universo Cinematográfico de Marvel, e incluso se habló de una película propia. Entre ellos podrían estar la propia Kate Bishop junto a Ms. Marvel, Yelena Belova, Spider-Man, Billy y Tommy Maximoff, Ironheart o Cassie Lang.
Pero la compañía jamás confirmó esa producción y, cuando en el anuncio del reparto de Avengers: Doomsday la mayoría de esos nombres no estaban entre los elegidos, las esperanzas de verles formando una alianza se desvanecieron. Sin embargo, el regreso de Kate Bishop ha vuelto a encender la chispa. Porque lo más probable es que vuelva con la propia Ms. Marvel. Y con Yelena Belova y Cassie Lang también confirmadas en el filme, cada vez son más los que confían en que Marvel finalmente sí reúna a sus Jóvenes Vengadores para la batalla contra el Doctor Doom.
Avengers: Doomsday se estrena en cines el 18 de diciembre.

articles.title: Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang
articles.text:
After Nvidia’s board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Appearing on Stephen A. Smith’s radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump said that Huang would “end up on his feet.”
Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang
Trump got his wish to reinstate Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia — but investigations are still looming.
Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang
Trump got his wish to reinstate Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia — but investigations are still looming.
“You know the expression, anybody can be replaced,” Trump said, floating Apple’s ex-CEO Tim Cook as a potential CEO candidate.
It didn’t take long for Trump to begin softening his approach, making it clear he’d welcome Huang back into the role of CEO even if Nvidia’s own board wasn’t ready to do so. Behind the scenes, the Trump administration was working to grease the landing for Huang’s return. And soon, Nvidia’s board changed its tune: Barely a week after insisting they all agreed to shut the door on Huang’s return, they voted unanimously to reinstate him as CEO, president, and board director.
“There’s nothing wrong with a comeback,” Trump said in a celebratory call to CNBC.
Trump then posted an image on Truth Social of Huang transposed onto Trump’s own body in the infamous photo of him raising his fist after being shot at a campaign rally. In his raised fist, Huang-on-Trump’s-body is clutching a scarlet bra, holding it high in the air.
“There’s nothing wrong with a comeback”
Even after a decisive blow to the president’s power as Democrats swept the midterm elections, Trump appears to maintain his position as a corporate kingmaker. Trump said he spoke with Huang the night prior to his reinstatement and had been in communication with the board both “directly and indirectly.” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement that “President Trump was totally involved” in the board’s decision — Trump decided near the end of last week that he wanted to lead efforts to get Huang reappointed, per The New York Times, so he asked Vice President JD Vance to act as a liaison between Huang and Nvidia’s board, providing reassurances that the move wouldn’t pose a security risk. Trump also reportedly dialed into Nvidia’s Sunday night board meeting to make the case for his return. “I made the deal,” he told CNBC on Monday.
News of Huang’s reappointment, nearly as dramatic as Sam Altman’s return to his CEO role after being voted out by OpenAI’s board in 2023, was a widespread shock to experts, analysts, and investors, particularly after Nvidia’s board had assured stakeholders on its quarterly earnings call last Tuesday that the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” On Monday morning, a surge in NASDAQ-100 futures hit a circuit-breaker limit and caused a halt in trading over the volatility.
Trump has meddled in other messy incidents, including by repeatedly — and perhaps illegally — extending the deadline for TikTok to complete its sale to a US entity, and, he admitted on Monday, protecting Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Although he said on CNBC that Musk is “80 percent super genius, 20 percent he has other problems,” Trump said it’s important to protect people like him and Huang. “We have to protect our brilliant people because we don’t have enough.”
But the upcoming Democratic-majority Congress could test both Huang and Trump’s influence. As Republicans prepare for an open presidential primary in 2028, at least one potential candidate appears to be breaking with the president in their skepticism of Huang and Nvidia. And Democrats seem eager to probe both Nvidia and the Trump administration.
The past couple of weeks have been tumultuous for Nvidia. Huang admitted he had had an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom some US intelligence officers reportedly believed to be a potential Chinese spy. There were nearly immediate reports of an additional affair with a direct report, as well as an alleged third affair with a second employee. Megaspeed has reportedly also been investigated for a broader attempt to illegally funnel advanced Nvidia chips to China. Huang himself has pushed to open up more chip sales to China, and he reportedly lied to the Nvidia board about his infidelity. He’s scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1st.
The Nvidia board tried to address concerns about Huang in its announcement Monday, writing that members “received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” It made assurances that the independent investigation it had kicked off about Huang and foreign intelligence would “proceed to conclusion” with Huang’s cooperation.
The board also said it had recently formed an entirely new National Security and Export Control Committee “comprised solely of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks,” which is working with legal counsel and advisers who have national security experience. Nvidia will be hiring for a new C-suite position, the board said: chief compliance officer. The executive will “oversee compliance” across the company and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance committees. “NVIDIA will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries,” the board added.
Still, the reaction to Huang’s return reflects how small the chance of Huang’s return seemed before Trump’s efforts. Although Trump had previously cast doubt on multiple reports that Alice Huang was a spy, The New York Times reported on Sunday that she “kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year.” According to the Times, which cited multiple people with knowledge of US intelligence reports, Kang Wei — Alice Huang’s business partner and, by some reports, husband, who reportedly introduced her to the Nvidia CEO — worked with the same Chinese intelligence agency. But on Sunday evening, Trump still argued for Huang’s return and managed to continue flipping Nvidia’s board in his favor after a weekend’s worth of efforts.
“[I]ndefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible”
If the board maintained any hang-ups about bringing Huang back as CEO, Trump’s power over the executive branch — and the pressure he could exert with it — might have offered a compelling counterargument. The Securities and Exchange Commission had previously opened an investigation into whether Nvidia “misled investors,” according to The Wall Street Journal. But in a post on Truth Social Monday, Trump said that the attorney general “has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.” Reached for comment, the DOJ did not provide an on-the-record response in line with The Verge’s editorial policy.
Key Democrats have indicated that both Nvidia and the Trump administration will be under fire when the new Congress is sworn in — and momentum has built behind GPU export controls, which Huang lobbied extensively to loosen. “Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other NVIDIA executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain.” Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) said in a post on X, adding they’d work “on a bipartisan basis to continue advancing policies that stop the flow of our most powerful technology to the Chinese military and other adversaries.” Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) called the board’s decision “indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible” and pledged to investigate “business malfeasance by NVIDIA and corrupt abuse of power by Howard Lutnick and the Department of Commerce.” He called for “traditional Republicans” to join in the effort.
“The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company’s board still owe Congress answers about the company’s compliance with U.S. export controls,” Sen. Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, said in a statement. “Jensen Huang’s return only increases the urgency of passing bipartisan export control bills into law and making sure NVIDIA does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk.” Rep. Jamie Raskin, the top Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee, said, “A real Congress will find out” whether Trump and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had any alternative incentives for their role in Nvidia’s dealings. Sen. Mark Warner, the top Democrat on the Intelligence Committee, called Trump’s intervention to bring back Huang “outrageous.” Rep. Joaquin Castro (D-TX), a member of the House Intelligence and Foreign Affairs Committees, which are interviewing Huang next week, said he wants to know how Trump stands to benefit from “personally champion[ing] Huang’s return.”
“We need to know why Trump put his thumb on the scale to have Jensen reinstated as CEO”
At closed-door hearings next week, Democrats say they intend to press Huang and the administration further, and several accused the administration of corruption. “We need to know why Trump put his thumb on the scale to have Jensen reinstated as CEO and why his administration failed to restrict the PRC’s access to our most sensitive technology,” Rep. Gregory Meeks, the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said in a statement to The Verge. The board’s decision is “outrageous,” said Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), a member of the House Select Committee on China. “We still don’t know what information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from him, and neither the government nor Nvidia’s own board has completed its investigation,” Krishnamoorthi said in a statement, calling for Huang to testify publicly. “Reinstatement is no substitute for accountability,” Rep. Kathy Castor (D-FL), another China Committee member, said in a statement.
California Attorney General Rob Bonta also intends to continue an investigation into the company. “The reinstatement of Jensen Huang does not change the fact that the American people deserve to know what happened here — whether Nvidia misled investors and the public,” California Department of Justice spokesperson Elissa Perez said in a statement.
Last week, before Huang was reinstated, at least two Republican China hawks opposed the idea. Sen. Josh Hawley (R-MO), a rumored potential presidential candidate, told reporters that he would not like to see Huang return to the top post, but would “defer to the board how they want to run their company. If it were me and a guy who just was caught up in a Chinese honeytrap — I think is the technical term for it — I don’t think that I would impose massive security concerns, not just for the company, but for American national security.”
While it was up to the board to decide whether to bring Huang back, Hawley said, “We in Congress ought to be concerned about the American national security implications and I think we should be looking into that.”
Huang “has a serious credibility problem”
House China Committee Chair John Moolenaar (R-MI) said on stage last week at the Aspen Cyber Summit in Washington, D.C., that Huang “has a serious credibility problem, and I don’t believe he would be as effective now as he was before.” His office did not immediately respond to a request for comment after Huang’s reinstatement.
Sitting beside Moolenaar on stage last week, Rep. Greg Stanton (D-AZ) gave his advice to the board: “Don’t do it. Don’t bring it back. And at the very least, slow your roll, because there are so many questions that have to be answered. What else is out there that Jensen Huang has done to put US national security at risk?” Stanton warned that Congress is just beginning to probe what happened here. “There are going to be very serious investigations with very serious ramifications if in fact it is as it seems,” he said. “The company needs to know this ain’t going away for a while. This is a very serious issue.” After news of Huang’s return, Stanton doubled down on calls for investigations.
Other Republicans — some of whom are leaving Congress — notably disagreed with Trump’s jubilance for Huang’s return. “It’s inexplicable to me why they want this guy back as CEO,” retiring Rep. Don Bacon (R-NE) told CNBC. “To me it’s a failure of character.” Sen. Pete Ricketts (R-NE) wrote on X that Huang’s “behavior does not support reinstatement,” and said he must still testify before Congress. “It also doesn’t absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips,” he wrote. Senate Intelligence Committee Chair Tom Cotton (R-AR) wrote on X that he’s not done investigating. “The controversy with Nvidia and Megaspeed is just the tip of the iceberg, and it’s not resolved because Jensen Huang has his job back,” he said. “Congress has much to investigate and we will pass overwhelmingly bipartisan chip export-control bills, including my Chip Security Act, one way or the other.”
“Congress has much to investigate”
Market analysts have been watching and waiting for a Huang comeback since reports that he had assembled a “war room” of allies to help with his possible reinstatement. Not only did Huang cofound one of the world’s most valuable companies and arguably the most important one in the AI boom, but he has personally helped secure hundreds of billions of dollars in infrastructure funding from US financial institutions. Demand for Nvidia chips constantly outpaces supply, and Huang has had the president’s ear for months. Despite all that, though, Huang’s clout seemed like it wouldn’t help him up until the past 24 hours.
Lindsey Stewart, director of institutional insights at Morningstar, wrote in a note that although investors may consider this a “good move given his history of value creation at the company,” questions remain about the best way to provide corporate governance and oversight at such an important company.
Jacob Bourne, an eMarketer analyst specializing in ad tech and consumer technologies, said in a statement to The Verge that it was difficult to gauge “how much protection Trump’s assurances will ultimately provide Nvidia.” And Heather West, head of Eurasia Group’s geo-technology practice, highlighted the fact that Trump recently met with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum. The timing offers Democrats and China hawks “a great deal to work with in 2027 as they begin scrutiny into the administration, potential corruption, and large tech companies[‘] actions here,” said West.
Analysts at Yorkville Ives wrote in a note Monday that they consider Nvidia a $300 stock with Huang and a $225 stock without him, due to his hard-to-replace influence in the sector. They said an interim structure “could not replicate” his supply relationships with TSMC and others, as well as his place in AI industry dealmaking.
“This is a board that reversed itself because the alternative, a founder-less Nvidia at the start of the Rubin cycle with a CEO search running into next year, was the bigger risk to shareholders, and it chose to pair the reversal with the governance architecture investors will want to see around him,” the Yorkville Ives analysts wrote.
Even Trump admits, though, that a true comeback story can’t be called in a single day. “I’ve seen some pretty good comebacks but I’ll tell you, what you have to have for a comeback, really, is longevity,” he told CNBC. He described the pep talk he gave Huang the night before. “I said, ‘You’ve got to promise me one thing. You’ve got the brain, you’ve got everything going, you’ve got to work hard. And if you work hard nobody can beat you.’”
According to Trump, Huang told him, “I’m going to work harder than I’ve ever worked.”

articles.title: Après une cyberattaque, Nissan coupe un outil vital pour ses concessionnaires
articles.text:
Nissan est à nouveau dans le viseur des cybercriminels. Le constructeur automobile révèle avoir « identifié un accès non autorisé à une partie d’un système de diagnostic de véhicules utilisé par nos concessionnaires dans le monde ». Par précaution, le groupe japonais a coupé une partie de cet outil il y a dix jours, le 13 novembre. Celui-ci est toujours hors service au moment où cet article est écrit.
À lire aussi : C’est l’une des Nissan les plus populaires, mais vous ne verrez sans doute jamais sa version électrique
Des clés impossibles à reprogrammer
Le système Nissan compromis s’intitule CONSULT-III plus. Il est utilisé par les garages Nissan pour intervenir sur l’électronique des voitures et réaliser des réparations. Plusieurs fonctions en ligne ont été désactivées dans le sillage de la cyberattaque, à savoir la programmation des calculateurs de la voiture, le déverrouillage de certains modules et la gestion de l’antidémarrage, le système antivol électronique présent dans toutes les voitures récentes, qui empêche le moteur de démarrer si la clé n’est pas reconnue.
Concrètement, un client qui a perdu ou abîmé sa clé ne peut pas en faire programmer une nouvelle chez son concessionnaire. Selon les informations du New York Times, certaines réparations électroniques peuvent aussi être retardées.
En dépit de l’attaque informatique, les concessions Nissan restent ouvertes et peuvent effectuer la plupart des autres interventions, rassure le groupe nippon. L’entreprise précise que la nouvelle version de l’outil, baptisée CONSULT-IV, n’a pas été touchée par la cyberattaque. Sur son site destiné aux professionnels, Nissan indique que la coupure a été prolongée le temps de terminer l’enquête, sans donner de date de retour à la normale. Pour le moment, on ignore encore qui est derrière l’attaque, depuis quand les pirates avaient accès au système et si des données de clients ont été volées durant l’opération.
À lire aussi : Nissan va avoir un système de conduite autonome similaire à Tesla
Nissan, une cible récurrente pour les pirates
Ce n’est pas la première fois que Nissan se retrouve dans le viseur des hackers. En 2017, le fabricant automobile s’est déjà retrouvé dans le viseur du ransomware WannaCry. Plus récemment, c’est le gang Red Hat qui a piraté l’un des prestataires de Nissan, compromettant les données de plus de 20 000 clients.
