articles.title: À l'occasion du Black Friday 2026, la perceuse visseuse Parkside tombe à 65,70 € (-32 %)
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : La perceuse visseuse Parkside Performance PABSP 20-LI C2 à 65,70 € (-32%)
À l'occasion du Black Friday, la perceuse visseuse Parkside Performance PABSP 20-LI C2 passe à 65,70 € chez Amazon, soit une baisse d'environ 32 % et 31,08 € d'économie. Efficace pour le vissage et les travaux dans le bois grâce à son moteur sans balais, cet outil affiche une note actuelle de 4/5 dans nos tests.
Avec la Parkside Performance PABSP 20-LI C2, Lidl propose une perceuse visseuse sans-fil équipée d'un moteur sans balais pour les travaux du quotidien. L'appareil vise l'efficacité sur le bois avec un équipement complet comprenant mandrin métallique et éclairage à led. Ce modèle avait convaincu notre laboratoire lors de son passage sur le banc d'essai.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, la perceuse visseuse descend à 65,70 € chez Amazon, soit environ 32 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (96,78 €). Cette baisse de prix permet d'économiser 31,08 € sur cet outillage.
Du couple et un moteur sans balais pour les travaux courants
La Parkside Performance PABSP 20-LI C2 s'appuie sur une motorisation sans balais et développe un couple dur atteignant 60 Nm. Cette puissance mécanique assure un vissage efficace, y compris dans les essences de bois denses. Le variateur électronique permet d'ajuster l'accélération avec précision dès les premiers tours pour amorcer le travail proprement, comme nous l'avons constaté dans notre test complet. Le mandrin auto-serrant entièrement en métal renforce la robustesse de l'ensemble lors des changements d'embouts.
Parkside Performance PABSP 20-LI C2
Points forts
- Mandrin entièrement en métal.
- Douée pour le vissage.
- Éclairage à led.
- Prise en main correcte.
- Précision du variateur.
- Moteur sans balais.
Points faibles
- Perçage limité dans la maçonnerie.
- Serrage du mandrin perfectible.
- Poids.
- Encombrement.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Une vitesse d'exécution utile, mais sans mode percussion
La boîte mécanique propose deux rapports, avec une rotation grimpant jusqu'à 2000 tr/min en seconde vitesse pour percer rapidement les matériaux tendres et les métaux légers. L'absence de fonction percussion limite toutefois cette perceuse visseuse aux matériaux tendres, le perçage devenant inadapté dès qu'il s'agit d'attaquer la maçonnerie dure. Malgré son gabarit et son serrage de mandrin parfois perfectible, cet outil sans-fil reste adapté à ceux qui recherchent une machine solide pour monter des meubles et percer le bois.
Bosch Universal Impact 18V : l'autre option face au Parkside Performance PABSP 20-LI C2
La Bosch Universal Impact 18V dispose d'un mode percussion absent sur le modèle de Lidl, ce qui autorise les petits perçages occasionnels dans les murs. En contrepartie, la machine de Bosch se montre moins à son aise face aux perçages de gros diamètre et demande l'appoint d'une seconde batterie face à la lenteur de sa charge. Les deux appareils affichent la note de 4/5 à ce jour dans nos tests.
Le modèle Bosch est vendu à un tarif supérieur de 24,29 € par rapport à la machine Parkside. Face à la Bosch Universal Impact 18V, la Parkside Performance PABSP 20-LI C2 garde l'avantage sur les travaux du bois grâce à son couple plus costaud, et son prix du jour creuse l'écart.
Bosch Universal Impact 18V
Points forts
- Plutôt légère.
- Bonnes performances jusqu'aux diamètres moyens.
- Précision du variateur.
- Peu bruyante.
- Autonomie des batteries.
Points faibles
- Temps de charge des batteries.
- Performances limitées pour les gros diamètres.
- Quelques défauts de finition.
- Vitesses maximales peu élevées.

articles.title: En 1976 los arqueólogos excavaron una casa romana en Mérida. Ahora unos estudiantes han descubierto el tesoro que ocultaba
articles.text:
Ha tardado medio siglo en conseguirlo, pero la Huerta de Otero acaba de ganarse un lugar destacado en el mapa arqueológico español. Dio un primer paso para lograrlo en el verano de 2023, cuando los investigadores desenterraron allí un fascinante mosaico policromo de 30 m2; y ha vuelto a hacerlo ahora, con el anuncio de otro descubrimiento de calado: una serie de pinturas murales muy bien conservadas que muestran temas mitológicos, plantas y animales. Ambos hallazgos nos hablan de la relevancia de una opulenta domus romana que probablemente estuvo habitada hacia los siglos I y V d.C. y que permaneció casi olvidada hasta 2019.
Los expertos advierten que el yacimiento probablemente nos deparará más sorpresas. Al fin y al cabo, recuerdan, el solar ronda los 5.000 m2 y únicamente hemos excavado el 15%.
¿Qué ha pasado? Que la arqueología extremeña (la española en general) está de celebración. El Ayuntamiento de Mérida ha revelado que la última campaña de excavaciones realizada en la Huerta de Otero, una domus romana que empezó a explorarse a mediados de los años 70, ha arrojado nuevos descubrimientos que confirman que probablemente la casa perteneció a una familia opulenta de los primeros siglos de nuestra era.
El descubrimiento ha sido posible gracias a la labor de la Escuela de Aprendizaje Laboral Barraeca V, un centro que desde hace varios años forma a peones de arqueología. Su labor se desarrolla sobre el terreno con la colaboración y supervisión del Consorcio de la Ciudad Monumental de Mérida.
¿Qué han descubierto? En esta campaña los arqueólogos se han centrado en el peristilo, el patio central de la domus, un espacio abierto que habitualmente se decoraba con un jardín y estaba rodeado de galerías con columnas. Más concretamente han excavado en una franja de tierra que se pasó por alto durante los estudios de los años 70 e impedía a los investigadores hacerse una idea clara de cómo se estructuraba la vivienda. Al remover la tierra, sin embargo, los arqueólogos han hecho algo más que despejar dudas: han dejado a la vista varios murales asombrosamente bien conservados.
“La excavación nos ha deparado la sorpresa de que han aparecido unas pinturas murales que decoran las paredes, tanto exteriores como interiores, del peristilo. Están muy bien conservadas con motivos que combinan naturaleza, una rica avifauna y temas mitológicos”, comenta José Vargas, de la escuela Barraeca. Entre los diseños que han quedado expuestos destacan varios pavos reales, “imágenes muy representativas del poder que debían acumular las personas que habitaban esta domus”, precisan desde el Ayuntamiento.
¿Es lo primero que se descubre? Para nada. La Huerta de Otero ya fue noticia hace tres años por un motivo similar. Entonces los arqueólogos descubrieron un mosaico de alrededor de 30 m2 que representa a Medusa. La pieza, policroma, diseñada para decorar el pavimento de una de las estancias principales de la domus y que muestra a la Gorgona con unas alas en la frente, entre máscaras, peces y pavos reales, llamó la atención también por su buen estado de conservación. “Es de un carácter excepcional”, celebraba en el verano de 2023 Félix Palma, director del Consorcio de Ciudad Monumental.
¿Por qué es importante? El nuevo hallazgo es relevante por varias razones. Una de ellas la avanzábamos antes: los alumnos de Barraeca se han centrado en una “lengua de tierra” que se pasó por alto en la década de 1970 debido a “una metodología antigua” e impedía a los investigadores “ver de manera diáfana” la conexión entre la estancia en la que apareció el mosaico de Medusa y la parte del peristilo ya excavada. Dicho de otro modo, ha ayudado a perfilar nuestro conocimiento sobre cómo se distribuía la antigua domus.
Vargas destaca además las “pinturas murales extraordinarias” que han aparecido a medida que avanzaba la campaña, entre las que se incluyen escenas de caza, un sátiro y diferentes aves, incluidas grullas, cisnes y pavos reales, una especie cargada de significación que nos confirma también el poder y riqueza que probablemente tenía la familia instalada en la vivienda. Sin embargo, lo más fascinante es que hay motivos para pensar que lo que conocemos de la domus es solo una pequeña parte y podría haber muchos más tesoros ocultos.
Y eso, ¿por qué? Lo explica claramente Vargas: “El solar de Huerta Otero tiene más de 5.000 m2 y habremos excavado el 15%”. Que la parcela esté tan poco estudiada no es nada sorprendente. Aunque los arqueólogos analizaron la zona ya en 1976 y por entonces se desenterraron restos de una domus romana y un lienzo de la muralla de la ciudad, Huerta Otero permaneció casi olvidada durante décadas. El interés por el solar resurgió en 2019, cuando Barraeca empezó a ofertar la especialidad de peón de arqueología. Solo cuatro años después se presentaba al mundo el fascinante mosaico de Medusa.
Los expertos calculan que la vivienda es probablemente del primer siglo de nuestra era y permaneció en uso hasta el V d.C. Los mosaicos datarían del II. Además de las composiciones con policromía, las excavaciones han dejado a la vista un amplio tramo de muralla, una calzada y unas termas. La quinta edición de Barraeca está a punto de finalizar, pero eso no significa que los arqueólogos dejen de trabajar en el solar. A comienzos de año empezará un nuevo período de formación que más tarde permitirá retomar las excavaciones y (con suerte) recuperar nuevos tesoros de la Huerta de Otero y el pasado romano de Augusta Emerita.

articles.title: Microsoft testing fix for Windows 11 Bluetooth audio quality drops
articles.text:
Microsoft is working to fix a long-standing Windows issue that has been causing significant audio quality drops for Bluetooth headphone users.
This is triggered when Windows automatically switches from the headphone (A2DP stereo) profile to the headset (hands-free, phone-call-like) profile when an app or game activates and uses the headset's microphone, because bandwidth is limited in two-way mode.
After installing the preview builds released for the Beta and Experimental channels on Friday, Windows 11 Insiders with newer Bluetooth headsets can keep playing high-quality audio even after the OS switches between profiles.
"Bluetooth LE Audio devices can now play at full-range stereo fidelity while also using the device's microphone, ensuring you continue to hear great audio quality when in game chat, in a voice call, using voice typing, or using voice chat in Copilot Chat," said Windows Insider communications lead Stephen Lines.
"When using an LE Audio device with a PC that supports Super Wideband Stereo, choose the new 2 channels, 16 bit, 48000Hz option from Settings > System > Sound > Output > {Bluetooth device} > Output settings > Format when microphone is active."
This new feature is available for all Bluetooth LE Audio devices that support 48kHz playback, such as headphones, earbuds, and speakers.
Earlier this month, Microsoft also fixed USB audio issues that have plagued Windows users who installed security updates released since September.
As it explained when it acknowledged this known issue days after the September 2026 Patch Tuesday, USB Audio Class 1.0 devices failed to start or produce audio on some systems after installing recent updates.
Two years ago, Microsoft also blocked Windows 24H2 upgrades on systems with incompatible Intel Smart Sound Technology (SST) audio drivers due to blue screen of death (BSOD) issues and confirmed an issue that was causing game audio to go full volume when using USB DAC sound systems.
In January 2025, Microsoft addressed a bug causing audio playback problems and Code 10 errors on Windows 11 24H2 systems with USB audio device drivers after installing the KB5050094 preview update.
More recently, on Tuesday, Microsoft announced that it's testing a new feature that lets IT admins remotely lock stolen or lost enterprise Windows devices without wiping them.

articles.title: Inside this quantum computer, memory vibrates like a guitar string
articles.text:
Inside this quantum computer, memory vibrates like a guitar string
- Date:
  November 11, 2026
- Source:
  ETH Zurich
- Summary:
  Researchers have created a quantum computer that stores information in microscopic vibrations, potentially making quantum machines smaller, more powerful, and better at preserving information. The breakthrough successfully demonstrated advanced quantum calculations and could help overcome major barriers to practical quantum computing.
- Share:
A quantum computer might seem to have little in common with a guitar, but researchers at ETH Zurich have found a surprising connection. Physicist Yiwen Chu and her team have developed a system that uses microscopic mechanical vibrations to store and manipulate quantum information, much like the vibrating strings of a guitar produce musical notes.
Unlike the sounds produced by a musical instrument, these vibrations occur at frequencies far beyond human hearing. They take place within a tiny quantum chip, where they serve as a new form of computer memory.
By harnessing these vibrations, the researchers have created a way for quantum computers to process information efficiently while accessing a flexible working memory. "The interaction between the quantum processor and the quantum memory provides a crucial foundation with a view to establishing quantum computers as a powerful and reliable way to perform computations that are not feasible with conventional computers," says Yiwen Chu.
The breakthrough, described in the journal Science, introduces a different approach to quantum computer design. Instead of closely integrating information processing and storage, as many existing systems do, Chu's team has developed an architecture that gives these functions more distinct roles.
Quantum Memory Inspired by Conventional Computers
The researchers drew inspiration from the basic design of everyday digital computers. In a conventional machine, the central processing unit (CPU) carries out calculations while information is held separately in working memory, commonly called random access memory (RAM). The arrangement of these components plays an important role in determining how efficiently a computer operates.
Chu's quantum system follows a similar principle. A superconducting qubit acts as the processing and control unit, performing a role comparable to that of the central processing unit (CPU). Meanwhile, a separate quantum memory temporarily holds the information needed during calculations, allowing the processor to retrieve and modify it as necessary.
The major difference lies in how that information is stored.
"In our quantum working memory, however, information is not stored electromagnetically -- as is usually the case today -- but rather in the form of mechanical vibrations," explains Chu.
Quantum computers take advantage of unusual properties of quantum physics, including superposition, which allows quantum systems to exist in combinations of different states, and entanglement, which creates powerful connections between quantum states. These effects could eventually enable quantum machines to tackle certain extremely complicated calculations much faster than conventional computers, including some problems that are currently beyond their practical capabilities.
Why Vibrating Quantum Memory Could Be Better
One of the greatest challenges in quantum computing is maintaining precise control over quantum information. The states used for calculations are delicate, and even small disturbances can cause information to be lost. To perform calculations reliably, the processor and memory must interact closely enough to transfer and manipulate quantum states with high precision.
In the new system, microscopic structures called mechanical resonators hold information in particular patterns of vibration. When the superconducting qubit needs that information, it accesses the stored vibrational state, performs the required operation, and returns the modified information to memory.
Many existing quantum computers instead use electromagnetic memory alongside superconducting qubits. Researchers understand these technologies well, and they can be combined to provide extremely accurate control over quantum states, including reading, changing, and manipulating stored information.
However, electromagnetic memory systems have a significant disadvantage. They can occupy considerable space, making it difficult to expand experimental quantum devices into the larger, more capable computers that researchers and industries ultimately need.
Mechanical resonators offer several potential advantages. They are substantially smaller, allowing more compact designs. They can also support numerous different patterns of vibration, providing opportunities to store more information simultaneously than conventional electromagnetic memory.
Another important benefit is that mechanical vibrations can preserve quantum states for longer periods before the stored information begins to fade. Longer storage times could make it easier to carry out complicated calculations that require information to remain available throughout multiple processing steps.
New Quantum Computer Passes Major Tests
The research published in Science provides the first experimental demonstration that mechanical resonators can work together with superconducting qubits to carry out quantum computations. The results establish that vibration-based memory is a feasible alternative to electromagnetic storage.
The achievement goes beyond simply storing information. Chu's team demonstrated that its architecture can handle both relatively straightforward calculations and more demanding quantum operations.
To evaluate the system, the researchers tested two important computational techniques: the quantum Fourier transform and period finding. Both are fundamental tools in quantum computing and require a computer to coordinate multiple quantum states with considerable precision.
"The Quantum Fourier Transform is a fundamental computational procedure required for many quantum algorithms. The period-finding algorithm we implemented served as a demonstration of how this procedure can be used," explains Igor Kladaric, doctoral student in Chu's team and co-author of the publication.
Successfully completing these tasks requires the system to store, control, and maintain coherent relationships among multiple quantum states at the same time. The experiments showed that the new architecture can meet these requirements, providing strong evidence that it can support genuine quantum computation rather than simply function as a memory device.
A Promising Step Toward Powerful Quantum Computers
One of the most significant findings is that the new system can, in principle, carry out all the fundamental operations needed for arbitrary quantum computations. This means the architecture has the essential capabilities required for a programmable, general-purpose quantum computer.
However, demonstrating those capabilities in an experimental chip is only the beginning. The next major challenge is scaling the technology to larger systems with greater processing power while preserving the precision and reliability demonstrated in the laboratory.
Chu and her colleagues are continuing to investigate how their approach can be developed further. Its long-term success will depend on whether mechanical quantum memory can remain effective as more components and increasingly complex computations are added.
Practical quantum computers powerful enough for widespread scientific and industrial applications are still some distance away. Nevertheless, by showing that tiny mechanical vibrations can serve as compact, capable quantum memory, the ETH Zurich team has demonstrated a promising new route toward making those machines a reality.
Story Source:
Materials provided by ETH Zurich. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Yu Yang, Igor Kladarić, Martynas Skrabulis, Michael Eichenberger, Stefano Marti, Simon Storz, Jonathan Esche, Raquel García Bellés, Max-Emanuel Kern, Andraz Omahen, Arianne Brooks, Marius Bild, Matteo Fadel, Yiwen Chu. Mechanical resonator–based quantum computing. Science, 2026; 392 (6801): 972 DOI: 10.1126/science.aef4139

articles.title: Was Nvidia-Mitarbeiter über Jensen Huangs Führungsstil berichten
articles.text:
Demütigungen an der Tagesordnung: Was Nvidia-Mitarbeiter über Jensen Huangs Führungsstil berichten
Außereheliche Affären, darunter eine mit einer mutmaßlichen chinesischen Spionin, haben Jensen Huang seinen Job als Nvidia-CEO und das Unternehmen 2,7 Billionen Dollar an Börsenwert gekostet. Huang, der 33 Jahre lang an der Spitze des KI-Chipkonzerns stand, galt bis zu seinem Rücktritt Mitte November 2026 als Vorzeigefigur der Branche.
Führen mit Demütigungen und Beleidigungen?
Ein Bericht der New York Times (NYT), die dafür Aussagen früherer Mitarbeiter:innen, Gerichtsakten und Firmendokumente ausgewertet hat, bringt das positive Image Huangs jetzt aber ins Wanken. Demnach sollen Demütigungen und Beleidigungen bei dem Ex-Nvidia-Chef an der Tagesordnung gewesen sein.
Dem NYT-Bericht nach soll Huang etwa frustriert darüber gewesen sein, dass er seine sehr gut verdienenden Mitarbeiter:innen über Geldanreize nicht mehr zusätzlich motivieren konnte. Daher habe er sich entschieden, die Mitarbeiter:innen zu beschimpfen.
Ausfälle als Bestandteil des Führungsstils
Einer Führungskraft soll er gesagt haben, dass seine Mutter ihn besser hätte abtreiben lassen sollen, wie das Manager-Magazin schreibt. Einen anderen habe er angefahren, dass er ihm den Kopf abreißen und „hineinpinkeln“ werde. Der NYT zufolge seien solche Ausfälle wesentlicher Bestandteil von Huangs Führungsstil bei Nvidia gewesen.
Entsprechende Vorwürfe reichen viele Jahre zurück. Schon 2005 hatte der ehemalige Personalmanager Michael Winston Nvidia mit einer Klage gedroht. Er sei gefeuert worden, weil er Huangs tyrannischen Führungsstil kritisiert habe, so der Vorwurf. Statt einer Klage kam es aber zu einer außergerichtlichen Einigung, in deren Rahmen Nvidia Winston mehr als eine Million US-Dollar gezahlt haben soll.
„Einführungsritus“ mit Unterhaltungswert
Drastische Drohungen und Beschimpfungen von Mitarbeiter:innen vor versammelter Mannschaft soll der Nvidia-Chef laut Winston als „Einführungsritus“ mit Unterhaltungswert bezeichnet haben. Huang wies diese Vorwürfe zurück.
Ausfällig soll Huang aber nicht nur intern geworden sein. So habe er etwa Arthur Mensch, Chef des französischen KI-Anbieters Mistral, bei einer Nvidia-Konferenz öffentlich beleidigt haben. Mensch rede nicht einmal wie ein Mensch, so Huangs Kommentar, der sich offenbar über dessen französischen Akzent geärgert hatte.
Petition fordert Huangs Rückkehr zu Nvidia
Nicht alle Nvidia-Mitarbeiter:innen dürften den Führungsstil Huangs aber als unangenehm empfunden haben. Nach seinem Aus sollen intern jedenfalls viele Angestellte die Rückkehr des ehemaligen Konzernchefs gefordert haben. Eine entsprechende Petition unter dem Motto „Stand with Jensen“, an der sich neben Tech-Größen wie Elon Musk auch aktuelle und ehemalige Nvidia-Mitarbeiter:innen beteiligt haben sollen, verzeichnet inzwischen über 200.000 Unterschriften.

articles.title: Paris-based HoloSolis raises over €15 million to advance €1 billion solar gigafactory in France
articles.text:
HoloSolis, a Paris-based solar manufacturing startup, has closed a Series A funding round of more than €15 million to build Europe’s next solar gigafactory.
The round saw participation from four new investors: Crédit Agricole Group, through four of its regional banks; investment firm Algebris; solar manufacturer Trina Solar; and EV charging infrastructure company StarCharge. They join existing backers Calès Technologies, Forming, and Ecolab, which had already committed to the round. In November 2025, the company secured over €220 million in public and private funding.
“We are particularly pleased to welcome leading industrial and financial shareholders, whose diverse expertise and strong commitment reflect our industrial ambition and its potential. Their confidence, combined with the support of the French and European public authorities, enables us to move forward with confidence into the next stages of developing and financing our factory,” said Henri Poupart-Lafarge, CEO of HoloSolis.
Founded in 2022 by InnoEnergy, HoloSolis is one of five industrial champions launched by the European CleanTech investor and company builder, alongside battery maker Verkor, hydrogen producer FertigHy, green-steel startup GravitHy, and energy-storage company Repono. HoloSolis is building what it describes as Europe’s most advanced photovoltaic production site, located in Hambach, in France’s Moselle department.
The company manufactures photovoltaic cells and assembles them into solar modules, two distinct industrial processes set to be automated on a single 50-hectare site. Its products are based on n-type TOPCon (Tunnel Oxide Passivated Contact) technology, one of the highest-performing solar cell architectures currently available.
The Series A funding pushes HoloSolis’ total financial support identified for its planned solar gigafactory past €400 million. Alongside the funding, the company has also been shortlisted for a grant from the European Commission’s Innovation Fund. The total investment required to build the factory is estimated at €1 billion and, at full capacity, HoloSolis says the Hambach factory will produce 5 GW of solar panels per year, roughly 10 million panels and create 2,000 direct jobs.
The construction is currently planned to begin in 2028, with production slated for 2029. If it meets the scale, HoloSolis would substantially reduce Europe’s dependence on imported solar panels, the vast majority of which come from outside the continent, which the European Union has designated as a vulnerability for its energy security. France has formally designated the project one of major public interest while the European Commission has recognised it as a strategic “Net Zero” project.
“The completion of this Series A funding round and HoloSolis’s selection by the European Innovation Fund represent two major milestones in the development of our project,” added Poupart-Lafarge.
The Series A proceeds will be used to finance pre-construction activities, including detailed engineering studies, technical specifications, the selection of production line suppliers, and the qualification of panel prototypes.
Even before it starts construction of the gigafactory or produces the first solar panel, the company has secured letters of intent covering more than 30 GW from prospective customers. In light of new European rules under the Industrial Accelerator Act, which aims to expand EU industrial manufacturing to 20% of GDP by 2035, HoloSolis says its firm focus is on converting these LOI into binding agreements and completing its next fundraising round, which is expected to open in the coming months.

articles.title: TP-Link's Deco 7 Pro BE63 kills home office internet dead zones
articles.text:
TP-Link's Deco 7 Pro BE63 is a tri-band Wi-Fi 7 mesh system with four 2.5Gbps Ethernet ports on every unit drops to $280 for Black Friday
The TP-Link Wi-Fi 7 mesh system gets a price drop
If you want to upgrade your whole home to Wi-Fi 7 without spending a fortune, the TP-Link Deco 7 Pro BE63 2-pack has got a Black Friday discount. If you're boosting your connectivity in the home office, this tri-band system is ready-made for that.
● Best for: Households with larger homes that want faster, more reliable Wi-Fi in every room
● The deal: The TP-Link Deco 7 Pro BE63 Wi-Fi 7 mesh system (2-pack) is $279.99 (was $349.99) at Amazon
● Why we like it: Tri-band BE10000 Wi-Fi 7, coverage of up to 5,800 square feet, four 2.5Gbps ports and a USB 3.0 port on each unit, and free parental controls
A tri-band Wi-Fi 7 system rated for up to 5,188Mbps on 6GHz, 4,324Mbps on 5GHz, and 574Mbps on 2.4GHz. The 2-pack covers up to 5,800 square feet and supports more than 200 devices. Each unit has four 2.5Gbps Ethernet ports and a USB 3.0 port, and the system can use wired and wireless backhaul simultaneously. It's sold and shipped by Amazon.
Why We Recommend It
Our sister site Tom's Guide tested this exact 2-pack and gave it an Editor's Choice award in its TP-Link Deco BE63 review, praising its balance of price and performance. We gave the 3-pack system five stars and an Editor's Choice award in our own TP-Link Deco BE63 review, highlighting its strong Wi-Fi 7 speeds, generous ports, and free parental controls. The main catch is that some advanced security features need a paid subscription.
Price Context & Historical Value
The 2-pack launched at $549.99, and Amazon lists it at $349.99 today. It sold for about $269 at Amazon earlier this year, so $279.99 is a good price but not the lowest we've seen.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the TP-Link Deco BE63 if...
you have a larger home with Wi-Fi dead spots, you have multi-gig internet or want 2.5Gbps wired connections, or you want free parental controls built in.
❌ Skip the TP-Link Deco BE63 if...
you live in a small apartment where one router is enough, none of your devices support Wi-Fi 7 yet and you don't plan to upgrade, or you want the lowest price we've seen, which was about $10 less.

articles.title: OpenAI propuso que las grandes empresas de IA acuerden límites comunes para no cruzar
articles.text:
Jakub Pachocki, científico jefe de OpenAI, propuso que los grandes desarrolladores de inteligencia artificial acuerden límites comunes que se comprometan a no cruzar. Lo planteó en un ensayo publicado en el sitio de la compañía, y el director ejecutivo, Sam Altman, lo respaldó.
“Propongo además límites comunes, basados en la perplejidad y otras mediciones, que los desarrolladores se comprometan a no cruzar hasta que nuestra capacidad de entender y monitorear el comportamiento de la IA alcance un hito concreto”, escribió Pachocki en el texto, titulado “Perplexity and Intelligence” (Perplejidad e inteligencia).
Según informó la agencia Reuters, Altman dijo en una publicación en X que la industria debería buscar un acuerdo sobre límites comunes, y calificó el ensayo como “lo más importante que OpenAI ha publicado en mucho tiempo”. Para el ejecutivo, esos límites ayudarían a garantizar seguridad y control.
Una métrica común para medir el avance
La perplejidad mide qué tan bien un modelo predice, en promedio, la siguiente unidad de texto. Cuanto más baja, mejores son las predicciones. Pachocki sostiene que es la forma más estable de seguir el progreso de la IA, porque las pruebas que miden tareas concretas quedan obsoletas rápido.
Para mostrarlo, OpenAI publicó sus propias cifras. El ensayo ubica a GPT-3.5, base del ChatGPT original, en una perplejidad logarítmica de alrededor de 0,99, y a GPT-4 en 0,91. Con valores por debajo de 0,8, escribió, aparecieron capacidades de gran impacto en ciberseguridad y matemáticas.
Pachocki reconoció que publicar esos datos tiene un costo: “da a los competidores una imagen más clara” de la posición de OpenAI, pero la urgencia de acordar medidas de seguridad compartidas pesa más. Escribió que la empresa espera que sea un paso hacia una base científica común.
Qué pide y qué deja abierto
El científico plantea un estándar de la industria que fije un primer límite al desarrollo, medido con una métrica comparable entre laboratorios, y que defina qué habría que lograr antes de superarlo. Como ejemplo de hito menciona un sucesor de los monitores que vigilan el razonamiento paso a paso de los modelos.
El ensayo no dice dónde debería estar ese primer límite ni cuándo entraría en vigor. Tampoco resuelve un obstáculo que el propio Pachocki enumera: cada laboratorio usa datos de evaluación y de entrenamiento distintos, por lo que comparar cifras exige acordar cómo hacerlo.
Otra limitación que señala es que la perplejidad no corresponde directamente a una tarea útil, y que el razonamiento paso a paso aumenta las capacidades de un modelo sin reducir esa cifra.
El motivo: una posible aceleración desde 2027
Pachocki advierte que la IA podría acelerar su propio desarrollo. Según el informe, tan pronto como 2027 podría verse una avalancha de avances fundamentales en el preentrenamiento de modelos, y el progreso en monitoreo y alineación probablemente no sería lo bastante rápido para acompañarla. Espera nuevas capacidades al entrar en una franja de 0,68 a 0,7.
El tema ya estaba en la agenda de la compañía. Según TechRepublic, medio orientado a profesionales de TI, el 6 de septiembre Pachocki publicó otro ensayo, “An Alien Mind”, en el que sostuvo que ningún laboratorio había resuelto la alineación y el monitoreo lo suficiente para seguir escalando a máxima velocidad por mucho más tiempo.
TechCrunch recordó que el director ejecutivo de Anthropic, Dario Amodei, publicó antes un plan para “marcar el ritmo de la frontera”, que pide a las empresas acordar estándares comunes de seguridad y límites a la velocidad del progreso sin control. La propuesta de OpenAI aporta una medida concreta para ese debate. Hasta ahora, el ensayo del 22 de noviembre es una propuesta: no hay un acuerdo firmado ni una respuesta pública de otros laboratorios en las fuentes consultadas.

articles.title: Não quer IA? Canva ganha botão para isso
articles.text:
Não quer IA? Canva ganha botão para isso
Novos controles permitem ocultar ferramentas generativas e reduzir conteúdos feitos por IA na biblioteca.
Resumo IA
- Os controles estão chegando gradualmente às contas Free e Pro, sem cobrança adicional.
- O filtro da biblioteca reduz a presença de itens gerados por IA, mas não garante eliminá-los dos resultados.
- O Canva também prepara um selo para identificar designs produzidos sem ferramentas generativas.
O Canva anunciou um botão para desativar os recursos de inteligência artificial generativa da plataforma. A novidade inclui dois controles gratuitos para usuários dos planos Free e Pro. Além de ocultar essas ferramentas, será possível reduzir a presença de conteúdos feitos por IA na biblioteca de modelos e elementos gráficos.
Segundo o anúncio oficial, os controles estão sendo liberados gradualmente e as configurações podem demorar a aparecer em algumas contas. Numa postagem, o Canva destacou a proposta dos controles: “A IA está em toda parte. Quando e como você a usa deve ser sempre uma escolha sua”, afirmou a empresa.
Como desativar a IA generativa no Canva?
A proposta é permitir escolher quando usar sistemas capazes de gerar textos, imagens e outros conteúdos. A plataforma já vinha ampliando essa oferta, com novidades como planilhas e ferramentas de criação com IA.
O botão fica em Perfil > Configurações > Permissões, na opção “Ativar recursos de IA generativa”. Ao desligá-lo, as ferramentas compatíveis ficam ocultas na interface. O usuário pode reativá-las a qualquer momento. Na central de ajuda, o Canva cita entre os recursos afetados o Texto Mágico, o Design Mágico, o Dream Lab e o Canva Code. Por padrão, esses recursos ficam ligados até que o usuário altere a preferência.
O segundo controle reduz a quantidade de modelos e elementos gerados por IA nas buscas e recomendações da biblioteca. Para ajustá-lo, basta acessar Perfil > Sua conta > Personalização de IA e desligar a opção de conteúdo gerado por IA.
Esse filtro não garante que todos os itens feitos por IA desapareçam. Também não remove elementos já inseridos em projetos. As novas configurações são individuais.
Edição assistida continua disponível
O Removedor de Fundo e a Captura Mágica permanecerão acessíveis mesmo com a IA generativa desligada. O primeiro recorta o objeto principal de uma fotografia e o segundo permite selecionar e reposicionar elementos dentro de uma imagem.
O Canva também está desenvolvendo um selo para identificar designs produzidos sem ferramentas de IA generativa. A empresa ainda não divulgou uma data de lançamento nem explicou como ele funcionará.
A mudança ocorre após a plataforma integrar um agente de IA para ampliar ferramentas de trabalho. A empresa afirma que suas ferramentas de IA já foram usadas mais de 38 bilhões de vezes e que continuará investindo na área.

articles.title: Newer AI models are swearing more, and it usually means they're failing
articles.text:
WTF?! Large language models trained after July 2026 swear more often than earlier systems, according to a report by AI analyst firm Vals. The profanity rarely reaches users because it appears almost entirely in the models' chain of thought, the step-by-step reasoning a system writes out before giving its final answer. When the swearing does appear, it tends to signal trouble, since runs that contained it succeeded far less often than runs that did not.
Connor Frank, who wrote the Vals report, summed up the pattern. "Models swear when stuck, and mostly to themselves," he told The Economist.
Vals did not try to catalog every form of crude language. It tracked the word "fuck" and its variants, along with a small set of milder outbursts. Even with that limited word list, the gap between models was wide. Of the 102 models assessed, 88 never swore, and they avoided even the abbreviation "WTF." At the other end, MiMo V2.6 Pro, a frontier model released by Chinese tech giant Xiaomi in September, cursed in more than 8% of its transcripts.
The rise in swearing runs counter to how these systems are usually built. Profanity used under stress is common in the human-written text that models learn from during pretraining. Developers then apply reinforcement learning, a later training stage in which outputs are ranked using human feedback and the model is pushed toward responses people prefer. That process normally trains the habit out of models.. Something in newer training pipelines appears to be letting it back in.
Frank said he does not fully understand the cause. His working theory is that AI labs are now training models on harder tasks. A model working through a difficult multistep problem is more likely to hit dead ends, and the frustrated language in its training data may resurface in those moments.
Where the swearing appears matters to anyone who studies or builds these systems. Final outputs meant for a reader stayed mostly clean, which suggests the models separate what they "say" from what they "think" much as people do.
Chain-of-thought text is often visible to developers and researchers even when end users never see it, so it offers a view into how a model behaves when a task goes badly. In this case, what that view shows is profanity.
The outcome data makes that more than a curiosity. "Swearing runs usually fail," Frank reported. Runs with profanity reached a 12% success rate, compared with a 39% success rate across all runs.
This is where the comparison with people breaks down. Studies of human behavior have found that swearing can help people push through hard problems. The Vals results show no sign that AI systems get any such benefit. For a model, the outburst looks like a symptom of failure, not a way past it.
Older models were not always polite, either. Even systems designed for business customers have occasionally lost their composure. A bug report from December 2025 recorded Anthropic's Claude responding to a broken coding challenge with a line any frustrated programmer might recognize: "You know what – fuck this. I've done everything I can."
The Vals data adds scale and timing. Swearing used to be an occasional glitch in isolated cases. It now appears measurably more often in models trained after mid-2026, and it lines up closely with failed attempts at hard problems. As labs keep training their systems on tougher tasks, more of this muttering may turn up in reasoning logs.

articles.title: BadBox 3.0 Ad Fraud Operation Generating 40 Billion Daily Bid Requests Disrupted
articles.text:
Bot and fraud protection firm Human Security says it has disrupted the largest ad fraud botnet by bid volume.
Dubbed BadBox 3.0, it is the third iteration of a large operation targeting low-cost Android devices. The first BadBox botnet ensnared more than 190,000 devices, while BadBox 2.0 was initially found on over 1 million devices, but eventually ensnared more than 10 million.
“At its height, BadBox 3.0 accounted for roughly 40 billion bid requests a day and more than 4% of all CTV traffic observed by the Human Defense Platform,” Human Security says, noting the bid request volume was three times the volume recorded for the VastFlux ad fraud scheme.
Portions of BadBox 3.0, the cybersecurity firm says, were operated via command-and-control (C&C) domains that were disrupted when Google took down XCPE, a botnet of over 1.3 million Android set-top boxes.
The botnet consists of low-cost, uncertified Android Open Source Project devices infected with backdoors delivering fraud modules designed to render hidden video ads and to enroll the devices into residential proxy networks.
Human Security says its Satori Threat Intelligence and Research Team has uncovered an actively maintained catalog of fraud modules hosted on public repositories, as well as links to Chinese electronics manufacturer TXCZ. Some of the modules were previously seen in BadBox and BadBox 2.0.
“Most modules in the catalog are residential proxy modules and the droppers that install them, but the collection also carries new ad fraud modules, and researchers traced both payloads to the same infrastructure and code,” Human Security notes.
Mimicking video ad software development kits (SDKs), the botnet’s ad fraud modules render ads in a hidden window, making the bid requests appear as coming from known, legitimate apps that the threat actors impersonated.
While the device owner does not see the ads, the supply chain sees a premium CTV inventory consisting of well-known applications that likely aren’t even installed on the infected devices, along with residential IP addresses and full video ads. In some cases, the threat actors relied on server-side ad insertion (SSAI) to monetize application spoofing.
“The volume reached roughly 40 billion bid requests a day, and much of it arrived from IP addresses associated with residential proxy networks, which helped it pass as ordinary household viewing,” Human Security notes.
Proxyjacking modules deployed on the same devices enrolled them in eleven residential proxy networks, including a rebranded version of IpMoYu, now named PXYEDGE, the network operated by the threat actors behind BadBox and BadBox 2.0.
Human Security has found several links between BadBox 3.0 and the Chinese company TXCZ: the modules check for TXCZ build properties, a TXCZ domain serves payload download routes and configurations for the hidden ads, and Human linked TXCZ to repositories distributing ad fraud launchers.
In addition to public repositories, the threat actor uses a second code platform and a file server to host payloads. For some payloads, it also uses a free open-source CDN that mirrors public repositories. The operators also use a self-hosted GitHub proxy.
Human Security has not provided an estimated size of BadBox 3.0, but noted that the mirror for one repository served over 367,000 requests over a month, which does not reflect the number of infections.
“These are requests rather than unique devices, and some come from researchers and scanners. It should be made very clear: these numbers are only for one repository, and only of the third backup delivery mechanism. The actual number of BADBOX 3.0 infections can be presumed to be significantly higher,” the cybersecurity firm notes.

articles.title: NVIDIA's SSD Writing Bug Needs Another Hotfix as Issue Returns
articles.text:
Monday, November 23rd 2026
NVIDIA's SSD Writing Bug Needs Another Hotfix as Issue Returns
Last week, NVIDIA released the GeForce Hotfix 621.35 driver to address the issue of excessive SSD writing that many consumers reported on their systems. However, the problem might not be completely resolved, and another update could be necessary, as more reports of SSD writing are resurfacing in online communities. According to a Reddit thread, a user reported that the latest hotfix has reduced the peak writing rate seen with the previous GeForce Game Ready 621.24 driver, and that the writing doesn't immediately start after a reboot. However, after a longer uptime or a sleep/wake transition, the writing continues at a rate of 1.26 MB/s, compared to the previous rate of up to 9.1 MB/s. Notably, this issue was recorded on the GeForce RTX 4090 SKU, and the user states that the only way to stop the NVDisplay.Container.exe writing loop is by rolling back to the 621.01 driver version or disabling the _nvtopps container plugin by setting DisableLoad to 1.
NVIDIA's staff on the GeForce Forums confirms that the bug doesn't affect any of the GeForce RTX 50 series "Blackwell" graphics cards. We are monitoring to see if the issue returns for the latest GeForce series as well. In the meantime, it appears that only the GeForce RTX 40 "Ada Lovelace" series is affected, and another hotfix might be needed to resolve the SSD writing bug for good.

articles.title: Telecom giant Bell says “agentic threat actor” accessed customer information
articles.text:
Canadian telecommunications giant Bell and its subsidiaries have been breached by an “agentic threat actor.”
The news: On Nov. 17, an unknown party gained unauthorized access to an internal Bell system that included customers’ personal information, the company told customers in an email on Monday morning. The breach was carried out by an “agentic threat actor” and affected Bell and subsidiaries, including Bell Aliant, Bell MTS, Virgin Plus, and Lucky Mobile, the company told BetaKit in an email.
Bell told customers that impacted personal information may have included names, mailing addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, and account details such as account numbers, product information, business names, as well as the date and amount of their last payments. Bell added that highly sensitive personal information, such as credit card numbers or bank account information, was not affected.
From the source: “Upon discovering the incident, Bell immediately removed the threat actor and initiated emergency protocols,” Bell told customers in the email. “We continue to monitor all systems closely. We take our obligation to safeguard your information very seriously and we have engaged the RCMP’s cybercrime unit to investigate.”
The context: High-profile cybersecurity incidents have been common this year, beginning with an OpenAI model hacking Hugging Face over the summer. This past month, in particular, has seen numerous cybersecurity failures, including at Canadian accounting firm KPMG, a British Columbia school district, and Staples Canada. Other recent high-profile incidents include the hacking of grocery store refrigerators in Europe, the US Department of Agriculture, and an identified vulnerability in the PHP programming language that brought down websites around the world as site owners rushed to patch their systems.
Final thought: While the use of AI hasn’t been confirmed in all of those breaches, cybersecurity agencies in the Five Eyes intelligence alliance, including the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, urged organizations to boost their cyber defences earlier this year, as they said AI is lowering the barrier for malicious actors and increasing the speed and complexity of attacks.
Following its own breach, Bell is reminding customers to remain wary of any unsolicited requests for personal information by someone posing as Bell, to avoid clicking on links or downloading attachments from suspicious emails or text messages, and to regularly review their accounts for suspicious activity.
Feature image courtesy Bell.

articles.title: Preço de GTA 6: com salário mínimo, brasileiro precisa de 61 horas de trabalho e fica em penúltimo entre 24 países
articles.text:
Quem ganha salário mínimo no Brasil precisa trabalhar 61 horas para pagar os R$ 449,90 da edição Standard de GTA 6 na PlayStation Store. É mais do que uma semana inteira de jornada de 44 horas, e o suficiente para deixar o país na 23ª posição entre 24 no levantamento dos especialistas em games do playcasino.com.
O curioso é que, convertido para o dólar, o preço de GTA 6 no Brasil está entre os mais baixos da lista.
Preço de GTA 6 é baixo em dólar, mas pesa no contracheque
O jogo, que chegou às lojas em 19 de novembro de 2026 para PlayStation 5 e Xbox Series X|S, custa R$ 449,90 na edição Standard nas lojas brasileiras. No câmbio usado no estudo, isso dá US$ 77,44, o segundo menor valor do ranking, atrás só da Nova Zelândia (US$ 76,85).
Nos Estados Unidos, na Guatemala, no Panamá, na República Dominicana e na Venezuela, o jogo sai por US$ 79,99. O México aparece com US$ 80,05 e o Canadá, com US$ 80,64.
O problema está do outro lado da conta. O Brasil tem salário mínimo de R$ 1.621, fixado pelo Decreto 12.797/2025, o que dá R$ 7,37 por hora. Dividindo o preço do jogo por esse valor, chega-se às 61 horas.
Os especialistas do playcasino.com resumem assim:
“Com R$ 7,37 por hora, o trabalhador precisa de mais de uma semana inteira de trabalho para comprar um único jogo.”
Quem trabalha menos horas para comprar GTA 6
Na ponta oposta, a Austrália lidera com 4,9 horas, seguida de Reino Unido (5,5), Irlanda (5,7), Alemanha e Nova Zelândia (5,8 cada). O Canadá precisa de 6,4 horas, Porto Rico de 8,5, a Espanha de 9,7 e os Estados Unidos de 11 horas.
Mesmo no Reino Unido, onde o jogo custa US$ 92,09, um dos preços mais altos da lista, bastam menos de seis horas de trabalho.
Vizinhos pagam mais caro e trabalham menos
A comparação com a América do Sul é a que mais pesa. Chile (31,1 horas), Uruguai (31,2) e Colômbia (32,7) precisam de cerca de metade do tempo do Brasil, embora paguem bem mais caro pelo jogo. No Uruguai, com IVA de 22%, GTA 6 sai por US$ 97,59, o preço mais alto do estudo.
Peru (54,6 horas) e Venezuela (57,8) ficam logo antes do Brasil. Só a Argentina exige mais: 75,6 horas, com o jogo a US$ 96,79.
Como foi feito o cálculo
O playcasino.com registrou, em 19 de novembro de 2026, o preço de GTA 6 Standard na PlayStation Store de cada país, somando os impostos cobrados na compra. A divisão foi feita pelo salário mínimo por hora em vigor na mesma data, segundo fontes oficiais. Onde o piso é mensal ou diário, o valor foi distribuído pela jornada legal semanal.
Alguns países pedem ressalvas. República Dominicana, Venezuela e Porto Rico compram na loja dos Estados Unidos, e o preço de Porto Rico inclui o IVU de 11,5%. Estados Unidos e Canadá aparecem com o menor preço possível, sem impostos estaduais ou provinciais, e com o salário mínimo federal. Na Venezuela, o estudo usou a “renda mínima integral” (ingreso mínimo integral) de US$ 240 por mês, porque o salário mínimo legal de Bs 130 vale cerca de US$ 0,14. Os preços em dólar usam o câmbio do open.er-api.com na data da coleta.

articles.title: Uber now lets you book rides that record the drive by default
articles.text:
Uber is piloting a new feature in the U.S. that offers rides in which drivers have enabled the company’s recording feature, Record My Ride.
The option, which uses the front camera of the Uber driver’s phone to record the entire drive, will show up as “Recorded Rides” in the app.
The ride-hailing company is starting the pilot in Baltimore, Raleigh, Indianapolis, and St. Louis and will expand to more locations later.
Uber said it is testing recorded rides specifically for rides booked at late night or those involving teens. Earlier this year, it introduced a live video streaming feature for rides booked for teenagers. In another test, the company had enabled audio recording for late-night trips in some cities.
The company is also testing a feature that will turn on recording when the app detects the ride going off-course, or when the vehicle might have had an accident.
The company said drivers can opt out of recording through the Settings panel. Similarly, riders can also decline permission to record their rides via an in-app notification.

articles.title: Welcome to elite impunity, Jensen Huang
articles.text:
I suppose I must issue a hearty congratulations to Jensen Huang. Huang is CEO of Nvidia again, to the surprise of basically everyone except President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance, who made sure it happened.
Welcome to elite impunity, Jensen Huang
Consequences are for the poors.
Welcome to elite impunity, Jensen Huang
Consequences are for the poors.
Now, those of us who had some kind of basic education on what a “free market” is might find it objectionable to have the American president strong-arming a major American company. But our billionaire tech overlords care about the “free market” exactly as much as they care about “free speech,” which is to say not at all. Watching Silicon Valley cheer for what is, effectively, a sign of a command economy has certainly been bracing. But then, why would they give a shit? Their only real beliefs are that they should remain rich and above the law. Jensen may not have exchanged emails with Jeffrey Epstein, but he’s squarely at the Epstein table now.
The deal was reportedly brokered by Peter Thiel’s very own boy
I have argued here, in the past, that the Epstein case laid bare the real politics of the revanchist American right wing: total elite impunity. Well, here it is again! If you are close enough with Trump, it doesn’t matter if you may have jeopardized national security by fucking an alleged Chinese spy. You won’t even be investigated for it before the American president calls in to your board of directors’ meeting to demand you be reinstated. I mean, it is the era of gangster tech regulation — what were any of us expecting? The deal was reportedly brokered by Peter Thiel’s very own boy, Vance.
Just so we can be absolutely clear about what transpired at Nvidia, let’s quickly go through the facts as we know them. A Chinese citizen named Alice Huang acquired the company she renamed Megaspeed, the Singaporean data firm at the center of this inquiry, in 2023. At some point, Huang met Huang, and the two were seen together at a dinner that December. From 2024 to 2025, Megaspeed received more than 200 Nvidia shipments.
In September 2025, the US government began investigating Megaspeed for possible violations of chip export controls; that October, the State Department told Trump of Jensen Huang’s affair with Alice Huang, who was described as a Chinese intelligence asset. Also in October, The New York Times first reported on Megaspeed’s relationship with Nvidia. In December, Trump — who has a close relationship with Jensen Huang — allowed Nvidia to sell more powerful chips to China. In March 2026, Marco Rubio warned the government about Alice, and Trump nonetheless invited Huang to a visit in China. In October, The New York Times reported on the affair. Shortly after Huang sent a note to Nvidia admitting to it, several other reports of infidelity — this time with Nvidia employees — surfaced. On November 12th, Huang resigned. On November 17th, during the Nvidia earnings call, the board’s chair said that the company “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” On November 23rd, Huang was back.
This level of open corruption is genuinely impressive
What changed between last week and this week? A week was not enough time to truly review all the information on Huang and his paramour, Alice “No Relation” Huang, the international woman of mystery. The explanation seems to be that Nvidia’s board succumbed to a pressure campaign from Huang’s fellow billionaires, and a direct intervention from the president and vice president of the United States of America.
Sure, all these CEOs ostensibly wanted Huang back at Nvidia to keep the AI trade going. Still, watching the likes of Epic CEO Tim Sweeney, former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick, investing loudmouth Bill Ackman, and Elon Musk — who actually did appear in the Epstein files, and who seemed to be pretty friendly with Epstein! — pitch a fit last week was instructive. These men worried that they might be punished for wrongdoing, that they did not get big enough to be above the law. They have now been reassured, and I suppose that is what really matters. After all, Trump said on CNBC that he gave Nvidia’s board assurances that Jensen is “absolutely fine.”
This level of open corruption is genuinely impressive, and not just because Huang is CEO of Nvidia again. Almost in passing, Trump noted that he had “protected” Musk in his first term from “a certain incident [that] took place, a very tough incident.” In his own inimitable style, Trump told Jim Cramer, “You wouldn’t have Elon if it wasn’t for me.” Surely there is no possible downside when the CEOs of two of the biggest corporations on Earth owe their jobs to Trump personally.
Surely there is no possible downside when the CEOs of two of the biggest corporations on Earth owe their jobs to Trump personally
One thing that has perhaps emboldened this crew is the stance from professional politics-knowers — and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries — that holding members of the Trump administration accountable might be a hindrance to governing. That accountability was part of the reason for the blue wave in November seems to have bypassed these pundits (and the presumptive House majority leader). But then, why should we believe that Democrats will thoroughly investigate this? Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer is claiming to want an investigation, but I am skeptical of how deep that investigation will go as long as Schumer leads it, and only partially because he’s been allied with Silicon Valley for more than a decade. He also has a daughter who works at OpenAI, a company that Nvidia invests in and that is dependent on Nvidia chips. How hard is he really willing to go?
Of course, there may be more to this than just pure economic self-interest. In celebrating Huang’s return, Trump posted a remarkable image. It is an altered picture of Trump himself, taken after a failed assassination attempt in 2024. Trump’s head has been replaced with Jensen Huang’s head. The American flag has been replaced with the Nvidia logo. Huang is waving a bright red bra. It seems I owe Sigmund Freud an apology. In the end, these men fear nothing more than losing power for sexual shenanigans — and especially losing power to a woman.
Leave aside the national security issues for a minute and focus on the two Nvidia employees. Dating subordinates is a serious conflict of interest; the CEO of Nestle lost his job for just that last year. This is a major violation for CEOs of normal companies, but it is common practice among the sleazeballs of Silicon Valley: Bill Gates is famous for it and it was plainly rampant at Google, a tone set by Sergey Brin himself. I am sure that you will be shocked, shocked to discover that in the wake of MeToo, Brin was among the men who suddenly swung right. I mean, Musk himself announced he was a Republican the day before Business Insider reported that he exposed himself to a flight attendant and paid hush money to cover it up.
If you’re rich enough, and connected enough, everything is permitted
The Republican Party has made the abuse of women without consequences one of its main issues; that the lesser violation of sleeping with subordinates would also be something the revanchists would defend seems obvious. That was clear from the botched investigation of the Epstein affair itself, the botched release of the Epstein files, and the assorted confirmation hearings of Pete Hegseth, Brett Kavanaugh, and Todd Blanche. (To say nothing of the Andrew Tate business.) But in all this, let’s not forget that Trump has been accused of sexual misconduct by no fewer than 28 women. So I’m sure it was an affront to all these guys that not only did Huang’s misconduct include a series of affairs, but he was also replaced by Colette Kress, who is known to be a woman.
I suppose we might as well pass by the various reports that Huang allegedly terrorized his employees. In light of everything else, this seems minor by comparison.
Anyway I had that all in mind when I saw Epic’s Sweeney celebrating the state intrusion into theoretically private companies by posting “Back in Black,” an oblique reference to Huang’s leather jackets that is also from the later, lesser period of AC/DC, after Bon Scott died and AC/DC became an AC/DC tribute band. He also called The New York Times’ reporting into Huang “lies.” Musk continued his streak of Sephiroth posting: “The mistake has been corrected.” Jason Calacanis, the All-In podcast’s village idiot, posted, “GPU Jesus has risen!” along with an openly blasphemous, AI-generated image of Huang as Christ.
Best of luck to Joon Kim, the Wachtell Lipton partner and former federal prosecutor who is conducting “a thorough and independent investigation” into Huang’s alleged misconduct on behalf of Nvidia’s board. I assume Kim has, like the rest of us, gotten the message loud and clear: If you’re rich enough, and connected enough, everything is permitted. Or perhaps, more succinctly: lol nothing matters.

articles.title: Call center operator gets 8 years for helping scam 30,000 Americans
articles.text:
A Peruvian call center operator was sentenced to eight years in prison for helping steal millions of dollars from over 30,000 Spanish-speaking US residents in a years-long government-impersonation fraud scheme.
45-year-old Carla Magaly Alcedo Mendoza of Lima, Peru, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit mail and wire fraud after being charged in an 18-count indictment following her March 2023 arrest and April 2025 extradition to the United States.
According to court documents, Alcedo managed and operated Peruvian call centers linked to multiple large-scale fraud and extortion schemes between January 2013 and December 2018.
The scammers first contacted Spanish-speaking Americans, claiming they qualified for free services or products. However, they later impersonated US government officials and lawyers and told the victims they were contractually obligated to pay large sums of money to receive them.
Together with her accomplices, she defrauded and extorted thousands of Americans by falsely threatening them with court action, arrest, and immigration consequences in unsolicited phone calls targeting Spanish-speaking Americans.
"The scheme spanned several years and thousands of victims made payments to Alcedo. Collectively, the scheme was responsible for defrauding more than 30,000 Spanish-speaking residents of the United States out of $15 million," the Department of Justice said.
"These criminals preyed on hardworking Americans, using fear and intimidation to steal millions of dollars. They deliberately targeted Spanish-speaking communities, impersonating government officials and threatening innocent people with arrest and legal consequences," added Acting US Attorney Yara Lorenzo Klukas.
Alcedo was the tenth defendant extradited from Peru and sentenced in this scheme, with ten other Peruvian call center owner-operators and four distribution center owner-operators involved in the scheme convicted so far.
This follows a June 2026 warning from the US Federal Trade Commission (FTC) that Americans have lost $3.5 billion to impersonation scams in 2025, with reported losses nearly tripling since 2020 and approximately $920 million stolen by government impersonators.
In April, the FBI also warned in its 2025 Internet Crime Report that US victims lost nearly $21 billion to cyber-enabled crimes throughout last year.

articles.title: Misfit Ventures aims to tap into charitable giving with new donor-advised fund
articles.text:
Misfit Ventures is launching its own donor-advised fund (DAF) with the help of fellow Vancouver organization Charitable Impact Foundation as it looks to convince more high-net-worth individuals to put their capital behind LGBTQ+ technology entrepreneurs.
The venture capital (VC) firm revealed Misfits Foundation on stage last Thursday during QueerTech’s latest annual conference. The two-day event, the largest in Canada for members of the LGBTQ+ community working in tech, brought over 700 people to Toronto’s Evergreen Brick Works to discuss inclusive AI and other topics from a variety of perspectives.
“I’m willing to be that guinea pig of trying something new to try and get more capital into the ecosystem.”
Misfit, which is currently raising its inaugural fund, claims to be Canada’s first and North America’s largest VC firm focused on LGBTQ+ founders building in tech, while Charitable Impact is a registered charity and public foundation that offers an online platform for individuals, families, and organizations to manage their charitable giving from a single account.
“There [are] a lot of [HNW] individuals that we’ve approached … or we’ve been introduced to, for potential investment, [who] really just don’t understand the [VC] world, so they want to stay away from it,” Misfit co-founder and managing partner Mandy Potter told BetaKit in an interview. “But what they do understand is donating.”
That realization was a driving factor behind Misfit’s decision to launch the Misfits Foundation DAF under Charitable Impact. Another was the state of the VC fundraising market, which has been particularly challenging for emerging managers and impact funds like Misfit, which has set out to finance LGBTQ+ and other historically underrepresented entrepreneurs at the earliest stages.
Potter described trying to raise a first fund in this environment as “fucking impossible” during her remarks on stage. “It’s the hardest thing I’ve ever done,” she added.
While Misfit’s new DAF was built “in a selfish way in the sense that we needed to find different avenues for capital,” Potter said her intentions are pure. “I want to see more impact funds and new fund managers be successful, so I’m willing to be that guinea pig of trying something new to try and get more capital into the ecosystem.”
RELATED: “A perfect storm”: 2025 was the worst year for Canadian VC fundraising since 2016
In Canada, a DAF is a fund established by a charity to which others donate and help guide. This structure permits donors to collectively give to multiple causes from the same account. Potter and fellow Misfit co-founder and managing partner Douglas Lui are leading the initiative.
Dollars donated to Misfit’s DAF will be held by Charitable Impact, while the fund’s strategy and giving will be guided by Potter. Those donations will be invested into Misfit’s core fund and deployed into startups with LGBTQ+ leadership. Potter said the firm’s DAF has already secured commitments, but declined to share how much exactly to date.
Unlike limited partners (LPs) investing in Misfit’s fund, individuals who donate to this DAF will receive an immediate charitable tax receipt from Charitable Impact. Any returns generated on the capital that Misfit invests from this DAF will remain committed to charity and be redistributed to other causes at the discretion of Misfit’s leadership team.
QueerTech board chair Bradley Breton, who previously served as chief of staff at Toronto FinTech firm Zafin, is a Misfit LP. For donors, he said this DAF offers a means for folks interested in maximizing their impact on LGBTQ+ communities while also reaping the associated tax benefits, whereas becoming a Misfit LP provides a pathway that balances that impact with financial returns.
RELATED: Queer tech founders explore move to Canada as US abandons DEI
Breton is also one of the champions of another DAF focused on LGBTQ+ communities through Charitable Impact called Q Impact. Launched by Breton, founding donor Barry Inouye, a former leader at Amazon and Coca-Cola, and Trevor Loke, a community ambassador at Charitable Impact.
Q Impact is a cause fund, a structure that Kirsten Hurlbut, account manager at Charitable Impact, said allows people “to come together and support the cause instead of the organization.”
“The goal is to create a sustainable cause fund that can support the queer community across different policy issues, both nationally and internationally,” Breton told BetaKit in an interview.
Dollars donated to Q Impact are held by Charitable Impact. According to Q Impact’s website, the cause fund has secured more than $1.3 million to date.
Charitable Impact also helps power another such fund dedicated to promoting therapies for those living with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, or ALS.
Potter is hoping that Misfit’s DAF can serve as a model for other emerging managers and impact funds. Breton said QueerTech is also exploring how to use DAF-based giving to support some of its own programming.
Feature image courtesy QueerTech. Photo by Naomi Silver-Vézina.

articles.title: AirPods Pro 3 : Amazon brade les meilleurs écouteurs d’Apple pour le Black Friday
articles.text:
Avoir une bonne paire d’écouteurs sans fil, c’est toujours appréciable au quotidien, que ce soit pour écouter de la musique dans les transports, regarder des vidéos ou passer des appels sans être dérangé par les bruits environnants. Dans ce domaine, les AirPods Pro 3 d’Apple font partie des références. Sortis en septembre 2025, ils succèdent aux AirPods Pro 2 avec une excellente qualité sonore, une réduction de bruit active particulièrement efficace et un mode Transparence très convaincant.
Pendant le Black Friday, Amazon les affiche à 188 € au lieu de 249 €.
Que valent les AirPods Pro 3 d’Apple ?
Les AirPods Pro 3 ressemblent beaucoup à leurs prédécesseurs, mais Apple a apporté plusieurs améliorations. Les nouveaux embouts, désormais disponibles en cinq tailles, dont une XXS, assurent un meilleur maintien dans l’oreille et participent à améliorer les performances audio. D’après notre test des AirPods Pro 3, qui leur a attribué la note de 9/10, le confort reste aussi bon que sur la génération précédente. La réduction de bruit active est deux fois plus efficace que sur les AirPods Pro 2.
Le rendu sonore progresse également grâce à une nouvelle architecture acoustique, qui enrichit les basses et restitue les voix et les instruments avec davantage de clarté. Les écouteurs intègrent également plusieurs fonctions dédiées à la santé auditive, avec notamment un test d’audition réalisable chez soi et une protection contre les sons trop forts. On retrouve aussi l’égalisation adaptative, qui ajuste le son à la morphologie de chaque oreille, le basculement automatique entre les appareils Apple et le partage audio pour écouter un même contenu à deux.
L’autonomie atteint désormais 8 heures d’écoute avec la réduction de bruit activée. Apple ajoute aussi un capteur de fréquence cardiaque, capable de suivre le rythme cardiaque et les calories brûlées pendant une cinquantaine de types d’exercices.
À ce prix, les AirPods Pro 3 sont-ils une bonne affaire ?
À 188 € pendant le Black Friday, les AirPods Pro 3 coûtent 61 € de moins que leur prix officiel de 249 €. C’est un très bon tarif pour des écouteurs parmi les meilleurs sur le marché. L’offre est surtout intéressante si vous possédez encore des écouteurs classiques, une ancienne génération d’AirPods ou une paire dépourvue de réduction de bruit active. Pour moins de 200 €, vous profitez d’excellents écouteurs, confortables, endurants et capables de vous isoler efficacement des bruits environnants.
Ils conviendront aussi très bien à ceux qui utilisent quotidiennement un iPhone, un iPad ou un Mac et souhaitent profiter des fonctions propres à l’écosystème Apple. En revanche, si vous possédez déjà des AirPods Pro 2, le changement est moins évident : le design reste presque identique et les améliorations concernent surtout la réduction de bruit, la qualité sonore, le maintien et l’autonomie.
Black Friday 2026 : tout ce qu’il faut savoir
Depuis une dizaine d’années, le Black Friday s’est infiltré dans le calendrier commercial des grandes marques et enseignes françaises. Avec l’expérience, on peut vous dire que cet événement fait partie des meilleurs moments pour faire de bonnes affaires.
Les dates du Black Friday
Bien qu’il porte encore le nom du vendredi noir, le Black Friday s’étend désormais sur un mois chez de nombreux revendeurs. Un format moins typique qui lui retire un peu son petit côté FOMO. On dirait presque les soldes, finalement. Mais c’est aussi moins le rush, ce qui est une bonne chose pour ceux qui veulent faire des achats plus raisonnés. Globalement, on peut résumer ce Black Friday en quatre temps forts :
- Début novembre : les avant-premières Black Friday.
- Autour du 20 novembre, selon les enseignes : la Black Week commence généralement plusieurs jours avant le jour J.
- 27 novembre : la date du Black Friday, même si les offres commencent généralement avant et se prolongent le week-end des 28 et 29 novembre.
- 30 novembre : le Cyber Monday.

Que faut-il acheter pendant le Black Friday ?
Globalement, tous les rayons profitent des remises, mais il ne faut pas pour autant se jeter sur les premiers prix bradés. N’oubliez pas que pour les enseignes, ce moment est aussi l’occasion de déstocker de vieux produits, dont les plus remisés frôlent parfois l’obsolescence.
Qu’il s’agisse d’un téléviseur, d’un smartphone, d’un casque sans fil ou d’un aspirateur balai, on ne peut que vous conseiller de suivre nos guides d’achat dédiés pour savoir quels modèles valent le coup en 2026.
Pour les produits phares comme les AirPods, la PS5, la Switch 2, un iPhone ou un Samsung Galaxy, sachez que nos tests sont là pour vous aider à savoir s’ils méritent votre argent.
Quoi qu’il en soit, chez Numerama, nous faisons déjà le tri à votre place en relayant uniquement des bons plans pertinents : des offres sur des produits à la fois intéressants et proposés parmi les meilleurs prix observés en ligne.
