articles.title: Blade Runner 2099 : on a vu la série événement de Prime Video à 180 millions de dollars, voici notre avis
articles.text:
| Réalisateur | Silka Luisa | 
| Acteurs | Michelle Yeoh, Hunter Schafer, Dimitri Abold, Tom Burke, Maurizio Lombardi, Sheila Atim, Matthew Needham, Lewis Gribben | 
| Genre | Action, Science-fiction | 
| Durée | 60 min | 
| Date de sortie | 25/11/2026 | 
| Episodes | 8 | 
Le monde dystopique et cyberpunk de Philip K. Dick se retrouve à nouveau porté à l'écran avec une audacieuse série sur Prime Video. Voici notre critique de Blade Runner 2099, garantie sans spoiler.
Une petite décennie après la sortie au cinéma du film Blade Runner 2049, l'univers imaginé par Philip K. Dick fait l'objet d'une onéreuse série produite par Amazon pour sa plateforme de streaming Prime Video, disponible à partir du 25 novembre 2026.
Cette nouvelle adaptation impressionne à plusieurs niveaux, mais elle a la lourde tâche de rendre enfin populaire une franchise pourtant fondatrice de la pop culture. Voici notre critique de Blade Runner 2099, garantie sans spoilers.
50 ans après les événements de Blade Runner 2049, Los Angeles renaît, mais ce n'est pas grâce à l’humanité. Cora, une fugitive qui tente une dernière fois de mettre fin à sa cavale, endosse une ultime identité : celle d’une Blade Runner. Contrainte de faire équipe avec Olwen, une répliquante dont les jours sont comptés, elle se lance à la poursuite d’un fugitif qui cache une vérité susceptible de faire s’effondrer une ville déjà fragile.
Publié en 1968, le roman Les Androïdes rêvent-ils de moutons électriques ? de Philip K. Dick est l'un des grands classiques de la littérature d'anticipation, dépeignant un futur où la Terre a été dévastée par une guerre nucléaire et où vivent les rares humains qui ont choisi de ne pas émigrer sur Mars (ou qui n'en avaient pas les moyens).
Adapté pour la première fois en 1982 avec le film Blade Runner de Ridley Scott, le long-métrage fut un bide en salles avant de gagner un statut culte au fil des années. En 2017, sa suite signée Denis Villeneuve, avec Ryan Gosling et Harrison Ford au casting, a également été un échec financier.
Là réside tout le paradoxe de Blade Runner : c'est l'un des univers de science-fiction les plus importants de l'histoire (le récent jeu vidéo Cyberpunk 2077 l'a encore prouvé), mais le grand public ne semble pourtant jamais s'y intéresser au box-office. La série Blade Runner 2099 peut-elle réussir là où ses prédécesseurs ont échoué ?
La nouvelle série, au budget annoncé de 180 millions de dollars, s'est en tout cas donné les moyens de ses ambitions, à commencer par une ambiance remarquablement soignée. C'est simple, Blade Runner 2099 s'impose dès les premières minutes comme l'une des productions les plus abouties de l'année, offrant un véritable festin pour les sens.
Des costumes aux multiples décors fourmillant de détails — météo, lieux de vie, établissements nocturnes, transports… — en passant par ce futur crasseux et analogique, la musique entêtante de Leopold Ross (Shōgun, Monarch) et la direction artistique prégnante, le programme parvient avec brio à nous immerger dans sa dystopie.
Loin de singer le film original, Blade Runner 2099 réussit notamment son jeu d'échelle vertigineux qui raconte quelque chose de la société qui l'habite, du plus modeste bar aux constructions monumentales, jusqu'à la multitude d'âmes qui survivent dans ses plis. Au visionnage, il est difficile de ne pas penser à Andor, qui avait apporté une granularité inédite à la saga Star Wars.
Car au-delà de cette réussite plastique, Blade Runner 2099 a surtout saisi toute l'essence de son histoire et n'oublie pas de tisser une aventure captivante. En plaçant au cœur de son intrigue une humaine et une répliquante toutes deux à bout de souffle, la créatrice Silka Luisa (Shining Girls, Halo) reconnecte son œuvre à l'ADN du film noir, peuplé de figures désespérées.
Celles-ci sont incarnées par les habitées Michelle Yeoh (Wicked) et Hunter Schafer (Euphoria), épaulées par des seconds rôles aux “gueules” trop rares à l'écran, à l'image des excellents Tom Burke (Furiosa), Matthew Needham (House of the Dragon) et Sheila Atim (The Vampire Lestat).
Plus ambitieuse encore, la série développe une véritable suite à l'univers de Philip K. Dick, revenant aux origines du projet d'Eldon Tyrell et des Nexus. Entre le legacyquel (mot-valise anglais fusionnant héritage et suite) et son récit proche des populaires Silo et For All Mankind, le format tente ainsi de séduire à la fois les fans historiques et les nouveaux venus. Et nous disons bien “tente”.
Car Blade Runner 2099 se perd parfois dans l'immensité de son bac à sable et son imposante narration chorale, certaines sous-intrigues mettant du temps à décoller. Si les fans apprécieront sans réserve le voyage, le programme demande un certain investissement de la part des curieux avant de voir tout son potentiel dramatique porter ses fruits.
C'est peut-être là que réside la limite de la série. Car si Blade Runner 2099 a pour vocation de s'adresser à un public profane, elle fait ce travail de vulgarisation de manière assez bourrative, et l'amas d'informations à ingérer en peu de temps peut être rébarbatif. La série arrive ainis avec une proposition audacieuse, massive et exigeante à tous les niveaux (visuel, narratif, dramatique), mais qui pourra rebuter certains spectateurs.
Croyez-nous : le jeu en vaut la chandelle. Même si elle ne réussit pas tout ce qu'elle entreprend, la série est une aventure d'une beauté folle et d'une richesse remarquable pour qui s'y abandonne, et qui ouvre des horizons excitants à l'univers de Philip K. Dick.
Blade Runner 2099 sort le 25 novembre sur Prime Video.
Grâce à une direction artistique impressionnante et une production soignée, Blade Runner 2099 donne à voir un monde de Philip K. Dick plus vibrant que jamais, et se place comme l'une des plus belles séries de l'année. Si cette nouvelle plongée dans un L.A. dystopique peuplé de Réplicants ravira sans aucun doute les fans, elle reste toutefois une porte d'entrée exigeante (et potentiellement rebutante) pour les néophytes. Le voyage mérite toutefois qu'on s'y investisse, car Blade Runner 2099 s'impose comme une proposition de SF ambitieuse, immersive et passionnante, qui ne se contente pas de prolonger un univers culte, mais qui lui donne de nouvelles perspectives excitantes. Un petit 4 étoiles, mais un 4 étoiles quand même.

articles.title: CISA flags critical Cisco RCE flaw as actively exploited in attacks
articles.text:
The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned federal agencies that attackers are now exploiting a recently patched critical Cisco Expressway vulnerability in the wild.
Cisco Expressway Series devices are enterprise collaboration gateways (deployed as virtual machines or physical hardware appliances) that connect internal voice and video systems with outside networks and remote users via a secure connection.
Tracked as CVE-2026-76466, this security flaw stems from the use of hard-coded credentials and a failure to fully validate client certificates, enabling unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute arbitrary operating system commands as root on affected Cisco Expressway-C and Cisco Expressway-E devices configured in a cluster.
"An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands," Cisco said in late October, when it released security patches to address the issue.
While Cisco says that its Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) is not aware of active exploitation in the wild or publicly available proof-of-concept exploits targeting this vulnerability, CISA tagged it as actively exploited on Friday.
The cybersecurity agency also added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on Tuesday and ordered US Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies to secure their systems within three days, as mandated by Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04.
Although BOD 26-04 targets only federal agencies, CISA urged all network defenders, including private-sector security teams, to prioritize patching this flaw to block ongoing attacks that may target their networks.
"These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise," it warned.
Exploited to gain root on Internet-exposed devices
While CISA has yet to share details on these ongoing attacks, Russian cybersecurity company F6 said on Thursday that it spotted attackers using an unnamed AI assistant to successfully exploit CVE-2026-7646 and gain remote command execution with full root privileges on Internet-exposed Cisco Expressway devices.
"The attackers initially compromised two Cisco Expressway internet-facing devices. Through one of them, they gained access to two additional cluster nodes located on the organization’s internal network," F6 security researchers noted.
"After obtaining root access, the attackers began preparing tooling for further lateral movement across the infrastructure. They used custom Python scripts designed to scan the network, discover accessible SMB resources, interact with SQL Server and WinRM, and explore GitLab repositories in order to exfiltrate credentials and other sensitive information."
Two weeks ago, CISA also flagged a high-severity Cisco BroadWorks vulnerability (CVE-2026-20320) as actively exploited in attacks and ordered federal agencies to patch their systems by November 24.
According to threat intelligence firm Malbear Labs, a Chinese-speaking threat actor abused CVE-2026-20320 in autonomous AI attacks targeting a European telecommunications provider and 13 organizations that used its data centers and cloud infrastructure.
CISA has added 103 Cisco vulnerabilities to its list of actively exploited flaws since November 2021, seven of which ransomware gangs have also used in the wild.

articles.title: « C'est GTA 6 dans la vraie vie » : comment le nouveau FSD v15 de Tesla génère une vue photoréaliste de la route en temps réel
articles.text:
Il est des comparaisons auxquelles on ne résiste pas lorsque la moitié d’Internet est plongée dans GTA 6. Elon Musk a ainsi résumé sur X la nouvelle interface de ses véhicules d’une formule choc : « le FSD, c’est GTA dans la vraie vie ».
Le parallèle saute aux yeux dès les premières vidéos publiées par les propriétaires : caméra placée derrière la voiture à la troisième personne, bitume texturé, voitures de police reconnaissables et même reflets de la pluie sur la chaussée.
Le blockbuster de Rockstar étant sorti le 19 novembre (lancement que nous avons suivi en direct) et le FSD v15 deux jours plus tard, Tesla n’aurait pu rêver meilleur alignement des planètes.
    Pour aller plus loin
GTA 6 est disponible en France : tout savoir sur lancement du jeu phare de Rockstar
            
Baptisée Tesla Reality View, cette interface débarque avec le FSD (Supervised) v15.0.1, distribué depuis samedi aux premiers testeurs du programme d’accès anticipé via la mise à jour 2026.38.6.11 avant un déploiement élargi en décembre selon Elon Musk. Elle enterre les anciennes modélisations austères faites de fonds sombres et de voitures réduites à de simples boîtes grises.
Seule condition matérielle : disposer de l’ordinateur embarqué AI4 des Tesla récentes, ce qui exclut d’office les quelque 4 millions de voitures équipées de l’ancien matériel HW3.
Votre production solaire dépasse votre consommation ? Stockez le surplus au lieu de le revendre à bas prix. Le SolarFlow 2400 AC+ se branche sur votre installation existante, 100 % plug-and-play, et s’amortit plus vite grâce au Black Friday.
Pour le reste des nouveautés, du nouvel encodeur de vision au ralentissement devant les radars, nous avons déjà passé en revue toutes les nouveautés du FSD v15.
Une image dessinée par l’IA de conduite
Derrière la ressemblance visuelle, la mécanique n’a pourtant rien de commun avec celle d’un jeu vidéo. Un titre comme GTA 6 calcule ses décors grâce à un moteur 3D qui assemble des objets modélisés à l’avance par des artistes, exigeant une machine musclée comme le rappelle la config à viser pour GTA 6 en 60 images par seconde.
La Tesla, elle, n’embarque aucune banque de décors préfabriqués. Selon Ashok Elluswamy, directeur de l’IA chez Tesla, c’est le même modèle « de bout en bout » qui pilote la voiture et génère l’affichage : un unique réseau neuronal analyse les flux des caméras jusqu’aux commandes du volant et dessine directement ce qu’il comprend de son environnement.
Elon Musk précise qu’il s’agit d’une génération vidéo par IA en temps réel, sans moteur de jeu, qui tourne sur la moitié d’un seul des accélérateurs d’IA de la puce AI4. Concrètement, l’écran affiche la représentation mentale que la voiture se fait de la rue, avec des flèches annonçant les virages prévus et la possibilité de choisir sa place de stationnement d’un simple appui.
Tesla présente la fonction comme un moyen intuitif de voir et de contrôler ce que le FSD s’apprête à entreprendre, tout en mobilisant moins de puissance de calcul que l’ancienne interface selon les notes de version.
    Pour aller plus loin
GTA 6 sur PC en 60 FPS : voici la config à viser, en tour PC comme en PC portable
            
Vraie aide à la conduite ou effet de vitrine ?
Sur le papier, l’apport ergonomique est indéniable. Le FSD demeurant une assistance de niveau 2 qui exige une vigilance constante, visualiser avec précision la trajectoire anticipée par la voiture aide le conducteur à reprendre la main au bon moment.
Ce photoréalisme cache toutefois un revers psychologique : une image générée par IA peut se tromper, et une erreur habillée de reflets et d’ombres réalistes inspire bien plus confiance qu’une simple boîte grise mal placée. Or Tesla ne communique rien sur la fidélité réelle de ce rendu ni sur la façon dont l’interface signale ses doutes, d’autant qu’un écran aussi spectaculaire attire davantage le regard au moment même où la v15 assouplit la surveillance des yeux du conducteur dans les modes de conduite les plus rapides.
Et en France ?
Rien n’est prévu à court terme pour les propriétaires français. En Europe, le système est déployé sous le nom Tesla Assisted Driving dans douze pays seulement, sur une branche v14 encadrée par l’autorité néerlandaise RDW qui vient précisément de durcir les règles d’attention au volant.
La France reste à l’écart dans l’attente d’un vote européen qu’Elon Musk espère au premier trimestre 2027, et nous avons déjà expliqué pourquoi cette v15 risque de retarder encore son arrivée chez nous.
    Pour aller plus loin
Tesla lance son spectaculaire FSD v15 : pourquoi ces nouveautés vont encore retarder son arrivée en France
            
D’ici là, pour admirer des rues aussi détaillées sur un écran en France, il faudra se contenter de GTA 6 sur console, ou de préparer son PC pour le jour où il y débarquera.

articles.title: CrowdStrike to Acquire Zscaler in $43.9 Billion Deal
articles.text:
CrowdStrike (NASDAQ: CRWD) on Monday said it has agreed to acquire Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS) in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $43.9 billion.
The deal would combine one of the largest endpoint security providers with a pioneer in cloud-delivered zero-trust access and give CrowdStrike a much larger presence in network security.
The two companies already share more than 2,000 customers and have 16 product integrations. In September, they announced plans to expand their partnership so Falcon could continuously assess user risk and share that information with Zscaler’s access controls. CrowdStrike said it plans to bring the products together on a single platform with a common data layer and a single customer contract after closing.
Zscaler’s own acquisition spree
Zscaler has used acquisitions to expand beyond its core network security business. In February 2026, it acquired SquareX, whose browser extension helps enterprises enforce security policies on unmanaged devices. In November 2025, it bought SPLX, adding tools to discover, test and protect AI models, applications and agents.
Zscaler also completed its acquisition of managed detection and response provider Red Canary in August 2025, expanding its presence in security operations. The deal followed Zscaler’s 2024 purchases of Avalor, a $350 million acquisition that added technology for combining security data and prioritizing risk, and Airgap Networks, which brought network segmentation capabilities.
CrowdStrike expects the combined company to have more than $10 billion in annual recurring revenue at closing and projects about $1 billion in additional annualized revenue within 30 months, in part from selling more products to existing customers.
The deal would put CrowdStrike in more direct competition with broad cybersecurity platform providers such as Palo Alto Networks.
Both boards unanimously approved the deal, which is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike’s fiscal 2028.
Unter the terms of the agreement, Zscaler shareholders would receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each Zscaler share. Based on Friday’s closing prices, the exchange ratio values Zscaler at $260.41 per share, a premium of roughly 34%. CrowdStrike shareholders would own approximately 84.1% of the combined company, with Zscaler shareholders holding the remaining 15.9%.
Zscaler founder and CEO Jay Chaudhry will continue to lead the Zscaler business and join CrowdStrike’s board after the deal closes.

articles.title: Cómo silenciar en WhatsApp las llamadas de números desconocidos y qué datos muestra la app
articles.text:
WhatsApp permite que el teléfono no suene cuando llama alguien que no está en la agenda. El ajuste se llama “Silenciar llamadas de desconocidos” y está en los menús de Privacidad, tanto en Android como en iPhone. Las llamadas no se bloquean: quedan registradas.
Según el Centro de ayuda de WhatsApp, cuando escribe alguien que no es un contacto, la app indica si el usuario tiene grupos en común con esa persona y si su número está registrado en un país distinto del propio. Con esos datos, el usuario decide si responde, agrega el contacto, lo bloquea o lo denuncia.
Ante una llamada que llega de un número que no está guardado, estos son los datos que conviene mirar antes de atender: si hay grupos en común y el país de registro. Un número de otro país, sin ningún grupo compartido, es una señal para no contestar.
Cómo activar el silencio en Android
Primero se abre WhatsApp y se toca el menú de tres puntos verticales. Luego se elige Ajustes, después Privacidad y, al final de la lista, Llamadas. Allí se activa el interruptor de silenciar llamadas de desconocidos.
Para desactivarlo, solo hay que repetir el recorrido y apagar el interruptor. La opción puede cambiarse tantas veces como se quiera.
Cómo activarlo en iPhone
En el iPhone, el camino empieza en la pestaña Ajustes de la parte inferior de la pantalla, o en la foto de perfil. Después se toca Privacidad, luego Llamadas y se activa el mismo interruptor.
La posición del menú puede variar según la versión de la aplicación. Si no aparece Llamadas dentro de Privacidad, conviene actualizar WhatsApp desde la tienda de aplicaciones.
Qué pasa con las llamadas silenciadas
Con el ajuste encendido, el teléfono no suena, pero las llamadas aparecen en la pestaña Llamadas y en las notificaciones. Así, un repartidor o un técnico que llama desde un número nuevo puede ser atendido después.
Para devolver la llamada se toca el número en esa pestaña o el mensaje “Llamada de desconocido silenciada” dentro del chat. Hay una excepción: si el usuario llama o escribe a ese número, WhatsApp deja de silenciar sus llamadas futuras.
Quien quiera cortar todo contacto con un número concreto debe bloquearlo, una opción distinta que el Centro de ayuda de WhatsApp también menciona. La app permite además denunciar al contacto. WhatsApp recuerda que las estafas pueden afectar a cualquiera y pide desconfiar de mensajes de números desconocidos y de pedidos de dinero o datos personales.
Cuáles funciones de WhatsApp ayudan a proteger la cuenta
WhatsApp ofrece la verificación en dos pasos, que permite añadir un PIN para dificultar el acceso de terceros, incluso si obtienen el código de registro enviado por SMS. También permite activar alertas cuando alguien intenta registrar el número en otro dispositivo y revisar los equipos vinculados desde la configuración de la cuenta.
La aplicación cifra los mensajes y las llamadas de extremo a extremo, y suma opciones como el bloqueo de chats con huella o código, los mensajes temporales y la posibilidad de ocultar la dirección IP en llamadas. Para reforzar la privacidad, conviene limitar quién puede ver la foto de perfil, la última conexión, los estados y quién puede añadir al usuario a grupos.
Cómo reconocer un mensaje sospechoso antes de contestar
Las estafas suelen apelar a la urgencia: premios inesperados, supuestos problemas con una cuenta, pedidos de dinero de un contacto conocido o solicitudes de códigos de verificación. Son señales de alerta los errores de redacción, los números desconocidos, los enlaces acortados o las ofertas que parecen demasiado convenientes.
Antes de abrir un enlace o compartir datos, es recomendable confirmar la identidad del remitente por otra vía y no reenviar nunca códigos recibidos por SMS o WhatsApp. Si el mensaje genera dudas, la plataforma permite bloquear y denunciar el contacto, sumado a borrar la conversación para evitar nuevas interacciones.

articles.title: Anthropic tested the market. Will Cohere follow?
articles.text:
Anthropic just answered a question that, until Friday, investors have mostly had to guess the answer to. Until now, markets have priced the value of AI features or integrations, but not a frontier lab itself. So what is a pure-play AI company worth?
It turns out: a lot. Anthropic closed its first day on the Nasdaq on Thursday with a market cap of nearly $1.3 trillion USD, the largest IPO in history.
Now, that solid debut isn’t a guarantee of continued momentum or overall faith in the AI trade, as anyone staring into a sea of red in their portfolios would have told you on Friday. Analysts have noted that it’s likely many traders dumped other tech stocks to give Anthropic a heavier weight in their portfolios. Meanwhile, lingering anxiety over inflation and massive capital expenditures on AI infrastructure contributed to a nasty end to the week as stock markets entered correction territory.
But as the first frontier company to test the waters, Anthropic appears to have found them decently warm.
Canada’s entrant in the frontier model race was watching closely, even though it doesn’t seem ready to jump in just yet. “A rising tide lifts all boats, and a very successful IPO is good for everyone,” Cohere co-founder Aidan Gomez wrote on X, congratulating Anthropic, followed by a small dig: “I hope Anthropic adjusts its strategy to support a healthy community of competitors and a diversity of different ideologies and opinions.”
Gomez said last year he thought Cohere could IPO “soon,” but told the Wall Street Journal earlier this month that timing is still uncertain. Instead, Cohere appears to be focusing on M&A—it’s made four this year, all in Europe. Given the broader tech selloff and its new pile of government money, Cohere is likely in no rush to join Anthropic all that “soon.”
Sarah Rieger, 
Managing Editor

articles.title: Il y a une nouvelle bande-annonce pour Avengers Doomsday : voici la vidéo
articles.text:
Avengers: Doomsday sort au cinéma en France le mercredi 16 décembre, deux jours avant les États-Unis. Dune 3, de Denis Villeneuve, sort le même jour. Les deux films vont se disputer le box-office de fin d’année.
Marvel Studios a mis en ligne une nouvelle bande-annonce ce 23 novembre 2026, très attendue. Des informateurs l’annonçaient pour le 16 ou le 18 novembre, mais le 18 novembre, le studio s’était contenté d’un teaser de 26 secondes et d’une vidéo de coulisses avec Robert Downey Jr.
Le retour des frères Russo et le pari de Robert Downey Jr. pour Avengers: Doomsday
Marvel compte sur Avengers: Doomsday pour relancer sa franchise phare. Le studio a rappelé Anthony et Joe Russo, déjà réalisateurs d’Infinity War et d’Endgame, pour mettre en scène cette nouvelle réunion de super-héros.
La vraie surprise du projet reste le retour de Robert Downey Jr. dans le MCU. Sept ans après le sacrifice mémorable de Tony Stark, l’acteur oscarisé passe du côté des méchants et incarne Victor von Doom, le Docteur Doom (longtemps appelé Fatalis en français), grand méchant du film. Kevin Feige, patron de Marvel Studios, a d’ailleurs assuré au magazine Empire que ce Doom n’est pas une variante de Tony Stark.
Un casting XXL avant le rendez-vous du 16 décembre
Face à lui, le casting réunit des Avengers de la première heure, comme Chris Hemsworth (Thor) et Chris Evans, de retour en Steve Rogers, et Anthony Mackie, devenu Captain America. Il accueille aussi les X-Men des films Fox, emmenés par Patrick Stewart et Ian McKellen, et les Quatre Fantastiques de Pedro Pascal. Disney a même créé un label pour les salles haut de gamme, Infinity Vision.
Avengers: Doomsday sort au cinéma en France le mercredi 16 décembre 2026. D’ici là, Disney a donné rendez-vous aux fans le 30 novembre pour une présentation spéciale du film.

articles.title: Which iPad Model Should You Get? Full 2026 Update
articles.text:
Apple's iPad lineup has an unusual pecking order in 2026. The newest iPad mini packs an OLED display and the A20 Pro chip, while the larger iPad Air still uses an LCD. With current discounts, the Air can even cost less. Meanwhile, a round of price hikes has pushed the entry-level iPad to $449 and the Pro into territory where a MacBook starts to look tempting.
The result is that there's no obvious best iPad for everyone. We still believe Apple leads the way in tablets, thanks to hardware and software that work remarkably well together. But which model is best for you? That's what this guide is for.
We've updated our guide to reflect the latest models, prices, and accessories. Below is a side-by-side look at the current lineup, followed by the trade-offs that matter most when deciding which iPad is worth your money.
| Model | iPad | iPad Mini | iPad Air M4 | iPad Pro M5 | 
| Generation | 11th-gen | 8th-gen | 8th-gen | 8th-gen | 
| Release Date | Mar 2025 | Nov 2026 | Mar 2026 | Oct 2025 | 
| MSRP / Amazon | $449 / $399 | $699 / $699 | $749 / $649 | $1,199 / $1,099 | 
| Processor | A16 | A20 Pro | M4 | M5 | 
| Display Size | 10.9" | 8.5" | 10.9" or 12.9" | 11" or 13" | 
| Display Technology | 60Hz LCD | 60Hz OLED | 60Hz LCD | 120Hz OLED | 
| Min / Max Storage | 128GB / 512GB | 128GB / 512GB | 128GB / 1TB | 256GB / 2TB | 
| Keyboard | Magic Keyboard Folio | n/a | Magic Keyboard for iPad Air | Magic Keyboard for iPad Pro | 
| Pencil | 1st-gen & USB-C | Pencil Pro & USB-C | Pencil Pro & USB-C | Pencil Pro & USB-C | 
Is the base iPad all you need?
If you're looking for a great tablet for watching videos and browsing the web, the basic and most affordable iPad will cover your needs well. The base iPad has the same display resolution (2360 x 1640) and maximum brightness (500 nits) as the 11-inch iPad Air. Additionally, it features an ultra-wide 12MP front camera, like the other models.
If you want a tablet that can double as a basic laptop, the iPad supports the Magic Keyboard Folio, which includes function keys and a trackpad. While you could get the MacBook Neo for the combined price of the iPad and the keyboard, the iPad can provide a more portable solution if you want a tablet first and foremost, plus it offers a better camera. Although the kickstand design requires more desk space, it allows you to detach the keyboard when needed.
For the price, the base iPad offers impressive features, but it's not the best choice for everyone. The display lacks an anti-reflective coating, making it less ideal for outdoor use. If you use your iPad for drawing, you'll appreciate the fully laminated display and broader color gamut available on other models, too.
Most notably, the A16 SoC and 6GB of RAM pale in comparison to the Apple M4 and 12GB offered by the iPad Air. That also makes it the only current model that can't run Apple Intelligence, which utilizes on-device processing.
Although the iPad includes a USB-C connector, it still supports the 1st-gen Pencil. If you already own the 1st-gen Pencil, you'll need a $9 adapter to connect it. Alternatively, it supports the more affordable USB-C Pencil, which forgoes pressure sensitivity but attaches magnetically to the iPad's bezel.
The iPad's MSRP has been raised to $449 from $349, but can still be had for $399 with the 128GB Wi-Fi model. For an additional $100, you can upgrade to 256GB, and upgrading from 256GB to 512GB costs another $200. Color options include silver, blue, pink, and yellow, offering some vibrant choices even without a case.
The iPad mini goes premium
The iPad Mini has been updated in 2026 with the same A20 Pro chip found in the iPhone 18 Pro series, and 12GB of RAM. It outperforms the M4 chip found in the iPad Air in single-core and graphic tasks, although it still trails in multi-core performance.
You'll struggle to find anything faster in such a small package and at this price, making it a great choice for mobile gaming or 3D modeling on the go.
However, only the 512GB model comes with a fully enabled chip, including two performance cores, four efficiency cores and a dual neural engine. The other versions have one efficiency core and one neural engine disabled.
The Mini is among the largest tablets that most adults can comfortably hold in one hand, measuring 7.7 x 5.2 inches (19.5 x 13.3 cm). Thickness has been significantly reduced to 0.21 inch (5.4mm) from 0.25 inch (6.3mm) in the previous, A17-based model. If you need a tablet you can use while standing, the Mini may be your best choice. Strangely, the front camera has been moved to the longer edge, like the other models, making it less ideal for one-handed use.
With a resolution of 2316x1512, the new 8.5-inch display has slimmer bezels than its predecessor and the highest pixel density of any iPad. It uses an OLED panel with 1,200 nits of peak brightness (600 nits for the entire screen) while still being able to display true black at the pixel level.
It's also the first iPad with an "acoustic display," which uses vibrations from the screen to help produce sound. By eliminating traditional speaker grilles, Apple has also made the mini IP67-rated for water and dust resistance.
It only supports Bluetooth keyboards, but it does support the wireless Pencil Pro, which adds features like rotation, squeeze, haptic feedback and Find My compatibility. Even with the USB-C version, the Mini supports the mouse-like Pencil hover feature. It supports 35W fast charging, although the included adapter only provides 20W.
Unlike previous Mini models (and like the iPad Pro), the new Mini only comes in two colors: "midnight" and "starlight." The Mini starts at $699 with 128GB of storage and Wi-Fi. The storage upgrade options are the same as the basic iPad's. An optional nano-texture display reduces glare for another $100, but is only available on the 256GB and 512GB models.
If you're interested in the Mini for its size rather than its performance, you can still get the previous model for just $499.
The iPad Air remains the sweet spot
The iPad Air is powered by a cut-down version of Apple's M4 chip, with three performance cores and five efficiency cores, and 12GB of RAM. It excels in multitasking, video editing, and other demanding tasks, although its LCD display isn't ideal for HDR work. It's a good choice if you want something larger than the iPad mini without the limitations of the basic iPad. The Air is compatible with the space-efficient Magic Keyboard as well as the Pencil Pro.
The 11-inch iPad Air currently starts at $649 with 128GB of storage, and for an additional $200, you can upgrade to the 13-inch model. The larger version offers higher maximum brightness (600 nits), enhanced bass, and a 4:3 aspect ratio, which reduces scrolling when held horizontally. A comparable upgrade to the iPad Pro would cost $300.
The Air's color options include starlight, space gray, and subtle shades of blue and purple.
Like the Mini, the Air allows upgrades to 256GB and 512GB of storage. For an additional $300 (up from $200), you can expand from 512GB to 1TB – still a more affordable option than the $400 cost on the iPad Pro.
If you're looking for an iPad with a 13-inch display and 1TB of storage, the Air can save you hundreds compared to the Pro.
When is the iPad Pro worth the premium?
The iPad Pro is designed for professionals who demand top performance. Graphic artists will appreciate the smooth experience of drawing on a 120Hz display. For interior designers who need to show clients room layouts in real time, the built-in LiDAR can be genuinely useful.
Video editors who work on the go may find the Pro to be the device of their dreams. Its tandem OLED display uses two stacked panels to achieve up to 1,600 nits of peak HDR brightness, with 1,000 nits sustained across the entire screen.
It's also a great backup camera, with ProRes recording (the 256GB versions can only shoot ProRes at 1080p, though), audio zoom and stereo recording.
The Apple M5 chip easily outperforms the cut-down M4 in the Air, with a USB-C port that supports USB4/Thunderbolt speeds. Only the 1TB and 2TB versions feature a fully enabled M5 with four performance cores, six efficiency cores, and 16GB of RAM, ideal for heavy multitasking.
Other versions of the iPad Pro have one disabled performance core and 12GB of RAM, but they still outperform the Air's M4.
The iPad Pro is compatible with the Pencil Pro, and the Magic Keyboard for iPad Pro, which includes function keys and haptic feedback on the trackpad. The device also boasts four speakers and a TrueDepth front camera with Animoji and Memoji support. It supports 60W fast charging, but not with the included 20W adapter.
The 11" iPad Pro Wi-Fi model currently starts at $1,099 with 256GB of storage (Amazon discounts it $100 vs. Apple's MSRP). The larger 13" iPad Pro is currently an extra $300 (that's a cool and hefty $1,399). Increasing storage to 512GB will be $200. Going from that to 1TB will be $400, ane upgrading from 1TB to 2TB will add $500 to the price. The iPad Pro only comes in black and silver.
Should you add 5G to your iPad?
Adding sub-6GHz 5G to your basic iPad, iPad Mini or iPad Air will make it $150 more expensive. Adding the exact same capability to your iPad Pro will add $200 to the price. Sure, you can turn your smartphone into a hotspot, but doing so will drain the battery of both devices.
The more expensive the iPad, the more practical it may be to invest in cellular connectivity. For a Pro model with 1TB or more of storage, the extra $200 is likely a worthwhile expense.

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.text:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
  November 4, 2026
- Source:
  Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
  Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or significantly disturbing the information it contains.
The research, supported by FAPESP, was published in Physical Review B Letters. It was led by José Carlos Egues, a full professor at the São Carlos Institute of Physics at the University of São Paulo (IFSC-USP) in Brazil, and Yugui Yao of the School of Physics at the Beijing Institute of Technology in China. If experimentally confirmed, their method could simplify quantum computing by removing the need for extra qubits used in certain measurement techniques.
Why Measuring Quantum Information Is So Difficult
Conventional computers store information in bits that have one of two values, 0 or 1. These values can be checked repeatedly without changing the information. Quantum computers work differently because their qubits can exist in superpositions, meaning they can combine the states 0 and 1 in ways that are not possible with conventional bits.
This unusual ability is central to the potential power of quantum computing. However, it also creates a major vulnerability. Quantum states can be disrupted by interactions with their surroundings, including the instruments scientists use to examine them.
"In the conventional formulation of quantum mechanics, a projective measurement causes the system to assume one of the states associated with the measured quantity. Thus, if a qubit has been prepared in a certain superposition of 0 and 1, its direct measurement tends to destroy that superposition and, consequently, the information it contained," says Egues.
To minimize this problem, physicists developed techniques known as "quantum nondemolition measurements," or QND. Many of these approaches use an additional quantum system called an ancilla. Rather than measuring the original qubit directly, researchers transfer information to the ancilla and measure that auxiliary system instead.
The term "ancilla" comes from a Latin word meaning "slave" or "servant." In modern scientific usage, it describes something that performs a supporting function. Here, the ancilla acts as an intermediary, allowing researchers to obtain information while preserving the original qubit as much as possible.
Although effective, these procedures come with practical disadvantages. Scientists must prepare the auxiliary qubits, connect them to the qubits being studied, transfer information between them, and perform repeated measurements. These additional steps require time and equipment, and the complexity becomes increasingly significant as the number of qubits grows.
"Our strategy is different. Instead of transferring the information to an auxiliary qubit, we seek to obtain it from a signal produced by the qubit under study itself," says the researcher.
A Special Quantum Bit That Produces Its Own Signal
The proposed technique relies on the unusual properties of an Andreev qubit. Its name honors Soviet physicist Alexander Andreev (1939-2023), who identified a distinctive quantum process in 1964 that occurs where normal materials meet superconductors.
Superconductors are materials that can conduct electricity without electrical resistance under appropriate conditions. At the boundaries involving these materials, special quantum states known as "Andreev states" can form. In the system studied by the researchers, these states are confined to an extremely small region between two superconducting materials.
These quantum states can represent the basic values 0 and 1, along with superpositions of those values, making them suitable for storing quantum information.
"In the system under consideration, this region is a quantum dot - that is, a nanoscale structure in which electrons are spatially confined - formed in an indium arsenide [InAs] nanowire connected to superconducting materials on both sides. It's in this environment that the states characterizing the Andreev qubit are formed," Egues explains.
The key to the new approach is an electrical phenomenon called a "supercurrent." Unlike the current flowing through ordinary electrical conductors, a supercurrent moves without resistance.
The researchers found that when the Andreev qubit exists in a superposition, the supercurrent develops a component that oscillates over time. These fluctuations arise from quantum interference between the different states making up the superposition.
Crucially, the oscillations are not random. Their behavior contains information about the qubit's underlying quantum state, potentially allowing scientists to determine what that state is without directly measuring the qubit.
"It's precisely that property that we use to read the qubit. It's that supercurrent that lies at the heart of our proposal," the researcher points out.
How a Tiny Electrical Current Reveals Quantum Information
To understand how the technique works, it helps to consider how physicists describe a qubit's state mathematically.
One common representation is the "Bloch sphere," a geometric model in which every possible pure state of a single qubit corresponds to a point on the surface of a sphere. Two angles determine the location of that point.
The first angle describes how much each of the two basic states contributes to the superposition. The second describes their relative phase, which specifies how the quantum components are aligned with one another. Together, these two measurements provide the information needed to identify the qubit's state.
According to the new research, both pieces of information can be extracted from the supercurrent. Its steady component and the size of its oscillations reveal the relative contributions of the two basic states. Meanwhile, the timing of the oscillations provides information about their phase relationship.
"Our study showed that this information is encoded in the supercurrent itself. The supercurrent has a constant component and a fluctuating component. The value of the constant component and the amplitude of the oscillation reveal the proportion of each state (0 and 1) in the superposition, and the moment when that oscillation begins reveals the phase relationship between them. Thus, by measuring how the current varies over time, it's possible to reconstruct the initial state of the qubit," Egues explains.
This means the electrical current effectively carries a signature of the quantum information stored in the system. By observing how that signature changes over time, researchers could reconstruct the qubit's original state.
A Supercurrent That Oscillates Without Voltage
Another surprising feature of the proposed system is that the electrical current can oscillate without an externally applied voltage.
Ordinarily, producing an oscillating supercurrent in this type of superconducting system requires a voltage. This familiar phenomenon is called the "AC Josephson effect."
The researchers predict something different in their Andreev qubit. Here, the current's oscillations arise naturally from the qubit's own quantum evolution. No outside voltage is required to generate them.
"Our system generates a supercurrent that varies over time like an alternating current but without voltage. It's the very evolution of the qubit's state that produces that oscillation," says Egues.
This behavior is important because it transforms quantum activity occurring on an extraordinarily small scale into a detectable electrical signal. The current provides a connection between the microscopic world of quantum states and the larger physical systems scientists can measure.
That connection is what makes the proposed reading technique possible.
Detecting Quantum States With an Extremely Sensitive Sensor
The researchers envision placing the Andreev qubit inside a closed superconducting circuit, allowing its supercurrent to circulate continuously.
Next to the circuit would sit a SQUID (superconducting quantum interference device), a highly sensitive instrument capable of detecting extremely weak magnetic fields.
Whenever an electric current flows, it produces a magnetic field. Because the supercurrent in this system oscillates, the magnetic field it generates also changes over time.
The nearby SQUID could detect these tiny magnetic variations and use them to determine the behavior of the circulating current. Since the current contains information about the qubit's quantum state, the researchers could then reconstruct that state without measuring the qubit directly.
Egues compares the arrangement to two compasses that interact through a magnetic field.
"We can think of the qubit as one compass and the SQUID as another compass. The current in the circuit produces a magnetic field, and the SQUID 'senses' that field. Since the coupling between the two is very weak, the effect of the measuring instrument on the qubit tends to be very small."
The weak interaction between the sensor and the qubit is especially important. It offers a way to gather information while minimizing the disturbance that normally accompanies quantum measurements.
Reading Quantum Information With Almost No Disturbance
In quantum physics, observing a system is not necessarily a harmless process. A measuring instrument interacts with whatever it is attempting to measure, and that interaction can change the system's behavior.
This fundamental difficulty puzzled the earliest researchers studying quantum mechanics. It remains an unavoidable feature of quantum measurements today.
The proposed technique does not eliminate this effect entirely. The SQUID still interacts with the circuit, creating a small amount of feedback that can influence the qubit. However, the team's simulations suggest that this disturbance can be reduced to a level so small that it becomes effectively negligible.
"Our method doesn't eliminate the fundamental problem of quantum measurement. But it can approach the limit of a non-destructive readout and, at the same time, avoid the use of auxiliary qubits - the ancillas - employed in other non-destructive quantum measurement protocols," Egues notes.
The approach could also remove another complication found in some existing techniques. Because researchers would not need to restore the qubit to its original state after every measurement, they could make repeated observations as the state changes.
This would allow scientists to follow the qubit's quantum evolution over time, rather than obtaining information only through separate measurement and reset cycles.
Simulations Achieve Up to 99.85% Accuracy
To investigate whether the method could work outside ideal theoretical conditions, the researchers performed computer simulations designed to account for imperfections that would arise in real experiments.
These calculations included measurement noise, as well as the small amount of feedback introduced by the detection coil. The goal was to determine whether the qubit's state could still be reconstructed accurately despite these disturbances.
The results were encouraging. Depending on the number of measurements used, the simulations produced accuracies of 99.52%, 99.81%, and 99.85%.
According to the researchers, these values fall within the standard thresholds used in quantum error correction schemes, which are designed to manage errors in quantum information processing.
The findings suggest that the method could provide highly accurate quantum state reconstruction without the additional complexity of auxiliary qubits.
However, the technique has not yet been demonstrated experimentally. The results come entirely from theoretical analysis and computer simulations, so researchers still need to establish whether a physical device can achieve comparable performance.
Could This Make Quantum Computers Simpler?
Despite the lack of experimental confirmation, the researchers emphasize that their proposal does not depend on technologies that have yet to be invented.
The calculations use realistic properties drawn from existing quantum systems, and SQUID sensors are already established tools for detecting exceptionally weak magnetic fields and electric currents.
What remains to be built is the specific arrangement of components required to implement the proposed measurement technique.
"All the numbers we used are realistic. In principle, this can be achieved. In fact, we used parameters from existing systems in our calculations. What doesn't yet exist is that geometry, that setup that we proposed," he argues.
This makes the approach different from theoretical concepts that cannot be realized until scientists develop entirely new materials or manufacturing techniques. In principle, the necessary components already exist, although assembling them into the proposed configuration and demonstrating the predicted behavior remain important challenges.
The research offers two potentially significant advances.
From the standpoint of fundamental physics, it predicts that a qubit can produce an oscillating supercurrent resembling the AC Josephson effect, but without requiring an external voltage. Instead, the oscillations emerge from the qubit's own coherent quantum evolution.
From a technological perspective, the study shows how those oscillations could serve as a measurable signature of the qubit's internal state. By analyzing the electrical current, researchers could recover quantum information while causing very little disturbance to the system.
If future experiments confirm these predictions, the method could make reading Andreev qubits substantially simpler. Eliminating auxiliary qubits and repeated resets could reduce the equipment and procedures needed to retrieve quantum information.
More fundamentally, the work points toward an intriguing possibility: information hidden in the microscopic quantum world may be accessible through an electrical current produced by the quantum system itself, offering a promising new way to observe delicate quantum states without destroying them.

articles.title: Apple renews Ted Lasso for season 5
articles.text:
One of Apple’s biggest shows is sticking around for at least one more season. The streamer announced today that Ted Lasso has been renewed for a fifth season on Apple TV, after what the company calls a “record-breaking season four debut.” There are currently no details about the new season nor when it might debut.
Apple renews Ted Lasso for season 5
No word yet on when it might be streaming.
No word yet on when it might be streaming.
Ted Lasso has proven to be one of the tentpole series for Apple TV, and it returned in 2026 after a three-year hiatus. While the season 3 finale seemed to mark the end for the show, season 4 introduced a new cast of characters with head coach Ted — played by Jason Sudeikis, who also just appeared as a voice actor in Grand Theft Auto VI — managing a new professional women’s team.
The news comes amidst a handful of other recent renewals from Apple — including a second season of Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed and multiple new seasons of Slow Horses — in what is turning out to be a strong year for the streaming service, as it attempts to reach a larger audience.

articles.title: Merry Making: Play, Build and Create With NVIDIA Technologies This Holiday Season
articles.text:
The elves don’t have to be the only ones busy in the workshop this holiday season. With the lights twinkling and the gift wrap out, it’s the perfect time to give someone — or yourself — a spark to take a hobby to the next level.
For some, that means diving into a new game. For others, it’s video editing or even building a robot.
NVIDIA technologies offer something for everyone on Santa’s list. Read on to unwrap the details.
Make Time for One More Game
With the holiday break here, everyone can be online to score bragging rights or explore a world that’s only been seen in video game trailers.
For some players, an upgrade means a desktop that brings out the detail in every scene. For others, it’s a laptop they can take along when visiting family, or a way to play in the cloud on a device they already own.
The right setup depends on where and what to play:
- GeForce RTX 50 Series laptops and desktops power the action. Built on the NVIDIA Blackwell architecture, they feature fifth-generation Tensor Cores and fourth-generation RT Cores for AI-enhanced graphics, detailed ray-traced worlds and high frames-per-second gaming.
- NVIDIA RTX Spark PCs combine RTX graphics with NVIDIA’s full-stack AI platform on a single superchip, bringing decades of NVIDIA innovation to slim, premium laptops and compact desktops on the familiar Windows platform. One PC can handle every workflow, from accelerated creation and immersive gaming to powerful local AI — with a variety of designs and all-day battery life.
- See games in a new light with NVIDIA DLSS 5 technology, which boosts performance and enhances image quality. The newest feature, DLSS 3D-Guided Neural Rendering, infuses scenes with lifelike lighting and materials in supported games. Get a glimpse of NBA 2K27 with DLSS 5.
- NVIDIA Reflex and G-SYNC make gameplay more responsive and fluid. Reflex reduces system latency in supported games, while G-SYNC displays use variable refresh rates to deliver smooth, tear-free gaming.
- The GeForce NOW cloud gaming service enables playing top titles anywhere. Stream supported games on compatible laptops, TVs, handhelds and more. Connect to supported game stores to play owned PC games, with more than 4,500 titles available across the service.
Make Something Worth Sharing
For creators with a project that’s been on the backburner, the right gift this season can be the push to finally make it happen. Maybe it’s holiday clips becoming a short film, a snowy scene coming together in 3D or a livestream that brings friends across time zones to the same virtual table. Creators can use NVIDIA systems — such as GeForce RTX 50 Series and RTX Spark devices — to keep up with the workflows, along with NVIDIA Studio tools and technologies for AI acceleration.
Studio Drivers support video editing, 3D design and livestreaming. In supported applications, faster processing gives more room to experiment and refine.
Build a Robot That Thinks
Every robot starts somewhere. This season, it could be under the tree.
Building a robot is an experiment in teaching a device to see or sense its surroundings. A first project might be as simple as using a camera to identify a candy cane or a gingerbread man, then moving on to an app that probes what the camera sees.
Testing brings new questions. Can the robot recognize the candy cane under twinkling lights? Can it tell a frosted gingerbread man from an unfrosted one? Each experiment leaves more to improve and explore.
The NVIDIA Jetson edge AI platform provides the hardware and software to build projects like these. It combines compact computers with the NVIDIA JetPack software development kit to help makers build robots, autonomous machines and intelligent devices.
A Jetson Developer Kit is a gift to explore computer vision, generative AI and multimodal robot control, with the option to add cameras and sensors suited to various projects. AI runs directly on the device, processing information from its surroundings. When ready to take a prototype further, production systems powered by Jetson modules provide a path to deployment.
See how Microduck comes to life with NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super, bringing together robot movement, visual understanding and natural-language interaction. With Hermes Agent and NVIDIA Cosmos, developers can explore how AI connects everyday requests with actions in the physical world.
Bring an SO-101 arm to life with NVIDIA Jetson Orin and explore agentic robotics. Give OpenClaw a simple request, and watch it plan the steps, call NVIDIA tools and check the results. OpenShell runs the agent securely in a sandbox, controlling its access to models and robot tools. Based on ASPIRE skills, the system reuses lessons from past attempts to guide future tasks.
Build a robot companion that chats, moves and understands what it sees, with NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt and Cosmos open models running locally on Jetson Orin Nano 8GB.
For more advanced projects, explore vision language action models and world action models to enable increasingly sophisticated robotic behaviors — beyond simple perception and predefined actions toward understanding natural language instructions, reasoning, planning multistep tasks and interacting with the physical world.
Dive into setup guides and project tutorials in Jetson AI Lab.
Whether it’s a gaming upgrade, a creative project or a first robot, the right tools can open up new possibilities well beyond the holidays.
Explore NVIDIA’s holiday lineup for gamers, creators and makers.
